items.title: Quantifying the geographic mosaic of coevolutionary temperature: from coldspots to hotspots
items.abstract: Abstract The Geographic Mosaic Theory of Coevolution (GMTC) predicts that reciprocal evolutionary effects vary across landscapes, generating hotspots and coldspots. Traditionally, these states are treated as discrete categories, even though the intensity of coevolutionary selection can vary continuously. To capture this variation, we introduce a concept of coevolutionary temperature, ranging from coldspot to hotspot. We propose two complementary metrics to quantify it: reciprocity and strength of pairwise evolutionary effects. We also extend the GMTC framework beyond its traditional focus on pairwise systems to species-rich communities. Applying this approach to empirical plant-pollinator networks in a fragmented landscape, we find pronounced geographic mosaics in coevolutionary temperature. Smaller habitat patches support small, highly connected, and weakly nested communities with high reciprocity and strength, suggesting that they act as coevolutionary hotspots. In contrast, larger patches host species-rich, poorly connected, and highly nested communities with low reciprocity and strength, consistent with coldspots. At the interaction scale, reciprocity depends on degree similarity, with interactions between species that have similar numbers of partners exhibiting higher reciprocity. Together, these results highlight the strong dependence of coevolutionary effects on spatial variation in community structure and show how extending the geographic mosaic framework to species-rich communities can deepen our understanding of coevolution in complex systems.

items.title: Climate‐driven compositional shifts across a temperate–subtropical island ecotone
items.abstract: Climate change is expected to drive substantial shifts in species distributions, yet ecological responses are often delayed under disequilibrium dynamics, limiting the effectiveness of range‐based indicators for detecting ongoing change. Compositional approaches have been proposed as an alternative; however, conventional comparisons based on gradient shape or pointwise differences may fail to detect change when the overall gradient structure is conserved, because small and spatially heterogeneous differences cancel out across the gradient. Here, we address this limitation by presenting a direction‐sensitive analytical framework that integrates signed differences along environmental gradients. Using a comprehensive dataset of island floras across a temperate–subtropical transition in South Korea, we quantify temporal changes in the relative representation of warm‐temperate and subtropical plant (WTSP) assemblages. By emphasizing proportional changes along latitudinal gradients, we detect directional redistribution within communities even in the absence of pronounced changes in gradient shape. Our results reveal patterns consistent with northward redistribution of WTSP composition across survey periods, despite minimal changes in overall gradient form, indicating that community‐level redistribution can occur prior to detectable range shifts or richness changes. These findings highlight the sensitivity of cumulative, direction‐sensitive compositional metrics for detecting early ecological responses to climate warming. More broadly, this study provides a generalizable framework for detecting compositional redistribution through cumulative inference, even when conventional approaches may have limited sensitivity under some conditions, and for identifying early signals of climate‐driven change across gradient‐structured ecological systems. Transitional systems may therefore serve as particularly sensitive contexts for detecting incipient biogeographical change under ongoing warming.

items.title: Tools for the computation of acoustic parameters of narrow band high frequency clicks of odontocetes
items.abstract: Acoustic recording can be a very interesting way of monitoring cetaceans for conservation purposes. However, some sympatric species produce very similar sounds and are thus difficult to study specifically. In this work, we are interested in characterizing the narrow band high frequency (NBHF) clicks emitted by several species of odontocetes, among which all porpoises and some species of dolphins. The traditional acoustic parameters (durations, frequencies, bandwidths) of NBHF clicks show several drawbacks, such as redundancy, lack of precise definition, and poor robustness to noise. In this study, we propose a new method of characterizing NBHF clicks by fitting a Gabor wavelet to the signal and thus extracting two specific metrics, the Gabor frequency and the Gabor duration. We first assess the theoretical usefulness of this mathematical model, and then test it against traditional measurements in numerical examples with varying levels of noise. Our method is then applied to two empirical datasets recorded in South America, a place were many sympatric species are found to emit NBHF clicks. Two large sets of signals are thus analyzed and compared : one of clicks of Peale’s dolphins (Cephalorhynchus australis) from Chaihuin bay, Chile, and the other of clicks of Franciscana dolphins (Pontoporia blainvillei) from San Clemente del Tuyu, Argentina. Our metrics allow a good characterization of each species’ clicks with quick and efficient computation, with good reproducibility across different recording devices, and a clear separation of the two species. We suggest it could be applied to more datasets from different species, and possibly be used to classify NBHF of sympatric species.

items.title: Fate of legacy ammonium in the coastal Baltic Sea
items.abstract: Abstract. Eutrophication has enriched coastal sediments globally with organic matter (OM), fuelling internal nutrient loading once benthic hypoxia occurs. Internal ammonium (NH4+) loading may be particularly prominent in the coastal Baltic Sea due to the existence of a substantial NH4+ pool in its sediments, accumulated via OM burial and mineralization over long-term eutrophication. However, despite its potential to exacerbate eutrophication, internal NH4+ loading has so far received little attention in the coastal Baltic Sea. It remains poorly understood for how long the benthic legacy OM may affect both the benthic NH4+ pool and the internal NH4+ loading via sediment-water NH4+ effluxes, especially under varying oxygen availabilities. To reconstruct past and predict future NH4+ effluxes in response to different OM loading and bottom water oxygen conditions, we developed a reactive transport model for muddy, organic-rich sediments of the coastal Baltic Sea. Our model results suggest that the legacy OM in the coastal sediments is the key driver sustaining benthic NH4+ pools and effluxes both today and well into the future. As today’s OM loading is constantly adding new OM to the already existing legacy loading, the benthic NH4+ pool will continuously grow and result in persistently elevated NH4+ effluxes in the future, even under oxic conditions. If external measures strongly reduce OM loading to eventually pre-industrial levels, the NH4+ pool still continues to grow for at least 80 years due to the continued mineralization of legacy OM, which keeps NH4+ effluxes elevated for at least 180 years before eventually returning to pre-industrial levels in the year 2300. These model results highlight the persistence of eutrophication legacy effects and their importance for ecosystem management of the coastal Baltic Sea. The knowledge obtained is beneficial also for other anthropogenically impacted coastal seas with similar geomorphology as the Baltic Sea.

items.title: Impact of climate extremes on socio-economic characteristics of peri-urban mountain settlements
items.abstract: Abstract Rapid urbanisation and a changing climate are transforming the Indian Himalayan Region (IHR), driving profound socio-economic and environmental changes. Himachal Pradesh, located in the western IHR, exemplifies these transformations. As climate change undermines the viability of traditional livelihoods such as agriculture and pastoralism, rural households are increasingly shifting towards secondary and tertiary occupations through livelihood diversification within villages or migration to urban peripheries. This trend is particularly visible in settlements located near major infrastructure, such as highways and hydropower plants, and urban centres where economic opportunities are concentrated. However, such peri-urbanisation often unfolds in an unregulated and unplanned manner, straining the fragile mountain ecosystems and amplifying vulnerabilities to extreme climate events. Despite this, peri-urban mountain settlements remain largely overlooked in policy and research. Fragmented governance structures and overlapping rural and urban jurisdictions result in administrative neglect, exposing these areas to cascading social, environmental, and economic pressures. This study investigates the developmental and climate-induced challenges faced by peri-urban settlements in Himachal Pradesh. Drawing on policy reviews, secondary literature, and primary research, it examines the interlinked risks of climate change and unregulated peri-urban growth, their impacts on livelihoods and infrastructure, and the associated gendered vulnerabilities. A review of the Indian policy landscape highlights critical gaps in existing plans, frameworks, and governance approaches for addressing these compounding challenges. Building on field-based and policy best practices, the study proposes context-sensitive recommendations to strengthen adaptation planning and support climate-resilient development across the peri-urban regions of the IHR.

items.title: Evolutionary history suggests nymphal origin of antennal expansions in adult leaf‐footed bugs
items.abstract: Abstract Insect antennae morphology is highly conserved in many insect families, yet in some clades, elaborations of antennae form are more common. Leaf‐footed bugs (Hemiptera: Coreidae) are one case where there is considerable variation in antennal morphology. Antennae can be rectilinear, with cylindrical antennomeres, or have laterally flattened expansions that differ in which antennomeres they occur. Strikingly, such variation is also found across development, where nymphs and adults can also display different antennal shapes. Thus, Coreidae presents a unique opportunity to study how much shared ancestry and development influence antennal variation. We characterized the antennal expansion across a recent Coreidae phylogeny using research‐grade iNaturalist photos and primary taxonomic descriptions of adults (species) and nymphs (genus). We then performed ancestral reconstructions to estimate how many transitions between antennal states occurred across the phylogeny and compared these patterns between adults and nymphs. We found that adult antennal expansions are rare and restricted to Coreinae. The reconstructed history is consistent with repeated transitions to expanded adult antennae across Coreinae, with expansion most commonly confined to the third antennomere and concentrated in a few genera. In contrast, nymphal data reveal that antennal expansions are more widespread and often occur in genera whose adults lack expansions, suggesting that conspicuous antennal morphologies can be developmentally transient and frequently lost before adulthood. Together, our results indicate that adult antennal expansion is associated with nymphal expansion in the sampled genera and may reflect repeated retention or prolongation of a morphology expressed during development. Additionally, we provide a comparative framework for future work on the functional and developmental bases of exaggerated antennal forms.

items.title: Suspected white shark (Carcharodon carcharias) predation on an adult Atlantic sturgeon (Acipenser oxyrinchus) from the Gulf of Maine
items.abstract: Abstract Atlantic sturgeon ( Acipenser oxyrinchus ) are threatened under the United States Endangered Species Act in the Gulf of Maine (GoM), where natural sources of adult mortality remain poorly documented. We report a stranded adult female Atlantic Sturgeon (224-cm total length) recovered in Scarborough, Maine, USA, with injury consistent with predation by a juvenile white shark ( Carcharodon carcharias ) and inconsistent with vessel strike. Bite-mark analysis indicated a shark of at least 2.6 m total length, matching juveniles increasingly documented in nearby Saco Bay. The stranding coincided with peak seasonal white shark activity within known sturgeon foraging area, supporting predation as the most parsimonious cause of death. Predation on adult Atlantic sturgeon has only been known via tooth-mark injuries on surviving individuals in Canadian weir fisheries making this the first direct evidence of the interaction in the GoM. As white sharks expand into warming GoM waters, such encounters may become more frequent, highlighting the need for continued monitoring of shifting predator-prey dynamics.

items.title: Динамика роста и половые различия длиннотных размеров верхней конечности и ее звеньев обследуемых детско-юношеского возраста (обзор литературы)
items.abstract: Роль верхней конечности в жизни человека зачастую недооценивают, в то время как она является сложноустроенным и высоко координированным органом труда, выполняющим разнообразные двигательные функции. Цель исследования: изучить особенности возрастной изменчивости продольных размеров верхней конечности и ее звеньев (плеча, предплечья и кисти) обследуемых детско-юношеского возраста мужского и женского пола. Материалы и методы. В работе использованы теоретические методы исследования: анализ и сравнение данных литературы. Методология исследования включала сопоставление результатов за период с середины XX века по настоящее время. Общий объем изученных рукописей составил 39 штук. Выполнена критическая оценка анализируемого материала авторов, занимающихся изучением особенностей развертки, интенсивности роста и сроков достижения зрелости продольных размеров верхней конечности и ее звеньев у лиц мужского и женского пола. Результаты и обсуждение. Выполненный анализ показал отсутствие единых критериев оценки динамики роста верхней конечности и ее звеньев. Рассогласованность выявлена при сравнительной оценке таких ключевых параметров как: количество и сроки начала и окончания перекреста кривых роста длины верхней конечности ее звеньев у лиц разного пола, возраст начала проявления выраженных половых различий и сроки их завершения, которые могли варьировать в широких пределах. Установленные различия связаны с изучением лиц разных регионов проживания, влиянием на них различных климатогеографических и социально-экономических условий, приводящих к рассогласованности в проявлении эпохальных тенденций. items.title: From Jiangnan water land to Greater Shanghai: exploring ‘nature-culture holistic conservation’ in an international metropolis
items.abstract: Abstract In this paper, through a policy and planning analysis of nature-culture integration, a ‘nature-culture holistic conservation’ paradigm is proposed to address the disconnection between nature and culture in the development of Chinese metropolises. Drawing on the historic urban landscape (HUL) approach and integrating the Eastern philosophy of ‘harmony between heaven and humans’, this study takes Shanghai as a case to construct a theoretical framework for the holistic conservation of 'nature-culture ecosystems' tailored to megacities. The research reveals that Shanghai’s urban genetic code is deeply embedded in a nature-culture foundation characterised by the organic integration of ‘mountains, waters, settlements, and fields’, which has shaped the city's distinctive urban character and value. However, owing to factors such as the megacity’s vast spatial scale and fragmented administrative governance structures, the existing conservation system suffers from significant fragmentation at the planning, governance, and practice levels, which constrains the realisation of holistic value. The paper argues that Shanghai should transcend the single-element conservation model by incorporating the recognition and interpretation of ‘nature-culture’ relationships into planning frameworks across different scales and by considering the natural foundations and cultural genes of the Jiangnan water system as core strategic resources for sustainable development. Strategies include the following: at the cognitive level, constructing a ‘nature-culture system’ framework; at the planning level, integrating holistic conservation into territorial spatial planning (TSP) and identifying high-composite-value areas; and at the governance level, establishing multiscalar coordination mechanisms. This study provides theoretical support for shaping Shanghai into an ‘international metropolis with Jiangnan characteristics’ and offers a reference for the sustainable development of comparable metropolises.

items.title: Dynamic Natural-Capital Accounting under Tipping Risk and Spatial Contagion: A Regenerative Forest Network Model
items.abstract: Abstract Classical renewable-resource models value the biological stock that remains after current extraction, whereas ecological resilience theory emphasizes the possibility of alternative regimes separated by tipping boundaries. This paper combines these perspectives in a networked forest-management problem with two continuous ecological states---harvestable biomass and resilience---and a discrete ecological regime for each patch. Harvesting lowers biomass and resilience and increases the endogenous intensity of a harmful regime shift; regenerative effort rebuilds ecological capital and reduces that intensity. The hazard also rises with exposure to degraded neighboring patches, generating spatial contagion. The planner solves an infinite-horizon controlled piecewise-deterministic Markov decision problem. Rather than assuming positive ecological shadow values, we derive them from primitive order conditions by monotone dynamic programming. Six structural results follow. The model nests Clark's classical target-stock problem; sufficiently large expected tipping losses generate \emph{regenerative inactivity}, with zero harvest and positive restoration; the optimal harvest rule contains a direct tipping-risk precautionary wedge; degraded neighbors can induce preventive closure before local collapse; a next-generation matrix yields a spectral threshold for early-stage landscape cascades; and Perron--Frobenius sensitivity identifies the patches at which restoration most effectively reduces systemic ecological risk. A stylized numerical illustration shows how restoration can move a connected forest from a supercritical to a subcritical cascade regime. The framework extends the economics of endogenous regime shifts by making resilience a managed state and by adding network contagion and systemic restoration targeting. JEL codes: C61; Q23; Q28; Q57. items.title: An escalation toward risk: climate change impacts on the distribution, genetic diversity, and conservation of Neesiochloa barbata (Poaceae: Chloridoideae: Pappophorinae)
items.abstract: Abstract Climate change represents a primary threat to global biodiversity, particularly in seasonally dry tropical forests (SDTF), affecting species distribution, genetic diversity, and ecosystem conservation. Neesiochloa barbata (Poaceae: Chloridoideae: Pappophorinae) is a grass species belonging to a monotypic genus endemic to the Caatinga, the largest SDTF in South America. In this study, we addressed conservation issues related to the impacts of the climate crisis (2080–2100) on the potential distribution, genetic diversity, and structure of N. barbata populations to: (a) assess extinction risk; (b) estimate the future distribution overlap with protected areas (PA); and (c) identify priority areas for conservation. We assessed the current conservation status from Not Evaluated (NE) to Least Concern (LC), however, under future climate scenarios, suitable habitat for N. barbata will be reduced, elevating the threat level to Near Threatened (NT) and finally to Endangered (EN). This severe contraction of climatically suitable areas results in a progressive escalation in extinction risk: LC > NT > EN. Despite the overall loss of suitable habitat, the remaining future niche shows a slight spatial shift toward the boundaries of existing PA (increasing from 39% to 43%). The haplotype network (nrDNA and cpDNA) showed distinct polymorphism rates between the genomes, consistent with the DAPC clustering (best K = 2 and Northern and Southern haplogroups). This genetic structure highlights lineages with distinct evolutionary histories that must be preserved. The reduction in suitable areas and the rising extinction risk underscore the urgent need for targeted conservation in the Caatinga. While the current PA system is crucial for protecting climatic refugia, the expansion and connection of these areas are essential to ensure the long-term persistence and genetic heritage of N. barbata against the climate crisis.

items.title: Carbon balance, canopy spatial structure and renovation benchmarks in old cocoa agroforestry systems of the Dominican Republic
items.abstract: Abstract Rehabilitation and renovation (Rh/Re) are essential elements in the cocoa cultivation cycle. Cocoa farmers must decide on whether to rehabilitate (Rh) or to renovate (Re) a cocoa orchard when its productivity declines due to ageing, disease outbreaks or other causes. Cocoa Rh/Re interventions alter standing biomass while retaining variable amounts of old canopy, roots and soil carbon. We quantified carbon stocks and structural attributes across a 52-farm project frame in in two growing regions in the Dominican Republic using 40 vegetation inventories, 50 soil records, 26 preparation-site intervention records and 25 matched inventory–intervention pairs. Above-ground biomass was estimated with diameter-compatible allometry; woody roots and 0–15 cm soil carbon was accounted for separately. Mean live-biomass stock was 192.63 ± 34.21 Mg CO₂e ha⁻¹ (n = 40) and mean live-plus-soil stock was 306.60 ± 36.45 Mg CO₂e ha⁻¹ for 38 farms with linked soil data. In matched farms, estimated preparation-site above-ground removal averaged 93.72 ± 11.44 Mg CO₂e ha⁻¹, which is almost half of the above-carbon stocks. Group-specific Clark–Evans spatial indices, vertical structure and soil latent factors were integrated at farm level. Across all farms, 21 total-stem arrangements (cacao + companion trees) were classified as aggregated, 16 as approximately random and 3 as regular. Finally, a fixed 35-year renovation scenario produced 73.94 Mg CO₂e ha⁻¹ of new cocoa and boundary-tree stock, 19.78 Mg CO₂e ha⁻¹ below the mean removal proxy suggesting that Rh/Re interventions do not compensate for the above-ground carbon removed from target cacao orchards. This study provides a reproducible plot-level accounting framework for Rh/Re implementation while distinguishing measured stocks, removed above-ground stocks, residual below-ground reserves and future regrowth and carbon sequestration scenarios.

items.title: Aquatic subsidies increase the resilience of riparian spider communities after pulse disturbance
items.abstract: Climatic events such as intense winds and rainfall act as strong pulse disturbances in many ecosystems. Although these disturbances can abruptly alter community structure and dynamics, recovery depends on community resilience, which may be enhanced by resource availability. Cross-ecosystem subsidies can increase prey availability for generalist predators, potentially buffering communities against the effects of disturbance. In this study, we tested whether aquatic subsidies (i.e., emergence of aquatic insects) enhance the resilience of spider communities following unpredictable climatic pulse disturbances. We conducted a field experiment in four Atlantic Rainforest streams, simulating pulse disturbances in riparian and inland plots. We surveyed vegetation-dwelling spiders one day before and four times after disturbance simulations to estimate changes in abundance and community resilience, while stable isotope analyses assessed the contribution of aquatic insects to spider diets. Riparian spiders consumed more aquatic insects than inland spiders, and spider abundance was 24% higher in riparian plots. Disturbance effects were also 43% stronger in riparian communities. Despite this stronger immediate impact, recovery models indicated greater resilience in riparian spider communities, highlighting the role of emergent aquatic insect subsidies in post-disturbance recovery. Our findings demonstrate that cross-ecosystem resource linkages can enhance the resilience of terrestrial predator communities to climatic pulse disturbance.

items.title: Above-ground biomass recovery after fire in a West African semi-deciduous forest invaded by Cedrela odorata L.
items.abstract: Abstract Key message Invasion by Cedrela odorata L. can substantially contribute to above-ground biomass recovery after fire while simultaneously altering forest composition. Context Tropical forests are increasingly exposed to successive disturbances that can alter forest dynamics and ecosystem functioning. Understanding long-term responses to disturbances offers a solution for sustainable ecosystem services management. Aims This study assessed the long-term aboveground biomass recovery in a tropical semi-deciduous forest that has undergone silvicultural treatments, devastating fire, and invasion by Cedrela odorata L . We also aimed to quantify the contributions of three species groups: local commercial species (Com), C. odorata (Ced), and non-commercial species (Sec), i.e., all other species. Methods First, we used tree inventory data (diameter at breast height ≥ 10 cm) collected over 42 years from 25 permanent plots covering 100 ha. Then, we used a Bayesian framework to infer the aboveground biomass recovery trajectory. Finally, we analyzed the respective effects of fire severity and silvicultural treatment intensity on above-ground biomass recovery. Results Following invasion by C. odorata, 90% of the biomass lost after the fire will be recovered in less than 50 years. Fire severity affects biomass recovery more than silvicultural treatments. Predictions at the end of recovery indicate a biomass composed of 33% C. odorata , 50% commercial species, and 17% non-commercial species. Conclusion Invasion by C. odorata has advantages and inconveniences for the recovery of forest attributes. These results highlight the importance of adapting forest management strategies to balance ecological resilience and timber production in West Africa, where forest resources are threatened.

items.title: Diversity of Cladocera and Cyclestherida (Crustacea, Branchiopoda, Diplostraca) in continental waterbodies of southern Vietnam
items.abstract: Microscopic crustaceans, particularly Branchiopoda, often dominate the zooplankton and microzoobenthos of continental waterbodies and are widely utilised in aquaculture as a vital food source for fish and invertebrates. Despite their ecological and economic importance, the knowledge of their diversity and distribution remains highly uneven across the globe. Tropical Southeast Asia, in particular, harbours a rich but, still inadequately documented cladoceran and branchiopod fauna, with many regions remaining largely unexplored or represented only by few historical records. The Republic of Vietnam represents an example of territoty with such knowledge gap: the last comprehensive, systematic survey of its branchiopod fauna was conducted as early as 1980 and, since that time, only fragmented and localised contributions have been added. Consequently, our current understanding of the species richness, biogeographical patterns and environmental drivers in this biodiversity hotspot is severely outdated and incomplete, hampering both fundamental research and applied conservation efforts.To address this gap in current knowledge, we present a new, extensive dataset on samples collected during 2023–2025 in southern Vietnam within the framework of the Joint Vietnam–Russia Tropical Science and Technology Research Center. In total, 476 samples from 360 distinct localities were investigated, covering a wide range of permanent and temporary waterbodies of various types (e.g. ponds, lakes, reservoirs, rice paddies and temporary pools). Sampling was performed using plankton nets and all material was processed at the A.N. Severtsov Institute of Ecology and Evolution following standard hydrobiological protocols. Species identification was based on both recent taxonomic monographs and the extensive expertise of our team, which is internationally recognised as a leader in Southeast Asian Cladocera research. The resulting dataset is published as a Darwin Core Archive in the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF) and includes, for each sampling event, precise geographic coordinates, date of collection and collector information. This comprehensive, georeferenced resource not only fills a critical geographic and temporal gap in branchiopod biodiversity data, but also provides a solid baseline for future monitoring, biogeographic analyses and assessments of environmental change in the rapidly developing landscapes of southern Vietnam. The dataset contains information on branchiopod zooplankton and microzoobenthos (Branchiopoda, Diplostraca, Cladocera and Cyclestherida) from many permanent and temporary waterbodies in southern Vietnam. The branchiopod communities of the region were poorly known as taxonomy of the group has changed a lot since the latest revision of the local fauna (Thang et al. 1980). Our core data table contains 2415 records belonging to 80 presumptive (76 recognised) species and 45 genera of Cladocera and Cyclestherida from 360 locations. The families Chydoridae with 45 (42 recognised) species from 27 genera and Sididae (nine species from five genera) are the most diverse. No invasive species were found. Results of the current study increase our knowledge about microplankton and microzoobenthos of Vietnam and SE Asia in general.

items.title: Same Void, Different Spatial Logics: Rethinking Natah through Asian Courtyard Traditions
items.abstract: The morphological similarity of courtyards across cultures leaves a fundamental question: are seemingly similar empty spaces also understood, shaped, and valued in the same way? This study examines the Balinese natah, with traditional Chinese and Indian courtyards as conceptual comparisons, through a structured literature review and comparative document analysis. The data were analyzed through ontological, epistemological, and axiological dimensions. The results show that all three regard emptiness as a meaningful space, but through different mechanisms. The natah functions as a relational center that orients building masses and is shaped through spatial knowledge and socio-ritual practices; the Chinese courtyard emphasizes axiality, hierarchy, and privacy; whereas the Indian courtyard demonstrates diverse relationships among central space, Vastu, ritual, and social order. These findings question the adequacy of the courtyard as a cross-cultural morphological category. This study offers an ontological-epistemological-axiological framework for interpreting empty space and emphasizes that the conservation of the natah needs to preserve the relationships, knowledge, and practices that make it meaningful.

items.title: Integrating ecohydrological modelling and participatory processes to co-design multifunctional forest management
items.abstract: Mediterranean forests are becoming denser, drier, and more combustible because of natural and human-driven factors. Forest managers report that managing them is increasingly costly relative to its economic returns and requires informed decision-making supported by appropriate tools and dialogue. This study couples the Decision Support System (DSS) CAFE (Carbon, Aqua, Fire and Eco-resilience) with structured participatory processes across four Living Labs in Spain, Morocco, and Italy, representing distinct Mediterranean socioecological systems: semiarid Aleppo pine forests, traditional argan woodlands with goat grazing, and cork-oak silvopastoral systems. The aim was to evaluate whether management co-designed in this way is resilient to climate disturbance while improving ecosystem services (ES). In three rounds of co-design workshops, stakeholders identified priority ES, agreed on the management actions to enhance them, and evaluated alternatives generated by the DSS. Their priorities were remarkably consistent across sites, focusing on wildfire risk, water availability, and biomass extraction. Preferred interventions were ecologically sound and consistent with field evidence. To this end, CAFE was expanded to quantify locally relevant ES that had not previously been modelled, including argan fruit production, cork extraction, fodder availability, and bark regeneration. Model outputs agreed well with published data at all sites. However, in none of the four sites did stakeholders select the most resilient options available, and their selections were statistically indistinguishable from random choice. These findings highlight that resilience to climate disturbance remains difficult to perceive without appropriate metrics. Making resilience an explicit objective of participatory planning is a necessary contribution of decision-support tools for Mediterranean forests facing increasing uncertainty.

items.title: Salinity filtering and hydrological stage transitions drive the community reassembly of eukaryotes and particle-attached bacteria in Yuncheng Salt Lake
items.abstract: Extreme salt lakes represent natural model systems for investigating microbial community assembly under strong environmental filtering. However, cross-kingdom associations between eukaryotes and particle-attached bacteria, as well as the combined effects of salinity and hydrological phase transitions on community structure, remain poorly unresolved. We conducted a field survey in Yuncheng Salt Lake, comparing eukaryotic and particle-attached bacterial communities across high-salinity and low-salinity habitats during crystallization and stabilization phases. Salinity served as the dominant environmental filter and exerted stronger filtering effects on eukaryotes than on particle-attached bacteria, whereas phase effects were more pronounced under low-salinity, particularly for eukaryotes. Within deterministic processes, the relative contribution of variable selection for eukaryotes increased from 13.33% to 24.44%, while particle-attached bacteria became increasingly dominated by stochastic processes from crystallization to stabilization. The high-salinity network exhibited greater connectivity than the low-salinity network and was characterized by bacterial connectors as topologically central nodes. Functional potential of particle-attached bacteria was phase-dependent: crystallization was associated with carbon and energy metabolism pathways, whereas stabilization shifted toward heterotrophic carbon utilization and motility. In the high-salinity network, connector taxa were additionally associated with predicted functional potential related to attachment, nutrient acquisition, stress tolerance, and sulfur/methane metabolism. These findings elucidate the assembly and adaptive strategies of microbial communities in salt lakes, underscoring the critical roles of both salinity and hydrological phase in driving cross-kingdom community reorganization. This study provides novel insights into the ecology of extreme saline environments and the dynamics of aquatic microbial communities under environmental stress.

items.title: Aromatic polyketides from the marine-derived fungus Aspergillus unguis PM03: α-glucosidase inhibitory activity, structure-activity relationship, molecular docking and ADMET evaluation
items.abstract: Chemical investigation of Aspergillus unguis PM03 yielded eight known aromatic polyketides, including unguinol (1), nidulin (2), 2,4-dichlorounguinol (3), 2-chlorounguinol (4), emeguisin B (5), aspergillusether A (6), guisinol (7), and isosclerone (8). Their structures were established by spectroscopic analysis and comparison with published data. All isolated compounds were evaluated for cytotoxicity against four human cancer cell lines (KB, Hep-G2, A549, and MCF-7) and for α-glucosidase inhibitory activity. None of the compounds exhibited significant cytotoxicity (IC50 > 128 μM). Compounds 1, 3, 5, 7, and 8 inhibited α-glucosidase, with guisinol (7) showing the strongest activity (IC50 = 4.01 μM), followed by isosclerone (8) (11.39 μM), emeguisin B (5) (24.31 μM), unguinol (1) (26.28 μM), and 2,4-dichlorounguinol (3) (28.83 μM). To our knowledge, this is the first report of the α-glucosidase inhibitory activity of compounds 1–7. A preliminary structure–activity relationship analysis suggested that the substitution pattern of the aromatic polyketides may affect their inhibitory activity. Molecular docking of compounds 1–7 and four aromatic polyketides previously isolated in our studies was performed against penicillin-binding protein 2a (PBP2a; PDB ID: 1MWT), together with in silico ADMET prediction to assess their pharmacokinetic properties.

items.title: Rights of Nature and the Rights of Wild Animals: Guiding Principles for Resolving Human–Wildlife Conflicts
items.abstract: Abstract Rights of Nature (RoN) is increasingly used to challenge conventional legal frameworks, restructure governance over ecosystems and living beings, and rethink human–nature relations; however, its role in addressing human–wildlife conflict remains undertheorized and insufficiently defined. Using the case of the Andean (spectacled) bear ( Tremarctos ornatus ) in Ecuador’s Andean Bear Corridor, and the emerging conflict between individual bears and local farmers, this article presents an innovative RoN framework for conflict governance. The research employs a socio-legal approach – doctrinal analysis, qualitative interdisciplinary fieldwork (2022–2025) across five local communities in the Ecuadorian Andes and informal expert interviews – to compile a set of rights at multiple scales (ecosystem, species, individual animal) and identifies relevant principles of human–wildlife conflicts based on jurisprudence. Practical tests for consideration by courts and regulators are proposed: (i) an interspecies capabilities assessment outlining parameters for individual animal well-being and flourishing; (ii) a precautionary and eco-proportionality framework to balance the interests of humans, animals, and ecosystems; and (iii) adherence to principles that prioritize nature in decision-making (including for individual wild animals). Applied to the Andean bear case study, the proposed RoN framework could shift practice from conflict and killing to coexistence. The article argues that the RoN framework, including rights for wild animals, is more than solely a legal instrument, but a catalyst for reshaping human–nature relationships. The RoN framework presented provides a model to implement and operationalize RoN approaches in the wider Andean Bear Corridor and transnationally for other species in other countries accounting for individual animal rights.

items.title: First Integrated Ecological Assessment of a Marginal Golden Eagle Population in the Moroccan Atlantic Sahara
items.abstract: Las poblaciones marginales de Aquila chrysaetos que habitan el Sahara se encuentran entre las menos estudiadas y más aisladas de la especie. Realizamos la primera evaluación ecológica integrada de la población de A. chrysaetos del Sahara Atlántico marroquí, combinando datos reproductivos, de dieta, climáticos, morfométricos y de movimiento. En abril de 2026, muestreamos seis territorios históricos y confirmamos la reproducción en tres, con cuatro pollos registrados en tres nidos activos. Estimamos en aproximadamente 2500 ha (25 km2) el área defendida por una pareja reproductora. La dieta estuvo dominada por Uromastyx y Lepus, que conjuntamente representaron 51 de las 56 presas identificadas. Equipamos tres pollos con transmisores GPS-GSM, pero solo uno proporcionó datos de movimiento. El juvenil permaneció cerca de su territorio natal durante aproximadamente 40 días después de abandonar el nido e inició la dispersión natal a los 115 días de edad. Recorrió aproximadamente 460 km en 3 días y alcanzó un punto artificial de abastecimiento de agua para ganado en Mauritania, a unos 100 km del territorio natal. La temperatura máxima diaria alcanzó 48°C. El juvenil entró en un depósito elevado de agua para ganado el 27 de mayo y no pudo salir; la actividad del acelerómetro cesó el 29 de mayo y el cadáver fue localizado durante una inspección de campo el 30 de mayo. El ahogamiento fue la causa de muerte más probable. Aunque un único evento de mortalidad no permite establecer efectos a escala poblacional, identifica un riesgo antropogénico potencialmente prevenible en un paisaje hiperárido. Estos resultados aportan información ecológica de referencia para esta población marginal y ponen de manifiesto la necesidad de continuar los censos reproductivos, ampliar el seguimiento mediante GPS-GSM, evaluar la variabilidad de las presas y las precipitaciones y analizar las infraestructuras de abastecimiento de agua para ganado como posible fuente de mortalidad. [Traducción de Jesús Bautista-Rodríguez]

items.title: Constraints on cosmology and baryonic feedback with a joint analysis of Dark Energy Survey Year 3 lensing data and ACT DR6 thermal Sunyaev-Zel’dovich effect observations
items.abstract: We present a joint analysis of weak gravitational lensing (shear) data obtained from the first three years of observations by the Dark Energy Survey and thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (tSZ) effect measurements from a combination of Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) and Planck data. A combined analysis of shear (which traces the projected mass) with the tSZ effect (which traces the projected gas pressure) can jointly probe both the distribution of matter and the thermodynamic state of the gas, accounting for the correlated effects of baryonic feedback on both observables. We detect the shear$~\times~$tSZ cross-correlation at a 21$σ$ significance, the highest to date, after minimizing the bias from cosmic infrared background leakage in the tSZ map. By jointly modeling the small-scale shear auto-correlation and the shear$~\times~$tSZ cross-correlation, we obtain $S_8 = 0.811^{+0.015}_{-0.012}$ and $Ω_{\rm m} = 0.263^{+0.023}_{-0.030}$, results consistent with primary CMB analyses from Planck and P-ACT. We find evidence for reduced thermal gas pressure in dark matter halos with masses $M < 10^{14} \, M_{\odot}/h$, supporting predictions of enhanced feedback from active galactic nuclei on gas thermodynamics. A comparison of the inferred matter power suppression reveals a $2-4σ$ tension with hydrodynamical simulations that implement mild baryonic feedback, as our constraints prefer a stronger suppression. Finally, we investigate biases from cosmic infrared background leakage in the tSZ-shear cross-correlation measurements, employing mitigation techniques to ensure a robust inference. Our code is publicly available on GitHub.

items.title: How well can we forecast local magnetic ground perturbations with existing space weather monitoring resources?
items.abstract: Abstract. In this study we examine how a deep-learning based forecast of local, ground-based geomagnetic field variations trained on solar wind parameters available in real time might be improved by including information contained in an accurate forecast of solar wind conditions. This is accomplished using a long short-term memory (LSTM) model together with magnetic field measurements made at the Rørvik magnetometer station in Mid-Norway. We use Advanced Composition Explorer (ACE) satellite measurements of solar wind and interplanetary magnetic field (IMF) conditions at the first Sun-Earth Lagrange point, and historical lists of coronal mass ejection (CME) impacts at Earth to train and validate the LSTM model. We find that accurate information about the IMF Bz component and solar wind speed are important for obtaining a reasonably accurate (r² ≥ 0.5) forecast of local geomagnetic activity over forecasting horizons beyond ~ 3 h. Information about CME arrival time is only important when simultaneously accompanied by accurate, relatively high-resolution information about IMF Bz. In the absence of the latter, CME arrival time information does not contribute to model performance. This empirical result amounts to a quantitative demonstration of the widely recognized impact of IMF orientation on CME geoeffectiveness. This result also highlights that new innovations, probably in the form of new prediction capabilities of conditions in interplanetary space, will be required to produce accurate forecasts of local geomagnetic disturbances beyond a forecast horizon of 1 h.

items.title: On sub-sevenfold symmetries in LH2 stacked ring scaffolds: A quantum optical perspective
items.abstract: Abstract For highly efficient light-harvesting, purple photosynthetic bacteria rely on light-harvesting 2 (LH2) complexes featuring ninefold, eightfold, and sevenfold rotational symmetries; however, sub-sevenfold scaffolds have not yet been observed in nature. To investigate this absence, we utilize a closed coupled-dipole model that neglects dissipative effects, which remains valid for a temporal window shorter than the interlayer excitation energy transfer time (on the picosecond scale) in an LH2 scaffold. We examine collective eigenmodes across $C_n$ stacked model ring geometries for $n=9,8,7,6$. Our results demonstrate that the minimum energy separation between specific collective bands occurs at the angular-momentum modes $m=\pm 1$ for known geometries, effectively predicting the photoactive absorption wavelengths of the lower bacteriochlorophyll (BChl) ring. Specifically, we predict peaks at 851, 848, and 825 nm for ninefold, eightfold, and sevenfold symmetries, respectively, which agree well with experimental observations. Applying this analysis to a hypothetical sixfold geometry, we predict a significant blue shift in the photoactive wavelength of the lower BChl ring, suggesting inefficient harvesting of the available solar spectrum and offering a quantum optical perspective on the evolutionary absence of sub-sevenfold scaffolds in LH2 complexes. Our study demonstrates that quantum cooperative models can elucidate specific aspects of biological LH systems.

items.title: Radial dependency of ICME-associated particle acceleration processes: Statistical multipoint observations from 2016-2023
items.abstract: During the propagation of interplanetary coronal mass ejections (ICMEs), evolution of the ICME-driven shock along with interactions with other solar wind structures, planetary bodies, and general changes to their morphology can alter particle acceleration efficiency and transport effects at their associated shocks. While the underlying mechanisms for these processes have been studied, the connection between the radial evolution of the ICME-driven shock during propagation and the resulting gradual solar energetic particle and energetic storm particle (ESP) intensities, composition, and acceleration has yet to be fully understood. The current distributed array of spacecraft at varying heliocentric distances provides a welcome opportunity to statistically analyze the radial dependency of particle populations and acceleration mechanisms present at ICME-driven shocks. We compiled a database of multipoint ICME events from 2016--2023, focusing our analysis on 23 events that were observed in situ by at least two of the following spacecraft: Parker Solar Probe (PSP), Solar Orbiter, ACE, Wind, and STEREO-A. Using the magnetic field, plasma, and ion compositional data provided by these spacecraft, we derived both local shock and ESP spectral shape parameters. By comparing the changes in these parameters at different stages of ICME propagation, we analyzed the connection between the evolution of the local shock conditions and the spectral shape. We find evidence to suggest a consistent increase in shock acceleration efficiency with heliocentric distance while the parent ICME is within 0.7 au, followed by a reduction in shock efficiency at further distances.

items.title: Can Phaseless Auxiliary-Field Quantum Monte Carlo with Broken Symmetry Trials Describe Iron–Sulfur Clusters?
items.abstract: Abstract Phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC) has in several cases been found to perform well on strongly correlated systems, including compounds containing transition-metal elements. Here, we benchmark the method for three iron–sulfur clusters ([2Fe-2S], [4Fe-4S], and the FeMo cofactor) using a hierarchy of systematically improved trial states derived from coupled cluster (CC) theory, including up to quadruple excitations relative to the Hartree–Fock (HF) reference, as well as multi-Slater trial states derived from unrestricted density matrix renormalization group wave functions. Our results reveal for these systems that, as the symmetry-broken trial is improved beyond the mean-field level, the phaseless AFQMC energy can become less accurate, and in some cases even less accurate than the underlying trial projected energy itself, displaying an inverted energy pattern that is only corrected once the trial fidelity is sufficiently high. For [2Fe-2S], we show that a decreased accuracy in the AFQMC energy can coincide with a simultaneous improvement in the trial state and the walker ensemble, as measured by their fidelity relative to the exact ground state, a behavior which is allowed by the nonvariational nature of the phaseless AFQMC energy estimator. We further find that this is not solely due to the use of spin-unrestricted trial states, as the inversion persists in [2Fe-2S] when we explicitly break the symmetry of the Hamiltonian by applying a fictitious local spin-Zeeman field. Instead, we find that the energy inversion is related to the choice of measurement trial in the estimator, where using a high-order CC trial state for measurements may introduce errors that are suppressed when the measurement wave function is restricted to lower excitation subspaces. In particular, measuring the energy with the mean-field reference while guiding the walkers with a CC trial removes the inverted pattern and improves the overall accuracy across the iron–sulfur clusters, with a possible exception for [4Fe-4S] where energies with a CCSDT guide may be less accurate than those guided by CCSD for some broken-symmetry families. Taken together, our findings suggest that the relatively accurate energies obtained with an HF trial state in these systems arise from favorable error cancellation, warranting significant caution about the reliability of phaseless AFQMC with such trials for strongly correlated transition-metal systems of this kind.

items.title: The first 3D magnetohydrodynamic core-collapse progenitors. I. General properties, convection, and nuclear burning
items.abstract: The most energetic core-collapse supernovae are thought to arise from rapidly rotating, magnetised progenitors, yet the 3D structure of their pre-collapse interior remains poorly constrained, and realistic distributions of magnetic fields, angular momentum, and convective asphericities are still lacking. We constructed physically consistent 3D pre-supernova progenitors, from the stellar core to the helium shell, including rotation and magnetic fields. In this first paper, we focus on the behaviour of turbulence and nuclear burning in the shells surrounding the stellar core. We assess their deviations from 1D stellar-evolution models. The magnetorotational properties of the progenitors are discussed in the second paper of this series. We used to perform 3D magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations of two compact Wolf--Rayet progenitors obtained from the stellar evolution codes and The models were mapped onto the multidimensional domain several minutes before collapse and evolved until the onset of core collapse. We find that in extended oxygen-burning shells, turbulent velocities exceed the standard mixing-length-theory (MLT) predictions by approximately a factor of 2. In contrast, a thin silicon-burning shell is poorly described by MLT: mixing is reduced near both shell boundaries, and the inferred effective diffusion profile departs significantly from the standard 1D prescription. These differences directly affect the spatial extent and efficiency of nuclear burning. In one of our models, a late shell merger present in the 1D stellar-evolution calculation does not occur in the 3D MHD evolution, indicating that such events may be sensitive to the specific modelling framework adopted. We present the first 3D MHD pre-supernova progenitors of this kind, suitable for subsequent collapse and explosion calculations. We show that multidimensional effects can significantly modify turbulent mixing and shell burning during the final stages of massive-star evolution. We propose prescriptions to account for these effects in the advanced phases of stellar evolution.

items.title: Alternative origins of polarity in compressively strained SrTiO3-RENiO3 capacitors
items.abstract: Since its original prediction 25 years ago, room-temperature out-of-plane ferroelectricity in compressively strained SrTiO3 remains an ongoing pursuit. In this work, we investigate the structural, electrical, and electromechanical properties of highly strained epitaxial SrTiO3 capacitors with rare earth nickelate electrodes. The SrTiO3 layers experience compressive strains up to −3% and exhibit pronounced tetragonality, comparable to that of bulk PbTiO3. Variable-temperature electrical measurements and room-temperature piezoresponse force microscopy reveal butterfly-shaped capacitance–voltage hysteresis and domain-like electromechanical response typical of ferroelectric materials. However, the overall behavior is inconsistent with a stable ferroelectric state. We therefore propose an alternative mechanism for the observed polarity in our samples based on spatially inhomogeneous internal fields. Our first-principles calculations show that such fields may arise from charge discontinuities between the formally charged NdNiO3 layers and charge-neutral SrTiO3 layers.

items.title: Probing $$\varvec{\Lambda }$$CDM-mimicking $$\varvec{f(Q)}$$ gravity model using gravitational waves from compact binary coalescences
items.abstract: Abstract The direct detection of gravitational waves (GWs) is a very significant achievement in the history of physics and has opened a new window to probe the possible deviations of physics from that of general relativity (GR). In this work, we forecast constraints on the free parameter of an f ( Q ) gravity model that mimics a $$\Lambda $$ Λ CDM background at the level of cosmic expansion. We consider modified gravitational wave signals from inspiraling of compact binary systems such as binary black holes (BBH), binary neutron stars (BNS) and black hole neutron star binary (BBHNS) systems in the context of the f ( Q ) gravity model and perform parameter estimation for two future third-generation ground-based GW detectors, namely Einstein Telescope (ET) and Cosmic explorer (CE), respectively. Our results show that both detectors can give tight constraints on the model parameter up to a significantly high redshift. These results show the potential of future GW observations to probe the deviations of the nature of GWs from that of GR within the framework of f ( Q ) gravity.

items.title: Density-wave order enhances the phonon thermal Hall effect in a trilayer nickelate
items.abstract: Ruddlesden--Popper nickelates have emerged as a promising platform for high-temperature superconductivity, yet the role of lattice degrees of freedom in their correlated normal state remains largely unexplored. Here, we report the observation of a finite phonon thermal Hall effect in the trilayer nickelate La$_4$Ni$_3$O$_{10}$ at ambient pressure. Remarkably, the thermal Hall response is strongly enhanced below the density-wave transition at $T^*\approx140$ K, exhibiting two distinct plateaus in the thermal Hall resistivity. The characteristic energy scale extracted from the thermal Hall response ($\sim4.1$ meV) closely matches the magnon--phonon crossing span energy ($\sim3.2$ meV), pointing to magnon--phonon hybridization as the primary mechanism enhancing the thermal Hall effect. These results provide new insight into the interplay between lattice and spin excitations in nickelates, with implications for understanding both their superconductivity and the multiple possible origins of insulating thermal Hall signals.

items.title: Spin–torsion interaction and geodesic bending
items.abstract: Abstract The intrinsic spin of fermions induces torsion in spacetime, leading to an effective four-fermion interaction. This affects the bending of null and timelike geodesics inside a star with a spherically symmetric distribution of gravitationally dense fermionic matter of constant density. Our analysis shows an additional torsional contribution to the geodesic deflection, alongside the conventional curvature-induced effect. This change depends on the fermion number density, coupling constants of the different species of fermions with different chiralities, and the temperature of the matter distribution. We have shown that the torsion-induced corrections to null geodesic bending remains very small for both low- and high-mass white dwarfs, whereas significantly larger effects may arise in more compact astrophysical objects such as neutron stars.

items.title: Attosecond delay metrology beyond the photon coherence time with spectrally resolved Hong-Ou-Mandel interferometry
items.abstract: Abstract Hong–Ou–Mandel (HOM) interferometry enables delay estimation at the quantum precision limit but is traditionally constrained to path differences within the coherence time of the interfering photons. Here, we demonstrate single-shot path-delay sensing using spectrally resolved HOM interference, achieving a precision near the measurement Cramér–Rao bound over an operating range of approximately ±300 μm, removing the conventional dynamic-range limitation imposed by the photon coherence window. By extracting delay information from the spectral interference fringes of spectrally entangled photon pairs, we retain near-optimal sensitivity over an operational range exceeding the photon coherence time by over two orders of magnitude. Using one million detected photon pairs, we achieve a time-delay precision of 13 attosecond (4 nm), while real-time operation (at 1 Hz) with 2000 detected photons yields 330 attosecond (100 nm) precision. Because the estimator relies on fringe periodicity rather than absolute coincidence rates, the method is intrinsically robust to variations in interference visibility, eliminating the need for recalibration. As a practical demonstration, we measure the thickness of a nominally 300 μm transmissive target with nanometer-scale precision. These results mark a significant step towards deploying quantum-enhanced HOM interferometry for high-precision displacement sensing in real-world applications.

items.title: Evidence for the Moon and Sun shadows with cosmic rays at an average energy of 7 × 10 17 eV
items.abstract: Interactions of cosmic rays with the Moon and the Sun produce deficits in their arrival-direction distributions relative to an isotropic flux. Such shadows have been observed previously at energies between $10^{12}\,$eV and $10^{16}\,$eV. We report the first observation of the Moon and Sun shadows at cosmic-ray energies larger than about $10^{16}\,$eV (average energy of $7\times10^{17}\,$eV), using data collected by the Pierre Auger Observatory. We employ data from three detector arrays covering $3000\,\text{km}^2$, $27\,\text{km}^2$, and $2\,\text{km}^2$, with spacings of $1500\,\text{m}$, $750\,\text{m}$, and $433\,\text{m}$, respectively. The data amount to over 10.6 million events. The Moon and Sun shadows are detected with a combined significance of approximately $3σ$. These observations confirm the pointing accuracy of the Surface Detector of the Pierre Auger Observatory using celestial bodies. From the combined Sun and Moon shadows, we infer an overall angular resolution of $(0.59^{+0.15}_{-0.11})^\circ$.

items.title: Electrical control of valley hybridization in moiré quantum dots
items.abstract: The search for scalable, electrically controlled qubits remains a central challenge in quantum technology. We introduce gate-defined moiré quantum dots as a promising platform for valley-based qubits. Moiré engineering resolves the central conflict of valley physics: momentum-space separation protects the states, while the enlarged moiré length scale allows smooth gates to mix them controllably. Dot geometry and confinement strength program valley hybridization, while a displacement field controls detuning, providing two noncommuting electrostatic axes for qubit control.

items.title: Density-induced dark baryon conversion in Δ − admixed hypernuclear neutron stars
items.abstract: We investigate density-induced conversion of neutrons into a neutral dark baryon $χ$ in cold, charge-neutral, $β$-equilibrated neutron-star matter containing hyperons and all $Δ(1232)$ quartet. The hadronic sector is modeled within a density-dependent covariant density-functional framework using the DDME2 parametrization. A scalar Higgs portal is included as a possible interaction channel between the visible and dark sectors, although its mean-field contribution is negligible for the couplings adopted here. Unlike fixed dark-matter admixture models or scenarios in which nucleon-to-DM conversion is driven by Higgs exchange, the $χ$ abundance is determined self-consistently from chemical equilibrium and baryon-number conservation. We find that hyperons and $Δ$ resonances alter the neutron chemical potential, delay the onset of $χ$, and suppress its abundance relative to nucleonic matter. This competition induces characteristic changes in the equation of state, particle fractions, sound speed, and adiabatic index. For $m_χ=1250$, $1300$, and $1400$ MeV, the maximum masses of the complete $N+Y+Δ+χ$ configurations are $1.806$, $1.899$, and $2.024,M_\odot$, respectively, indicating that the massive-pulsar constraint disfavors the lighter dark-baryon benchmarks. The radial profiles further show that for $m_χ=1400$ MeV, $χ$ is confined to the inner core of the most massive stars, while canonical configurations remain essentially unaffected. Thus, the stellar modifications arise primarily from conversion-induced rearrangement of the equilibrium composition rather than from Higgs-mediated interactions. These results highlight the importance of treating conventional non-nucleonic degrees of freedom and density-generated dark baryons on an equal footing when assessing the astrophysical viability of dark-sector extensions of dense matter.

items.title: AT 2016blu: Accretion-powered Outbursts in a Luminous Blue Variable and Compact Object Binary
items.abstract: Abstract We present the first X-ray detection of the supernova (SN) impostor AT 2016blu in NGC 4559. AT 2016blu exhibited 27 detected quasiperiodic (∼113 day) outbursts between 2012 and 2026 June, presumably triggered by periastron passages in an eccentric binary system in which the primary is a ≳33 M ⊙ luminous blue variable (LBV). AT 2016blu was serendipitously observed by Chandra in 2001–2002, prior to its first documented outburst in 2012, but the stacked archival data show no X-ray detection. We monitored the source’s visual-wavelength variability around its predicted outburst time and triggered a Chandra Target of Opportunity (ToO) program in 2026 March, obtaining observations with detections over five closely spaced epochs. These data indicate an X-ray luminosity of log L X ≈ 38.64 ± 0.11 erg s −1 and an accretion rate of M ̇ ≳ 8 × 1 0 − 8 M ⊙ yr − 1 , consistent with the presence of a compact companion. We therefore conclude that AT 2016blu is the first known case of an LBV SN impostor where X-ray observations clearly favor intermittent accretion onto a compact object as the cause of the outbursts. Given that the system consists of a massive star and a compact companion, AT 2016blu is a high-mass X-ray binary (HMXB), similar to SN 2010da, although the donor star in SN 2010da is a red supergiant (RSG).

items.title: Frequency-domain extended-effective-source gravitational self-force for eccentric Schwarzschild orbits
items.abstract: Effective-source formulations provide a practical route to gravitational self-force (GSF) calculations when singular retarded fields cannot be handled directly mode by mode. Up to now, only frequency-domain first-order GSF for circular orbits in Schwarzschild spacetime was obtained with the effective-source method. We construct and implement a frequency-domain extended effective-source (EES) formulation for first-order Lorenz-gauge GSF on eccentric orbits in Schwarzschild spacetime. The central obstacle is that radial libration forces the physical puncture and effective source to switch between interior and exterior branches, limiting their differentiability and producing slow spectral convergence. We overcome this obstruction by analytically extending both branches across the libration region and solving the coupled Lorenz-gauge perturbation equations for the resulting smooth extended sources. This provides an end-to-end gravitational EES implementation for eccentric motion and validates a computational ingredient needed for extending frequency-domain effective-source calculations toward second order.

items.title: Composition gradients in sub-Neptunes: K2-18 b and TOI-270 d as case studies
items.abstract: Structure models of sub-Neptunes commonly assume purely adiabatic interiors with distinct layers of homogeneous composition. We assess how allowing for more complex interiors with composition gradients affects the inferred internal structure and bulk compositions of the sub-Neptunes K2-18,b and TOI-270,d. We compare purely adiabatic models with distinct layers against models that include composition gradients and stable non-convective regions. We present solutions that are consistent with the observed masses, radii, and atmospheric boundary conditions. Generally, interior degeneracy remains substantial even at a fixed mass and radius. We further find that composition gradients significantly increase the range of viable interior structures. For example, the maximum hydrogen--helium (H--He) mass fraction can increase significantly, by a factor of about three at a 1,bar temperature of 300,K and by a factor of about 10 at 600,K for K2-18,b. For TOI-270,d, the increase is generally more than an order of magnitude. Composition gradients additionally weaken parameter correlations. For K2-18,b and TOI-270,d, the Spearman rank correlation between the H--He and iron abundances drops from sim0.7 to sim0.3, with a similar weakening between the H--He abundance and the rock-to-iron mass ratio. However, other correlations, such as that between the H--He abundance and the water-to-rock mass ratio, persist or even strengthen and remain non-negligible. Purely adiabatic models underestimate the range of plausible compositions and overestimate the impact of more precise measurements, atmosphere models, and host-star constraints on a more accurate characterisation. We suggest that interior models of sub-Neptunes should by default include more complex interiors, such as composition gradients and non-convective regions, when using data for interpreting the planetary structure, formation, and evolution.

items.title: The JWST Ultramassive Galaxy Sample -- II. Supermassive Black Hole Masses for 8 Extreme Early-Type Galaxies via Jeans Anisotropic Modelling of High-Resolution Integral-Field NIRSpec Stellar Kinematics — E8 Intelligence Research
items.abstract: We present central supermassive black hole (BH) mass measurements for the JWST Ultramassive Galaxy Sample, comprising 8 galaxies selected from a complete sample of the most massive early-type galaxies in the nearby Universe ($M_\star \gtrsim 2\times10^{12} M_\odot$). Building on the MGE photometric profiles and JWST/NIRSpec stellar kinematics from Paper I, we use the Jeans Anisotropic Modelling (JAM) framework to reconstruct the nuclear dynamics. Given the unique structural properties of these dry-merger-dominated systems, our Bayesian MCMC analysis explicitly tests both oblate and prolate intrinsic geometries. By marginalizing over classical dynamical degeneracies (including orbital velocity anisotropy, mass-to-light ratios, and inclination), we extract robust BH masses. We demonstrate that JWST's exceptional resolution allows JAM to tightly constrain the central potential using nuclear kinematics alone. items.title: A strategy for astrometric quasar selection with Gaia DR3 and its application to discover new luminous z>2 quasars
items.abstract: We provide a cookbook for a purely astrometric selection of quasars with Gaia DR3 and provide an example of its use for the identification of very luminous z>2 quasars. We also show the importance of properly taking the correlation between proper motions in right ascension and declination into account, as well as the non-linear error propagation. We adopted the Mahalanobis distance to the null proper-motion hypothesis. A scaled ̧hi^2 distribution with k=2 and scale s=1.1485 was fitted to Gaia-CRF3; the corresponding pm2σ Gaussian-equivalent threshold is D^2_ M(μ) 2 quasars without redshifts in the literature. Our proposed astrometric selection strategy recovers 95% of the known quasars. Its potential use for new discoveries was demonstrated by the identification of 24 very luminous z>2 quasars. Of these, 10 are new discoveries, and for an additional 7, we corrected the redshifts determined by other methods.

items.title: Nova shells in 3D. I. A catalog of integral field spectroscopic observations
items.abstract: Classical novae eject material during thermonuclear eruptions on the surface of accreting white dwarfs, forming expanding shells (the so-called nova remnants or nova shells). The physical structure and kinematics of nova shells shed light onto the eruption mechanism and binary interaction. Nova shells are typically characterized using direct imaging and spectroscopy, but their intrinsic 3D structure remains poorly constrained. The aim of this work is to present the first 3D catalog of nova shells based on integral field spectroscopic observations, allowing us to investigate the diversity of their physical structures beyond projection effects. We compiled integral-field spectroscopic observations of 19 nova shells obtained with MUSE at the VLT, complemented by new observations obtained with MEGARA at the GTC and WEAVE at the WHT. We constructed 3D visualizations of the emission lines of interest. The 3D visualizations of nova shells reveal a wide variety of structures, including ellipsoidal or spherical (round) shells, ring-like and bipolar features, and clumpy or irregular components. Many of these structures are not evident in two2D projections alone. Approximately 60% of the sample exhibits predominantly ellipsoidal or spherical shapes, while about 30% shows ring-like structures or is bipolar. Several objects show strong line-dependent morphological differences, with the iii or N ii emission lines tracing distinct kinematic components distinct from those in Hα. Compared with imaging studies, integral field spectroscopic observations reveal a larger fraction of bipolar or toroidal nova shells. Their physical structures differ considerably among different emission lines, highlighting distinct excitation mechanisms and physical properties within the ejecta. The comparison of the expansion velocities of nova shells on the plane of the sky and along the line of sight implies that their intrinsic aspect ratios are low, consistent with the conclusions derived from their projected aspect ratios.

items.title: Tracking a solar energetic eruption and associated energetic particles from the Sun to spacecraft
items.abstract: Solar energetic particles (SEPs) in the heliosphere are produced by flaring processes on the Sun or shocks driven by coronal mass ejections (CMEs). Electrons in particular are regularly detected remotely as electromagnetic radiation (X-rays or radio emission) --- which they generate through various processes --- as well as in situ by spacecraft monitoring the Sun and the heliosphere. We aim to combine remote-sensing and in situ observations of an energetic solar eruption to link energetic processes in the solar corona to energetic particles observed in situ in the heliosphere. This will be done using the tools developed in the Horizon Europe SOLER project. We investigated a solar energetic eruption at the Sun together with its associated signatures of accelerated electrons observed at radio and X-ray wavelengths and combined these remote observations to in situ particles observed by spacecraft on 10 March 2024. These observations were combined with a magneto-hydrodynamic (MHD) model of the solar corona in order to make the remote to in situ connections. We observe a high-energy SEP event at multiple spacecraft (>25 MeV protons and 1 MeV electrons), despite the event being associated with a slow white-light CME. Remote observations of the Sun show that the event was associated with a fast, large-scale coronal wave (1400 km/s) and multiple regions where electrons are accelerated around this large-scale wave observed as type II radio bursts. In addition, we observe a strong coronal dimming away from the main flaring region, providing evidence of field lines being opened onto interplanetary space and dislocated from the flare site. Although we observe a slow, co-temporal CME in white light, we show that an expanding extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) dome corresponding to the upper portions of the large-scale coronal wave is likely to steepen into a shock, as shown by the presence of multiple type II radio bursts on the surface of the dome. The EUV dome, and thus a coronal shock, is a likely source of energetic particles since it is the main feature intersecting magnetic field lines connecting to spacecraft. The SEPs observed in this study also have consistently hard spectral indices at two different locations.

items.title: Breaking the symmetry: X-ray polarization from a spreading layer on a tilted weakly magnetized neutron star
items.abstract: When modeling the emission from an X-ray binary system, we often assume that the rotational axis of the compact object is aligned with that of the binary system. While often considered irrelevant for spectroscopic observations, the orientation of the binary system is crucial for polarimetric properties. With the recent advent of X-ray polarimetric observations enabled by the ( Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer indications of a possible misalignment of the neutron star's rotational axis with respect to the binary axis have been reported. Following these indications, we present an analytical model for the polarimetric properties of emission arising from a spreading layer on an inclined weakly magnetized neutron star (WMNS). We discuss the expected polarimetric properties and study the impact of the geometrical parameters of the system on the polarization of WMNS emission. We compare our results with those for aligned systems. Finally, we discuss applications of the model to recent and upcoming X-ray polarimetric observations with and mention the suggestions for further development of the model.

items.title: A neural-network model for finding correlations in astrochemical space
items.abstract: The detection of new interstellar molecules is a central objective of astrochemistry, and arguably the most transformative development in the field over the past decade has been the dramatic increase in both the number and diversity of detected species. Using state-of-the-art natural language processing models, we developed a machine-learning pipeline, in line with recent approaches reported in the literature, to establish relationships between molecular structures, encoded as chemical strings, and molecular column densities in the prototypical dark cloud TMC-1. The workflow generates astrochemically informed embeddings that can be employed in subsequent supervised learning tasks. In this work, these representations are used within a neural-network framework to perform column-density regression on both the original molecular inventory and out-of-distribution species. The resulting model achieves mean squared error values of 0.17 and 0.58 and mean absolute error values of 0.29 and 0.59, all expressed in logarithmic units of the column density, together with coefficients of determination of 0.88 and 0.51 for the train+validation and validation datasets, respectively. The latent vectors learned by the model represent a rich mathematical object that captures not only the underlying chemical relations but also the potential interstellar detectability of the molecule. Using these vectors in molecules obtained from systematic permutations of the TMC-1 inventory allowed us to identify several promising candidates for future detection in this cloud, together with a large number of apolar species. Furthermore, by training the model on datasets reflecting different historical epochs of molecular detections in TMC-1, we show that recent molecular detections have substantially reshaped our understanding of interstellar chemistry in a transformative, rather than incremental, way. Beyond the accurate prediction of column-density trends for both in-distribution and out-of-distribution molecules, the latent-space representations produced by the model provide a stepping stone for developing new forms of data-driven astrochemical intuition and exploration.
