items.title: Faint companions to hot stars. Spectroscopic detection sensitivity and implications for survey design
items.abstract: Searches for black holes in binaries must distinguish genuinely dark companions from faint luminous stars. This is particularly challenging for massive hot stars. Their masses can exceed those of typical stellar black holes, while their spectra contain only a few broad lines. We developed a Fourier-domain method that converts isolated, broadened spectral lines into calibrated constraints on faint companions. In Fourier space, Doppler shifts are encoded in the phase, while the line profile defines a smooth amplitude envelope. A faint secondary introduces an oscillatory perturbation to the otherwise smooth log-amplitude. Expanding this perturbation to first order in the secondary-to-primary line-depth ratio, α, allows it to be profiled against the smooth baseline in a likelihood-ratio test with the single-star model. Because the model is analytic and nearly linear, its sensitivity can be evaluated transparently for individual spectra and at survey scale. It can be applied to single or multiple epochs without requiring full spectral disentangling. At small velocity separation v, the companion signal becomes degenerate with the smooth single-star profile. For the Fourier log-amplitude, the fractional uncertainty scales as Δα/α ∝ v^ -4 . If the primary velocity is known, the Fourier phase provides a more favorable detection channel whose sensitivity scales as v^-1. We demonstrated the method on archival FEROS spectra of the massive binary CPD-41^̧irc7742. We detected the known secondary in He,I 6678 Å and obtained a stringent nondetection in He,II 5411 Å, where its contribution is expected to be negligible. The same framework yields local detection efficiencies as functions of line-depth ratio, velocity separation, noise, and instrumental setup. These can be combined across lines, epochs, and targets to construct survey selection functions for spectroscopic black-hole searches, including those enabled by SDSS-V and Gaia.

items.title: J-PAS: Exploring the connection between local environment and the triggering of bursty star formation in extreme emission line galaxies
items.abstract: Extreme emission line galaxies (EELGs) are typically compact low-mass systems undergoing intense bursts of star formation whose spectra are dominated by very strong nebular emission lines. Their physical conditions resemble those of galaxies in the early Universe, making them ideal analogues for investigating the processes that regulate star formation, feedback, and chemical enrichment at low redshift. Our objective was to characterise the local environment of a sample of EELGs identified in the J-PAS survey in order to determine whether their extreme properties are associated with the presence of nearby companions, as expected if galaxy–galaxy interactions were the main trigger of the burst. Using the J-PAS internal data release, we analysed a sample of 917 EELGs in the redshift range of 0.03łesssim złesssim0.9, previously selected using photometric and machine-learning methods over an area of ∼30 deg2$. We employed the pair probability function formalism, which combines the full photometric redshift probability distributions of galaxy pairs, to statistically identify companions within projected separations up to 200, and velocity differences up to $500, . Stellar masses, star formation rates, dust attenuation, and metallicity estimates were derived for the EELGs and their companions through spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting using , and Monte Carlo simulations were performed to correct for projection and completeness effects. -1 CIGALE The derived average pair fraction of the EELGs is f_ = 0.162^ pair +0.048 _ -0.033 , indicating that only ∼16% of the sample has detectable companions, a value lower than the observed average for other star-forming galaxies within the adopted limits. When companions are identified within the sensitivity and stellar-mass completeness limits of J-PAS, they tend to be more massive and to show higher SED-based metallicity estimates than the EELGs, suggesting that the latter are typically low-mass components in asymmetric pairs. However, lower-mass companions below these limits may remain undetected. Finally, no statistically significant correlation was found between the equivalent widths of the O III $,łambda5007$, Hβ, and Hα emission lines and the projected separation to the detected companions within the limits of the J-PAS data.

items.title: A potential observational test to disentangle the companion of the binary millisecond pulsar PSR J1928+1815
items.abstract: Recently, the binary millisecond pulsar (MSP) PSR J1928+1815 (J1928) was reported to be experiencing regular radio eclipses. As it produces radio pulse emission and regular radio eclipses, this source was proposed most likely to be an MSP with a He star companion. However, the possibility that the companion is a white dwarf (WD) cannot be completely ruled out. Considering the uncertainty of interstellar dust extinction, it is difficult to confirm the nature of the companion star in the near-infrared and optical bands. Based on the measured mass function and orbital-inclination angle inferred by the radio eclipses, the gravitational radiation can produce a period derivative of -(6.8-9.6) -13 -1 when the companion star of J1928 is an extremely massive WD (1.4 M_⊙). Therefore, its companion star can be identified as a He star with a mass higher than 1.4 M_⊙ if the measured period derivative exceeds -9.6 ̊m s,s^ -13 -1 . However, the expansion of a He star could cause a transfer of angular momentum from the orbital motion to the spin of the He star through a tidal interaction. The loss of orbital angular momentum results in a negative orbital period derivative, which produces an extra contribution to the period derivative due to gravitational radiation. If the companion of J1928 is a 1.0-1.6 M_⊙ He star, the predicted period derivative is in the range of -(4.9-13.5) ̊m s,s^ -13 -1 . In particular, the tidal interaction could help to confirm a He star with a mass of 1.35-1.5 M_⊙. We also constrain the maximum evaporation efficiency of spin-down luminosity to be 0.006 when the companion star of J1928 is a He star.

items.title: On-chip multimode vibrational strong coupling of polar dielectrics within hybrid metal–dielectric nanocavities
items.abstract: Abstract Vibrational strong coupling (VSC) provides a powerful route to manipulate energy exchange and polaritonic energy landscapes through the hybridization of vibrational modes with optical resonances, offering significant potential for ultrasensitive infrared spectroscopy, biochemical sensing, and the control of chemical reactivity. Plasmonic nanocavities can achieve strong confinement, but their substantial ohmic losses often broaden the optical resonance and obscure the intrinsic evolution of hybrid branches. In contrast, low-loss dielectric platforms generally suffer from insufficient field overlap with the vibrational medium. Moreover, in dual-channel or mode-selective architectures, coupling behavior is highly sensitive to localized hotspots and the precise placement of the active layer. Consequently, achieving simultaneous and robust access to both transverse-optical (TO) and longitudinal-optical (LO) channels remains challenging, especially within systems that require continuous tunability and fabrication simplicity. Here, we experimentally demonstrate multimode VSC in a hybrid metal–dielectric nanocavity, where the optical field is strongly confined inside the SiO 2 layer. Owing to the coexistence of in-plane and out-of-plane electric field components in the vibrational layer, the same photonic mode can simultaneously couple to both the TO and LO phonon responses of SiO 2 . The measured Fourier transform infrared spectra agree well with full-wave simulations and are quantitatively reproduced by an effective three-oscillator model. By varying the thickness of SiO 2 , we further reveal the relationship between the coupling strength, the polar molecular layer thickness, and the effective mode volume. The proposed architecture also shows good robustness against the fabrication distortions, establishing a low-loss and experimentally feasible platform for multimode VSC in polar dielectrics.

items.title: THE ”BIG G” CRISIS: The relationship between the magnitude of the discrepancy in the ‘Big G’ values and the critical acceleration of the MOND.
items.abstract: Measurements of the gravitational constant G conducted at the world’s leading laboratories contradict one another and diverge in an unexplained manner. We solved the inverse problem: based on the known experimental “Big G” discrepancies, we calculated the magnitude of the hidden acceleration. The hidden acceleration coincided in order of magnitude with the critical acceleration of MOND, which is driven by the gravity of the entire universe. This fact refutes the seemingly chaotic spread of G values and calls into question the very possibility of using Newton’s local equation without accounting for the gravity of the entire universe. Is this an intriguing coincidence, or a direct consequence of the fact that all research groups calculated “Big G” from the local gravity equation without accounting for the acceleration caused by the gravity of the universe? Discrepancies were not caused by instrument errors, but by the omnipresent gravity of the universe, which was not accounted for in the calculations. Paradoxically, it was precisely the discrepancies that became the most valuable result of all the G measurements. In their pursuit of “Big G,” the experimenters missed a scientific discovery. A new law of nature was right within their grasp, yet they mistook it for equipment malfunction. Dear metrologists! Hidden within your vast archives lies the most monumental discovery in the field of gravity since Newton! Don’t let it slip away! Remember: the number of fundamental laws of nature is limited—there aren’t enough to go around!

items.title: The idea of innovation in Restoration science and medicine
items.abstract: This article traces the language of innovation through mid-seventeenth-century science and medicine, focusing on controversies surrounding the Royal Society and the proposed Society of Chymical Physicians. 'Innovation' in early modern England was primarily a term of abuse directed against the alleged enemies of the church or state. Following the Civil Wars, defenders of Aristotelian and Galenic learning used the term to implicate the new philosophers and chymical physicians in the radicalism of the previous decades. In response, such thinkers as Walter Charleton, Robert Boyle, John Evelyn, Thomas Sprat and Marchamont Nedham sought to rehabilitate the concept. They aligned innovation with the new experimental philosophy and, crucially, distinguished innovation in philosophy from innovation in divinity. Freed from the stigma of heresy and sedition, the concept could serve rather than undermine the restored church. Innovation, then, was secularized for religious ends: to reconcile the new philosophy with ecclesiastical authority and Christian doctrine. But the alliance between philosophical innovation and religious orthodoxy remained precarious, not least because the boundaries of orthodoxy were far from settled. The debates over innovation reflect competing efforts to define the cultural politics of the new philosophy at a moment of profound religious, political and intellectual contestation.

items.title: Early Martian Habitability and Directional Lithopanspermia Across the Solar System
items.abstract: Abstract Whether life arose independently on habitable worlds or dispersed through interplanetary exchange remains unresolved. Here we investigate early Mars as a potential biological nursery by integrating comparative planetary thermal evolution, subsurface aqueous habitability, impact-driven ejecta transport and probabilistic biological survival. Models spanning 4.4 billion years indicate potentially habitable pore-water environments on both Mars and Earth at 4.4 Ga, with mean eligible water temperatures of 35.84 °C and 42.34 °C, respectively, at 4.2 Ga. Simulated 10-Myr material-transfer fractions are 2.588% for Mars→Earth, 1.523% for Mars→Venus and 0.182% for Earth→Mars, yielding an inward-to-reverse transfer ratio of 14.23 (95% interval: 11.41–17.99). Conditional biological-establishment simulations yield a mean Mars→Earth probability of 0.2465%, although outcomes remain strongly dependent on uncertain survival parameters. Exploratory outward-transfer simulations identify rare Mars→Jovian-orbit encounters (0.07% within 0.05 AU), without establishing delivery to individual moons. A prior-dependent Bayesian comparison does not presently favor Martian biological ancestry over independent terrestrial origins. These findings identify directional asymmetries in modeled material exchange while demonstrating that successful biological dispersal remains unverified. Early Mars therefore represents a testable, rather than established, source of potential biological exchange across the Solar System.

items.title: From David Chalmers's Hard Problem of Consciousness to the Ben-Yehudah Investigation of SOURCE CONSCIOUSNESS: The Origin of Experience Beyond the Biological MIND
items.abstract: From David Chalmers's Hard Problem of Consciousness to the Ben-Yehudah Investigation of SOURCE CONSCIOUSNESS: The Origin of Experience Beyond the Biological MIND This independent scientific, philosophical, phenomenological, and comparative research manuscript examines David Chalmers's Hard Problem of Consciousness alongside Yeshayahu Ben-Yehudah's independent investigation of SOURCE CONSCIOUSNESS, the Ben-Yehudah Transducer Model, and the relationship between consciousness, the biological brain, and the interpretive MIND. David Chalmers's influential 1995 article, Facing Up to the Problem of Consciousness, distinguished the functional problems of cognition from the fundamental question of why physical and neurological processes are accompanied by subjective experience. His subsequent scholarship, including The Conscious Mind: In Search of a Fundamental Theory (1996), examined the limits of reductive materialism, phenomenal consciousness, naturalistic dualism, and the possibility that consciousness constitutes a fundamental feature of reality. This manuscript compares Chalmers's philosophical arguments with Ben-Yehudah's independent proposition that SOURCE CONSCIOUSNESS is foundational, the biological brain functions principally as a receiver, and the MIND performs an interpretive function rather than constituting the ultimate SOURCE of consciousness. The investigation also examines the author's lived SUBJECT–WITNESS–OBSERVER framework, continuous STILLNESS and RECEPTION, ZERO INTENT, and the distinction between direct experience and subsequent interpretation by the MIND. Particular attention is given to the explanatory gap, philosophical zombies, psychophysical principles, the double-aspect view of information, the limitations of neurological measurement, and the distinction between philosophical explanation and independently established scientific evidence. Central Finding “Consciousness is the source of ALL” ~ YBY The central finding is that Chalmers's Hard Problem of Consciousness and the Ben-Yehudah investigation of SOURCE CONSCIOUSNESS share a fundamental question concerning whether biological and functional processes provide a complete explanation of subjective experience. Chalmers argues that explaining how physical systems process information, generate behavior, and perform cognitive functions does not necessarily explain why those functions are accompanied by experience. Ben-Yehudah advances an independent foundational proposition: consciousness is not produced by the interpretive MIND, and the biological brain functions principally as a receiver within the Ben-Yehudah Transducer Model. The author's understanding is further expressed through the statements: “I AM Consciousness experiencing Human Form” ~ YBY “I AM the Subject and Witness in All of My Life” ~ YBY “I LIVE and REST in STILLNESS” ~ YBY The investigation identifies conceptual convergence between Chalmers's challenge to reductive explanations of consciousness and Ben-Yehudah's understanding of SOURCE CONSCIOUSNESS as foundational. However, their positions remain distinct. Chalmers's philosophical arguments concerning phenomenal experience, naturalistic dualism, and fundamental psychophysical principles do not independently establish the Ben-Yehudah Transducer Model or a biological receiving mechanism. The manuscript's central scholarly contribution is the preservation of this distinction while examining the origin of experience beyond explanations confined to the biological MIND. Scope of the Investigation This manuscript is an independent historical, philosophical, theoretical, phenomenological, and comparative scientific investigation. It does not report original controlled experiments in neuroscience, cognitive science, or consciousness studies. The investigation examines Chalmers's Facing Up to the Problem of Consciousness (1995), The Conscious Mind (1996), Consciousness and Its Place in Nature (2003), and The Character of Consciousness (2010), together with relevant philosophical contributions by Thomas Nagel and Joseph Levine. These works are compared with Ben-Yehudah's previously published investigations concerning SOURCE CONSCIOUSNESS, the Ben-Yehudah Transducer Model, the relationship between consciousness and physical form, observational fidelity, and the SUBJECT–WITNESS–OBSERVER framework. The author's continuous STILLNESS and RECEPTION are preserved as lived conditions rather than temporary states deliberately entered to produce intellectual work. ZERO INTENT remains foundational to the author's account and is not reinterpreted as an intention to eliminate intention. The Ben-Yehudah Six-Pillar Discipline remains: STILLNESS → AWARENESS → OBSERVATION → DISCERNMENT → INTEGRATION → TRANSMISSION SOURCE CONSCIOUSNESS is foundational and is not designated as a seventh pillar. The manuscript distinguishes the philosophical argument that reductive explanations may be incomplete from the separate proposition that consciousness originates beyond the biological MIND. It does not claim that Chalmers's Hard Problem experimentally establishes SOURCE CONSCIOUSNESS, nor does it present the biological receiving function proposed in the Ben-Yehudah Transducer Model as an independently verified neuroscientific mechanism. The investigation preserves the unresolved questions concerning the origin of subjective experience, the relationship between consciousness and biological processes, and the distinction between experience itself and interpretation by the MIND. Artificial Intelligence Disclosure Artificial intelligence was used to assist with historical research, comparative philosophical and scientific analysis, manuscript organization, drafting, language refinement, bibliographic development, reference identification, and editorial preparation. The foundational philosophical concepts, theoretical propositions, lived experiences, original observations, attributed quotations, the Ben-Yehudah Transducer Model, the SUBJECT–WITNESS–OBSERVER framework, and the Ben-Yehudah Six-Pillar Discipline are attributed to Yeshayahu Ben-Yehudah. The comparison between David Chalmers's philosophical investigation of consciousness and the Ben-Yehudah investigation of SOURCE CONSCIOUSNESS was developed through human–AI scholarly inquiry. Chalmers's published philosophical arguments are distinguished from the author's independent theoretical framework and reported lived experience. The manuscript does not report original controlled experiments in neuroscience or cognitive psychology, nor does it present independently verified evidence establishing that consciousness exists outside the biological brain. Its discussion of the hard problem of consciousness, phenomenal experience, naturalistic dualism, SOURCE CONSCIOUSNESS, and the biological MIND concerns philosophical analysis, historical research, theoretical investigation, and phenomenological inquiry rather than experimental confirmation of the Ben-Yehudah Transducer Model. Historical, philosophical, scientific, and bibliographic claims remain subject to source verification and independent scholarly evaluation. The author retains responsibility for determining whether the manuscript accurately preserves his philosophical positions, observations, theoretical distinctions, and scholarly conclusions. items.title: The Automatic Processing of Emotion-label Words and Emotion-laden Words in Chinese-English Bilinguals
items.abstract: Two core controversies persist in the research on the automatic processing of emotional words. The first centers on how emotion-label words and emotion-laden words differentially modulate the automatic processing. The second concerns whether the automatic processing of emotional words in a second language (L2) can attain native-like automaticity and efficiency. To examine these questions, the present study employed an emotional Stroop task with 31 Chinese-English bilinguals of upper-intermediate proficiency. Results demonstrated a cross-language positivity advantage, reflected in faster responses to positive than to negative and neutral words. Critically, word type significantly moderated this valence effect: it was robust for emotion-label words but attenuated for emotion‑laden words. Reaction-time data further indicated no significant disadvantage for L2 relative to L1 processing, suggesting that upper intermediate L2 proficiency can support near-native automatic access to emotional words. Notably, however, accuracy patterns diverged across languages: a negativity bias emerged in L1, whereas L2 processing exhibited a positivity bias. Together, these findings underscore that even among upper intermediate bilinguals, automatic emotional processing remains sensitive to lexico-semantic distinctions, highlighting the need for theoretical models to incorporate such subtleties in bilingual emotion representation.

items.title: Vivekananda's Educational Philosophy and Its Relevance to Twenty-First Century Learning
items.abstract: Background and Aim: India’s education system in 2026 is mid-implementation of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, even as the Indian classroom grapples with digital distraction, uneven policy rollout, and fast AI adoption. Questions remain about the effects on students’ concentration, values, and overall development. This paper examines whether Swami Vivekananda's four core educational concepts — man-making education, concentration of mind, universal access, and character-building — offer a workable framework for analysing this learning crisis, read against NEP 2020 and NCF 2023. Scholarship on Vivekananda’s views on education and the academic discussion on contemporary Indian policy discourse have developed quite independently. There has been very little discussion of the relationship between Vivekananda’s ideas, formulated a century ago, and modern empirical work on attention, equity, and character formation. Materials and Methods: This study uses qualitative, conceptual, and comparative textual analysis and not primary data gathering or statistical testing. The main sources are the speeches and writings of Vivekananda in the Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda. Secondary sources include Indian government documents (NEP 2020, NCF 2023) and articles about policy implementation, digital attention, digital divide, and SEL. Recurring themes in Vivekananda's writings were identified, then compared against the stated goals of these policy documents and against the empirical literature, organised around four core concepts: man-making education, concentration of mind, universal access, and character-building. Analytical Insights: The results indicate a close alignment between Vivekananda’s framework and NEP 2020’s structural goal, especially surrounding holistic development and character-centred learning. Evidence from studies on mindfulness, Social-Emotional Learning, and the digital divide shows strong conceptual resonance with his arguments regarding concentration, character, and accessibility, though this resonance falls short of empirical validation. Nonetheless, his spiritual and individualistic model, which was meant for dedicated learners in colonial India, cannot replace structural investments at the national level. Conclusion: Vivekananda’s philosophy serves as an effective normative framework for the modern Indian education system and defines the values that should be upheld in the classroom setting. However, this philosophy only works if it's paired with real structural change, not tradition alone.

items.title: Fuentes primarias en la enseñanza de la historia nacional y pensamiento crítico en estudiantes de 3.º BGU [Primary sources in the teaching of national history and critical thinking in 3rd-year BGU students]
items.abstract: La enseñanza de la historia nacional en el bachillerato ecuatoriano sigue apoyada en el libro de texto y en la memorización, por cuanto las fuentes primarias aparecen poco y casi nunca se evalúan como evidencia. Es así que el estudio se planteó como objetivo analizar las fuentes primarias en la enseñanza de la historia nacional y el pensamiento crítico en estudiantes de 3.º BGU. En este sentido se empleó una metodología descriptiva, documental y comparativa, teniéndose como corpus 25 fuentes (1991-2025) de Ecuador, Latinoamérica, España y el ámbito anglosajón, contrastadas mediante matrices. Entre los resultados se obtuvo que las intervenciones con documentos mejoran el análisis, la interpretación y la evaluación, mientras libros y currículos los relegan a ilustración. Entre las conclusiones se estableció que el pensamiento crítico en 3.º BGU depende de convertir cada fuente nacional en un problema de procedencia, contexto y contraste.

items.title: The Fluidity of the Self: From the Struggle of Forces and Language Games to Neural Networks of Self-Awareness
items.abstract: Self-awareness is a longstanding problem in philosophy, psychology, and cognitive science, particularly with regard to how a single individual can represent the self from first-, second-, and third-person perspectives. This article develops a theoretical framework that distinguishes referential identity, understood as the continuity of the individual to whom self-representation refers, from perspectival fluidity, the capacity to represent and evaluate that individual from different linguistic and psychological standpoints. It argues that shifts among “I,” “you,” and third-person self-reference need not imply changes in the identity of the subject; rather, they may reflect different modes of self-representation with distinct interpretive and regulatory functions. To develop this account, the article brings Nietzsche’s conception of the self as a provisional configuration of interacting forces into dialogue with Wittgenstein’s analysis of meaning as embedded in language use and forms of life, and with neuroscientific research on self-referential processing, autobiographical memory, and internally oriented cognition. These perspectives operate at distinct but complementary levels: Nietzsche provides a philosophical account of the plurality and instability of the self, Wittgenstein elucidates the linguistic and social conditions under which self-descriptions acquire meaning, and neuroscience investigates the distributed cognitive and neural processes associated with self-related experience. Findings concerning networks such as the default mode network are treated as empirical evidence about particular cognitive processes, not as proof of the philosophical interpretations advanced here. The proposed framework therefore does not assume a one-to-one correspondence between grammatical person, psychological perspective, and neural activity. Instead, it conceptualizes self-awareness as an ongoing process shaped by interactions among psychological organization, linguistic practices, social contexts, and neural-cognitive mechanisms. This distinction offers a basis for examining how perspectival shifts may relate to self-reflection, self-distancing, rumination, and emotion regulation, while recognizing that these relationships are context-dependent and require further empirical investigation. The framework thus provides a conceptual foundation for future interdisciplinary research on the relationship between linguistic self-reference, perspectival shifting, and the dynamic organization of self-awareness.

items.title: Beyond Translation:
items.abstract: This study addresses the problem of decontextualized readings of the Qur'an that are often exploited in extremist narratives. While most counter-radicalization efforts rely on translation and legalistic exegesis (tafsīr fiqhī), they overlook the cognitive-linguistic layer of the Qur'ān itself. Using Cognitive Semantics, Conceptual Metaphor Theory (CMT) of Lakoff and Johnson, and Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA), this study analyzes 15 key Qur'anic verses related to jihād, qitāl, sayf, and sabīl in their original Arabic context. The unit of analysis is the verse as a discursive unit, examined together with its immediate co-text (preceding and following verses), its sabab al-nuzūl, and its interpretation in three tafāsīr: al-Ṭabarī, al-Rāzī, and Ibn 'Āshūr. The extremist reading of each verse is traced through selected excerpts from ISIS/Dabiq propaganda (2014-2017) and BNPT counter-narrative modules, as a comparative corpus. Findings reveal three dominant qualitative patterns of distortion, identified through close reading and conceptual mapping: (1) Literalization of War Metaphors, where a figurative expression such as ḍarb al-riqāb is collapsed into a literal instruction; (2) Erasure of Contextual Deixis (maḥw al-qayd), where limiting phrases such as fī sabīlillāh, allażīna yuqātilūnakum, and wa lā ta'tadū are omitted; and (3) Ignoring Qur'ānic Co-text (qaṭ' al-naẓm), where a verse such as QS. 9:5 is cited without QS. 9:4 and QS. 9:6, and QS. 2:191 without QS. 2:190 and QS. 2:192. Building on these findings, this paper proposes the Quranic Metaphor Deconstruction Model (QMDM) / Rahmah Framework as a theoretical proposition, not as an empirically tested intervention. The model consists of three steps: (1) Re-Metaphorization, restoring subulanā as journey; (2) Re-Deixis Restoration, restoring the qayd of QS 2:190; and (3) Re-Co-textualization, reading QS 9:5 together with QS 9:4, QS.9:6, and QS. 60:8. As a textual study, this research demonstrates the theoretical potential of QMDM to reframe extremist readings at the cognitive level. Its practical effectiveness in deradicalization programs, however, has not yet been demonstrated and requires further empirical testing, for instance through classroom action research, focus group discussions with dā'ī and santri, and pilot testing in pesantren and BNPT modules. This study therefore moves Applied Qur'anic Studies from theological refutation (radd) toward a proposal for cognitive intervention ('ilāj idrākī) — from talqīn to tafkīr — whose impact remains to be validated.

items.title: "Neuroeducation: How Brain Science Can Improve Teaching Methods"
items.abstract: Neuroeducation integrates neuroscience, psychology, and education to create teaching methods based on how the brain learns.This research examines key brain functions such as memory, attention, emotion, and neuroplasticity, and challenges myths like fixed learning styles.It highlights evidence-based strategies including retrieval practice, spaced repetition, and multisensory learning that improve retention and engagement.The study also explores how managing cognitive load and emotional regulation can enhance classroom learning.By applying these neuroscience insights, educators can design more effective, inclusive, and scientifically grounded teaching practices that better support student learning and development.Ultimately, this interdisciplinary approach empowers teachers to bridge the gap between brain research and classroom practice, fostering deeper learning and long-term academic success.

items.title: Analysis of Natural Regeneration and Vegetation Status of Tree Species of a Biodiversity Hotspot in Bangladesh
items.abstract: Natural regeneration is crucial for ecosystem restoration and sustainable forest growth. This study provides first comprehensive assessment of naturally regenerating tree species in the Rema-Kalenga Wildlife Sanctuary (RKWS), Bangladesh. Data was collected via systematic random sampling, using 50 plots (20m × 20m), each containing five 1m × 1m subplots, and totaling 250 subplots. The study found 859 individuals representing 67 identified species across 34 families, alongside 5 unidentified species. Among them, 774 individuals (63 species) were native, 24 individuals (4 species) were exotic, and 61 individuals remained 5 unidentified species. Moraceae was the most prevalent family (Family Importance Value = 23.11%) with Streblus asper emerging as the most prevalent dominant species (Important Value Index =19.71). Biodiversity indices revealed structural differences between native and exotic regeneration. Native species demonstrated high diversity, richness and evenness (Shannon-Wiener = 3.4540, Richness = 9.3211, Evenness = 0.8337), indicating a mature, stable ecosystem with high functional resilience and even distribution. Conversely, exotic species exhibit low richness and evenness but a paradoxically higher species diversity index (exotic 0.1667 vs. native 0.0814). This disparity reflects the extreme dominance of a few aggressive individuals, signaling an early-stage invasion risk capable of gradually displacing native flora despite the current limited abundance of exotic species. These findings offer crucial baseline insights into the sanctuary’s current vegetation status. Ultimately, this study provides a vital scientific foundation for selecting appropriate tree species for future afforestation initiatives and sustainable conservation management strategies within the RKWS.

items.title: The sun, moon, and wormholes: Exploring ecological imperialism in Pokémon Sun and Pokémon Moon
items.abstract: This study aims to explore ecological imperialism, mechanics as meaning, and ecological literacy in the 3DS video games Pokémon Sun (2016) and Pokémon Moon (2016), developed by Game Freak, which are set in a Hawaii-inspired fictional region. Recognizing the Pokémon franchise’s worldwide appeal and the lack of postcolonial-ecocritical studies on Pokémon; the concepts of Ecological Imperialism and Entitlement by Graham Huggan and Helen Tiffin, Mechanics as Meaning by Catherine Canning, and Ecological Literacy by David Orr; and the descriptive-analytical research design, this study explores the varying relationships between the environment and living beings by identifying the anthropocentric and biocentric actions of human characters, which stem from entitlement or lack thereof; the natural and artificial islands of the Alolan region, the former teeming with biodiversity and the latter with inhumane experiments and suffering; and the Pokémon characters as parts of either the ecology of Alola as native biota or the invasive Ultra Beasts as portmanteau biota. With the gameplay expressing the wonders of biodiversity and the influence of living beings on one another, as well as the narrative addressing issues of invasive species and entitlement to space and life, Pokémon Sun and Pokémon Moon can be considered ecologically literate games.

items.title: Mini-review on the production of Primordial Black Holes fromFirst-Order Phase Transitions in the Early Universe
items.abstract: Primordial black holes (PBHs) can provide a possible connection between the physics of the early Universeand the dark matter. Among the various PBH formation mechanisms, cosmological first-order phase transitions (FOPTs) can generate PBHs through density perturbations arising from the stochastic nucleation oftrue-vacuum bubbles. In this mini-review, we focus on PBH formation from delayed false-vacuum decayduring slow and strongly supercooled FOPTs. We first review how stochastic bubble nucleation can generate non-Gaussian density perturbations and how these perturbations can lead to PBH formation and anextended PBH mass function. Wethendiscussagaugeinconsistency in the conventional treatment, arisingfrom combining density perturbations and the PBH collapse threshold defined in different gauges, and itsimplications for the predicted PBH abundance. Finally, we discuss delayed reheating and the possibility ofan intermediate early matter-dominated epoch as a potential way to revive PBH formation, and highlightthe remaining theoretical uncertainties and future directions

items.title: Axion Electrodynamics in Presence of a Stellar Non-homogeneous Background Magnetic Field
items.abstract: We re-assess effects of Axion Electrodynamics in the presence of non-homogeneous background magnetic fields. The Primakoff effect, which is an ALP-photon mixing induced by a background magnetic field, is generalized to the case of non-homogeneous backgrounds. The production of ALPs from a magnetized plasma thermal medium is also computed. The Eddington's solar standard model is adopted as the phenomenological scenario for our settings, and new bounds on the Axion Electrodynamics parameter space are imposed by considering helioseismological and neutrino observational measurements.

items.title: Capacity Limits in Cognitive Processing Reflect the Curse of Generalization
items.abstract: The striking constraints of some human cognitive processes stand in stark contrastto the near limitless capability of others. While we can acquire and flexibly use vast amountsof information, the amount we can process at any one time is often stiflingly limited: forexample the number of items we can hold in working memory or the number of tasks that canbe performed at once. Here, we integrate ideas from information theory, cognitive science,and neuroscience to offer a unified account of why processing is often so limited. We arguethat this reflects a fundamental tradeoff between generalization—how effectively existingrepresentations can be used in novel settings—and how many distinct representations canbe processed in parallel. Representations that best promote strong forms of generalization— a characteristically human cognitive strength — come at the expense of surprisinglystrict limits in the number of items that can be processed at once, an equally characteristichuman weakness. We refer to this as the “curse of generalization.” We formulate this first ininformation-theoretic terms, and then in process models, including a neural network modelof classic tasks used to demonstrate strict limits in human processing capacity. This tensionoffers a potential explanation for a range of phenomena — from performance on the tasks onwhich we focus, to representational learning and skill acquisition more broadly — as wellas the performance of modern machine learning architectures that exhibit generalizationcapabilities comparable to humans.

items.title: Recurrence quantification analysis of the effects of height-induced postural threat and arm movement restriction on balance performance in children and young adults.
items.abstract: Nonlinear methods such as recurrence quantification analysis (RQA) have been used to provide complementary information into the effects of height-induced postural threat, however, without considering age- and task-related aspects. Thus, RQA was applied to investigate the effects of height-induced postural threat and arm movement restriction on balance performance in children compared to adults. In Experiment 1, 49 participants (26 children, 23 young adults) performed the tandem stance, while 48 participants (25 children, 23 young adults) conducted the unipedal stance with contralateral leg swing in Experiment 2. In both studies, standing at ground-level (no threat) and 80 cm above ground (threat) was performed with both free and restricted arm positions. RQA was conducted on center of pressure data from two previously published studies. In both experiments, group-by-threat interactions were detected, with adults demonstrating decreases in RQA parameters (Experiment 1: %DET AP, ENT AP, %LAM AP; Experiment 2: TT AP) when standing at height but children showing no adjustments. However, restriction of arms did not change the observed patterns. Overall, RQA provided information about the temporal organization of COP dynamics (more variable, less predictable, less complex, more random, less discontinuous, and shorter periods of invariant movement patterns due to height) that complemented the previously reported linear measures.

items.title: Inferring viral variants and fitness advantages from longitudinal wastewater sequencing data
items.abstract: During the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, wastewater-based epidemiology emerged as an effective tool for monitoring infection dynamics. However, wastewater represents a pooled sample of incomplete viral genomic fragments originating from multiple individuals in the catchment area of a wastewater treatment plant, preventing the assembly of complete viral genomes. Existing computational pipelines are therefore limited in detecting new variants that are absent from clinical sequencing data. We developed FitNMF, an integrated viral dynamics and non-negative matrix factorization model that leverages the temporal structure of wastewater sequencing data and the underlying variant competition to jointly infer mutational signatures, relative abundances, and fitness advantages of circulating variants directly from wastewater next-generation sequencing data. Using simulated data as well as wastewater time-series data collected between 2021 and 2024 across six Swiss wastewater treatment plants, we demonstrate FitNMF's ability to identify and quantify emerging variants de novo, offering a powerful tool for real-time variant surveillance in settings with limited clinical sequencing.

items.title: Co-production of an oral health intervention: Enabling Service Users with Severe Mental Illness to Learn about and Engage (SMILE) with Good Oral Health
items.abstract: Background: People with severe mental illness (SMI) experience poorer oral health than the general population. They are less likely to visit the dentist or brush their teeth and face unique barriers to accessing oral health support. There is a limited number of oral health interventions for people with SMI, and there is no conclusive evidence on their effectiveness. An integrated oral health intervention delivered by mental health professionals in a community mental healthcare setting could offer a scalable option to oral health support for people with SMI. In this paper we report on the process of co-producing such an intervention in England. Methods: The intervention development process was informed by Hawkins co-production framework. In this paper we report on stages 2 (co-production) and 3 (prototyping). Two online and two face-to-face co-production workshops took place (N=22) involving service users with SMI (n=6), mental health professionals (n=8) and dental health professionals (n=8). Two online patient and public involvement consultations, and a professional stakeholder meeting were held during the co-production process to provide feedback on the co-production process. The workshops informed the core components, format and content of the intervention. Results: The co-production process resulted in five intervention components: 1) Initiating a conversation about oral health, 2) providing advice to people with SMI on keeping their teeth and mouth healthy, 3) weekly tooth brushing text reminders, and 4) mental health professionals updating the care record to document the administration of this intervention. To support intervention delivery, we co-produced an intervention flowchart, an intervention leaflet for people with SMI, and a training manual for mental health professionals delivering the intervention. Conclusion: We co-produced an integrated oral health intervention to be delivered to service users with SMI in community mental health settings. The next stage of the research is a single-arm feasibility study to assess whether the intervention is acceptable to people with SMI and feasible to deliver within the NHS.

items.title: On conducting diary-based social contact surveys to inform transmission models of close-contact infections: a systematic review and expert-informed questionnaire
items.abstract: Background: Diary-based social contact surveys are widely used to parameterise transmission models of close-contact infections. However, variation in study design, contact definitions, and questionnaire content limits comparability across studies. These challenges became particularly evident during the COVID-19 pandemic, when rapid and repeated data collection was urgently needed, often without harmonised instruments. To address these challenges, we aimed to develop an expert-informed questionnaire and update the recommendations on conducting diary-based social contact studies previously proposed by Hoang et al. (2019). Methods and findings: We conducted a systematic review of diary-based social contact surveys published between 31 January 2018 and 25 September 2025 using PubMed and the Web of Science Core Collection, extracting information on study design, survey methodology, contact definitions, and survey items from available questionnaires. Methodological quality and reporting were assessed using an adapted AXIS tool, with results summarised for each criterion. In total, we identified 129 studies across 62 countries, with most studies conducted during the COVID-19 pandemic (59.7% in 2021-2022). Retrospective reporting (86.0%) and non-probability sampling (77.5%) were largely adopted and became increasingly common during the pandemic, while non-paper-based data collection rose sharply from 2021 onwards. Across 36 retrievable questionnaires from general-population surveys, we identified 54 survey items. An online assessment involving 26 experts informed the classification of these items according to their perceived importance, resulting in an expert-informed questionnaire comprising 22 core items. Based on our findings, we updated previous recommendations on sampling, survey methods, contact definitions, behavioural change, essential contact information, and data governance. Conclusions: This study provides an expert-informed questionnaire and updated recommendations to support harmonised social contact data collection, improve comparability across studies, and strengthen preparedness for future public health emergencies.

items.title: Investigating Climate-Driven Disruption of Malaria Transmission Following the 2022 Sindh, Pakistan Floods: An Interrupted Time Series Study
items.abstract: Malaria remains a major global public health challenge in developing countries, with climate change intensifying its impact, particularly in vulnerable populations. Rising temperatures can expand the geographic range and local abundance of malaria vectors, Anopheles mosquitoes, which thrive in warm climates, with 25C representing the optimal temperature for malaria transmission. In Pakistan, malaria is primarily spread through P. falciparum and P. vivax. Pakistan is one of the seven countries in the Eastern Mediterranean Region that accounts for 98% of the total malaria burden in the region. Recently, after catastrophic flooding in Pakistan in 2022 and the subsequent increase in malaria incidence, it has become imperative to estimate the climate change-attributed increase in the risk of malaria. In this study, we analyze the time series malaria case incidence data from the province of Sindh, Pakistan, and the climate data to quantify climate-attributed malaria cases in Sindh, Pakistan. We fit a negative binomial generalized linear model (GLM) to monthly case counts with interrupted time series and seasonality terms. The majority of malaria-confirmed infections were Plasmodium Vivax (40-95%) between 2016-2024, followed by Plasmodium falciparum infections. The positivity rate for malaria remained <10% until June 2022, and increased massively after the July 2022 flooding. After accounting for this case momentum, the onset of the 2022 floods was associated with an immediate, independent increase in malaria cases of approximately threefold (IRR 2.985, 95% CI 1.878-4.751, p < 0.001). These findings suggest that post-flooding malaria surveillance and response in flood-affected settings should anticipate not only an acute environmentally driven surge in cases but also a subsequent period of elevated, self-sustaining transmission that may persist well beyond the resolution of the initiating environmental disruption, in this case the flooding.

items.title: MICE: Multi-animal Interaction Context Encoder - A Hierarchical Foundation Model for Mouse Behavior
items.abstract: Quantifying mouse behavior from pose is a foundational tool in neuroscience, ethology, drug discovery, and animal welfare. Self-supervised foundation models are a natural fit, but a foundation model for mouse behavior must handle social behavior - many behaviors that matter (aggression, courtship, mounting, allogrooming) are inherently multi-animal. Existing self-supervised pose models fall short: they encode each animal independently and discard interaction signal, hard-code the animal count, and pretrain one dataset at a time. We introduce MICE (Multi-animal Interaction Context Encoder), a hierarchical foundation model for mouse behavior that pretrains jointly on six mouse-pose corpora spanning one to four mice and 7 to 27 keypoints. MICE combines a hierarchical individual encoder capturing per-mouse kinematics at multiple temporal scales with a Perceiver-style social encoder whose learned latent codebook decouples parameter count from animal count, so a single checkpoint serves any group size without retraining. Across four evaluation protocols spanning six datasets, MICE matches or exceeds prior keypoint-based baselines, and layer-wise probing shows the social stage incrementally improves discriminability beyond the individual encoder. Code, weights, and data are available at https://github.com/eric0708/MICE.

items.title: From MNH to the Friedman--Komogortsev Method---which changes improve eye-movement classification?
items.abstract: The Friedman-Komogortsev Method (FKM) is a rule-based classifier of fixations, saccades, and post-saccadic oscillations in 1000-Hz recordings, developed from the modified Nyström-Holmqvist algorithm (MNH) and used in several recent studies. FKM changes MNH in many ways at once: it centres MNH's Savitzky-Golay filter, adds a position-based test for whether an apparent post-saccadic oscillation continues the saccade, adds rejection tests, and changes several thresholds. We asked which of these changes alter agreement with human classification. Both algorithms were scored against twenty 26-s GazeBase reading recordings hand-classified by three trained raters, and each change was reverted in turn. FKM agreed better than MNH as MNH was used: saccade Cohen's kappa rose on all 20 recordings (median +0.034), and saccade boundaries moved from 2-3 ms late to the raters' sample. One change produced this: centring the filter, which removes a three-sample delay. Reinstating the delay returned FKM's saccade kappa to MNH's value, and centring MNH's filter alone made MNH match FKM on saccades and exceed it on post-saccadic events. The position-based test changed how saccades with several velocity peaks were divided, splitting 8% of rater-labelled "wavy" saccades into a saccade and a spurious oscillation against 39% for delay-corrected MNH. FKM's higher post-saccadic velocity floor traded recall for precision. The remaining changes had no measurable effect on these recordings. FKM's improvement over MNH is therefore a filter-alignment correction that MNH users can apply directly, plus a segmentation rule for multi-peak saccades.

items.title: Mean-level arithmetic computation via stochastic reaction networks
items.abstract: Reaction networks provide a natural model for analog computation in which inputs and outputs are encoded by molecular abundances. Much of the work on analog computation with chemical reaction networks (CRNs) has focused on deterministic mass-action systems. In DNA- and protein-based circuits, however, low copy numbers can make intrinsic fluctuations significant, motivating the use of stochastic models. In this paper, we develop a framework for computation with stochastic CRNs at the level of stationary means. Specifically, we construct elementary arithmetic modules for identification, addition, and multiplication, and analyze their mean-level correctness and convergence rates. We focus on these three modules because they are simple enough to analyze explicitly while already exhibiting the new issues raised by stochastic mean-level computation. Unlike in deterministic systems, the computed value cannot be read from a single output measurement. Instead, readout requires Monte Carlo estimation, with error arising from transient bias as the system approaches stationarity and intrinsic sampling noise that persists even at stationarity. We therefore study the convergence rates of output means, variances, and autocovariances to their stationary values, as well as the stationary fluctuations governing sampling error. We also show that this readout cost can depend strongly, and sometimes unexpectedly, on the architecture of the computation. In particular, comparing linear-chain and binary-tree implementations reveals that binary trees can greatly reduce stationary variance for addition, but can instead produce exponentially larger variance for multiplication.

items.title: Toward Self-Evolving Geospatial Algorithms: An LLM-Driven Framework with a Case Study on Spatial Regime Discovery
items.abstract: Geospatial algorithms have been developed through expert-driven discovery: a researcher spots a limitation, proposes a structural fix, and checks it by hand. With LLM-driven multi-agent systems becoming practical, much of the candidate-generation, evaluation, and selection work can now be largely automated, while the researcher's role shifts upstream toward problem formulation, evaluation design, and interpretation. We refer to this paradigm as Self-Evolving Geospatial Algorithms (SEGA) and propose a framework with three required modules: a two-loop architecture with embedded geographic knowledge as the inner-loop engine; an automatic code formatter that converts any raw geospatial algorithm into the standardized triple required by the inner loop; and a simulation-driven training protocol, in which evolution runs only on synthetic data with known ground truth, and the discovered algorithm is applied unchanged to real data, keeping real-world results out-of-sample. We use spatial regime discovery as a case study, seeded with the Two-stage K-Models algorithm. Evolution uses the Rand Index against the ground-truth partition as fitness signal; the frozen algorithm is then evaluated on 150 simulated grids and 11 real-world datasets across climate, health, hydrology, and politics. The evolved algorithm outperforms its seed, knowledge-free baselines, and four classical regionalization methods. Ablations further indicate that the channel of geographic-knowledge injection, structured retrieval versus prompt-level hints, is itself load-bearing. In this case study, LLM-assisted search sped up the inner loop; whether it does so for other seeds and task families remains open. The geographer's role -- asking the right questions, designing trustworthy evaluation -- grows more central.

items.title: The AI research space shapes country academic performance
items.abstract: Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI) have demonstrated great potential across diverse domains, prompting increasing attention to understanding the AI ecosystem. As knowledge production is often perceived as a process of connecting existing pieces of knowledge, mapping the interconnections of AI knowledge is crucial for unraveling the dynamics of scientific production in AI. However, maps created so far have fallen short of capturing knowledge relatedness, focusing instead on citation relationships between subfields. Here, we build an AI research space by connecting pairs of AI research topics based on their proximity measured through author-topic coupling. Projections of country level performances onto the space reveal that countries exhibit distinct baskets of specializations. We further examine the role of the structure of the AI research space in the scientific development of nations. We find that countries are more likely to gain specialization in topics that have high proximity to already specialized neighbor topics, and that publications whose topics align more with the developed topics in the country are more likely to become high impact. Our results highlight the AI development gaps across nations and the path-dependence in the development induced by the AI research space.

items.title: Evolving stellar wind environment around M dwarfs and its influence on magnetic star-planet interactions
items.abstract: M dwarfs are the most abundant group of stars in the Galaxy and they are expected to host a large number of exoplanets orbiting in the habitable zone. It is believed that stellar winds of M dwarfs can have a substantial effect on these exoplanets and on the observations of these systems. However, a systematic investigation of how the stellar winds of M dwarfs varies on timescales of a few months to years and how this impacts exoplanets around these stars is missing. We aim to investigate how variability of magnetic field properties of M dwarfs affects their stellar winds, which is essential for future studies of star-planet interactions (SPIs) and planetary habitability. Such variability might shed light on whether SPI signatures are going to repeat. We have compiled a total of 18 magnetic field maps for 6 M dwarfs, with masses between 0.1 and 0.6 $M_\odot$, and rotation periods between 2.7 and 175.6 days. We use these maps as input of 3D magnetohydrodynamic stellar wind simulations. We derive the mass-loss rate, the angular momentum-loss rate, and the Alfvén radius. For the stars with confirmed exoplanets (DS Leo, YZ Cet, and GJ 1151) we investigate the variability of stellar wind properties at the orbit. We find mass-loss rates between $1.0\times10^{-14}~M_\odot~{\rm yr^{-1}}$ and $2.3 \times 10^{-13}~M_\odot~{\rm yr^{-1}}$ and angular momentum-loss rates between $4.6 \times 10^{27}~{\rm erg}$ and $4.9 \times 10^{31}~{\rm erg}$. For individual stars the Alfvén radius, mass-loss rate, and angular momentum-loss rate varied with time by up to a factor of 1.5, 3.8, and 7.4 respectively. Our results follow the observational relation between mass-loss rate and X-ray flux. Due to the time-varying Alfvén surface, exoplanets orbiting DS Leo and YZ Cet move in and out of the sub-Alfvénic regime, affecting the nature of star-planet interactions and prospects for their detection.

items.title: Retrospective Analysis of Team-Following Trading Profitability in Pumpfun Meme Coins Using Funding Networks
items.abstract: If the right token-creation teams had been known, how much could following them have returned, and what is left when only information available before each launch is used? We study ten separately recorded Pumpfun windows (April 2024 to September 2026), each reconstructed independently from real-SOL reserve states and finite-capital accounts that start with one SOL. Teams are directed funding groups ranked in hindsight. When every team exits at its own best reserve threshold, chosen in hindsight, the main account ends above one SOL in all 8 windows that have a qualifying team (1.10 to 11.32 SOL), but free cash exceeds one SOL in only 5, and marks of positions that never reached their threshold make up 17--94% of equity. If teams are recognised online, from tokens whose first hour has completed, 9 of 19 teams become identifiable only after their last launch; the remaining 10 end above one SOL in 10 cases, with free cash above one SOL in 7; funding links in this step still come from the full window, so even these results are not a fully realisable signal. A large model balance, a result above random cohorts that repeat the threshold search, and a statistical rejection in the selection-matched nulls (3 of 40 tests after Holm adjustment) are three different statements, and these nulls condition on the discovered funding graph, so they do not calibrate the whole selection procedure. Midpoint tests describe a further source of apparent opportunity. A detailed analysis of the best and the worst window, with every analysis parameter varied, shows that the worst result, which is close to break-even, rises several-fold with a stop rule or another funding-graph construction. The results are conditional retrospective model accounts, not executable profits, and not evidence of a causal effect of the SOL price.

items.title: Evolutionary games on networks with negative edge-based environmental feedback
items.abstract: Environmental feedback can fundamentally alter the game payoff structure underlying the evolution of cooperation. How feedback-evolving games interact with population structure under non-weak selection remains incompletely understood. We study an evolutionary game on networks in which each edge has a binary environmental state that determines the payoff matrix used by the two connected individuals. By assumption, cooperation tends to improve the local environment, which in turn favors defection, thereby creating negative feedback between strategies coupled with the environmental condition. We analyze the model under strong selection using a mean-field approximation, a pair approximation that tracks both strategy pairs and edge environments, and agent-based simulations. In well-mixed populations, the feedback can generate bistability between full cooperation and full defection, as well as sustained oscillations arising through a Hopf bifurcation. Sparse networks (i.e., with low nodes' degrees) can eliminate bistability, suppress oscillations, and produce stable intermediate levels of cooperation. The pair approximation captures these effects and generally agrees more closely with simulations on sparse networks than the mean-field approximation. Our results show that edge-based environmental feedback and network structure, such as density of edges, interact to determine whether the fraction of cooperators stabilizes or oscillates over time.

items.title: Investigation of Quasiperiodic Oscillations in the Flaring State of Swift J1727.8‐1613 With Insight‐ HXMT During Its 2023 Outburst
items.abstract: ABSTRACT We present a timing analysis of the black hole x‐ray binary Swift J1727.8‐1613 during its 2023 outburst using Insight‐HXMT observations. In the flaring state, we reveal a highly synchronized positive correlation between the quasiperiodic oscillation (QPO) frequency and the x‐ray count rate. Notably, near the count rate peak (around MJD 60206), we detect a dramatic QPO frequency jump from 3.75 to 8.61 Hz, accompanied by a sharp drop in the root mean square (RMS) amplitude to 2.5%. We demonstrate that the fundamental and harmonic frequencies strictly obey a 1:2 ratio, with a fitted slope of 2.0178 ± 0.0066. These results strongly support the Lense–Thirring precession model, indicating that an increased accretion rate shrinks the inner disk radius and decreases the corona's geometric thickness. This work provides crucial observational constraints on the geometric evolution of black hole accretion flows.

items.title: The IMUNOPOLI Board Game: Effects on Students’ Self-Efficacy and Emotional Intelligence in Learning the Immune System
items.abstract: This study aimed to examine the effect of the IMUNOPOLI board game on students' self-efficacy and emotional intelligence in immune system learning, with concept mastery included as a supporting variable to contextualize learning outcomes. A quasi-experimental method with a Non-equivalent Control Group Design was used, involving 60 students, at a state senior high school in Bandung City, divided into an experimental and a control group (each with 30 students). Data were collected using a self-efficacy questionnaire (15 items), an emotional intelligence questionnaire (33 items), and a concept mastery multiple-choice test (25 items). Data were analyzed using the Mann-Whitney test, score categorization, effect size via rank biserial correlation, and Spearman correlation to explore the relationships among the variables. Descriptively, the experimental group showed a greater shift toward high self-efficacy than the control group, though this difference did not reach statistical significance. Emotional intelligence in the experimental group remained stable due to a baseline ceiling effect, whereas the control group showed a more noticeable increase, resulting in no statistically significant post-test differences between groups. Furthermore, no statistically significant correlations were found among self-efficacy, emotional intelligence, and concept mastery. These findings indicate that while IMUNOPOLI descriptively supported self-efficacy and maintained high emotional intelligence levels, it did not demonstrate statistically significant superiority over conventional instruction, highlighting the importance of initial student conditions in game-based learning interventions.

items.title: A systematic map of syntheses on anthropogenic noise impacts on wildlife: evidence gaps, policy attention, and quality appraisal
items.abstract: As systematic reviews on the effects of anthropogenic noise on wildlife increasingly inform policy, a critical evaluation of this secondary evidence is essential. We assessed the coverage, methodological quality, and policy relevance of existing syntheses in this field. Following a preregistered protocol, we conducted a systematic search using Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, that identified 50 syntheses (systematic reviews, maps, and meta-analyses). Of these 50 syntheses, we included 47 in the bibliometric analysis, 23 in the policy attention analysis, and 44 in the critical appraisal. The included syntheses were published between 2008 and 2025, but mainly in the last six years, and focused on behavioural, physiological, and communication outcomes in animals. Most syntheses looked at the effects of transportation and energy industry activities. Syntheses were most likely to review evidence from marine, followed by terrestrial ecosystems. We found critical gaps in the coverage in terms of their taxonomic scope, with notable underrepresentation of invertebrates, amphibians, and reptiles. Most syntheses were first-authored by researchers based in the United Kingdom, Canada, and the United States. Although many syntheses had authors from more than one country, authors from non-English-speaking countries were largely absent. Almost half of syntheses were cited in policy documents, mainly government policies and regulatory submissions. Syntheses of evidence on marine environments received the most policy citations and urban noise the least. There was no significant difference in quality scores between policy-cited and non-cited syntheses, and most of them are rated low due to methodological and reporting shortcomings. Given these findings, it is critical to fill the synthesis gaps and improve methodology and reporting of future evidence syntheses in this area.

items.title: Examining factors that increase tuberculosis knowledge: a multigroup comparison of the cognitive mediation model based on belief in science
items.abstract: Abstract Drawing upon the Cognitive Mediation Model (CMM), this study aims to examine how attention to television, text-based social media, and video-based social media influence knowledge acquisition about tuberculosis (TB) via elaboration and interpersonal discussion. A total of 467 Chinese respondents participated in our survey. The results demonstrated that attention to text-based and video-based social media significantly promoted elaboration, which, in turn, enhanced both subjective and factual knowledge about TB. Attention to television, text-based, and video-based social media also facilitated interpersonal discussion; however, interpersonal discussion only increased subjective knowledge, not factual knowledge. The multigroup analysis demonstrated that the effects of (a) attention to television on interpersonal discussion and (b) elaboration on subjective knowledge were more pronounced among participants with high level of belief in science than among those with low science belief. These findings contribute to the CMM literature and offer practical implications for designing targeted health communication strategies to combat TB.

items.title: The spatial specificity and recovery from visual adaptation in causality perception
items.abstract: Abstract When one object approaches another object which, upon touching, moves in the same direction, humans report a vivid impression of one launching the other. Visual adaptation can alter this perception of causality: observers less often report seeing a launch after viewing a stream of launch events. In three experiments, we further characterised how visual adaptation influences the perception of causality by determining the spatial specificity of adaptation and timecourse of recovery from adaptation. In Experiment 1, observers saw ambiguous test events (i.e., the overlap between the two objects varied over trials) at three different horizontal eccentricities. Adaptation was strongest when adaptor and test event were presented at the same eccentricity, and absent when the two were separated by just three degrees of visual angle. Moreover, the perception of causality gradually recovered from adaptation, but remained incomplete. In Experiment 2, both long and short adaptation sequences were highly effective in driving adaptation, and showed no difference in the recovery timecourse, which was complete following more experimental blocks. In Experiment 3, a break without any task-relevant visual input also led to a recovery over the same timespan, but this time, the recovery was instantaneous and incomplete. Altogether, our results provide evidence for highly spatially specific computations, instananeously responding to the onset of adaptation and then gradually recovering from the adaptation over a short time window.

items.title: Existential Positive Psychology as an Integrative Evidence-based Paradigm: Theory, Advances, and Future Directions
items.abstract: Abstract In memory of the recent passing of Prof. Paul T. P. Wong, this article synthesizes the current state of existential positive psychology as part of his profound legacy in the field of psychology. The primary aim is to present existential positive psychology as a unique evidence-based paradigm of vital relevance to today’s global challenges. To this end, the paper reconceptualizes the entire paradigm and its six foundational pillars, while reviewing the existing body of research supporting their significance for well-being. These pillars are: (1) life is viewed through a realistic existential lens that integrates both life’s bright and dark aspects; (2) personal suffering is approached with a positive mindset that accepts and makes meaning of vulnerability; (3) dialectical coping is crucial for resilience and flourishing; (4) meaning in life is central to well-being amid adversity; (5) meaning in life is inherently relational and grounded in self-transcendence; and (6) existential well-being takes the form of mature happiness and culminates in authentic flourishing and fructification (a novel construct proposed in this paper). These pillars capture the fundamental assumptions that underpin an existential positive psychology approach to human nature, theory, principles, models, and methodology. The article further proposes an integrative process model and outlines promising future directions for this emerging psychological paradigm. With its integrative and cross-cultural foundation, existential positive psychology provides a unifying framework for guiding scientific inquiry across psychology and the broader field of human flourishing.

items.title: To check or not to check: Adolescents’ sourcing practices when writing from multiple texts
items.abstract: Abstract Writing from multiple texts is a crucial academic literacy practice at the university level. Therefore, students should learn to attend to, evaluate, and use information about the sources by the time they reach the end of upper secondary school. The present study investigated differences in upper secondary school students’ ( N = 87) sourcing practices when composing a short article based on multiple texts. The data consisted of students’ written articles and log files recording their time spent on the task and revisits to the source texts during the writing task. Based on analyses of sourcing in students’ written articles, five source user profiles were identified: (1) Advanced source users ( n = 18); (2) Elaborative source users ( n = 15); (3) Basic source users ( n = 15); (4) Vague source users ( n = 15); and (5) No-source users ( n = 24). Students in the three more capable profiles incorporated at least once an explicit source-content link into their articles, varying the number of source features used. During the writing task, Advanced source users revisited both more credible texts more frequently than less capable source users. Their composed articles also most often included citations and main claims from both more credible texts. Conversely, the other students who engaged in sourcing revisited and referenced only one more credible text. The results of the present study implicate that students might benefit from differentiated instructional support to accurately and elaborately cite sources in their writing.

items.title: دراسة إحصائية عن التخلف العقلي وعلاقته بزواج الأقارب في الجبل الأخضر
items.abstract: يعتبر زواج الأقارب ظاهرة اجتماعية هامة، فهو مرتبط بشكل كبير بالعادات والقيم الاجتماعية السائدة للمجتمعات، وهو من الموضوعات التي تحتل مرتبة هامة في البحوث العلمية، كونه من أكثر الأنماط شيوعا، ونظرا لعدم وجود دراسات مماثلة عن هذا الموضوع، تم أجراء البحث بهدف معرفة نسبة انتشار زواج الأقارب والأمراض الوراثية الأكثر شيوعا في المنطقة الشرقية من ليبيا، حيث تم جمع العينات من خلال مدرسة الاشراقة بمدينة البيضاء وإجراء بعض المقابلات مع أهالي المرضى والإطلاع على التقارير الطبية وتاريخ العائلة، وأجريت الدراسة على 21.351 حالة جمعت من بعض المدن الليبية من 2003 الى 2010، تم من خلالها التعرف الى بعض الأسباب التي تساعد على ظهور الأمراض الوراثية، سواء كان السبب زواج الأقارب أو بسبب مؤثرات خارجية، حيث أظهرت النسبة الكلية وجود تشوهات خلقية 3% ، والتخلف العقلي 26% ، والمكفوفين %2% ، والصم والبكم 5% وضعاف السمع 15% ، وضمور العضلات %1% ومتعددي الإعاقة 4% ، وغيرها من الأمراض 44% ، وقد تطرقنا الى دراسة احصائية على التخلف العقلي وعلاقته بزواج الأقارب، وتوصلنا الى وجود فروق معنوية واضحة بين الذكور والإناث، حيث كانت نسبة الاصابة في الذكور اعلى من الإناث، وكانت اعلى نسبة اصابة في مدينة المرج 40% تليه البيضاء 35% ثم القبة 14 % وشحات %11% ، وتمت مقارنة السنوات فوجدت زيادة بنسبة عالية في 2010 تقدر بـ 21% عنها في 2003 بـ 0.5% ، وبعد تحليل البيانات توصلنا الى اشتراط الفحص قبل الزواج للمتزوجين الأقارب ونشر الوعي الثقافي بمخاطر زواج الأقارب.

items.title: AI & Cognitive Work
items.abstract: Artificial systems now perform a striking range of cognitive tasks. This Element defends three claims. First, the status quo for cognitive work cannot survive. Whatever AI's trajectory, the package of features defining cognitive work – high skill requirements, credentials, wage premiums, resistance to automation, and low productivity growth – will be radically transformed. Second, the widespread displacement of humans from cognitive work, though it sounds alarming, may pose no special threat to human flourishing. Whatever makes work good for people is equally available outside cognitive work, and displacement enables leveraged gains in research and access to justice. Third, a world of ubiquitous cognitive assistance, though it sounds benign, carries distinctive moral risks, especially for children. Cognitive assistance works by reducing cognitive difficulty. But cognitive difficulty is necessary for the normal development of executive function – the capacities constitutive of autonomous agency. This title is also available as Open Access on Cambridge Core.

items.title: Clinical expertise and cognitive reflection predict fewer misconceptions in Bayesian diagnostic reasoning
items.abstract: Abstract Background For many years, research has consistently confirmed that even medical experts fail to solve Bayesian diagnostic tasks. These tasks require correctly estimating a diagnostic test’s positive predictive value based on sensitivity, specificity, and the disease’s prevalence. Previous research has primarily focused on improving task presentation, for example by using natural frequencies or visual aids. The present study introduces the Medical Bayesian Performance Score (MBPS), a confidence-weighted measure that distinguishes confidently held misconceptions from missing concepts. Participants completed eight medical Bayesian diagnostic tasks and rated their confidence after each response. Using this approach, we examined whether medical knowledge, clinical expertise, and cognitive reflection are associated with performance in Bayesian diagnostic reasoning. Methods In an online survey, we compared MBPS values via t tests along two independent variables: (a) medical knowledge (physician group: N p = 30 vs. student control group: N s = 56) and (b) clinical expertise within the physician group (specialists and senior physicians: N e = 19 vs. resident physicians: N r = 11). Furthermore, we analyzed correlations between MBPS values and Cognitive Reflection Test (CRT) scores. Results Physicians did not achieve significantly higher MBPS values than the student control group. In contrast, specialists and senior physicians scored significantly higher than resident physicians. Across all groups, average MBPS values were negative, indicating that confidence-weighted incorrect responses outweighed confidence-weighted correct responses, a pattern consistent with misconceptions. Furthermore, higher CRT scores correlated significantly with higher MBPS values. Conclusions The MBPS provides a complementary perspective to conventional accuracy measures by distinguishing misconceptions from missing concepts and linking Bayesian diagnostic reasoning research with conceptual change theory. Consistent with this perspective, our findings suggest that formal medical knowledge alone was not associated with fewer misconceptions, whereas greater clinical expertise and higher cognitive reflection were. Future research should evaluate evidence-based conceptual change interventions for medical education, such as specific refutation-based training, as a means of improving Bayesian diagnostic reasoning.
