items.title: Written exposure therapy as treatment for comorbid PTSD and SUD: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Purpose of review This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness, feasibility, and acceptability of Written Exposure Therapy (WET) when it is used as a component in integrated treatment of comorbid PTSD and Substance Use Disorder (SUD). A systematic review and meta-analysis was used to synthesise foundational knowledge regarding WET. Recent findings Twelve studies were included and analysed in the review. Random-effects meta-analysis of six studies showed large overall pre/post decrease in PTSD severity (Hedges’ g = 1.18, 95% CI [0.68, 1.72], p < 0.001). Rate of retention (69.03%) was higher than typically seen in integrated prolonged exposure treatments for PTSD-SUD. The majority of participants and providers found WET feasible and acceptable. A minority of participants found concurrent treatment for both disorders burdensome. Summary Findings suggest that can be an effective component in integrated treatment of PTSD-SUD, owing to its efficacy, brevity, and low-burden of integration. Limitations of the current findings include small samples, lack of comparator groups, and limited information regarding treatment components and change in SUD.

items.title: Influence of Sea Surface Temperature and Chlorophyll-a on Biomass Availability and Body Size of the Black Skipjack (Euthynnus lineatus) in the Mexican South Pacific
items.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the relationship between oceanographic variability, specifically sea surface temperature ( SST ) and chlorophyll- a (Chl- a ) concentration, and the abundance and size structure of Euthynnus lineatus (black skipjack) along the southern Pacific coast of Mexico from October 2022 to October 2024. The region experiences two distinct seasons: a dry season with strong “Tehuano” winds causing upwelling, and a rainy season influenced by the Costa Rica Coastal Current. High-resolution satellite data were integrated with biometric and catch data from local artisanal fisheries. Seasonal catch patterns peaked between April and July, following increased productivity and rising SST. The highest catches coincided with SST around 31.0°C, suggesting a thermal preference that enhances aggregation and catchability. Significant interannual variability was observed; 2023 catches were more than double those of 2024, likely associated with the presence of a warm pool in 2023 and varying environmental conditions. Morphometric analysis indicated larger individuals during cooler, productive months (October–March) and smaller fish during warmer periods, possibly due to temperature-driven metabolic responses. Principal component analysis (PC1: 38.4%; PC2: 27.7%) confirmed a strong seasonal modulation of environmental and biological variables. These findings suggest that monthly SST and Chl- a variability are primary drivers of E. lineatus dynamics in Oaxaca, providing essential data for sustainable fisheries management and assessing the impacts of climate change and extreme events on artisanal fisheries.

items.title: A strongly annotated passive acoustic dataset for tropical bird monitoring
items.abstract: Abstract Passive acoustic monitoring enables continuous, non-invasive biodiversity assessment across diverse ecosystems. The scale of these datasets has driven the adoption of machine learning, with supervised approaches showing strong performance. However, supervised methods require time-resolved annotated datasets, which remain scarce, especially in complex tropical soundscapes. We present PteroSet, a curated dataset of strongly annotated Neotropical bird vocalizations recorded in Puerto Asís (Putumayo) and Pivijay (Magdalena), Colombia, between 2023 and 2025. The dataset comprises 563 recordings (73.62 h) and 15,372 time–frequency annotations, including 6,702 events identified to the species level across 168 species. We release the annotations in a COCO-inspired JSON schema that unifies audio files, taxonomic categories, and labels for machine learning workflows. Beyond providing annotated data, PteroSet serves as a realistic benchmark that highlights key characteristics of tropical soundscapes, including acoustic co-occurrence and domain shift across recording sites. We provide a deep learning baseline for binary bird detection, demonstrating PteroSet’s usability and the challenges it presents.

items.title: Microplastic ingestion is ubiquitous in threatened stingrays from the Amazon estuary
items.abstract: Microplastic pollution has become pervasive across freshwater ecosystems worldwide, including the Amazon Basin, where increasing levels of plastic contamination have been reported. Despite growing evidence of microplastic (MP) ingestion in aquatic organisms, studies focusing on threatened species remain extremely scarce, particularly for estuarine elasmobranchs. Rays present high extinction risk among vertebrates and in majority are apex predators, which enhance direct interaction with MPs. The present study investigated, for the first time, MPs ingestion by threatened stingray species from the Amazon Estuary, assessing particles' occurrence and characteristics. Twelve individuals belonging to four elasmobranch species, incidentally caught by artisanal fisheries in Marajó Bay, were examined. Microplastics were detected in all specimens, totaling 181 particles. Fibers predominated (97%), followed by fragments (3%), with black (30.9%) and blue (30.4%) being the most frequent colors. Raman spectroscopy identified Polyester and Polyamide (Nylon) as the dominant polymers (25% each), followed by Polyethylene, Polypropylene, and Polyurethane (16.7% each), a polymer composition consistent with the major anthropogenic plastic previously reported in the Amazon Basin. Although ingestion levels varied considerably among individuals and species, contamination was ubiquitous. This study provides the first record of microplastic occurrence for the stingray species investigated, expanding current knowledge of plastic exposure in threatened Amazonian elasmobranchs. By establishing a baseline for future monitoring, our findings support the incorporation of plastic pollution into conservation assessments of threatened freshwater and estuarine rays.

items.title: Population genomic differentiation and demographic history across an elevational gradient in an endemic bromeliad of the Atlantic Forest mountains
items.abstract: Abstract Montane elevational gradients provide natural laboratories for investigating how environmental heterogeneity, geographic isolation, and historical climatic dynamics shape demographic history, population divergence, and diversification. Topographic complexity and historical climatic oscillations are major drivers of biodiversity patterns in mountain regions worldwide. The Brazilian Atlantic Forest (BAF), a Neotropical biodiversity hotspot characterized by naturally fragmented montane habitats, provides a suitable system for investigating these processes. Here, we used over a thousand SNPs from populations of Pitcairnia flammea Lindl. (Bromeliaceae) distributed across an elevational gradient to investigate patterns of genetic diversity, population structure, and demographic history. Bayesian and coalescent-based analyses revealed strong population structure, with two major genetic groups broadly contrasting higher-elevation populations with low- and mid-elevation populations, although elevation itself was not directly supported as a driver of genetic divergence. Demographic modeling supported early asymmetric gene flow between the two major genetic groups, with higher migration from Group 2 towards Group 1, followed by subsequent isolation. Divergence-time estimates and heterogeneous changes in effective population size further suggest distinct demographic trajectories during the Middle and Late Pleistocene. Together, our results reveal divergent evolutionary trajectories within a single endemic species and suggest that population differentiation across the Atlantic Forest mountains reflects the combined effects of habitat fragmentation, historical connectivity and isolation, genetic drift, and demographic changes potentially associated with Pleistocene climatic oscillations.

items.title: The hydro-politics of rehabilitating fish migration: The Dutch Haringvliet storm surge barrier
items.abstract: Flood barriers impede fish mobility, so one would expect environmentalists to welcome the current vogue for dam decommissioning and dam removal. Dam removal, however, may also contend with strong stakeholder dissent and opposition. Influential community members may have developed a stake in the infrastructure’s functioning and rally behind keeping it in place. Drawing on Yong’s (2021) application of Cresswell’s politics of mobility applied to fish and flood infrastructure, this article applies a fish mobilities framework to a European case of multilevel conflict: the partial opening of the Haringvliet flood barrier on the Dutch coast to restore tidal dynamics in the Rhine-Meuse estuary. It charts how a very local bottleneck could hold up the implementation of basin-level fish migration policy for 19 years. Based on literature review and interviews with key stakeholders, it is found that in the tussle over the (re)opening of the Haringvliet sluicegates, environmental, water quality and navigation interests) backgrounded the interests of migratory fish and fishers for most of the stand-off’s course. This negates that the return of migratory fish to the Rhine was the main (symbolic) driver for the intervention in the first place. Now that their passageway has been partly re-enabled, it turns out fish migration is not as predicable and controllable as believed; given the choice, migratory fish migrate as they please.

items.title: Energysheds and the Urban Energy Transition: A Method for Assessing Spatial Imbalances in Energy Flow
items.abstract: Abstract Urban areas are facing the challenges of transitioning toward a low-carbon society as a response to climate change. However, the benefits and burdens of this energy transition are not evenly distributed across cities. To address this disparity, the concept of energy justice has emerged. The issue of urban energy justice can be understood as a manifestation of geographical energy disparities where energy-consuming regions enjoy significant benefits, while energy producing regions suffer from externalities. In this paper, we propose a method that utilizes the notion of “energyshed” to align city energy consumption with power plant energy generation, addressing geographical energy (im)balances. The proposed method maps the spatial supply–demand relationships between regions and power plants without relying on proprietary algorithms or territory-specific cutoff distances. Although spatial imbalance alone does not establish energy injustice, the resulting energysheds provide a diagnostic basis for identifying energy-generating regions that bear disproportionate burdens and for informing a fairer allocation of resources during the energy transition.

items.title: Large language models for tech mining and technology opportunity analysis: A diffusion of innovation perspective on detecting evolutionary stages of innovative practices using ChatGPT
items.abstract: Technology opportunity analysis (TOA) traditionally examines technological developments to identify opportunities, but typically conceptualizes these opportunities at the level of technologies or fields. This study advances practice-level TOA by conceptualizing technology-enabled innovative practices as technology-process-industry configurations and using their evolution to identify technology opportunities. It extends TOA by integrating diffusion of innovation theory and operationalizing its constructs to explain how opportunity spaces evolve. A seven-stage evolutionary model tracks how configurations emerge, diffuse and consolidate over time, identifying an opportunity window where configurations remain vacant, exploratory, emerging or promising. To investigate this perspective and respond to recent calls for generative AI in informetrics, the study develops an AI-enabled Tech Mining framework based on large-scale analysis of full-text scientific articles. ChatGPT-4o operates within an LLM+ architecture, combining prompt engineering with a rule-based expert system. The framework is benchmarked against expert coders, near-graduate students, a fine-tuned BERT classifier and alternative LLMs, and applied to 129,566 articles (2019–2024). The resulting dataset of 43,632 practices across 11 enabling technologies is analyzed using supervised machine learning to identify plausible vacant configurations. The study shows how controlled LLM workflows can make theory-informed opportunity analysis scalable and support a more managerial understanding of technology opportunities.

items.title: Compartment-specific root microbiomes are associated with regional variation in Salvia miltiorrhiza quality with functional assessment of a Pseudomonas putida isolate
items.abstract: Danshen ( Salvia miltiorrhiza Bunge) exhibits marked regional differences in secondary metabolism, but their relationships with root-associated microbiomes remain insufficiently understood. Relationships between root-associated microbiomes and regional quality traits of Danshen were examined using samples from 19 cultivated fields in five major production regions of China. Root biomass, major bioactive constituents, and bacterial and fungal communities in root-inhabiting and rhizosphere compartments were analyzed. Regional patterns were distinct. Samples from Shandong (SD) had higher root biomass and tanshinone (TS) contents, whereas those from Sichuan (SC) had higher salvianolic acid B levels. Root-inhabiting bacterial alpha diversity was lowest in SD samples, where specific taxa, including Pseudomonas and Pantoea , were enriched. Salvianolic acid variation exhibited distinct associations with fungal communities. Variance partitioning also indicated that soil properties and microbiome variation explained both shared and independent fractions of regional quality differences. Network and trait-correlation analyses identified a Pseudomonas -affiliated operational taxonomic unit closely associated with both root biomass and TS accumulation. A bioaugmentation assay examined the functional potential of a culturable Pseudomonas isolate, Pseudomonas putida strain 3–37, obtained from Danshen roots. Under the tested conditions, strain 3–37 treatment promoted plant growth and increased total TS accumulation. These findings indicate closer associations of root-inhabiting bacterial communities with root biomass and tanshinone accumulation and of fungal communities with salvianolic acid variation. Therefore, strain 3–37 may serve as a candidate microbial resource for Danshen cultivation.

items.title: Abundancia y riqueza específica en un ensamble de aves en un Área Importante para la Conservación del sudeste bonaerense
items.abstract: Sectores costeros de la provincia de Buenos Aires son considerados como sitios importantes de invernada y reaprovisionamiento para una gran diversidad de aves playeras, marinas y costeras. En este trabajo caracterizamos la variación intra-anual en la abundancia y riqueza del ensamble de aves que hace uso de un sector de la costa del sudeste bonaerense, el Área Importante para la Conservación de Aves AICA BA12: Playa Punta Mogotes y Puerto de Mar del Plata. Durante un año y con una frecuencia quincenal, registramos, a lo largo de tres transectas (con características ambientales y actividades antrópicas contrastantes), la diversidad y abundancia de aves junto con sus principales actividades comportamentales en las playas del complejo de balnearios Punta Mogotes, ubicado en la costa sur del Partido de General Pueyrredon. Registramos un total de 12,820 individuos representados por al menos 33 especies. El ensamble de aves varió en función de la transecta y la estación del año. La abundancia total de aves fue menor durante la primavera. El sector norte del AICA fue identificado como aquel en albergar el mayor número y riqueza de aves. Este sitio se encuentra lindante a la Reserva Natural Puerto Mar del Plata, por lo que podría proponerse ser incorporado a la Reserva, lo cual permitiría la regulación legal de las actividades humanas que se desarrollan en el sector norte del AICA.

items.title: Multi-scale modeling of continent-wide tracking data confirms the importance of landscape mosaics for the European wildcat
items.abstract: Abstract Context Land use change is a major threat to the persistence of wildlife in human-dominated landscapes, making the knowledge of the amount and spatial configuration of suitable habitat essential for conservation. The European wildcat ( Felis silvestris ) currently persists in fragmented populations and faces ever increasing human pressure. Objectives We modeled and mapped suitable wildcat habitats at the continental scale, to identify opportunities and constraints for its conservation. Methods We compiled a large telemetry dataset comprising 200 wildcats across Europe and developed multi-scale habitat suitability models using Maxent. Habitat selection was analyzed at two hierarchical levels: home-range placement within the wider landscape and selection within the established home ranges. Results At both levels, wildcats selected broadleaved forests, mixed forests, and grasslands, while avoiding landscapes dominated by large continuous forests. For home-range placement, they preferred lower terrain ruggedness and less intensive agriculture. Within the home ranges, wildcats selected forest edges and small woody features. Conclusions Our results highlight the importance of heterogeneous forest–grassland mosaics habitats. More than half of the predicted suitable habitat occurred outside protected areas, highlighting the need for effective conservation strategies beyond their borders. Predictions of suitable areas should, however, be interpreted cautiously in regions where environmental conditions extend beyond those represented in the calibration data. By providing the first continental-scale habitat suitability map based on a large European telemetry dataset, our study offers a spatial foundation for identifying conservation priorities and supporting the long-term connectivity and recovery of wildcat populations.

items.title: Plant volatile organic compounds as mediators of plant insect communication
items.abstract: Plants are sessile organisms exposed to a constant dialogue with various pests, insects, and microbes. After communication through various interactions (mutualism, predation, and parasitism), the plants trigger a range of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) through the modulation of the host gene. Plants responded to insect interactions both specifically and broadly. These interactions are controlled by various metabolic tracks such as the cytosolic mevalonic acid (MVA) pathway, plastidic methylerythritol phosphate (MEP) pathway, the phyto-oxylipin pathway, and shikimate pathways, where terpenoids, green-leaf volatiles (GLVs), and benzenoids/phenylpropanoids like VOCs are produced. Moreover, VOCs play a central role in chemical and visual communication, primarily by attracting pollinators and deterring herbivores, although in some cases, they may also manipulate herbivore behavior. The transmission of VOCs during insect attack is orchestrated via the signaling pathways of jasmonic acid (JA) and salicylic acid (SA). VOC biosynthesis is regulated at transcriptional, post-transcriptional, and epigenetic levels, involving transcription factors (TFs), miRNAs, long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), DNA methylation, chromatin remodeling, and histone modifications that modulate genes in VOC biosynthetic pathways. Subsequently, insects also developed approaches to conquer the plant hurdle as well as consequently established a plant–insect relationship. In this review, we concentrate on the roles of plant volatiles, including their production, functions, regulation, and defense system.

items.title: ADVANCING BIODIVERSITY CONSERVATION IN A RAPIDLY CHANGING WORLD: PLANT-CENTERED STRATEGIES FOR ECOLOGICAL RESILIENCE, RESTORATION AND SUSTAINABLE FUTURE
items.abstract: Biodiversity conservation is shifting from the paradigm of species protection to the maintenance of ecological, genetic, and functional integrity. Earlier biodiversity research and conservation practice focused on understanding and responding to the drivers of biodiversity loss, e.g., habitat loss, climate change, environmental degradation, invasive species, and overexploitation. This review synthesizes the role of plants in sustaining ecosystems, with an emphasis on genetic conservation, ecological restoration, connectivity, conservation biotechnology, monitoring, and adaptive governance. The current crisis of biodiversity loss affects a million species, threatening their extinction, while plant genetic diversity is also disappearing at an alarming rate. According to the Food and Agriculture Organization’s (FAO) Third Report on the State of the World’s Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture, 42% of the plant genetic resources evaluated for taxonomic diversity were no longer present in at least one country. By the end of 2024, 6 million plant accessions were stored in medium- and long-term gene bank facilities. Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework promotes the restoration of at least 30% of ecosystems and the conservation of 30% of land, inland waters, coasts, and oceans by 2030. These goals will require more than expanding the number of protected areas. To increase resilience to climate change, conserve genetic resources, and restore degraded ecosystems, it will be critical to ensure genetic and functional diversity while promoting native plant species and improving connectivity at multiple scales through restoration and adaptive management. Moreover, achieving the targets set for 2030 will contribute to food security, sustainable livelihoods, and ecosystem service provision.

items.title: Exploring Sustainable Tourism in the Western Ghats of Karnataka: Community Participation, Ecological Risks and a Policy Framework
items.abstract: Tourism has enormous potential in the Western Ghats of Karnataka, owing to the presence of biodiversity, forests, scenic beauty, waterfalls, wildlife and heritage. But, increased tourism activity in the region may lead to adverse impacts on the environment, including infrastructure expansion, waste generation and natural habitat disturbance. This study looks at sustainable tourism development in the Western Ghats of Karnataka, specifically in relation to tourism development, community involvement in tourism development and ecologic conservation. For this study, the approach employed is descriptive, exploratory and conceptual, based mainly on secondary sources and institutional literature. This study analyzes the tourism potentials and challenges, involvement of local community in tourism development and destination management and the need for integration of tourism with ecology and environment. Based on thematic analysis, this study suggests an integrated policy framework related to ecological carrying capacity, community involvement, responsible tourism infrastructure development, waste management, climate risk management, biodiversity conservation and institutional coordination. The study makes the case for a change in focus from tourism promotion to destination stewardship, whereby the considerations of economic development, community wellbeing and ecological preservation would be taken into account. The framework presented here could help stakeholders such as policymakers and tourism authorities develop sustainable tourism in Western Ghats of Karnataka

items.title: Role of Biodiversity in Agriculture: Harnessing Ecosystem Services for Resilient Food Systems
items.abstract: Biodiversity is key to supporting agricultural productivity because it sustains major ecosystem services, including pollination, biological pest control, soil fertility, and climate resilience. Despite its importance, the contribution of agrobiodiversity remains underutilized due to systemic challenges such as intense agrochemical use and simplified farming systems. As climate variability increases, the use of biodiversity-based ecosystem services is key to designing resilient and sustainable food systems. This chapter reviews existing literature on how biodiversity sustains sustainable agriculture through crop genetic diversity, diversified farming systems, and ecology-based pest and disease management. Conservation of locally adapted crop varieties and integration of microbial-based integrated pest and disease management further reinforce the practice of climate-smart agriculture. The chapter stresses the need for robust monitoring of biodiversity, forward-looking policies, and involvement of stakeholders to maximize ecosystem service benefits for food security and resilient rural livelihoods in the long run.

items.title: Ultra-high precision speckle spectrometer enabling radio-frequency scale resolution of atomic spectra
items.abstract: Abstract Laser speckle, the granular intensity pattern arising from random optical interference, provides a high-dimensional encoding of spectral information that can be exploited for precision metrology. Speckle-based spectrometers have advanced rapidly owing to their compact footprint, mechanical robustness and alignment agnostic nature, yet their spectral resolution has remained limited to the picometre scale. In this work, we break this limit by employing an integrating sphere as a multiply scattering cavity with access to a high range of path lengths to enhance spectral sensitivity. At 780 nm, the resulting device achieves a resolution of 6 fm, corresponding to a resolving power of 1.3 × 10 8 , representing an approximately 80-fold improvement over previous implementations. This ultra-high resolution enables clear discrimination of laser sidebands generated by an electro-optical modulator, with extracted sideband powers agreeing with expected values to within 1%. It further permits a direct speckle-based measurement of the hyperfine structure of the D 2 transition in 85 Rb, with transmission spectra differing by no more than 3.7% from independent wavemeter-referenced measurements. These results establish speckle as a platform for ultra-high precision spectroscopy, radio-frequency spectrometry, and microwave photonics.

items.title: Probabilistic redshift estimation of undetected galaxies from multi-band background light maps
items.abstract: Accurate knowledge of the redshift distributions of undetected galaxy populations is essential for extracting the cosmological information encoded in the cosmic optical background. We present the first framework for estimating these distributions directly from multi-band maps of unresolved background light, using conditional normalising flows trained on realistic image simulations. For imaging quality comparable to that expected from the survey and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), our model achieves sub-per cent accuracy in both the mean and standard deviation of the flux-weighted redshift distributions when the training and target samples are statistically well matched. Furthermore, the network proves highly resilient to incomplete photometric coverage when combined with tailored data imputation strategies. To address the challenge of statistical mismatches between simulations and real observations, we propose incorporating observational quantities into the target variables, providing a built-in diagnostic to assess model reliability and uncertainty from the predictions themselves. We also demonstrate the feasibility of map-based tomographic analyses, showing that the model retains sufficient pixel-level detail to recover redshift distributions for tomographically defined subsamples with near sub-per cent accuracy across all bins. items.title: Molecules in the shadows of the protoplanetary disk HD 143006. Evidence of C/O,≳,1 from simultaneously modeling fourteen ALMA lines
items.abstract: The inner disk of the T,Tauri star HD,143006 is inclined and casts a broad shadow over a large portion of the outer disk. We use this extraordinary geometry to study the impact of stellar ultraviolet (UV) irradiation on disk chemistry, temperature, and line formation. We present new ALMA observations of this disk, covering CO, 13 CO, C^18O, CN, HCN, HCO^+$, CS, and C_3H_2. Combined with previously published C_2H, N_2H^+ and H_2CO observations, these data constitute an extensive dataset of fourteen ALMA lines from nine different molecules. We subdivide these data into two disk halves: the illuminated part and the shadowed part. We develop ProDiMo models for these two disk halves by optionally including an inclined inner disk that blocks the stellar illumination of the upper layers of the outer disk without hindering the stellar illumination of the outer disk along the midplane. The observed line flux contrasts between the illuminated and the shadowed disk sides are not very pronounced. We explain this phenomenon by introducing ``equilibrated models'' that consider a slow heating and cooling relaxation of gas parcels orbiting in and out of the shadow. Our results fit the radial line intensity profiles of all ALMA lines, both in flux and radial shape, with an overall reduced ̧hi of about 2.3, both from the illuminated and the shadowed disk sides, along with two ALMA continuum images, where we see evidence of radial drift, and the spectral energy distribution (SED) beyond 20,μm, all with one model. In most cases, the line intensities only increase slightly on the illuminated side because the gas warms up slowly, although fast UV photochemistry significantly reduces the observable molecular concentrations. The dust temperatures increase even more rapidly, but this has little effect on the line formation. However, for the lines of N_2H^+ and CS, which probe deeper layers where the gas and dust temperatures are coupled, slow UV desorption of ices such as NH_3 and H_2S plays a crucial role. This can result in a brightening of these lines on the shadowed side. Our analysis suggests with high confidence that the carbon-to-oxygen ratio in the outer disk of HD,143006 is slightly greater than one (∼,1.05). The disk mass is fit to be as low as 0.0012,M_⊙. However, almost equally well-fitting models with a fixed disk mass of $0.021 M_⊙ can be obtained after readjusting the disk shape, dust, and gas heating and cooling parameters.

items.title: Machine learning-based classification of type 1 active galactic nuclei
items.abstract: Quasars and Seyfert galaxies are two prototypes of type 1 active galactic nuclei (AGNs). The current view posits that they belong to a uniform population with continuous distributions of the bolometric luminosity and the contribution from host galaxy. Clarifying whether physical differences exist between them would be helpful in improving our understanding of the nature of accretion of supermassive black holes and the co-evolution with their host galaxies. Although the sample sizes and studies of quasars have been growing rapidly recent years, research on Seyfert galaxies continues to be limited. Methods used to select Seyfert galaxies in large surveys or to distinguish quasars and Seyfert galaxies in broad-line AGNs have also received scarce attention in the literature. We aim to provide a machine learning-based method to distinguish type 1 quasars and type 1 Seyfert galaxies based on photometric data, which could be applied to large all-sky surveys. The method can also be used to obtain relatively complete samples of Seyfert galaxy candidates when broad-line AGNs have been selected. A principle component analysis (PCA) was first applied to reduce the dimensionality and visualize the separation between quasars and Seyfert galaxies based on multidimensional data. Then we trained an supervised classifier to distinguish quasars and Seyfert galaxies with optical and mid-infrared photometric data. The results of PCA show that quasars and Seyfert galaxies are partially distinguishable. The supervised classifier based on a random forest (RF) algorithm achieves a good level of performance for type 1 quasars, with a F_1 score of 0.967. The performance for classifying Seyfert galaxies was worse, with a F_1 score of 0.791. Increasing the classification threshold can help derive a sample of Seyfert galaxies with a high level of purity. The classifiers were then applied to the cross-matched sample with DESI DR1. When compared with the results of spectroscopic classification, quasars identifications were also accompanied by a high level of precision and recall. For Seyfert galaxies identified by RF classifier, there are plenty of less luminous sources who are classified as quasars by spectroscopic method. If they are regarded as Seyfert galaxies, our classifier also performs well for predicting Seyfert galaxies. Both the median SEDs and the fraction of Seyfert galaxies derived by our classifier are similar to those in the training sample, while the fraction of Seyfert galaxies for spectroscopic classification are lower at all redshifts. These results indicate that our classifier has the capacity to recover the features of Seyfert galaxies-at least with respect to the ones that are similar to the Seyfert galaxies in the training sample.

items.title: Hamilton Halo: Founding Declaration
items.abstract: Hamilton Halo (H2) is an independent research initiative formally established by Adam Hoo on November 7, 2026. This founding declaration records the initiative's origin, the founder's account of independently conceiving its name earlier in 2026, and its intended scholarly and educational direction. Inspired by the fictional "gas halo" described in Peter F. Hamilton's Commonwealth Saga novels Pandora's Star (2004) and Judas Unchained (2005), H2 proposes to investigate the phenomenon's scientific plausibility through established principles of physics, astronomy, mathematics, and scientific reasoning. The initiative also seeks to explore the phenomenon's educational potential as a setting for scientific inquiry, academic assimilation, and interdisciplinary learning in secondary education. Intended outcomes include a scientifically grounded scholarly paper and potentially accompanying modular instructional resources. This declaration records the initiative's founding intentions rather than completed research findings. Hamilton Halo is undertaken independently and acknowledges Peter F. Hamilton as the creative source of the fictional phenomenon. Guiding principle: Follow the science. Honor the fiction. Serve the students.

items.title: Conceptual divergence analysis: LLM-assisted mapping of a researcher’s conceptual vocabulary against their curated literature
items.abstract: Abstract Large language model (LLM)-based research tools often overlook a researcher-specific problem in manuscript writing: where does my use of a key theoretical term stand relative to the literature I want to address? We introduce Conceptual Divergence Analysis (CDA), an LLM-based retrieval-augmented generation pipeline to compare theoretical term usage in a researcher’s manuscripts with usage in a researcher-curated literature corpus. We propose reflective calibration as the individual-level scientometric function this workflow performs. We demonstrate CDA on two research programs, encompassing corpora of roughly 3,200 and 2,800 papers and four theoretical terms. The analyses reveal researcher-specific divergences consequential for theoretical positioning. In one case, the researcher draws a distinction the literature leaves underarticulated. In another case, CDA reveals how a term carries different meanings across disciplinary traditions, helping the researcher anticipate how different scholarly audiences may interpret its use. Register assignments are anchored to pre-computed clusters. An optional researcher-led validation step records the researcher’s judgment before revealing the model’s interpretation, making agreement or disagreement explicit. We release the complete pipeline as an open-source resource with a no-installation hosted demonstration on a public toy corpus, extending an individual-level tradition in scientometrics from citation structure to conceptual vocabulary.

items.title: M. B. Brauns Theorie der Chronogenese: Das Prinzip der rekursiven Kosmologie, der partizipatorischen Quantenzeit und des kausalen Zivilisationsursprungs
items.abstract: Contemporary foundational research faces persistent anomalies across seemingly separate disciplines: in theoretical physics, the black hole information paradox, baryon asymmetry (baryogenesis), the fine-tuning of fundamental constants, and the role of time in quantum state reduction; in information philosophy, Nick Bostrom’s Simulation Argument, which lacks a compelling physical motive as to why an advanced civilization would expend vast computational energy simulating its own ancestors; and in archaeology and cultural anthropology, the abrupt emergence of monolithic architecture, agricultural genetics, precision astronomy, and writing immediately following the Younger Dryas (~9,600 BCE, Göbekli Tepe), accompanied by globally isomorphic primary traditions of anthropomorphic teachers and encoded cosmological metaphors (Norse Ragnarök describing a black hole devouring the sun, the ancient Egyptian Nu representing the primordial quantum vacuum, and the Mesoamerican Long Count epochal boundary in late December 2012 coinciding with global smartphone saturation and continuous digital archiving), where classical paleo-SETI fails on exobiological and archaeological grounds. Under the concept of Chronogenesis, M. B. Braun formulates a unified theory in five postulates (1st–5th Braunian Postulates), demonstrating that all of these anomalies resolve without contradiction once supermassive black holes are understood as unitary holographic quantum memory and CPT-symmetric phase-transition nodes of a cyclic cosmos, ancestor simulations as mandatory boundary-value calculations prior to utilizing closed timelike curves, and the Neolithic leap as an intraspecific, causality-preserving knowledge transfer governed by the Novikov self-consistency principle—complete with Popperian falsification criteria across cosmology, quantum interferometry, paleogenetics, and marine geology. Die gegenwärtige Grundlagenforschung sieht sich über Fächergrenzen hinweg mit fundamentalen Erklärungsdefiziten konfrontiert: In der theoretischen Physik betreffen diese das Informationsparadoxon am Ereignishorizont Schwarzer Löcher, die ungeklärte Materie-Antimaterie-Asymmetrie (Baryogenese), die extreme Feinabstimmung der Naturkonstanten (Fine-Tuning) sowie die Rolle der Zeit im quantenmechanischen Messprozess. In der Informationsphilosophie postuliert Nick Bostroms Simulationshypothese zwar die statistische Wahrscheinlichkeit hochauflösender Vorfahren-Simulationen, bleibt jedoch eine physikalisch zwingende Erklärung schuldig, warum eine fortgeschrittene Zivilisation gewaltige Energiemengen für die Berechnung vergangener Epochen aufwenden sollte. In der Archäologie und Kulturanthropologie schließlich steht das abrupte Einsetzen von Megalitharchitektur, Agrargenetik, Astronomie und Schrift nach dem Ende der Jüngeren Dryas (~9.600 v. Chr., Göbekli Tepe) im Raum — begleitet von weltweit isomorphen Primärüberlieferungen über menschengestaltige „Lehrer“ sowie kosmologischen Metaphern (Ragnarök als Beschreibung eines die Sonne verschlingenden Schwarzen Lochs, das altägyptische Nu als Konzept des Quantenvakuums und der Maya-Kalender-Epochenwechsel Ende Dezember 2012 synchron zur globalen Etablierung des Smartphones und lückenloser digitaler Echtzeit-Archivierung), an deren exobiologischer und archäologischer Widersprüchlichkeit wiederum die klassische Prä-Astronautik (Paläo-SETI) scheitert. Unter dem Begriff der Chronogenese (Entstehung von Ordnung, Kosmos und Zivilisation aus geschlossener Zeit-Rekursion) formuliert M. B. Braun eine eigenständige, vereinheitlichte Theorie in fünf Postulaten (1. bis 5. Braun’sches Postulat): Sie weist nach, dass sich sämtliche genannten Anomalien widerspruchsfrei auflösen, sobald supermassereiche Schwarze Löcher gemäß dem holographischen Prinzip als unitäre Quantenspeicher und CPT-symmetrische Resetknoten eines zyklischen Universums und der neolithische Zivilisationssprung als kausalitätswahrender Wissenstransfer entlang geschlossener zeitartiger Kurven (Novikov-Selbstkonsistenzprinzip) verstanden werden — überprüfbar anhand konkreter Falsifikationskriterien in der Kosmologie, Quantenoptik, Paläogenetik und Meeresgeologie.

items.title: Born at the right time: Examining the effect of age at school entry on mental health in adulthood
items.abstract: This paper examines the largely understudied effect of age at school entry on adult mental health. Using nationwide Finnish register data, we capture a broad spectrum of mental health conditions, ranging from severe disorders to less severe problems. To identify causal effects, we implement a regression discontinuity design around the January 1 school-entry cutoff. We find that being born at the beginning of the year improves mental health outcomes, with the effects concentrated among women in their late twenties.

items.title: Plant invasion alters rhizosphere microbial communities across temperate ecosystems
items.abstract: Invasive plants threaten ecosystems, and their management remains a challenge in ecological restoration. Control and replanting outcomes can vary considerably, with restoration sites often experiencing re-invasion, secondary invasion, or failed native plant establishment. While impacts are often focused above ground, plant invasion can also alter rhizosphere microbial communities in ways that may inhibit recovery. This study characterized bacterial and fungal communities of native and invasive shrub-layer plants across three British Columbia ecosystems (coastal forest, riparian forest, and coastal wetland) and tested whether invasion-associated taxonomic shifts corresponded with differences in predicted microbial functions and ecological guilds. Rhizosphere soils were sequenced for 16S rRNA and ITS2 markers and analyzed in QIIME2 using weighted UniFrac and PERMANOVA. Functional potential (PICRUSt2 MetaCyc pathways) and fungal guilds (FUNGuild) were compared using Bray-Curtis dissimilarities and PERMANOVA. Microbial communities differed significantly by plant species and invasion status in the riparian site, by plant species in the coastal forest site, and showed no significant differences with lower amplicon sequence variant (ASV) richness at the coastal wetland site. Predicted functional composition differed among plant species in coastal forest bacterial MetaCyc profiles, while fungal functional groups differed by both plant species and invasion status at the riparian site, where invasive Japanese knotweed showed a predicted shift from ectomycorrhizal toward saprotrophic fungi. Responses were strongly context-dependent across ecosystems. These findings highlight the importance of belowground microbial variation in invasion ecology and support further investigation on whether targeted soil interventions, such as inoculation or soil transfer, can improve restoration outcomes.

items.title: The political geography of memoricide: Embodied memory and the struggle over olive trees in Area C, West Bank
items.abstract: This article provides a critical, decolonial analysis of ongoing settler-colonial violence in Area C of the occupied West Bank, focusing on the material and epistemic struggles surrounding Palestinian olive trees. Theoretically grounded in the concepts of memoricide, politicide, and embodied memory, the study investigates how state-led apparatuses of dispossession dismantle indigenous socio-ecological knowledge. Methodologically, it develops a rigorous qualitative discourse analysis of a systematically gathered corpus of subaltern testimonies and institutional documentations spanning from 2017 to mid-2026. The empirical findings reveal that spatial erasure operates through a multi-layered mechanism. While the direct, spectacular uprooting of ancient olive trees marks an immediate physical loss, a secondary, more insidious register of memoricide is executed through the structural enforcement of agricultural monoculture. This forced ecological flattening is further accelerated by contemporary digital-bureaucratic statecraft (most notably the May 2026 online land registration system ), which compels farmers to use resilient olive groves as desperate political placeholders to legally defend their land against imminent expropriation. Ultimately, this study demonstrates that spatial confinement operates as an epistemic project of historical cancellation that narrows the parameters of indigenous life, while simultaneously illustrating that the subaltern act of replanting remains an indelible, embodied reality of counter-geographic resistance.

items.title: Human-cattle Relations in Selected Chinese News Discourse: A Corpus-assisted Ecolinguistic Analysis
items.abstract: In the context of modernity, profit-driven and unethical practices, such as artificially increasing beef weight and enhancing its visual freshness to meet consumer expectations, have led some traders to inject water into live cattle. Such practices not only violate animal ethics, undermine animal welfare, and disrupt species ecology but also prompt people to reconsider human–cattle relations in China. This study aims to explore ‘human-cattle relations’ in the Chinese context textually and visually, specifically, to examine the interspecies ethical issues involved in ‘human-cattle relations’ in China. This study draws on a self-compiled corpus of cattle representations in selected Chinese news discourse covering a period of six years (2020–2025) through the lens of the Hallidayan approach, Stibbe’s ecosophy and Kress and van Leeuwen’s visual grammar. A corpus-assisted and qualitative analysis was used to reveal more profound interspecies ethical issues. Qualitative findings further identify discursive patterns associated with industrial fatalism and technocratic optimism, whereby industrialized cattle farming is represented as a normalized pathway to economic development, while technocratic optimism is positively evaluated in relation to productivity and animal welfare. The results show that industrial fatalism and technocratic optimism can simultaneously shape the discursive representation of cattle welfare, with the former normalizing the inevitability of industrial exploitation, and the latter promoting technological solutions that appear to enhance animal well-being while leaving underlying structures of commodification largely unchallenged. The findings suggest that industrial fatalism and technocratic optimism frequently represent cattle as passive objects. The “water-injected live cattle” incident is not merely a cattle welfare issue, but also a problem concerning interspecies’ ecological ethics and the imbalance in human-cattle relations.

items.title: Governing the lithium boom in Ghana, South Africa and Zimbabwe: civil society and social accountability in critical minerals governance
items.abstract: The global demand for lithium and other critical minerals has reconfigured the politics of extraction in Africa, intensifying pressures on states to deliver both development and decarbonisation. Yet the governance of this new extractive frontier increasingly depends on the interplay between multiple actors, including states, corporations, financiers, and civil society. Drawing from literature review and semi-structured interviews, this paper examines how African civil society organisations (CSOs) contribute to multi-actor governance of lithium through mechanisms of social accountability. By referring to the three cases of Ghana, South Africa and Zimbabwe, we argue that CSOs are not merely reactive watchdogs but constitute a vital counterweight in shaping the legitimacy and direction of critical mineral development. Their capacity to play this role, which ranges from litigation and advocacy to community mobilisation and transnational campaigning, influences whether critical mineral development reinforces extractive inequality or enables more responsible and inclusive resource governance that can create wider societal benefits. Drawing on lessons from the three case studies the paper concludes by providing recommendations for enhancing the participation of CSO in the governance of critical minerals and outlines some directions for future research.

items.title: Institutional Embeddedness and Collaborative ESG Governance: Configurational Mechanisms of Green Transformation Among Heavily Polluting Firms in China
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Improving ESG governance in heavily polluting firms has become a critical yet insufficiently understood issue. Existing studies predominantly examine the net effects of individual factors, but pay limited attention to the configurational logic through which internal structures and external contexts jointly shape ESG outcomes. Drawing on the structure–context framework, this study integrates NCA and fsQCA to examine the driving mechanisms of ESG governance among 148 A‐share listed heavily polluting firms in China over 2021–2024. The NCA results reveal that shareholder network centrality (DC) and investor sentiment (SS) function as bottleneck‐like lower‐bound conditions for achieving a targeted level of ESG governance. Building on this boundary‐setting insight, the fsQCA results identify three equifinal pathways to high ESG governance: Agile Response–Policy‐Market Resonance, Resource‐Driven–Institutional Embeddedness, and Network Synergy–Low‐Carbon Leadership. In contrast, the configurational pathways leading to non‐high ESG governance are markedly different, confirming causal asymmetry. This study enriches configurational ESG research and provides differentiated strategic implications for the green transformation of heavily polluting firms under the Dual Carbon goals.

items.title: A preliminary sustainability assessment framework for traditional medicinal knowledge built from an existing ethnographic record: the Gayo ethnomedicine system, Lut Tawar, Central Aceh, Indonesia
items.abstract: Traditional medicinal knowledge (TMK) links human health, biodiversity and cultural continuity, yet sustainability-indicator frameworks rarely assess it directly. Our contribution is methodological: we show how an existing ethnographic record can be turned into a transparent, traceable sustainability assessment framework. We worked only from a 2024 ethnographic technical report on the Gayo community of Lut Tawar, Central Aceh, Indonesia, with no new fieldwork and no informant-level data. Its 51-species inventory (158 use reports across 67 ailment labels) and 65-entry remedy inventory were restructured into a dataset, from which we computed reported-use breadth (RUB), documented corpus consensus (DCC, calculated with the Informant Consensus Factor formula) and formulation richness (FR). We coded the report's account of knowledge erosion into 16 explicitly stated mechanisms (structural 6, cultural 5, ecological 5) and organised both profiles in a Pressure–State–Response structure, the Traditional Medicinal Knowledge Sustainability Profile (TMK-SP), without collapsing them into one score. RUB was right-skewed (median 2; ten species held 73 of 158 use reports). DCC was low (pooled 0.15; at most 0.27 in categories with eight or more use reports) and rose with category size. Sixteen of 65 ailments (24.6%; bootstrap 95% CI 13.8–35.4%) had a single recorded remedy. The composite pressure score (0.89; 0.84–0.96 under random weights) shows that erosion is documented in all three dimensions, not how severe it is. TMK-SP is a preliminary diagnostic profile, not a validated measure of sustainability; informant-level surveys, voucher specimens, expert validation and repeat surveys are needed before it can support comparison across sites.

items.title: Agrotourism’s Contribution to Total Factor Productivity: A Conceptual Framework for the Agrotourism-Induced Productivity Enhancement Model
items.abstract: The primary objective of this study is to analyze the mechanisms through which agritourism supports Total Factor Productivity (TFP) in rural economies across social, ecological, and economic-organizational dimensions and to propose a holistic conceptual model. Within the framework of qualitative research design, the document analysis method was employed to systematically evaluate policy documents from FAO, OECD, UNWTO, ENRD, and the European Union. While acknowledging the significance of diverse methodological approaches such as Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP), which are widely used in the literature to address gaps in agritourism planning; this study focuses on the structural processes that trigger productivity through document analysis. Findings indicate that agritourism is not merely a tool for income diversification but a multi-layered ecosystem that stimulates TFP through knowledge sharing, social capital formation, and sustainable resource management. Accordingly, the study proposes the "Agrotourism-Induced Productivity Enhancement Model" (AIPEM), which addresses the interaction between social capital and technological adaptation. The results suggest that agritourism should be positioned as a productivity tool focused on structural transformation and learning-oriented rural development.

items.title: Impact of Humic Acid on Bioanode Electrochemistry and Horizontal Diffusion Kinetics of Dissolved Organic Carbon in Marine Sediment Microbial Fuel Cells
items.abstract: Abstract The long-term utilisation of marine sediment microbial fuel cells (MSMFCs) faces the challenges of diminished power output and the ambiguous diffusion mechanism of dissolved organic carbon (DOC). Here, a regulation strategy for enhancing MSMFCs performance by adding humic acid (HA) is proposed. Through HA addition, the proportion and abundance of electroactive microbial communities were increased, thus leading to the excellent electrochemical activity of the bioanode. The results demonstrate that HA significantly improves the power generation and DOC horizontal diffusion of MSMFCs, with 1.0 g/L HA showing the optimal enhancement. After a 120-d of operation, the output voltage stabilised at 650 mV, the power density reached 65.32 mW/m 2 , and the coulombic efficiency was 86.8%. These results confirm that HA addition effectively enhances the operating time and energy generation capacity of MSMFCs. Moreover, an innovative DOC transport model incorporating a quantitative relationship among HA concentration, system lifespan, and distance to the anode is established, which provides theoretical support for future siting and long-term application of MSMFCs.

items.title: Environmental Stewardship Practices of Teachers and Ecoliteracy Skills of Grade Six Learners
items.abstract: This study was conducted to determine the relationship between environmental stewardship practices of teachers and ecoliteracy skills of Grade Six learners in public elementary schools in Maa District, Division of Davao City. The study used a non-experimental quantitative research design utilizing correlational method. The respondents of this study are composed of 47 grade six teachers in public elementary schools using a universal sampling. However, each respondent chose three grade six learners since they were the target of the study. The statistical tols used were Mean, Pearson Product Moment Correlation Coefficient (Pearson r), and Regression Analysis. The findings revealed that the teachers achieved a high level on environmental stewardship practices. Meanwhile, grade six learners established a high level of ecoliteracy skills. There was a significant relationship between environmental stewardship practices of teachers and ecoliteracy skills of grade six learners in public elementary schools. The domains of environmental stewardship practices of teachers were significantly influenced by the ecoliteracy skills of grade six learners. It is articulated in this study that ecoliteracy skills of grade six learners should be raised at a very high level. It was concluded that the high level of environmental stewardship practices of teachers would also increase the ecoliteracy skills of grade six learners.

items.title: Citizen science complements functional, taxonomic and spatial coverage of bird collections in the Pantanal, the world's largest tropical wetland
items.abstract: Species occurrence data are essential for understanding biodiversity patterns; however, the necessary fieldwork to generate them demands substantial resources and time. Citizen science programmes, such as birdwatching initiatives, can complement traditional sampling by expanding data collection. The Pantanal, one of the world's largest wetlands, hosts the highest avian diversity among such ecosystems and attracts intensive visitation by birdwatchers. However, scientific sampling in the region remains limited, leading to knowledge gaps. We analysed bird records from biological collections ( n = 5050) and citizen science observations ( n = 16 189) to examine the complementarity in taxonomic and functional diversity, as well as spatial and temporal coverage. The two datasets shared 318 species. Biological collections documented 62 exclusive species, whereas citizen science recorded 47 species found only in that source. Citizen science records captured a wider range of species traits but exhibited a slightly narrower distribution of traits than biological collections. Although both datasets occupy much of the same functional space, they remain complementary because each includes species with distinct traits. Records from both datasets concentrate in the northern Pantanal but show distinct spatial patterns. Citizen science provides approximately 2.4 times the spatial coverage of biological collections, with little spatial overlap between records from the two sources. However, the central and most of the boundary regions remain under‐sampled by either dataset. Both datasets negatively correlate with monthly flooded area extent, reflecting limited knowledge of avian diversity during flooding, when up to 80% of the Pantanal is submerged. Our results highlight that citizen science and biological collections can complement each other in capturing bird distribution, diversity and functional traits, which ultimately underpin ecosystem services at regional scales. Expanding similar integrative assessments across different ecoregions will improve biodiversity monitoring, refine conservation strategies and strengthen the value of citizen‐generated information in global ecological research.

items.title: Policy Integration in the Federal Governance of Food Security in Mexico
items.abstract: ABSTRACT This article analyzes the degree of public policy integration in the federal governance of food security in Mexico. Drawing on the policy integration framework proposed by Candel and Biesbroek, the study examines four key dimensions: (1) policy frame, (2) subsystem involvement, (3) policy goals, and (4) policy instruments. The analysis reveals a partial recognition of the multifunctional nature of food security, but this recognition does not translate into fully integrated policy design or implementation. Instead, food security interventions remain fragmented, concentrated within a limited number of institutions, and disproportionately focused on food utilization, to the detriment of availability and accessibility. Weak coordination across sectors and levels of government is further reinforced by a highly centralized financial architecture, which constrains policy coherence, limits instrument complementarity, and restricts the capacity of subnational actors to engage in coordinated action. Although many initiatives are formally aligned with national and international frameworks, implementation often remains rhetorical rather than operational. To address these limitations, the article argues for a shift toward polycentric governance supported by a reconfigured financial architecture and balanced policy instrument mixes. Finally, the study highlights the role of evaluation as a critical mechanism for advancing toward more integrated, coherent, and sustainable food security policies in Mexico. 摘要 本文分析了墨西哥在联邦层面治理粮食安全时的公共政策整合程度。基于Candel和Biesbroek提出的政策整合框架, 本研究考察了四个关键维度:(1)政策框架, (2)子系统参与, (3)政策目标, 以及(4)政策工具。分析表明, 尽管人们在一定程度上认识到了粮食安全的多功能性, 但这种认识并未转化为完全整合的政策设计或实施。相反, 粮食安全干预措施依然处于碎片化状态, 集中在少数几个机构手中, 且过度侧重于“粮食利用”环节, 从而忽视了“粮食供应”与“获取能力”方面的问题。高度集中的财政体制进一步加剧了跨部门及跨层级政府间协调不力的问题, 这不仅制约了政策的一致性与工具间的互补性, 还限制了地方主体开展协同行动的能力。尽管许多举措在形式上与国内及国际框架保持一致, 但在实际执行中往往流于形式, 缺乏实质性的操作落实。针对上述局限性, 本文主张转向多中心治理模式, 并辅以重构的财政体制与均衡的政策工具组合。最后, 本研究强调了评估机制的关键作用, 认为它是推动墨西哥建立更具整合性、一致性和可持续性的粮食安全政策体系的重要手段。

items.title: Uso del arbolado como sustrato de nidificación por la Cotorra (Myiopsitta monachus) en un parque urbano de Santiago de Chile
items.abstract: Las especies exóticas invasoras pueden generar impactos ecológicos, económicos y sanitarios, por lo que documentar su establecimiento en ambientes urbanos es relevante para su manejo. La Cotorra (Myiopsitta monachus) utiliza diversas especies arbóreas como soporte para sus estructuras comunales de nidificación. El objetivo de este estudio fue caracterizar los árboles ocupados y examinar la relación entre sus atributos estructurales y el número y ubicación vertical de dichas estructuras en el Parque O’Higgins, Santiago de Chile. Entre junio de 2023 y junio de 2024 se realizaron recorridos sistemáticos que cubrieron la totalidad del parque. En cada árbol ocupado se registraron su categoría taxonómica, altura, diámetro del tronco, número de estructuras y posiciones mínima y máxima. Se registraron 69 estructuras comunales de nidificación en 23 árboles. El número de estructuras presentó una relación negativa con el diámetro del tronco, sin detectarse asociación con la altura de los árboles. Cupressus sp. concentró aproximadamente la mitad de las estructuras registradas, seguido por Cedrus sp. y Araucaria sp., mientras que Eucalyptus sp. presentó una representación menor. Estos resultados concuerdan con estudios previos realizados en Santiago, que documentaron un uso predominante de árboles exóticos y valores similares de estructuras por árbol. Dado que no se cuantificó la disponibilidad de árboles, los resultados describen patrones de uso sin permitir inferir selección o preferencia por determinados sustratos. Este estudio proporciona una línea de base para futuras investigaciones sobre disponibilidad de sustratos, ocupación y dinámica reproductiva en ambientes urbanos.

items.title: Professional Roles of Agrochemical Dealers in Pest Management: Implications for IPM Adoption in Southeastern Anatolia, Türkiye
items.abstract: This study, conducted in Southeastern Anatolia in 2024, aimed to evaluate the communication and cooperation of plant protection product dealers with other agricultural actors, as well as their professional approaches. A survey was carried out with 131 randomly selected agrochemical dealers in Diyarbakır, Mardin, and Şanlıurfa. Results showed that 86% of dealers do not collaborate with any agricultural institution beyond official procedures. While 82% reported no deficiencies in identifying harmful organisms, 62% found plant protection product prices very expensive. The most sold products were insecticides (41%), followed by herbicides (39%) and fungicides (20%). Dealers stated that 65% of farmers lack knowledge about biological control, 45% about Integrated Pest Management (IPM) and early warning systems, and 34% about technical IPM support. Only 21% partially use early warning systems. While making pesticide recommendations, 85% of dealers prioritize registered products specific to pests, and 86% follow label dosages. Given the critical role of Agrochemical dealers in agricultural production, human health, and the environment, it is essential that they are professionally qualified and subject to effective monitoring to minimize potential economic and environmental risks. The findings indicate that agrochemical dealers function as de facto advisory actors rather than merely input suppliers, yet their limited integration with institutional IPM frameworks represents a critical bottleneck for sustainable pest management in the region.

items.title: Enhanced rock weathering for sustainable carbon capture: advances, challenges, and future prospects in terrestrial ecosystems
items.abstract: Abstract Enhanced Rock Weathering (ERW) is a carbon dioxide removal (CDR) strategy that accelerates mineral dissolution in terrestrial systems to draw down atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), with the potential for co-benefits across managed and natural ecosystems. This review evaluates ERW’s real-world effectiveness through the lens of measurable carbon fluxes and storage permanence. We synthesize evidence across geochemical kinetics, hydrology, mineralogy, particle size distributions, and biological mediation, showing that the wide range of reported field-scale carbon removal rates (approximately 0 to 9 t CO 2 per ha −1 yr −1 ) reflects diverse site-specific environmental conditions and complex geochemical, biological, and hydrological processes that cannot be explained by intrinsic mineral reactivity alone. Widely used proxies, such as total cation dissolutions, soil pH changes, or crop yield gains, are less reliable indicators of field-scale CDR than alkalinity export or cation mass balance. Furthermore, estimates of net CDR should account for both the efficiency of converting weathering products into durable carbonate storage and full lifecycle emissions. Lifecycle assessments consistently identify energy for grinding and logistics as the dominant sources of cost and emissions, implying an optimal particle fineness for maximizing net removal. A tiered appraisal of modeling approaches highlights remaining uncertainty across geochemical, ecohydrological, and socioeconomic processes in current models, with plausible 2050 deployment potential estimated at 0.2–4 Gt CO 2 yr −1 . We further assess environmental and social risks, including trace-metal accumulation, long-term soil health, and occupational hazards. We conclude by outlining a framework for credible scaling that integrates rigorous monitoring, multi-scale modeling, and precautionary governance. Under these conditions, ERW emerges not as a universal solution, but as a potentially meaningful component of a diversified carbon removal portfolio.

items.title: In vitro Micropropagation of Anacamptis laxiflora Growing Naturally in Elazığ Region
items.abstract: In this study, it was aimed to obtain tubers in vitro by using shoots obtained from the tubers of the Anacamptis laxiflora plant, which is under threat of extinction due to unconscious collection for salep production and whose micropropagation is intended, as an explant source. Murashige Skoog (MS) nutrient medium was used to obtain shoots from tubers. Shoots were obtained 45 days after the tubers were planted in MS nutrient medium after being sterilized by applying different concentrations of surface sterilizers for different periods of time and these shoots were observed for tuber formation by culturing in MS nutrient media containing two different concentrations of Benzyl Amino Purine (BAP) (0.5 mg L-1 and 1 mg L-1) and different concentrations and combinations of Naphthalene Acetic Acid (NAA), Picloram (P), Indole Acetic Acid (IAA), Indole Butyric Acid (IBA) and Dichlorophenoxy acetic acid (2,4D) plant growth regulators. As a result, a lump began to form after 30 days. The most effective concentration in terms of tuber formation was achieved with the combined use of 0.5 mg L-1 BAP and 0.5 mg L-1 NAA plant growth regulators, while the least effective plant growth regulators were 2,4D and IBA. The most important aspect that distinguishes this study from the limited number of micropropagation studies carried out with salep tubers in the literature is the use of shoots obtained from the tubers as an explant source and the observation of successful tuber regeneration as a result.

items.title: First total mitogenome of synanthropic Ctenolepisma lineatum (Fabricius, 1775): Insights into the mitophylogeny of Zygentoma
items.abstract: Zygentoma Börner, 1904 is an ancestral and species-poor insect order that includes several synanthropic taxa of ecological, economic, and public health importance. Despite this importance, knowledge of zygentoman distribution and diversity remains limited and geographically uneven, with available genetic data representing only a small portion of the order. In this study, a zygentoman specimen collected from Antalya, Türkiye, was examined using an integrative framework combining morphology, next-generation sequencing, complete mitochondrial genome characterization, total mitogenome and COX1 based phylogenetic reconstruction, and species delimitation methods to clarify the species identification. These analyses collectively supported the identification of the specimen as Ctenolepisma lineatum. The results confirm the occurrence of C. lineatum in Türkiye after a long period and emphasize the need for broader regional sampling and integrative taxonomic studies of the order, particularly in understudied regions. The newly generated mitogenome represents the first complete mitogenome of C. lineatum and shows the typical insect mitochondrial organization, consistent with the structurally conserved pattern observed in other zygentoman mitogenomes. However, despite this conserved mitogenomic structure, phylogenetic analyses revealed several polyphyletic genera, subfamilies and families, suggesting that current sampling remains insufficient to resolve phylogenetic relationships within the order and that some available records may require taxonomic reassessment.

items.title: Evaluating the Impact of Multiscale E‐Region Turbulence on HF Scintillation
items.abstract: Abstract Ionospheric scintillation driven by plasma irregularities disrupts radio propagation across frequencies from HF to L‐band. While phase‐screen methods dominate scintillation modeling, they can be inadequate in the E‐region where irregularity scales can be comparable to the radio wavelength or Fresnel scale and span orders of magnitude. Here we quantitatively evaluate scintillation with a new full‐wave methodology coupling particle‐in‐cell simulations of the gradient drift (GD) and Farley‐Buneman instabilities with finite‐difference time‐domain electromagnetic propagation. Using a frozen‐in approximation and spatial filtering, we evaluate the contributions of various turbulence scale sizes to HF (6–24 MHz) phase and amplitude scintillation. Long‐wavelength GD waves dominate the modeled amplitude scintillation through diffractive scattering, while Farley‐Buneman turbulence contributes negligibly. Amplitude spectra closely follow irregularities near the Fresnel scale, demonstrating a direct correspondence between scintillation and plasma structuring. These results demonstrate full‐wave scintillation modeling and provide a framework for investigating scintillation across a wide range of spatial scales.

items.title: Peripheral Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor Changes and Clinical Response to Electroconvulsive Therapy and Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation in Major Depressive Disorder: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a leading contributor to the global burden of disease, and a substantial proportion of patients experience inadequate responses to conventional treatments. Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), a key regulator of neuronal survival and synaptic plasticity, has been investigated as a potential biomarker of antidepressant response. However, its clinical relevance following brain stimulation remains uncertain. This systematic review evaluated changes in peripheral BDNF concentrations and their association with clinical outcomes following electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) and repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) in adults with MDD. The review followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines, and searches were conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE (Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online), PsycINFO, and LILACS (Latin America and the Caribbean Literature on Health Sciences). Study selection and data extraction were independently performed by two reviewers, with disagreements resolved through consensus or consultation with a third reviewer. Eleven studies met the eligibility criteria, including two randomized controlled trials and nine non-randomized investigations. Due to substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, a meta-analysis was not performed, and findings were synthesized narratively. Peripheral BDNF responses varied across interventions, biological matrices, and sampling intervals. While many studies reported increased serum or plasma BDNF following ECT, others documented substantial clinical improvement without corresponding biomarker changes. Evidence following rTMS was less consistent, with insufficient data to establish a reliable association between BDNF changes and antidepressant response. Overall, peripheral BDNF changes did not consistently parallel clinical improvement, and current evidence does not support their use as a standalone biomarker of antidepressant response. Further adequately powered studies with standardized biomarker measurements and longitudinal clinical assessments are warranted.

items.title: Bridging the Gap in Headache Care: Insights From the International Headache Society Survey in Nepal.
items.abstract: Background Headache disorders impose a substantial public health burden worldwide, with low- and middle-income countries like Nepal facing pronounced challenges due to limited healthcare infrastructure, inadequate provider training, and restricted access to essential treatments. Objective This study aimed to assess the current state of headache care in Nepal, focusing on the distribution and training of healthcare providers, access to medications, and socioeconomic factors that affect treatment adherence. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted as part of a multinational joint initiative by the International Headache Society and Middle East, North Africa and Asia Headache Group. Data were collected from 232 healthcare providers across Nepal using a survey questionnaire. Descriptive and comparative analyses assessed geographic disparities, medication accessibility, and provider preparedness. Results Most healthcare providers were concentrated in urban centers, with 80.2% reporting some form of training in headache care. However, training gaps persisted among rural and non-specialist providers. Overall, 72.0% of healthcare providers reported that their patients had to pay to access medications, while the median provider-estimated proportion of patients unable to afford medications was 40.0% (20.0%-60.0%). Access to migraine-specific therapies, such as triptans, topiramate, and amitriptyline, was substantially lower in rural areas. Providers in urban settings reported greater medication access and specialized care, while rural providers more frequently served younger, socioeconomically disadvantaged populations with limited treatment options. Conclusions This study highlights significant disparities in headache care delivery in Nepal, driven by geographic, economic, and educational barriers. Furthermore, financial and geographic barriers to effective headache treatment raise important concerns regarding health equity and patients' rights to appropriate relief from avoidable pain and disability. To bridge these gaps, national policies should prioritize structured headache training, ensure essential headache medications are included in public formularies, and deploy telemedicine-based models in underserved regions.

items.title: Creative cognition in frontotemporal dementia and brain health.
items.abstract: Creative cognition is central to human thought and is affected by brain disease. Recent findings by Altmayer and colleagues link creative impairment in frontotemporal dementia to rostral prefrontal functional differentiation. These findings motivate a framework for investigating network coordination, circuit physiology, experience-dependent plasticity, and bodily and social regulation in creativity and health.

items.title: Characterising the plasma metabolome following high intensity interval exercise in continuous and intermittent hypoxia in overweight individuals.
items.abstract: The aim of this work was to examine changes in the plasma metabolome in response to high-intensity interval exercise (HIIE) performed under three distinct hypoxia protocols. On separate days, 18 inactive individuals with overweight completed a HIIE protocol in randomised conditions: normoxia (N Ex -N Rec ), normobaric hypoxia (inspired O 2 fraction ∼0.14) during both the work and recovery (H Ex -H Rec ), normobaric hypoxia during recovery only (N Ex -H Rec ) and normobaric hypoxia during work only (H Ex -N Rec ). Venous blood samples were collected before and after each HIIE for metabolite analyses by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry and 1 H-nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy. Mean power output, averaged across the six work bouts, was lower in H Ex -H Rec compared to N Ex -N Rec , N Ex -H Rec and H Ex -N Rec (all P ≤ 0.009), with no differences (all P ≥ 0.11) between the other conditions. Arterial oxygen saturation was lower in H Ex -H Rec compared to other conditions (all P 0.37). The lactate to pyruvate ratio increased in all conditions, but did not differ between them. Free-fatty acid (FFA) classes (saturated, monounsaturated and polyunsaturated FFAs) showed consistent increases (all P < 0.001), while monounsaturated and saturated triacylglycerol (TAG) classes significantly decreased following HIIE (both P < 0.04). There were no condition × time interaction effects for any metabolites. HIIE significantly altered the concentration of glycolytic and TCA cycle intermediates, whilst concomitantly increasing FFA and decreasing TAG concentrations. Although hypoxia applied either continuously throughout HIIE or intermittently (work or recovery) during HIIE altered exercise performance and oxygen saturation, it had limited additional effect on metabolite concentrations.
