items.title: Effectiveness of Upfront Radiotherapy in Central Nervous System Germ Cell Tumors.
items.abstract: Background and purpose Radiotherapy (RT) is essential for curing central nervous system germ cell tumors (CNS-GCTs) except for pure mature teratoma (MT), but the optimal target volume, dose, and timing remain controversial. This study evaluated the benefit of upfront RT in CNS-GCTs. Materials and methods We reviewed CNS-GCT patients under 30-year-old treated from 2015 to 2023. Patients with pure germinomas (PG) received whole-ventricular irradiation (WVI) with tumor bed (TB) boost. Patients with malignant non-germinomatous germ cell tumor (MNGGCT) received WVI or whole-brain irradiation (WBI) with TB boost, with or without craniospinal irradiation (CSI), before or after platinum-etoposide-based chemotherapy (CTX). Serum alpha-fetoprotein and human chorionic gonadotropin levels guided diagnosis when histopathology was unavailable. Patients with MT were treated surgically. The primary endpoint was 5-year event-free survival (EFS); secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), neurocognitive outcomes, and endocrinopathy rates. Results Twenty-nine patients were analyzed: 13 PGs, 7 MNGGCTs with upfront RT, 7 MNGGCTs with upfront CTX, and 2 MTs. The median follow-up of these tumors was 6.0, 6.6, 3.7, and 10.3 years, respectively. PGs receiving upfront RT achieved 5-year EFS and OS of 100% and 100%, respectively. For MNGGCTs receiving upfront RT, 5-year EFS and OS was 85.7% and 85.7%, respectively; 1 patient died from post-treatment disease progression. MNGGCTs treated with upfront CTX had 5-year EFS and OS of 41.7% and 60.0%, respectively; 2 patients relapsed (1 died), and 1 died from treatment-related complications. Both MTs remained event-free over 6 years following surgery alone or with Gamma Knife radiosurgery. Conclusions Upfront RT provided excellent outcomes in PGs and may eliminate the need for CTX in those achieving complete response.

items.title: Optimizing cognitive and behavioural recovery after stroke: clinical integration of dietary supplements with a focus on ω-3 fatty acids.
items.abstract: Stroke remains a leading cause of long-term disability worldwide, with many survivors experiencing persistent cognitive and behavioural impairments despite advancements in acute management. Post-stroke neurorecovery is often incomplete, contributing to dementia, depression, and reduced quality of life, particularly in low- and middle-income settings where access to advanced rehabilitation and therapeutics is limited. This highlights an urgent need for accessible, adjunctive strategies that can enhance functional recovery. Emerging preclinical evidence indicates that dietary supplements can modulate key biological processes underlying neurorecovery, including neuroplasticity, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial function, and synaptic remodeling. In this narrative review, we examine the role of major classes of nutraceuticals such as omega-3 fatty acids, vitamins, minerals, polyphenols, and amino acids in supporting cognitive and behavioural recovery after stroke with particular emphasis on omega-3 fatty acids, given their central role in neuronal membrane integrity, lipid-mediated signaling, and resolution of inflammation. We integrate mechanistic insights with preclinical and clinical data explicitly highlighting that theoretical models and basic research demonstrate significant promise, while current clinical evidence remains heterogeneous and frequently inconclusive. We discuss how dietary supplementation might be strategically incorporated alongside conventional rehabilitation paradigms including physiotherapycognitive training, and pharmacotherapy. We further highlight emerging concepts such as the gut-brain axis, precision nutrition, and biomarker-guided interventions, which are shaping the future of personalized neurorehabilitation. Ultimately, while dietary supplements offer a promising, cost-effective and accessible adjunctive approach. their current clinical utility is constrained by mixed translational efficacy. Overcoming these limitations will require rigorous patient selection, optimized timing, and shift towards evidence-based personalized, multimodal strategies. This will be essential to fully harness their therapeutic potential in improving cognitive and behavioural outcomes in stroke recovery.

items.title: SHANK3 drives abnormal neurodevelopment in iPSC-derived 2D and 3D brain models of Phelan-McDermid Syndrome.
items.abstract: Phelan-McDermid Syndrome (PMDS) is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder caused by 22q13.3 deletion involving SHANK3. While SHANK3 is critical for synapses, its role in early human neurodevelopment remains elusive. Here, we generated induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived 2D neuronal cultures and 3D cerebral organoids from two twin Phelan-McDermid syndrome patients with a 1.7 Mb 22q13 deletion encompassing SHANK3 gene. PMDS organoids showed reduced volume due to impaired neural progenitor cells (NPCs) proliferation. PMDS NPCs exhibited biased differentiation with decreased excitatory neurons but increased GFAP + astroglia and GABAergic neurons. PMDS neurons displayed simplified morphology, reduced synapse density and diminished excitability. Importantly, lentiviral-mediated SHANK3 overexpression largely rescued these defects. Our findings identify SHANK3 as a key regulator of early neurodevelopment and provide mechanistic insights into PMDS pathogenesis.

items.title: The Separation-Distress Network as a Transdiagnostic Mechanism Linking Relational Adversity, Social Pain, and Psychopathology.
items.abstract: Relational trauma is a major contributor to the development of mental health disorders. This association likely reflects the social nature of humans and other mammals, whose survival depends on maintaining stable social bonds. When these bonds are threatened or disrupted, individuals experience social pain, a distress response mediated by the mammalian separation-distress network. During early development, this network is sensitive to maintaining proximity with caregivers, as independent survival is not yet possible. Converging evidence from ethology, psychodynamic and attachment theory, and social and affective neuroscience supports the function of this network. Because mammalian brains are inherently tuned to form social bonds, adverse relational experiences can disrupt socioemotional development and increase vulnerability to psychopathology. Neural substrates of separation distress include the anterior cingulate cortex, ventral septum, bed nucleus of the stria terminalis, dorsal preoptic area, dorsomedial thalamus, and periaqueductal gray, with endogenous opioids and glucocorticoids serving as key neurochemical modulators in the separation-distress response. Separation distress and adverse relational experiences also alter physiological systems implicated in psychopathology, including the HPA axis, autonomic nervous system activity, inflammation, and brain structure and connectivity. This paper argues that relational trauma and social pain are mediated by an evolutionarily conserved subcortical separation-distress network shared across predominantly mammalian species. Dysregulation of this network may represent one common mechanism underlying depression, social anxiety, suicidality, substance use disorders, borderline personality disorder, and other psychiatric conditions. Understanding the processes linking adverse relational experiences, separation-distress activation, and social pain may provide insights into the etiology and treatment of diverse disorders.

items.title: When Defense Becomes Compulsion: An Evolutionary and Circuit Framework for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.
items.abstract: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is characterized by intrusive thoughts and repetitive behaviors that are frequently organized around preventing potential harm. Although existing neurobiological models have focused on abnormalities in cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical circuits, habit formation, and cognitive control, they provide a less complete explanation for why compulsions preferentially take the form of precautionary actions. Here, we propose an evolutionary and circuit-level framework in which compulsive behavior is understood as a pathological dysregulation of neural systems that normally support adaptive defense. Integrating evidence from human studies with circuit-level findings from rodent studies, we organize defensive control into three sequential but interacting stages: threat appraisal, defensive action selection and execution, and post-defense safety assessment. During threat appraisal, abnormalities in sensory salience, threat valuation, contextual gating, and interoceptive processing may increase the salience or threat value of ambiguous cues. During action selection and execution, intolerance of uncertainty, impaired behavioral flexibility, corticostriatal dysfunction, and negative reinforcement may bias behavior toward premature and repetitive threat-reducing actions that can become increasingly habitual. Following defensive action, impaired outcome evaluation and safety-state updating may prevent successful actions from generating stable signals of safety or completion, allowing defensive responding to persist despite objective threat reduction. By organizing OCD-related circuitry according to when it contributes to defensive processing rather than solely where abnormalities occur, this framework integrates threat-based, corticostriatal, habit, and safety-learning accounts into a process-based model of how adaptive defense may transition into persistent compulsive behavior. This framework may help map stage-specific dysfunction onto symptom heterogeneity and guide more targeted interventions.

items.title: Examining the Relationship Between Regional Vulnerability and Psychotic-Like Experiences in Adolescents: The Potential Mediating Role of Cognition.
items.abstract: Background Psychotic-like experiences (PLEs) are subclinical hallucinations or unusual thought content that, when distressing or persistent, signal heightened risk for psychosis spectrum disorders and cognitive impairments. Methods We used data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study (N = ∼11,800) to examine if structural brain deviations toward neuropsychiatric disorders, quantified using disorder-specific Regional Vulnerability Indices (RVIs), were associated with distressing PLEs at age 13-14, and whether cognition mediated these relationships. Cortical and subcortical RVIs were calculated for schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, major depressive disorder, Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, metabolic disorder, and 22q11.2 deletion syndrome. Results Linear mixed-effects models revealed that higher cortical RVIs for schizophrenia, Alzheimer's disease, bipolar disorder, metabolic disorder, and Parkinson's disease-and all subcortical RVIs-were significantly associated with greater distressing PLE severity. Both cortical and subcortical RVIs were negatively associated with fluid and crystallized cognition, with subcortical RVIs showing the largest effects. Mediation analyses indicated that crystallized cognition, and to a lesser extent fluid cognition, mediated many RVI-distressing PLE relationships. Discussion These findings suggest that neuroanatomical differences confer risk for psychotic-like experiences partly through their impact on cognitive development. The results highlight RVIs as sensitive markers of distributed brain vulnerability in youth and suggest that cognitive function, particularly crystallized ability, is a potential pathway linking brain structural alterations to emerging psychotic symptoms.

items.title: Studying the pharmacological interaction of temozolomide chemotherapy with different antidepressant treatments in a rat glioblastoma model.
items.abstract: Purpose The present study evaluated the pharmacological interaction of temozolomide (TMZ) chemotherapy with 3 potential antidepressant treatments (cannabidiol, CBD; fluoxetine, FLX; metformin, MET) in a rat glioblastoma model with the objective of finding drug combinations to better treat the depressive symptoms observed in glioblastoma patients. Methods Adult male Fisher 344 rats were inoculated with syngeneic RG2 cells into the right striatum. Then, rats received the antitumoral drug (TMZ, 25 mg/kg) vs. its vehicle (C-group), and 3 h later, treated with CBD (30 mg/kg), FLX (10 mg/kg), MET (100 mg/kg) or vehicle (Veh-group) for 5 days. The forced-swim test was used to score antidepressant-like responses. Markers of treatment response were evaluated in brain samples (hippocampal neurogenesis) of the non-tumor-infiltrated hemisphere and in blood plasma (corticosterone and immune system cells). Results The main results showed that TMZ alone and/or in combination with different types of potential antidepressants (CBD, FLX, MET) did not alter behavioral performance assessed in the forced-swim test. The absence of behavioral effects, however, is not attributed to a lack of pharmacological effects of the specific drugs. TMZ treatment decreased body weight gain, reduced the number of hippocampal neural progenitors and diminished immune plasma markers, while CBD and FLX decreased plasma corticosterone. Conclusion In conjunction, our results did not support the hypothesis of a beneficial use of antidepressants as a combinational therapy with TMZ to attenuate the most associated comorbidity of glioblastoma, depression, at least in male rats with this specific model of experimentally induced glioblastoma.

items.title: Information, Mass, Energy Principles: A biophysical and ecological framework for understanding the brain.
items.abstract: The brain is a highly complex biological system whose structure, function, and evolution are constrained by material resources and energy availability, as any other natural system. Here, we extend the ecological Information-Mass-Energy (IME) framework (Peñuelas, 2024) to neuroscience. In contrast to purely computational models, we propose that the brain is an information-organizing system constrained by mass availability, energetic expenditure, and thermodynamic efficiency. Through comparative analyses across mammalian species, we identify a superlinear scaling relationship between white and grey matter volumes, alongside a positive association between white matter volume and inhibitory-control performance. This suggests that neural organization contribute to cognitive capacities beyond brain size alone. Integrating these findings with metabolic scaling principles, we propose that brain evolution involves trade-offs between increasing informational complexity and the material and energetic costs required to sustain it. Within this framework, we formulate testable hypotheses concerning how informational organization may scale with neural material and energetic expenditure. Furthermore, we introduce a quantitative disturbance-recovery model that incorporates carrying capacity, recovery rate, and disturbance magnitude and duration, generating testable predictions for neurological conditions such as stroke and neurodegeneration. By combining empirical scaling relationships with a mathematical framework for neural organization, energetic constraints, and resilience, the IME framework offers a novel biophysical and ecological perspective on brain evolution and function. This framework also provides a foundation for investigating energetically sustainable information processing in biological and artificial systems.

items.title: Fixed Dose Inferior Oblique Recession Has Self-Adjusting Effect.
items.abstract: Purpose This study aimed to determine the effect of a uniform dose of unilateral inferior oblique muscle (IO) recession on incomitant hypertropia. Design Retrospective consecutive case series. Subjects Thirty-three patients with incomitant hypertropia who underwent identical unilateral IO recession between June 2015 and June 2025. Methods Patients underwent unilateral IO recession by a single surgeon who reinserted the IO 4 mm posterior and 3 mm temporal to the temporal pole of the inferior rectus insertion. Hypertropia was measured in distant central and secondary gazes, and centrally at near. Surgical effects were evaluated by linear regression. Main outcome measures Postoperative hypertropia, incomitance, retreatment, and relationship of initial deviation to surgical effect. Results Mean patient age was 40±27 (standard deviation) years, and follow-up averaged 448±562 days. Twenty patients had superior oblique palsy. Mean hypertropia in central gaze decreased after IO recession from 8.8±7.9Δ to 1.2±2.9Δ, and in contralateral gaze from 17.0±9.6Δ to 2.1±3.6Δ. Mean preoperative horizontal incomitance decreased after IO recession from 13.7±8.4Δ to 2.4±4.1Δ. Mean vertical incomitance decreased from 6.8Δ to 2.0±4.4Δ. Surgical effect was proportionately greater with greater preoperative hypertropia, resulting on average in nearly ideal correction of all hypertropia at distance in central, ipsilateral, contralateral, as well as in near gazes. This effect generally eliminated incomitance. Three (9%) patients required additional strabismus treatment. Conclusions Fixed-dose IO recession corrects a wide range of incomitant hypertropia in a self-grading manner, achieving excellent effect for a wide range of hypertropia and incomitance.

items.title: Stroboscopic light stimulation in adults reporting depressive symptoms: Safety, tolerability, feasibility, and active-comparator development in a staged early-phase study.
items.abstract: Stroboscopic light stimulation (SLS) is a candidate non-pharmacological intervention that induces transient visual and affective experiences, with potential application in depression. Before efficacy testing, clinical development requires safety, tolerability, and feasibility data. We report a staged, single-site programme in adults reporting depressive symptoms. Study 1 tested 11 SLS parameter sets for safety and tolerability. Study 2 assessed whether an active comparator reduced subjective visual effects while preserving session context. Study 3 randomised 84 participants to four weekly supervised 31-minute sessions of strobe-emphasis or wash-emphasis SLS. In Study 1, 31 participants were analysed; no severe adverse reactions occurred, mean discomfort was low (0.49/10), and the highest session-level upper 80% confidence limit was 1.13/10, well below the prespecified threshold. Study 2 supported within-participant experiential separation between the two SLS configurations in healthy adults. In Study 3, endpoint data were available for 70/84 randomised participants (83.3%): 39/42 assigned to strobe-emphasis and 31/42 assigned to wash-emphasis. Discomfort remained low, with no serious SLS-attributable adverse events. Both configurations produced visual phenomenology in the Study 3 target sample, and the phenomenological separation observed during Study 2 was not reproduced between groups in Study 3. The comparison estimates differences between two active SLS configurations, rather than SLS versus no stimulation. Exploratory depressive-symptom estimates were imprecise, limited by differential endpoint availability, and should inform endpoint selection and subsequent trial design rather than efficacy. Overall, the programme supports further controlled evaluation of supervised SLS while identifying experiential separation, retention, masking, and endpoint selection as priorities for the next trial.

items.title: "Advancing Behavioral Neuroscience: New Tools and Techniques for Measuring Behavior".
items.abstract: Bridging neural activity and behavior remains a central challenge in neuroscience. Advances in quantitative behavioral measurement, automated tracking, machine learning, and multimodal recording now make it possible to characterize actions at spatial and temporal scales that were previously difficult to access. However, increased measurement capacity does not necessarily translate into better biological inference. New tools must be evaluated for measurement validity, reproducibility, robustness across experimental conditions, interpretability, and accessibility to other laboratories. This Special Issue of the Journal of Neuroscience Methods brings together methodological developments and applications spanning animal and human research, from temporal pattern analysis and automated behavioral phenotyping to integrated electrophysiological and neuroimaging approaches. Together, these contributions illustrate how transparent workflows, rigorous benchmarking, and integration of behavior with neural measurements can improve the study of brain-behavior relationships while exposing the limitations that still constrain generalization and mechanistic interpretation.

items.title: Comparisons of psychiatric diagnoses, medication prescription patterns, and psychiatric care utilization in first-degree relatives and spouses of individuals with and without Borderline Personality Disorder.
items.abstract: Objective Small-scale studies have shown that the next-of-kin of individuals with Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD) face elevated risk of symptoms of mental illness. Little is known about whether these increased symptoms correspond to psychiatric disorders. The aim of this study was to examine the risk of psychiatric disorders, use of psychotropic medication, and utilization of psychiatric care in the next-of-kin of individuals with BPD. Methods Individuals diagnosed with BPD in Sweden, from 2011-01-01 to 2022-12-31, were matched (1:3) by age and sex to individuals without BPD. The study and control cohorts comprised the first-degree relatives and spouses of individuals with BPD and matched controls (n = 24,769 vs n = 77,728). Cox proportional hazards and Poisson regression models assessed associations between having a next-of-kin with BPD and outcome measures during five years post index. Results After adjustment for potential confounders, the next-of-kin in the BPD cohort exhibited an increased risk of any of the included disorders (HR 2.08; 95% CI 1.94-2.24), as well as higher rates of psychiatric care utilization (IRR 2.21; 95% CI 2.13-2.29), including inpatient care (IRR 2.23; 95% CI 2.02-2.47), and psychotropic medication use (HR 1.75; 95% CI 1.65-1.85), compared with the next-of-kin in the control cohort. Conclusion In this nationwide study, the next-of-kin of individuals with BPD exhibited increased risk of psychiatric disorders, higher use of psychotropic medication, and greater utilization of psychiatric care. This study highlights the need of adequate care for individuals with BPD and emphasizes the importance of providing support to their next-of-kin.

items.title: Early self-regulation in context: Multidimensional organization of neonatal non-nutritive sucking and its association with subclinical maternal depressive traits.
items.abstract: From the very first days of life, infants' affective regulation unfolds within a dyadic co-regulatory system shaped by caregiver responsivity. In contexts of reduced maternal availability, such as maternal depressive states, infants may be required to compensate for diminished interpersonal regulation by increasingly relying on their internal resources. Neonatal non-nutritive sucking (NNS) represents one of the earliest spontaneously available regulatory behaviors, contributing to physiological and behavioral homeostasis from birth. However, it remains unclear whether its spontaneous organization is associated with early relational vulnerability indexed by maternal depressive symptoms. The present study aimed to characterize the spontaneous organization of NNS in a sample of newborns (N = 42) and to examine whether individual differences in NNS are associated with maternal postnatal depressive subclinical traits measured using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). Results from an exploratory principal component analysis indicated that neonatal sucking behavior was organized along two functional dimensions, reflecting overall sucking effort and behavioral activation, and the temporal organization of sucking bursts. Importantly, higher maternal depressive traits, though subclinical, were selectively associated with increased sucking effort, with infants of mothers reporting higher depressive traits showing more frequent and intense sucking, while no differences emerged for the organizational dimension. Overall, these findings suggest that individual differences in maternal depressive traits within the subclinical range may be associated with neonatal NNS effort, a precocious compensatory mobilization of regulatory resources, potentially serving both to support autonomous regulation and to elicit maternal engagement.

items.title: Consultant and trainee perspectives on endoscopic spine surgery training in Australia: A cross-sectional survey.
items.abstract: Background Endoscopic spine surgery (ESS) is expanding, but training access and educational preferences in Australia remain underexplored. We surveyed consultants and trainees/fellows to identify priorities for ESS education. Methods A 17-item cross-sectional online survey was circulated through an Endoscopic Spine Society of Australia (ESSA) professional group and an informal neurosurgical trainee network. Responses were summarised by cohort (consultants and trainees/fellows), and between-cohort comparisons were exploratory. Results Forty-five surgeons responded (27 consultants, 18 trainees/fellows); 35 (77.8%) were neurosurgical. Twenty-six consultants (96.3%) had performed ESS independently, whereas no trainee/fellow had done so. Lack of access to trained mentors (73.3%) and limited training/observation opportunities (71.1%) were the leading barriers. Support for curricular integration was high (mean 4.44/5). Cadaveric training (57.8%), live observation (55.6%), fellowship-style training (48.9%), and proctored cases (48.9%) were the most preferred formats. Most consultants (55.6%) viewed microscopic proficiency as beneficial but not mandatory; the most common trainee/fellow response (44.4%) was that ESS skills can be learned in parallel or independently. Most respondents in each cohort favoured starting training at or before Surgical Education and Training (SET) 1-3 (consultants 51.9%, trainees/fellows 66.7%), and 72.2% of trainees/fellows wished to learn both uniportal and biportal techniques equally. Conclusion Respondents, predominantly ESS-experienced consultants and neurosurgical trainees/fellows, identified mentorship and training opportunities as shared priorities and supported structured ESS education. Their preferences inform a proposed staged pathway combining early exposure, practical training, and supervised clinical experience, which requires evaluation in broader samples.

items.title: Trends in Antipsychotic Initiation and Use Among Adults With Dementia, 2016-2025: A Pharmacoepidemiologic Study Using the TriNetX Research Network.
items.abstract: To examine prescribing trends in prevalence and initiation of individual antipsychotics among a predominantly US-based cohort of adults with dementia from 2016 to 2025, with demographic stratification and formal trend analysis. Retrospective cohort study. This study used TriNetX Research Network data from 111 health care organizations. Adults aged ≥65 years with dementia between January 1, 2016 and December 31, 2025 were included; individuals with prior psychotic disorders were excluded. Eighteen Food and Drug Administration-approved antipsychotics, including 14 second-generation and 4 first-generation agents, were identified from electronic health record prescription data. Annual prevalence and initiation (proportion and rates) were calculated overall and by age, sex, and race. Joinpoint regression was used to estimate annual percent change (APC) and average APC in initiation. Among 950,573 patients with dementia (mean age, 82 years; 56.4% female), the prevalence of antipsychotic use increased from 2016 to 2025. Quetiapine and haloperidol were the most frequently used agents, increasing from 3605 to 18,432 and from 4745 to 15,829 per 100,000, respectively. Olanzapine prevalence increased from 1205 to 9264 per 100,000 patients. Initiation rates rose substantially, driven by select antipsychotics; quetiapine initiations increased nearly 5-fold, whereas olanzapine showed a steep increase (average APC, 30.51%; P < .001). Use was highest among individuals aged 75 to 84 years and varied by sex and race. Joinpoint analyses demonstrated late-period acceleration for several agents, including quetiapine, olanzapine, risperidone, and brexpiprazole. Antipsychotic use in dementia increased substantially over the past decade, driven primarily by rising initiation of selected agents. These findings highlight marked agent-specific and demographic heterogeneity in prescribing patterns and underscore the need for continued monitoring of antipsychotic use in this high-risk population.

items.title: Age and Neuroimmune Diseases.
items.abstract: With the aging population accelerating, age has become a core factor influencing the clinical phenotypes, treatment responses, and prognoses of neuroimmune diseases (NDs), including those affecting the central nervous system (CNS) and peripheral nervous system (PNS). This cross-disease review summarizes the shared and specific age-related characteristics of NDs, focusing on the pathological basis of immunosenescence and neurodegeneration underlying age-related ND progression. We extract the clinical manifestations, immune and neural mechanisms of elderly ND patients, and evaluate the challenges and individualized adjustment principles of therapeutic strategies for this population. We explore the age-related immune dysregulation features between NDs and other systemic autoimmune diseases (e.g., systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), type 1 diabetes (T1D)). This review aims to construct a cross-disease framework for the precision management of NDs in the aging era, identify research gaps and future directions, and emphasize age-adapted intervention strategies for optimizing the prognosis of elderly ND patients.

items.title: Antibacterial and pro-osteointegrative bioactive coatings on titanium implant surfaces for oromaxillofacial applications: a systematic review and bayesian network meta-analysis of preclinical studies.
items.abstract: Objectives Numerous preclinical studies have investigated bioactive coatings on titanium implant surfaces to enhance antibacterial and osteointegrative performance in oromaxillofacial applications. However, these studies employ heterogeneous experimental methods and biological outcomes, making it difficult to identify which coating strategies hold the greatest translational potential. This systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis (NMA) aimed to rank titanium coating strategies published over the last five years according to their biological performance, using a quantitative statistical framework. Materials and methods Nine coating categories of increasing compositional complexity, ranging from single-component (inorganic, organic, peptides/growth factors) to two-component and three-component formulations combining these classes with each other or with antibiotics, were compared across six biological outcomes in preclinical models. Inclusion criteria followed the PICOS framework for studies published between 2020 and 2025. Three databases were searched according to PRISMA 2020 and its NMA extension. Mean difference (MD) was used for outcomes on a common scale; ratio of means (RoM) when measurement units were heterogeneous. Treatment ranking was estimated using the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA). Study reporting quality and data completeness were assessed, and studies with insufficient quantitative data were excluded from the quantitative synthesis. Results Of 143 records identified, 59 met the inclusion criteria and 40 contributed to the quantitative synthesis. SUCRA rankings indicated that three-component hybrid coatings incorporating antibiotics achieved the highest antibacterial performance and osseointegration, while inorganic coatings functionalized with peptides or growth factors demonstrated superior osteogenic differentiation. Organic coatings combined with peptides or growth factors showed the greatest cell proliferation. Conclusions These findings provide the first evidence-based ranking of bioactive coating strategies for titanium implant surfaces, suggesting a potential advantage of multi-component formulations over single-agent approaches across biological outcomes. Clinical relevance The identified compositional complexity gradient may inform the rational design of future multifunctional coatings and help prioritize candidates for further preclinical and translational validation in oromaxillofacial applications.

items.title: Unleashing the potential of saturation-transfer MR fingerprinting (ST-MRF) in neuro-oncology: quantitative molecular CEST and MTC mapping.
items.abstract: Neuro-oncology biomarkers allow probing tissues beyond anatomical or relaxation contrast. However, new techniques are needed to achieve mechanistic elucidation and effective therapeutic interventions. Quantitative MRI techniques, such as T 1 , T 2 , diffusion, and perfusion imaging, provide insights into tumor biology, infiltration, microstructure, and hemodynamics, and have been implemented clinically, but are limited in probing cellular and molecular changes. Saturation transfer (ST) MRI methods, including magnetization transfer contrast (MTC) and chemical exchange saturation transfer (CEST), exhibit enhanced sensitivity to semisolid macromolecular content, mobile proteins, tissue metabolites, and acidosis. Despite these advantages, ST-MRI techniques typically have been qualitative or semi-quantitative, time-consuming, and impractical for clinical implementation. However, emerging ST-MR fingerprinting (ST-MRF) represents a significant analytical advancement by integrating RF saturation preparation into a pseudo-randomized MRF acquisition framework with a deep learning-based reconstruction. This approach enables simultaneous, clinically realistic, quantitative mapping of bulk water relaxation properties (e.g., T 1 and T 2 ), semisolid macromolecular parameters, and exchangeable solute dynamics (e.g., pool size ratios and exchange rates). We provide a comprehensive background, methodological principles, and evolving clinical applications of ST-MRF in neuro-oncology. We explore current advancements, strengths, limitations, and future possibilities for clinical translation into neuro-oncology workflows, including tumor characterization, treatment response monitoring, infiltration mapping, and biomarker development.

items.title: MORSE-PI: flexible and artefact-free image reconstruction for structural and functional QSM and other phase-critical imaging applications.
items.abstract: Purpose Phase imaging applications such as QSM are highly sensitive to noise amplifications, phase singularities, and other artefacts, particularly in challenging scenarios such as ultra-high field (7 T), under-sampled or single-echo acquisitions. We present a novel image reconstruction method, MORSE-PI, designed to produce high-SNR, artefact-free, and singularity-free phase images for both structural (SWI, QSM) and functional (fQSM) phase-based brain imaging. Methods MORSE-PI extends our previous approach, MORSE, by introducing a Virtual Reference Coil (VRC). The VRC is constructed as a linear combination of coil sensitivity maps, with correlations enhanced between coil elements using the noise covariance matrix. Such a VRC ensures robust signal support across the entire brain and is used to correct phase offsets in the MORSE-derived coil sensitivity estimates, resulting in artefact-free, high-SNR phase. Results Compared to GRAPPA with ASPIRE phase correction, MORSE-PI demonstrates greater robustness to artefacts such as noise amplification and aliasing, and shows improved reproducibility in structural imaging at both 3 T and 7 T. Unlike ESPIRiT and GRAPPA combined with adaptive coil combination methods, MORSE-PI yields singularity-free phase maps. MORSE-PI enables high-SNR reconstructions even for the most challenging scenarios, such as single-echo EPI at 7 T. Its efficient, containerised implementation using the Gadgetron framework supports deployment on the MRI scanner console during measurements. Conclusion MORSE-PI offers a flexible and computationally efficient solution for generating high-SNR, artefact- and singularity-free phase images in both single- and multi-echo GRE and EPI acquisitions. This makes it particularly well-suited for structural and functional QSM, as well as other phase-based MRI applications. Its robustness and rapid computational time facilitate efficient deployment on scanners across field strengths.

items.title: Burnout Among Professionals in ABA-Based Services in Brazil.
items.abstract: Purpose Burnout among professionals working in Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA)-based services has received increasing attention internationally; however, there is limited empirical data from low- and middle-income countries. This study aimed to describe the prevalence and characteristics of burnout among ABA professionals in Brazil and to examine how burnout indicators were distributed across professional and organizational characteristics within the sample. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted with ABA professionals working in different regions of Brazil. Participants completed the Maslach Burnout Inventory-Human Services Survey (MBI-HSS), together with a questionnaire covering demographic, professional, and work-related variables. Burnout was analyzed descriptively, with each dimension classified into low, moderate, and high categories using established cutoff scores, and distributions were examined across professional roles, age groups, academic backgrounds, salary ranges, and caseload. Results Burnout indicators were highly prevalent in this sample. High emotional exhaustion was identified in 77.4% of participants and low personal accomplishment (indicating greater burnout on that dimension) in 89.9%, whereas high depersonalization was less frequent (34.1%). Within this sample, the proportion of participants classified in the most severe category increased from behavior technicians to coordinators to supervisors across all three dimensions, and professionals managing more than 10 concurrent cases showed higher proportions of high depersonalization and low personal accomplishment. Categorical burnout distributions were similar across salary ranges. Conclusion These descriptive findings, which characterize the professionals surveyed rather than the Brazilian ABA workforce as a whole, point to the relevance of systemic and organizational responses to burnout in ABA services in Brazil. Improving working conditions, supervision quality, and support systems may contribute to better professional well-being and, consequently, to higher quality of care for individuals with autism.

items.title: Exclusive oscillator interactions generate globally coherent phase arrangements: insights from benchmark traveling salesman problems.
items.abstract: Various oscillatory phenomena are observed in nature. Oscillatory interactions can contribute to the self-organization of globally coherent relationships and may play important roles in information processing, control, and communication in biological systems. However, the mechanisms by which such relationships are generated remain unclear. This study used the traveling salesman problem, a classic combinatorial optimization problem, as a benchmark to investigate whether exclusive interactions between Kuramoto phase oscillators can generate globally coherent phase arrangements through self-organization. We assigned cities to individual oscillators and introduced mutual repulsive interactions based on inter-city distances and phase differences. Our analyses showed that the oscillators frequently converged to phase orders corresponding to the shortest tour, although two-cluster solutions were also observed for some distance sets. Even when two-cluster solutions emerged, adding a new oscillator at a sufficiently large distance from the existing oscillators markedly increased the probability of obtaining the shortest-tour solution. In a special case, convergence to the shortest tour was also successfully demonstrated in simulations with up to 50 oscillators. These findings suggest that exclusive oscillator interactions can generate globally coherent phase arrangements through self-organization and provide a simple framework for investigating biologically inspired collective dynamics. Although a precise mathematical understanding of these dynamics remains a subject for future investigation, the present framework provides a platform for exploring oscillator-based computation through self-organized phase dynamics.

items.title: TotalSpineSeg: automated whole-spine vertebral segmentation with high robustness to labeling errors.
items.abstract: Objectives To develop TotalSpineSeg, a robust tool for vertebrae and intervertebral disc instance segmentation, along with spinal cord and spinal canal segmentation, capable of processing any 3D medical image regardless of contrast, resolution, or field of view, while overcoming fusion and fragmentation errors common in standard segmentation. Materials and methods A two-stage cascaded deep learning model was trained on 1404 MRIs. To explicitly prevent errors where adjacent vertebrae merge or a single vertebra splits, the architecture employs a novel "odd/even" representation. The second stage is conditioned on an odd-intervertebral disc mask from the first stage to assign distinct semantic classes to alternating vertebrae, enforcing accurate separation between neighboring vertebrae. Finally, a landmark-based logic uses key anatomical points (C2-C3, C7-T1, T12-L1, and L5-S) to anchor sequential labeling, while a localizer-based strategy ensures accurate identification even in truncated, short field-of-view scans. Results Evaluation across diverse contrasts and pathologies yielded a vertebral identification rate of 96.22% on localizer MRI and generalized to CT scans with a 92.87% identification rate. For intervertebral disc instance labeling, where vertebral separation is not mandatory, both model stages attained 99% labeling accuracy with a mean positional L2 error of 1.55 mm, surpassing existing state-of-the-art methods. Conclusion TotalSpineSeg successfully generalizes to diverse 3D medical images, overcoming variations in contrast, resolution, and field of view. The proposed topological constraints effectively eliminate vertebral fusion and fragmentation errors, delivering a state-of-the-art identification rate for both vertebrae and intervertebral discs across MRI and CT modalities. Key points Question Can a topology-constrained framework overcome heterogeneous contrasts and resolution limits, including localizers, to ensure robust, automated vertebral and disc labeling? Findings TotalSpineSeg achieved a high identification rate across diverse contrasts, localizers, and CT, surpassing state-of-the-art methods by eliminating fusion and fragmentation errors. Clinical relevance TotalSpineSeg enables fully automated biomarker extraction from clinical scans, allowing precise assessment of stenosis, lesions, and atrophy against normative ranges.

items.title: Antibiotic Exposure and Treatment Outcomes in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma and Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: Purpose of review Systemic antibiotics may disrupt the gut and oral microbiome, potentially affecting anticancer treatment efficacy. Their prognostic relevance in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) and nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), particularly during immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based therapy or definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT), remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated associations between systemic antibiotic exposure around treatment initiation and oncologic outcomes. Methods PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched from January 2015 to March 28, 2026. Eligible studies included patients with HNSCC or NPC receiving ICI, definitive CRT, or chemo-immunotherapy and reporting overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), or objective response rate (ORR). Random-effects models pooled hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for OS and PFS; ORR was synthesized descriptively. Risk of bias was assessed, as appropriate, using ROBINS-I, ROBINS-E, RoB 2, or the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Results Eleven studies involving 6,293 patients were included; nine studies (4,507 patients) contributed to survival meta-analyses. Antibiotic exposure was associated with worse OS (HR 1.78, 95% CI 1.52-2.08) and PFS (HR 1.58, 95% CI 1.28-1.96). Associations were consistent in ICI-treated cohorts (OS HR 1.80, 95% CI 1.53-2.13; PFS HR 1.67, 95% CI 1.24-2.25) and CRT cohorts (OS HR 1.73, 95% CI 1.29-2.32; PFS HR 1.53, 95% CI 1.11-2.11). Heterogeneity was low-to-moderate for OS (I2=28.6%) and negligible for PFS (I2=0%). Leave-one-out analyses showed stable OS (HR range 1.76-1.86) and PFS estimates (1.58-1.63). Worse OS was observed for both 30-60-day pre-ICI exposure (HR 2.04, 95% CI 1.43-2.90) and concurrent/peri-treatment exposure (HR 1.74, 95% CI 1.49-2.04). ORR was descriptively lower in antibiotic-exposed patients. Most studies had serious/high risk of bias, primarily due to confounding by indication. Conclusions Systemic antibiotic exposure around treatment initiation is associated with inferior survival and response in HNSCC and NPC. However, predominantly observational evidence and substantial confounding preclude causal inference. Prospective microbiome-informed studies are needed.

items.title: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 2 in a North Indian endogamous community: clinical and genetic insights from multigenerational families.
items.abstract: Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 2 (SCA2) is an autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder caused by CAG repeat expansion in the ATXN2 gene. Endogamous populations may exhibit clustering of inherited disorders because of founder effects and restricted gene flow. This study aimed to characterize the clinical and genetic features of SCA2 in multigenerational Banjara families from North India. A total of 141 individuals from 23 multigenerational Banjara families were clinically evaluated. 55 clinically affected individuals and at-risk family members underwent molecular testing for ATXN2 CAG repeat expansions using flanking PCR followed by capillary electrophoresis. Clinical characteristics were summarized using descriptive statistics, and the relationship between CAG repeat length and age at onset was assessed by linear regression. Pathogenic ATXN2 CAG repeat expansions were identified in 39 of the 55 individuals who underwent genetic testing (70.9%), including 32 symptomatic individuals and seven asymptomatic carriers. The expanded alleles ranged from 33 to 48 CAG repeats (mean 41.6 ± 3.3). Gait ataxia was the most common presenting symptom. A significant inverse correlation was observed between CAG repeat length and age at onset (R² = 0.71, P < 0.0001). In this study, we found SCA2 across multiple multigenerational Banjara families from North India. The inverse relationship between ATXN2 CAG repeat length and age at onset was also observed in our cohort. The presence of asymptomatic carriers highlights the importance of early molecular diagnosis, family-based genetic counselling, and targeted screening in high-risk families.

items.title: GLP-1 receptor agonist use in patients with minor stroke is associated with lower risk of post-stroke dementia.
items.abstract: Background Minor ischemic stroke is associated with increased risks of post-stroke dementia independent of stroke recurrence, yet there are no guideline-recommended therapies targeted at cognitive outcomes. Glucagon-like peptide - 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have been shown to be associated with lower risk of dementia among diabetes patients; however, their effect on cognitive outcomes among minor stroke patients is largely unknown. Methods This retrospective cohort study used de-identified electronic health record data from the TriNetX US Collaborative Network (2016-2025). Adult patients with minor ischemic stroke (NIHSS ≤ 5 and non-disabling) were included. Patients with prior intracranial hemorrhage, mood disorders, anxiety disorders, cognitive impairment, or dementia were excluded. GLP-1RA use was defined as a prescription prior to or within 3 months of stroke diagnosis. After 1:1 propensity score matching on 75 baseline characteristics, outcomes were assessed over a 5 year follow-up using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. Results After propensity score matching, 1,425 patients per group were analyzed. Mean age was 60.7 years, with diabetes present in 92.7% and mean HbA1c of 8.7%. GLP-1RA use was associated with a 48% lower hazard of post-stroke dementia (3.4% vs. 7.0%, HR 0.52 [95% CI 0.37-0.74]) and a 31% lower hazard of other neurocognitive complaints (17.2% vs 25.6%, HR 0.69 [95% CI 0.59-0.81]) over 5 years. GLP-1RA use was also associated with reduced mortality (4.4% vs. 8.8%; HR 0.57 [95% CI 0.42-0.77]) and major ischemic stroke (1.5% vs. 2.7%; HR 0.59 [95% CI 0.35-1.01]). No significant difference in intracranial hemorrhage rates was observed. Conclusions Among this cohort of minor ischemic stroke patients mostly with concomitant diabetes, GLP-1RA use was associated with significantly reduced risks of post-stroke dementia and other neurocognitive complaints. These findings support prioritizing GLP-1RA use for diabetic patients who suffered minor ischemic stroke. Prospective trials are warranted to confirm causality and determine optimal implementation.

items.title: Two-stage spatiotemporal graph neural network framework for seizure onset zone localization.
items.abstract: Objective Accurate localization of the seizure onset zone (SOZ) is critical for the presurgical evaluation of drug-resistant epilepsy. Intracranial electroencephalography captures high-resolution seizure dynamics, but interpreting complex spatiotemporal patterns across implanted electrodes is clinically challenging. We propose a two-stage, uncertainty-aware framework for SOZ localization that integrates patient-specific seizure modeling with cross-patient probabilistic ranking to estimate the likelihood of each electrode belonging to the SOZ. Methods The framework was evaluated on a bi-institutional cohort of 36 patients (20 with good surgical outcome, 16 with poor surgical outcome), comprising 184 seizures. In the first stage, a patient-specific spatiotemporal graph neural network modeled seizure onset as a network-level transition using directed functional connectivity graphs derived from burst-integrated electrophysiological features. Trained solely to detect preictal-to-ictal transitions, this model generated electrode probability trajectories without SOZ supervision. In the second stage, these trajectories were summarized into interpretable descriptors and used to train a patient-agnostic classifier assigning SOZ likelihood scores to electrodes. Evaluation and hyperparameter optimization were performed using nested leave-one-patient-out cross-validation restricted to good outcome patients, ensuring strict patient-level separation between training, validation, and test data. Results Seizure onset detection was stable across patients, with comparable binary cross-entropy values between outcome groups (median = .495 vs. .438, p = .108). In good outcome patients, SOZ electrodes were prioritized among top-ranked contacts (area under the curve = .86 ± .06), with all patients exhibiting at least one SOZ electrode within the top positions. In poor outcome patients, predictions exhibited reduced spatial separability, lower likelihood magnitudes, and near-zero confidence gaps, reflecting attenuated model confidence. Significance This two-stage framework integrates spatial interactions, temporal dynamics, and probabilistic ranking within a pipeline. By providing graded SOZ likelihood estimates and uncertainty-aware prioritization, the approach is a decision-support tool to assist hypothesis refinement during presurgical evaluation rather than as a standalone diagnostic system.

items.title: SV2A PET imaging in Parkinson's disease and atypical parkinsonism: A systematic review of neuroimaging methodologies and regional findings.
items.abstract: BackgroundReduced presynaptic density, commonly referred to as synaptic loss, is an early and clinically relevant feature of parkinsonian disorders. The development of positron emission tomography (PET) radiotracers targeting synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2A (SV2A) has enabled in vivo quantification of synaptic density.ObjectivesThis systematic review examines neuroimaging methodologies and regional SV2A PET findings in Parkinson's disease (PD), progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), corticobasal degeneration (CBD), and multiple system atrophy (MSA).MethodsA systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines, including studies employing validated SV2A PET radiotracers to quantify synaptic density in parkinsonian populations. Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies (QUADAS)-2 tool. Substantial methodological heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis; findings were synthesized narratively.ResultsFourteen studies were included. In PD, the substantia nigra was the most affected region, with striatal involvement more prominent in advanced disease (>6 years duration). In PSP and CBD, synaptic loss was widespread, exceeded grey matter atrophy, and correlated with clinical severity and cognitive decline; longitudinal PSP data showed reductions of approximately 3-4% per year in frontal and caudate regions. In MSA, infratentorial involvement (cerebellum, pons, medulla) predominated, enabling diagnostic differentiation with high accuracy (AUC up to 0.99).ConclusionsSV2A PET reveals disease-specific patterns of reduced presynaptic availability, consistent with synaptic loss, across parkinsonian disorders, supporting its potential as a diagnostic and monitoring biomarker. Methodological harmonization and longitudinal multicenter studies are needed to establish clinical utility.

items.title: Feasible closed-loop stimulation for neural latent dynamics control
items.abstract: Modern neuroscience benefits from powerful computational and experimental methods for studying neural populations, including latent dynamics models that predict behavior with few dimensions. But despite their explanatory utility, latent factors are seldom targeted explicitly with experimental perturbations, leaving causal relationships to behavior and inferred dynamical landscapes untested. A promising solution is closed-loop, multi-channel optogenetic control, which, when paired with model predictions, could steer neural trajectories in real time—a feat impossible for traditional, hand-designed stimulation. However, because closed-loop latent control has not been demonstrated in vivo, the hardware and software requirements remain unclear—particularly the necessary stimulation dimensionality and how limited resources such as implant volume and bandwidth should be allocated between stimulation and recording capabilities. Preliminary experiments would thus help guide ongoing technological development. As large-scale exploration of these design spaces in vivo is prohibitively expensive, we conducted a high-throughput simulation survey using biophysically grounded spiking neural networks. We found that low-dimensional actuation is sufficient: in the reference configuration, ~20% of the stimulation channels achieved ~85% of peak control performance, far fewer than the number of neurons. Furthermore, allocating channels roughly equally between stimulation and recording optimized behavioral control, whereas pairing many electrodes with a single light source—the prevailing practice in experimental labs—performed poorly. Even without heavily optimizing modeling or control, we obtained >60% tracking error reduction and >90% evoked behavior accuracy on average for optimal channel counts. These results held across extensive parameter variations, suggesting that closed-loop latent control is feasible with accessible channel counts and establishing design principles for future tool development and in vivo experiments.

items.title: Amyloid deposition in carpal tunnel ligament in a p.Glu109Gln TTR variant carrier: is this enough to start treatment?
items.abstract: Hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTRv) is a rare, progressive and heterogeneous multisystem disease caused by pathogenic variants in the TTR gene. In the era of disease-modifying therapies, establishing the transition from presymptomatic carrier status to clinically manifest disease is crucial to enable timely treatment initiation. We report the longitudinal follow-up of a man carrying the heterozygous TTR p.Glu109Gln variant, identified because of a positive family history. For several years, routine and second-level neurological and cardiological investigations remained negative. When he developed carpal tunnel syndrome, he underwent carpal tunnel release, and histopathological examination of the transverse carpal ligament revealed Congo red-positive amyloid deposits with apple-green birefringence under polarised light. This finding prompted intensified surveillance, which subsequently demonstrated objective evidence of mildly impaired cardiovagal modulation, leading to treatment initiation with vutrisiran. Although neither carpal tunnel syndrome nor amyloid deposition alone can definitively establish ATTRv disease onset, amyloid deposition in the transverse carpal ligament may represent an early sentinel finding and should prompt close multidisciplinary surveillance to identify objective systemic involvement and support timely therapeutic intervention.

items.title: Genetic Structure of Harbour Seals Phoca vitulina vitulina Along the Coast of Norwegian Mainland: Implications for Management.
items.abstract: Alignment between biologically meaningful units and stock boundaries is one or the requirements for sustainable resource management. In Norway, harbour seals ( Phoca vitulina vitulina ) are managed at the county level and, when local populations are deemed sufficiently large to support harvesting, hunting is permitted under a quota corresponding to 5% of the counted individuals. An assessment of population structure along the entire Norwegian coastline based upon 16 microsatellites revealed significant overall differentiation ( F ST = 0.036, p < 0.001) consistent with a pattern of Isolation by Distance, in agreement with the estimated effective migration surface (EEMS). Pairwise differentiation among sampling sites challenged the current stock outline. Specifically, (a) geographically large counties (e.g., Finnmark, Nordland) could warrant subdivision into smaller management units, whereas (b) no differentiation was detected across the four south-eastern counties (Agder, Vestfold, Telemark and Østfold). Positive and statistically significant spatial autocorrelation detected at distances of 0-300 km invoked larger genetical similarity than expected by chance and agreed with the fine-grained population structure revealed by former tagging studies. The absence of evidence for recent bottleneck events suggests that populations remain at mutation-drift equilibrium.

items.title: Aniline Biodegradation and Nitrogen Removal by Salt-Tolerant Pseudomonas sp. H1: Performance and Potential Mechanisms of Catechol-Mediated Enhancement.
items.abstract: Industrial wastewater containing salts, nitrogen, and aromatic pollutants presents challenges for biological treatment. Although salt-tolerant microorganisms have shown potential for nitrogen removal and aromatic pollutant degradation, their functional versatility and the effects of co-substrates on pollutant biodegradation remain insufficiently understood. Here, we investigated the aniline degradation and nitrogen removal capabilities of salt-tolerant Pseudomonas sp. H1, with particular emphasis on catechol-mediated enhancement of aniline biodegradation. Strain H1 degraded only 9.11% of aniline (200 mg⋅L -1 ) within 60 h as sole substrate, but the degradation rate approached 100% within 24 h with catechol as co-substrate. Moreover, the strain tolerated high salinity (20-60 g⋅L -1 NaCl), achieving a maximum average NH 4 + -N removal rate of 10.98 mg⋅L -1 ⋅h -1 . Whole-genome sequencing, nitrogen balance analysis, and enzyme activity assays supported ammonium assimilation as an important nitrogen removal pathway. Transcriptomic analysis revealed differential expression of genes associated with antioxidant defense, carbon metabolism, and aromatic compound degradation under catechol-supplemented conditions, suggesting potential transcriptional responses associated with enhanced aniline biodegradation. These findings demonstrate that catechol supplementation can substantially improve aniline biodegradation by a salt-tolerant bacterium with nitrogen removal capability, providing a basis for the potential application of strain H1 in saline wastewater treatment.

items.title: Chromatin and transcriptional dynamics associated with seasonal growth across a latitudinal Cline in birch.
items.abstract: Introduction Seasonal growth-dormancy cycles determine the survival and distribution of trees, yet the chromatin and transcriptional changes associated with contrasting seasonal growth patterns in forest trees remain incompletely understood. Objectives In this study, we investigated chromatin regulation and transcriptional changes during seasonal growth in birch, focusing on changes that may link photoperiod responses to circadian regulation and bud-set. Methods We combined satellite-derived phenology from 96 Betula platyphylla (B. platyphylla) forest stands with a common-garden comparison of mid-latitude B. platyphylla and high-latitude B. pendula material established in 2008 and phenologically monitored from 2020. Seasonal buds were profiled across an annual cycle by RNA-seq and CUT&Tag for H3K4me3/H3K27me3. Diurnal RNA-seq across key months quantified circadian phase/amplitude changes. The contribution of BpREF6 to growth cessation and bud-set progression was investigated by assessing growth-cessation and bud-set progression under short-day conditions and profiling histone modifications in CRISPR/Cas9-edited B. platyphylla plants. Results Across natural stands, end-of-season timing and growing-season length were strongly associated with daylength, whereas temperature showed limited explanatory power for end of season (EOS). In the common garden, provenances shared similar bud break timing but differed markedly in bud set, consistent with photoperiod thresholds. Multi-omics analyses revealed extensive seasonal and between-provenance chromatin-state differences, with enriched REF6 motifs across chromatin states and pronounced divergence of BpREF6 expression during the transition to bud set. Network and diurnal analyses suggested that circadian- and photoperiod-related genes, including PRR5/PRR7, CCA1/LHY, TOC1, CO and FT, may participate in the BpREF6-associated regulatory network. bpref6 mutants showed accelerated bud-set progression and earlier observed growth cessation than control under short-day conditions, accompanied by an increased number of H3K27me3 peaks, lower H3K4me3 signals at the analyzed regions, and altered chromatin and transcriptional profiles at selected circadian-, photoperiod-, and growth cessation-related genes. Some transcriptional changes in bpref6 resembled those observed in high-latitude birch during bud-set. Because BpREF6 occupancy was not profiled by ChIP-seq, these chromatin and transcriptional changes cannot be assigned as direct BpREF6 effects or distinguished from indirect consequences of the mutation and altered developmental state. Conclusion Our findings reveal associations between photoperiod and seasonal phenology and identify BpREF6 as a chromatin-associated contributor to short-day-induced bud-set progression. The accompanying changes in histone modifications and circadian- and photoperiod-related transcriptional programs provide a framework for further investigating how chromatin regulation contributes to seasonal growth and latitude-associated growth cessation variation in birch.

items.title: Detection and characterization of RNA viruses in ticks of the genus Amblyomma Koch, 1844 (Arachnida: Acari: Ixodidae) from the Brazilian Amazon reveals a putative novel virus.
items.abstract: Ticks are among the major vectors of infectious agents to humans. These arthropods are known to transmit a complex of encephalitis-causing viruses responsible for severe acute and chronic neurological infections in both animals and humans. This study aimed to investigate the RNA virus of Amblyomma cajennense s.s. and Amblyomma geayi ticks collected in various municipalities within the state of Pará, in the Brazilian Amazon, using a viral RNA metagenomics approach. A total of 12 viral sequences were identified, distributed across four families: Chuviridae (n = 1), Rhabdoviridae (n = 7), Orthototiviridae (n = 1), and Partitiviridae (n = 3). Among the detected viruses, Geayi mivirus, identified in Amblyomma geayi, represents a possible new virus described in this study, thereby expanding knowledge regarding RNA viruses associated with ticks of the genus Amblyomma in the Brazilian Amazon.This study presents a comprehensive characterization of RNA viruses from Amblyomma cajennense s.s. and Amblyomma geayi in the Brazilian Amazon. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first characterization of RNA viruses from A. geayi and the first report of members of the family Partitiviridae in A. cajennense s.s. in Brazil. Furthermore, a possible new virus, named Geayi mivirus, was identified in A. geayi. We highlight the underrepresentation of RNA viruses associated with Brazilian ticks in reference databases, underscoring the importance of expanding metagenomic surveillance.

items.title: Unlocking the unique effect of moisture content on compost humification during electric field-assisted aerobic composting.
items.abstract: The distinctive characteristics of electric field-assisted aerobic composting (EAC) render the initial moisture content recommended for conventional aerobic composting potentially non-generalizable to EAC, necessitating an investigation into the effects of different initial moisture contents on humification and compost maturity. In this study, within 50%-80% initial moisture, the peak current response generally increased with increasing moisture, while the 70% moisture treatment (EF-70) presented superior humification performance over other groups. EF-70 realized efficient oxygen utilization, a peak temperature of 74.7 ℃ and a 15-day high-temperature stage, achieving the highest HA/FA ratio (2.19) and germination index (144.71) with optimal humus accumulation and compost maturity. The excellent EAC performance of EF-70 was attributed to microenvironment optimization, directional functional microbial succession and enhanced microbial synergistic interactions, rather than increased microbial diversity, which effectively coupled organic matter degradation and humification. This study optimizes key EAC parameters and provides a feasible technical basis for the resource utilization of high-moisture organic wastes.

items.title: Molecular drivers governing the bioavailability of fermentation liquid carbon source: deciphering thermodynamics and molecular profiles of dissolved organic matter under pH regulation and thermal pretreatment.
items.abstract: Anaerobic fermentation liquid from organic solid wastes is a promising low-cost carbon source, yet conventional indicators (e.g., VFAs) fail to accurately reflect its biological availability. This study elucidated the molecular drivers governing the thermodynamics and molecular profiles of dissolved organic matter (DOM) by coupling 500 Da membrane fractionation with Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR MS). Analyses were performed across variable pH regulation (uncontrolled vs. pH 10) for different feedstocks (carbohydrate-rich vs. protein-rich). Alkaline fermentation of carbohydrate-rich feedstock promotes the release of highly oxidized small molecules, which significantly enhances VFAs production. For protein feedstock, the 500 Da membrane effectively rejected highly negative nominal oxidation state of carbon (NOSC) macromolecular skeletons, while enriching active high-NOSC molecules, driving the BOD 5 /COD ratio from 0.35 (SCOD 1000 ) to 0.69 (SCOD 500 ). It is worth noting that thermal pretreatment feedstock yield distinct thermodynamic pathways: carbohydrate-rich feedstock underwent caramelization induced dehydration condensation, forming aggregates with elevated modified aromaticity index (AI mod ) and the double bond equivalent (DBE), whereas protein-rich feedstock suffered intense reductive aliphatic polymerization via deamination, leading to a surge in molecular weight (MW) and a sharp reduction in NOSC to -1.05. Furthermore, a multidimensional cross-validation framework integrating molecular drivers factors (NOSC, AI mod , DBE, MW), excitation-emission matrix fluorescence spectroscopy, and BOD 5 /COD ratio was proposed to fractionate the DOM into bioavailable and recalcitrant molecular pools. This work provides a novel thermodynamic and molecular-fingerprinting foundation for the targeted and efficient reuse of fermentation liquid carbon source.

items.title: A decision support framework for climate-oriented coastal wetland restoration through process-based ecosystem modeling and optimization.
items.abstract: Wetland restoration is increasingly recognized as a nature-based climate solution, but effective planning requires balancing nonlinear ecological responses with economic and implementation constraints. We propose a conceptual and computational framework for climate-oriented coastal wetland restoration that embeds process-based ecosystem modeling within restoration optimization. Restoration strategies are represented as portfolios combining discrete choices among restoration measures with continuous decisions on implementation intensity and area allocation. A vertically resolved ecohydrological model simulates soil organic carbon dynamics and decomposition-driven CO 2 and CH 4 emissions, allowing environmental outcomes to arise from the interaction between restoration decisions and ecosystem processes. These emissions represent decomposition-driven source fluxes and do not constitute a complete net ecosystem greenhouse-gas balance. The optimization is performed using a genetic algorithm with multiple independent runs and provides approximate solutions without a formal guarantee of global optimality. The framework is illustrated through a benchmark analysis and an application to the Ebro Delta. The benchmark shows that alternative objective specifications select distinct interior and corner solutions from the same ecological trade-off. In the Ebro Delta application, imposing a budget constraint reallocates restored area from the deep-rooted vegetation type toward the less expensive shallow-rooted type, while maintaining high vegetation densities and compliance with the methane target, although the CO 2 target is exceeded. Global sensitivity analysis identifies the density and area allocation of the deep-rooted vegetation type as the main drivers of restoration performance. The results show that restoration outcomes depend not only on total vegetation cover but also on portfolio composition and implementation intensity. The proposed framework provides a flexible methodology for integrating process-based ecological models into restoration planning under alternative environmental objectives and resource constraints.

items.title: Hydrodynamic control on sediment quality, geochemistry and benthic foraminiferal ecosystem in a monsoon-dominated tropical estuary.
items.abstract: Tropical estuaries experience strong seasonal dynamic interactions among seasonal freshwater input, sediment transport, and estuarine mixing processes that regulate the distribution and retention of elements, sediment quality, and influence benthic ecological conditions. However, the relative influence of hydrodynamic and sedimentary processes on these interactions is poorly understood. Hence, this study investigates multi-seasonal hydrodynamic, sediment characteristics, sediment quality, and benthic foraminiferal assemblages in the wave-dominated tropical Devi estuary on the eastern continental margin of India. Surface sediment samples were collected from 13 fixed stations during Pre-South West Monsoon (PSWM), South West Monsoon (SWM), and North East Monsoon (NEM). The estuary remained sand-dominated, persistently under high dynamic energy conditions. Seasonal satellite imagery revealed marked morphodynamic variabilities in channel configuration and sandbar morphology, indicating active sediment redistribution. Elemental distributions show strong seasonal contrasts, with stronger fluvial input during SWM enhancing Fe and associated trace metals (Co, Cr, Ni, and Zn) through FeMn oxyhydroxide scavenging, while stronger marine influence during PSWM and NEM increases concentrations of Ca, Na, and Sr. Sediment quality indices indicate low contamination, negligible potential ecological risk, and a predominantly geogenic elemental source. Benthic foraminiferal assemblages show spatial zonation. Persistently low abundance and reduced diversity in the middle estuary are likely associated with strong sediment reworking and substrate instability. Occasional morphological abnormalities were observed in the region with high-energy conditions. Overall, the finding suggests that hydrodynamic forcing, sediment mobility, and substrate instability regulate elemental distribution and retention, sediment quality, and benthic ecology in the tropical estuarine environment.

items.title: Beyond catch location, individual fish traits add little predictive power for DDX and PCBs in Southern California sport fishes.
items.abstract: Legacy contaminants (DDX and PCBs) persist in fishes of the Southern California Bight, yet most consumption advisories rely on species- and region-level averages that ignore within-species variation among harvested individuals. We evaluated whether individual traits improve prediction of contaminant burden in a "fish in hand," and whether any gains can be achieved using information available to anglers at capture (e.g., size, region) versus traits requiring post-hoc laboratory analysis (e.g., age, stable-isotope-inferred trophic ecology). Using individually sampled, angler-caught fish collected across the Southern California Bight with associated metadata, we compared five nested predictive frameworks of increasing complexity, from species alone to models adding region, angler-measurable traits (length, lifestyle), spatially explicit sediment-contamination estimates, and laboratory-derived age and trophic-isotope metrics. Region - when informed by underlying sediment contaminant burden maps - substantially improved predictions of individual contaminant concentrations, whereas fish length contributed little additional predictive power. Among laboratory-assessed traits, isotope-derived trophic ecology provided the largest improvement, but gains were modest relative to location-based models. Overall, our results indicate limited potential for individual traits beyond catch location to meaningfully refine advisories, and support place-based guidance that leverages spatial contaminant prediction tools to inform safer consumption of recreationally caught fish.

items.title: Growth and physiological responses of Qingtian paddy-field carp and Xingguo red carp to different light intensities.
items.abstract: Light intensity is a key environmental factor influencing fish growth performance and visual physiological homeostasis. This study compared the 28-day responses of red and black Qingtian paddy-field carp (Cyprinus carpio var. qingtianensis; PF-carp) and pond-domesticated Xingguo red carp (C. carpio var. singuonensis; RCC) under three light intensities (500, 5,000, and 10,000 lx). Both PF-carp color morphs showed their highest growth rates at 10,000 lx, whereas RCC exhibited its highest weight gain at 5,000 lx. PF-carp displayed treatment-associated changes in retinal morphology and generally higher SOD and CAT activities and GSH contents than RCC under moderate and high light. At 10,000 lx, MDA levels were lower in PF-carp than in RCC. At 5,000 and 10,000 lx, PF-carp also showed higher expression of Hsp70 and TNF-α and lower expression of NPY than RCC (p < 0.05). Although the two PF-carp color morphs shared similar growth patterns, their retinal and antioxidant responses differed in some respects. These findings suggest differences in light responsiveness between the tested carp lineages and may inform further evaluation of lighting conditions in carp culture.
