items.title: Advances in in silico prediction of antivenom efficacy: assessing Instituto Butantan commercial antivenom against venoms from medically relevant Ecuadorian Bothrops snakes.
items.abstract: Snakebite envenoming remains a major public health problem in Latin America. Although antivenoms are produced by many Latin American manufacturers, their use in accidents involving heterologous snake species or from different geographic areas requires preclinical testing, typically conducted in experimental animals. Here, we assessed whether toxin-centered in silico analyses can predict antivenom efficacy by evaluating the performance of the Instituto Butantan Bothrops antivenom against venoms from medically relevant Ecuadorian Bothrops asper, B. atrox, and B. bilineatus. We combined transcriptome-guided proteomics, toxin phylogeny, AlphaFold-based structural modeling, and DiscoTope epitope mapping to compare Ecuadorian venom toxins with those in the immunization mixture used for antivenom production. Although toxin abundance and composition varied among venoms, most Ecuadorian toxins had close orthologs in the immunization mixture, and most predicted epitope residues were conserved or showed conservative substitutions, suggesting broad antibody recognition. Divergent toxins, particularly some PLA 2 s, PI-class SVMPs, SVSPs, and CTLs, showed non-conservative substitutions that could reduce antibody binding. Experimental validation supported these predictions: ELISA and Western blotting showed strong antivenom reactivity, while in vivo assays demonstrated complete neutralization of lethality and hemorrhagic activity, with partial limitations against B. asper myotoxicity and the defibrinogenating activity induced by B. asper and B. atrox. These findings indicate that epitope-focused in silico approaches can support antivenom efficacy assessment and guide antivenom improvement while reducing reliance on animal testing. Moreover, we demonstrated that the Instituto Butantan Bothrops antivenom effectively neutralizes the lethality and specific toxic activities of important medically relevant venoms from Bothrops snakes in Ecuador.

items.title: Milu antler powder demonstrates efficacy in mitigating kidney damage induced by the aging process through the modulation of intestinal microbiota.
items.abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance Aging significantly affects the structure and function of the kidney, leading to profound changes. Ancient texts document that deer antler powder can ameliorate renal damage and aging, but its exact mechanism of action remains unclear. Aim of study To evaluate the renal protective capabilities of Milu antler powder in senescent mice and elucidate its mechanism of action in alleviating renal injury. Materials and methods We prepared and conducted the ultramicro-grade Milu antler powder (UGM) and evaluated its effectiveness in improving kidney function in D-galactose-induced senescent mice through biochemical indices and histological studies. We then employed UPLC-MS/MS and 16S rRNA gene analysis to analyze the changes in intestinal microbiota and metabolites. Finally, the effects of UGM and its metabolites on the aging phenotype and renal function in mice were verified through fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) and cell experiments. Results UGM significantly ameliorated brain aging and immune decline in senescent mice. Notably, it significantly reduced renal structural damage and aging phenotype, and improved renal dysfunction. The 16S rRNA gene analysis and its metabolite analyses showed that UGM was able to upregulate Akkermansia, Lachnospiraceae_NK4A136_group and downregulate Desulfobacterota, as well as alter metabolite expression (especially sodium acetate). Furthermore, through FMT and HK-2 cell experiments, we confirmed that Milu antler powder was able to attenuate renal aging by modulating the intestinal microbiota and their metabolites (sodium acetate). Conclusions This study provides a scientific basis for the anti-aging application of Milu antler powder by demonstrating its ability to attenuate renal aging through modulation of the gut-kidney axis.

items.title: Plasma proteomic profiling reveals mediating proteins and preventive targets linking ambient air pollution to type 2 diabetes incidence: a prospective cohort study.
items.abstract: Ambient air pollution has been associated with type 2 diabetes (T2D), but the underlying biological mechanisms remain poorly understood. We included 44,917 participants with 2,911 plasma proteins from a large prospective cohort and followed them for incident T2D. Long-term PM 2.5 , NO 2 , NO x , and SO 2 exposures were estimated via bilinear interpolation. Cox regressions assessed air pollutant-T2D associations. Elastic net regression identified air pollution-associated proteins and constructed a protein score. Mediation analyses identified top-mediating proteins. Functional and PPI analyses identified hub proteins. Druggability was screened using two drug databases, with binding potential evaluated by molecular docking across seven small-molecule databases. During 13.64 years of follow-up, 3,193 incident T2D cases occurred. Per IQR increase in PM 2.5 , NO 2 , NO x , and SO 2 was associated with 5%-14% higher T2D risk. We identified 187 proteins mediating the PM 2.5 -T2D association, 61 for NO 2 , 66 for NO x , and 14 for SO 2 . The protein score mediated 31.69% (PM 2.5 ), 18.06% (NO 2 ), 16.81% (NO x ), and 19.71% (SO 2 ) of the associations. Functional and PPI analyses revealed these proteins function through cytokine-cytokine receptor interactions, chemokine signaling, leukocyte migration, and inflammation-related pathways. We further identified 13 targeted proteins with approved drugs (4 in DrugBank, 4 in Therapeutic Target Database). Molecular docking indicated 5 have potential small-molecule binders. This study identified potential biological pathways and candidate mediators linking air pollution to T2D, particularly through inflammatory and immune-related pathways mediated by plasma proteins, and identified potential intervention targets, offering opportunities for drug repurposing and precise prevention.

items.title: PTSD is Associated with Advanced Epigenetic Age in 43,155 US Military Veterans.
items.abstract: Background Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) has been associated with advanced biological age in DNA methylation data, but results have been inconsistent. This study evaluated PTSD in association with epigenetic age in the largest cohort to date (by ∼20 fold). Methods Participants were 43,155 US Veterans (92.96% male) enrolled in the VA's Million Veteran Program, with VA electronic health record (EHR), self-report PTSD severity (n = 21,999), and DNA methylation and genotype data. PTSD diagnoses predated the blood draw for obtaining DNA by ≥ one year. Results PTSD diagnosis and symptom severity were associated with age-adjusted metrics of epigenetic age ("age residuals") per the Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, GrimAge, and DunedinPACE algorithms after multiple testing adjustment. PTSD severity showed the most consistent associations with epigenetic age residuals, ranging from up to ∼7 months (Horvath) to ∼2 years (GrimAge) advanced age and up to 16 days faster pace per year (DunedinPACE). The relationships between PTSD severity and GrimAge, PhenoAge, and DunedinPACE residuals were stronger among younger vs. older Veterans. PTSD was associated with all epigenetic age residuals in the European ancestry subgroup (n = 26,630), but fewer significant associations emerged in the African ancestry participants (n = 11,119). Associations were similar across male and female Veterans. Conclusions PTSD was associated with advanced epigenetic aging in the largest study to date to evaluate this question. Effects were generally small in magnitude, though meaningful when considering the personal and healthcare system impact of advanced aging in the large population of VA users with PTSD.

items.title: Statin Use and Age-related Macular Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Disease Outcomes.
items.abstract: Topic This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association between statin use and the prevalence, incidence, and progression of age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Clinical relevance AMD is a major cause of vision loss in older adults, many of whom receive statins for cardiovascular prevention. Methods We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library through October 2025 for randomized trials and cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies with comparators. We assessed risk of bias with tools appropriate to each design and pooled effect measures separately using random-effects models. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO. Results Twenty-eight studies included 1,918,120 participants. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) for the prevalence of any, early, and late AMD were 1.03 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.86-1.24), 1.10 (95% CI, 0.92-1.31), and 0.75 (95% CI, 0.46-1.25), respectively. For incidence of any AMD, the pooled hazard ratio (HR) was 1.04 (95% CI, 0.82-1.31) and the OR was 0.76 (95% CI, 0.43-1.34), with substantial heterogeneity. For neovascular AMD incidence, different study subsets suggested lower hazard (HR, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.60-0.85) and higher risk (risk ratio, 1.31; 95% CI, 1.18-1.44); the OR was inconclusive (0.93; 95% CI, 0.82-1.05). Progression evidence was limited and heterogeneous. Ten of 12 longitudinal nonrandomized studies had serious overall risk of bias. Conclusion The evidence was of very low certainty and insufficient to establish a protective or harmful effect of statins on AMD. These findings do not support prescribing statins specifically for AMD or discontinuing otherwise indicated therapy.

items.title: Liposomal delivery of triptolide fatty acid prodrugs with varied fatty acid chain lengths for breast cancer therapy.
items.abstract: Triptolide is a highly potent natural antitumor agent whose clinical translation has been limited by systemic toxicity, narrow therapeutic window, and insufficient formulation stability. To address these limitations from a formulation-oriented perspective, a liposomal platform based on fatty acid-conjugated triptolide prodrugs was developed to investigate how fatty acid chain length influences formulation and plasma conversion behavior. Triptolide was covalently linked to myristic (C14), palmitic (C16), stearic (C18), eicosanoic (C20), and behenic (C22) acids and subsequently formulated into liposomal systems using a thin-film hydration method. The physicochemical properties were characterized, and plasma conversion, cytotoxicity, local irritation, and in vivo antitumor activity were evaluated. The free TP-FA prodrugs and their corresponding liposomal formulations exhibited distinct plasma conversion profiles. At 48 h, free TP-SA, TP-EA, and TP-BA showed conversion percentages of 97.53%, 97.02%, and 97.21%, respectively, whereas the corresponding liposomal formulations showed conversion percentages of 90.96%, 80.31%, and 41.83%, respectively. The difference between the free and liposomal forms was more persistent for the longer-chain conjugates, although the relationship with fatty acid chain length was not strictly monotonic across all time points. Among the tested formulations, behenic acid-conjugated liposomes showed distinct plasma conversion behavior and were further evaluated in the local irritation and in vivo antitumor studies. These findings suggest that saturated fatty acid chain length represents one structural variable influencing the behavior of TP-FA liposomal formulations.

items.title: Combined exposure of copper and iron induces nerve damage in Caenorhabditis elegans through ROS-induced autophagy/mitophagy.
items.abstract: Copper (Cu) and iron (Fe) are essential trace elements that become biotoxic in excess. Their widespread coexistence in the environment poses a significant risk of co-exposure to human populations. This study aimed to elucidate the combined toxic effects and underlying mechanisms of Cu and Fe using Caenorhabditis elegans as a model organism. Our results demonstrated that combined exposure to Cu and Fe synergistically inhibited motor behaviors, including head thrashes and body bends, to a greater extent than individual metal exposures. Furthermore, this co-exposure exacerbated the degeneration of both dopaminergic (DAergic) and GABAergic neurons, revealing a potent synergistic neurotoxic effect. Mechanistic investigations indicated that the combined exposure group exhibited a significant increase in both cellular and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS), pointing to severe oxidative stress as a primary driver of toxicity. This oxidative stress led to profound mitochondrial damage, characterized by a reduced mitochondrial membrane potential and ultrastructural defects, such as rupture and cristae loss, as observed via transmission electron microscopy. Consequently, pathways for mitochondrial quality control and cellular clearance were activated, evidenced by the upregulation of PINK-1 (mitophagy), HSP-6 (mitochondrial stress), LGG-1 (autophagy), and the transcription factor HLH-30. Validation experiments using the antioxidant N-acetylcysteine (NAC) confirmed this mechanism. While NAC treatment effectively rescued neurodegeneration and motor deficits, it only partially mitigated the molecular damage in the co-exposure group, underscoring the severity of the synergistic interaction. In conclusion, our findings demonstrate that Cu and Fe co-exposure induces synergistic neurotoxicity mediated primarily by an oxidative stress-driven autophagy/mitophagy pathway.

items.title: Health impact and cost-effectiveness of delivering immunization services through mobile health and nutrition teams in hard-to-reach areas of Ethiopia.
items.abstract: Mobile Health and Nutrition Teams (MHNTs) represent one of the most prominent strategies to promote immunization equity and expand coverage in hard-to-reach areas of Ethiopia. Despite more than two decades of implementation, evidence on the health impact and cost-effectiveness of MHNT remains limited. This study therefore evaluates the cost-effectiveness and health impacts of MHNT-based immunization services in Afar and Somali regions. We estimated the incremental costs of MHNT immunization service delivery from the provider perspective, using facility-based immunization as a comparator in six districts. Cost data were collected using bottom-up, activity-based costing with primary data for the 2024 calendar year and reported in 2024 US$. Outcomes included additional vaccine doses delivered, zero-dose children reached, under-five deaths averted and Disability Adjusted Life Years (DALYs) averted. Under-five deaths and DALYs averted were modelled using the Lives Saved Tool based on vaccine coverage improvements attributable to MHNTs. The incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) was calculated and reported as cost per dose delivered, per zero-dose children reached, and per DALYs averted. Sensitivity analyses were conducted to assess the robustness of the results. The average annual incremental cost of immunization delivery through MHNT per district was $15,799 (including vaccines costs). MHNTs increased immunization coverage by 9.36 percentage point in selected districts. The incremental cost per dose was $2.31 excluding vaccine costs and $3.75 including vaccine costs. The incremental cost per zero-dose child reached was $129.32 (excluding vaccine costs). Immunization delivery through MHNTs in the selected districts was estimated to avert an additional 177 under-5 deaths. The ICER of delivering vaccines through MHNTs was $59.36 per DALYs averted. The sensitivity analysis showed that these results were robust over a range of uncertainties. Immunization delivery through MHNTs is impactful on immunization coverage and very cost-effective in hard-to-reach areas of Ethiopia.

items.title: Changes in childhood vaccination coverage and sociodemographic determinants across Nigerian states, 2018-2024.
items.abstract: Background Nigeria accounts for a substantial share of the world's zero-dose children and exhibits marked subnational disparities in childhood vaccination coverage. Although national estimates indicate modest gains in full vaccination, less is known about how vaccination outcomes and their determinants have changed across states over time, particularly following the COVID-19 pandemic. This study examines factors associated with changes in full vaccination coverage and zero-dose prevalence across Nigerian states between 2018 and 2024. Methods We conducted a repeated cross-sectional, state-level ecological analysis using data from the Nigeria Demographic and Health Surveys conducted in 2018 and 2024. Outcomes were full vaccination coverage and zero-dose prevalence among children aged 12-23 months. State-level sociodemographic, governance, and health system indicators were drawn from survey, administrative, and budget data. Ordinary least squares regression models assessed cross-sectional associations and relationships between changes in vaccination outcomes and explanatory variables over time. Results Mean full vaccination coverage increased from 33.0% in 2018 to 40.8% in 2024, while zero-dose prevalence rose from 14.1% to 24.2%. Geographic disparities persisted, with states experiencing high zero-dose prevalence in 2024 often showing the largest increases since 2018. Maternal education was consistently associated with higher full vaccination coverage and lower zero-dose prevalence. In 2024, higher state health budgets, greater trust in local government, and COVID-19-related service disruptions were associated with higher full vaccination coverage. Conclusions Despite modest national gains, zero-dose prevalence increased and disparities widened. Institutional factors appear increasingly important, underscoring the need for targeted, state-specific strategies to reach zero-dose children.

items.title: Immunogenicity and safety of two priming doses of an MF59-adjuvanted cell-based H5N8 influenza vaccine in healthy persons aged ≥18 years.
items.abstract: Background Increased transmission of avian influenza from animals to humans has elevated the risk of an H5 pandemic. Methods This phase 2, randomized, observer-blind, multi-center trial assessed the immunogenicity and safety of homologous priming with an MF59-adjuvanted, cell-based H5N8 A/Astrakhan/3212/2020 clade 2.3.4.4b vaccine (aH5N8c). We enrolled adults age ≥18 years, equally stratified into 18-64 (including a poultry-worker subset) and ≥65 year cohorts. Primary and secondary outcomes were homologous antibody responses against H5N8 measured in all participants by hemagglutination inhibition (HI) and in a subset by microneutralization (MN) assays on Days 1, 22, and 43. Solicited adverse events (AEs) were monitored for 7 days post-vaccination, with unsolicited AEs tracked throughout Day 43. Results 239 participants were vaccinated (18-64 years, n = 121; ≥65 years, n = 118). At Day 43 (21 days post second aH5N8c dose), geometric mean fold increases (GMFI) were 13.7 for the 18-64 cohort and 10.2 for the ≥65 cohort. HI seroconversion rates were 75.8% (95% CI 66.1-83.8%) for the 18-64 cohort and 71.0% (61.1-79.6%) for the ≥65 cohort. HI titers ≥1:40 were achieved in 75.8% (66.1-83.8%) and 73.0% (63.2-81.4%) of participants, respectively. MN seroconversion rates were 80.6% (68.6-89.6%) and 70.0% (56.8-81.2%), while MN titers ≥1:40 were 83.9% (72.3-92.0%) and 86.7% (75.4-94.1%), respectively. No notable differences in immune responses by poultry worker status were observed. Most solicited AEs were mild or moderate, resolving within 3 days. Unsolicited AEs were reported by 16.7% participants by Day 43. Conclusion These data support the use of the MF59-adjuvanted, cell-based monovalent H5N8 vaccine as a public health intervention against H5 influenza.

items.title: A rapid assessment of injecting drug use and HIV in Suva, Fiji.
items.abstract: Background Following a rapid increase in HIV notifications, the Government of Fiji declared an HIV outbreak in 2025 and an HIV emergency 2026. Unsafe injecting practices among people who inject drugs were identified as a major route of transmission. Despite this, little is known about drug use, injecting practices and HIV risk in Fiji. This study aimed to assess knowledge, attitudes, beliefs and practices related to injecting drug use and associated HIV risk to inform the public health response​. Methods Using a participatory action research framework and informed by rapid assessment methods, trained peers conducted semi-structured interviews with 56 people who inject drugs in Suva (March - April 2025). Participants were recruited using purposive sampling. Interviews were transcribed verbatim and data analyzed using iterative categorisation. Results Methamphetamine was the most reported drug injected by study participants. Almost half reported injecting the first time they used methamphetamine. Access to sterile injecting equipment was limited with all participants reporting receptive needle/syringe sharing. Participants reported routinely being injected by others, repeatedly reusing needle/syringes, often for long periods of time, and other unsafe injecting practices. Participants also described using blood drawn into the barrel of the syringe from the injection site to mix the drug (termed "koda", or in English, "raw"). Conclusions Needle/syringe scarcity, low knowledge about safer injecting, and unsafe injecting and drug preparation practices are increasing HIV risk in Fiji There is an urgent need to provide high coverage needle-syringe programs, implement peer-led interventions to improve awareness and reduce unsafe injecting practices.

items.title: Trends in cold-related injuries among patients experiencing homelessness across Ontario, 2018-2025: A retrospective population-based cohort study.
items.abstract: Objectives Prior research has demonstrated disparities in cold-related injuries among patients experiencing homelessness (PEH) compared to patients not experiencing homelessness (PNEH). We sought to assess regional variation in risks and evaluate trends following recent improvements to local homelessness winter services. Study design Retrospective cohort study using linked health administrative data from April 2018 to March 2025 METHODS: PEH were identified via a validated algorithm and frequency-matched 1:1 to PNEH on age, sex, and health region (LHIN). We observed emergency department (ED) visits for cold-related injury over the study period, estimating visit rate ratios (RR) across periods using modified Poisson regression. Results The final matched cohort included 1,312,078 ED visits representing 289,054 patients. PEH (n = 144,527) had significantly higher cold-related injury visit rates provincially (RR 12.4 [95% CI 10.4-14.7] and regionally (ranging from 6.22 [95% CI 2.61-14.85] to 32.30 [95% CI 5.47-190.70]). In 2024/2025, cold-related injury rates among PEH rose significantly province-wide (RR 1.36, 95% CI 1.12-1.65) and in the City of Toronto (RR 1.46, 95% CI 1.21-1.76). Regional increases were significant in six of 14 health regions. Conclusion There is strong variation in disparities in cold-related injuries between PEH and frequency matched PNEH. Despite improved homelessness winter programming in certain regions, disparities worsened across Ontario in 2024/2025. Stronger government and community responses to unsheltered homelessness are required to address such exposure-related outcomes.

items.title: The landscape and characteristics of LGBTQ+ community-controlled organisations delivering mental health and alcohol or other drug services in Australia.
items.abstract: Objective Lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer/questioning (LGBTQ+) people experience disproportionate mental health and alcohol and other drug (AOD) burdens and have distinct care needs, yet limited evidence on the characteristics of LGBTQ+ community-controlled organisations constrains optimal service design and delivery. This study aimed to map the landscape of LGBTQ+ community-controlled mental health and AOD organisations that provide mental health and AOD services across Australia. Methods A mixed-methods study involved 16 LGBTQ+ community-controlled organisations, using an online cross-sectional survey and semi-structured interviews. Descriptive and content analyses examined organisational characteristics and service provision. A common practice elements approach integrated both data sources to identify shared organisational and service elements. Results Organisations varied substantially in size, workforce composition, and service models. All organisations provided mental health services, and nine provided AOD services. Eight common practice elements were identified: LGBTQ+ governance and infrastructure, embedded community responsiveness, integrated holistic services, collaborative partnerships, community building, foundational knowledge, relational practice, and safety-oriented approaches. Conclusions LGBTQ+ community-controlled organisations provide essential, contextually safe mental health and AOD services and operate through distinctive yet commonly shared practices. Implications for public health Workforce development and integration with mainstream systems are critical to sustain LGBTQ+ community-controlled organisations and meet growing community demand for inclusive care.

items.title: Establishing First Nations governed health commissioning agencies: Innovations from northeast Australia.
items.abstract: Objective Commissioning health services for First Nations populations has evolved with the creation of independent bodies that are more responsive to community need. This paper provides a case study of the enabling environment required to establish the Cape and Torres Health Commissioning Ltd (CaTHC), an independent First Nations entity in northeast Australia. Methods Qualitative semi-structured interviews and workshops with reform stakeholders (n=48) were combined with program documents (n=148), to examine the organisational structure and governance, policy and funding changes, and the data systems and accountability frameworks required to operationalise CaTHC. Results Application of policy diffusion theory indicates that CaTHC was strongly influenced by health commissioning models in Australia and Aotearoa/New Zealand. Developing each component involved clear tensions between what First Nations stakeholders viewed as important and the standards that governments require. Conclusions CaTHC aims to embed First Nations community priorities in health service planning and purchasing to improve outcomes for the regional population. Adequate resources, supportive policy and systems change, and flexibility to innovate are required for success. Implications for public health With access to stable funding and increased capacity CaTHC could address challenges in the service market, leading to improvements in health system performance and healthcare outcomes aligned with end-user needs.

items.title: Integrated Prenatal Cardiopulmonary Assessment Using Fetal Echocardiography in Isolated Left-Sided Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia.
items.abstract: Objective Prenatal severity assessment in congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) primarily relies on lung-based parameters such as the observed-to-expected lung-to-head ratio (o/eLHR) and liver position; however, these markers do not fully reflect fetal cardiopulmonary adaptation. We investigated the prognostic significance of fetal echocardiographic parameters and integrated these in prenatal prediction models in left-sided CDH. Methods This nationwide multicenter retrospective study included fetuses with prenatally diagnosed isolated left-sided CDH. Gestational age-adjusted Z-scores were generated for fetal cardiac dimensions. Receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed to evaluate prognostic performance for survival. Results A total of 363 fetuses were included, with an overall survival rate of 74.9%. Non-survivors demonstrated significantly smaller right pulmonary artery and mitral valve dimensions than survivors. Among fetal echocardiographic parameters, the mitral-to-tricuspid valve ratio (MTR) demonstrated the strongest predictive performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.77. In fetuses evaluated at ≤ 29 weeks' gestation, an exploratory model combining MTR with o/eLHR and liver-up status achieved an apparent AUC of 0.827. Conclusion Fetal echocardiographic parameters were associated with survival in CDH. Integrated prenatal cardiopulmonary assessment incorporating MTR may provide complementary prognostic information although independent external validation is required.

items.title: Australian perspectives towards genomics informed risk-based cancer screening programs: a focus group study.
items.abstract: Background Predictions of cancer risk based on genomic data (polygenic risk scores) can stratify a population into different risk groups, allowing risk-tailored cancer screening programs. While such approaches are generally viewed as acceptable, there remain gaps in understanding Australian perceptions to guide implementation of future cancer control programs and policies. This project aimed to explore Australians' views on using genomic information to tailor cancer screening and how such programs could be implemented. Methods Four focus groups (n = 28) were held using a discussion guide that explored key features at each stage of potential programs: deciding to take the test, completing the test, receiving the results, and the subsequent impact on screening. Reflexive thematic analysis was used to identify, code and report themes. Results Three central themes emerged: (1) The value of knowing, which reflected motivations to test for personal as well as family and social benefits; (2) Navigating the complexity of genomics, highlighting challenges in understanding potential pre-test information and results; and (3) Trust in testing, providers, and government which influenced program acceptability for the initial genomic testing. However, this trust may not always result in participants following subsequent cancer screening recommendations. Conclusion Our study identifies the need for community education and clear communication about genomics-informed risk-tailored cancer screening. Potential screening programs should consider the role of healthcare professionals and ensure they receive appropriate training to meet public needs. Further research should explore potential adherence to risk-tailored screening recommendations.

items.title: Long COVID: A Modified Delphi Consensus on Definition, Burden, Diagnosis and Management in Southeast Asia.
items.abstract: Introduction Long COVID is a heterogeneous post-infectious condition following acute severe acute respiratory syndrome-coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection. Ongoing uncertainty around its definition, burden, diagnosis and management complicates clinical recognition and care in Southeast Asia. Methods A modified Delphi consensus study was conducted with twelve experts from six Southeast Asian countries to develop regional guidance on long COVID. Consensus was predefined as ≥ 80% agreement, corresponding to at least 10 of 12 experts selecting the same response in multiple-choice questions or indicating agreement on Likert-scale questions (e.g. agree/strongly agree, most important/more important, relevant/highly relevant). Questions that reached consensus were removed from the subsequent round, while unresolved questions were revised, consolidated, or expanded. In the final round, a post hoc descriptive category, 'moderate endorsement', was applied to Likert-scale questions that had not reached consensus, with 'important' as the midpoint category of the five-point importance scale ('most important' to 'least important'), to capture responses judged important but falling short of the consensus threshold. Results Consensus was reached for all 'definition', 'burden' and 'management' theme questions and most 'diagnosis' questions. Experts defined long COVID as unexplained symptoms persisting for > 3 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection, distinct from post-acute COVID-19, with no minimum severity threshold requirement. Long COVID was recognised as affecting approximately 6%-10% of individuals after SARS-CoV-2 infection, consistent with published WHO and KSID estimates; clinical evaluation and symptom-guided testing were recommended for its diagnosis. Hospitalisation during acute COVID-19 was identified as a risk factor for developing long COVID. The experts recommended multidisciplinary, symptom-directed care, rehabilitation, pacing and follow-up. Vaccination and reinfection prevention were supported as important long COVID risk-reduction strategies, and early antiviral treatment should be considered to prevent severe acute illness and hospitalisation in high-risk individuals. Consensus was not reached on the past medical history required for diagnosis; moderate endorsement was observed for booster status, absence of early antiviral treatment, pre-COVID health assessment and standardised patient-reported outcome tools. Conclusion This Delphi study provides a practical regional consensus framework for long COVID in Southeast Asia.

items.title: Development and initial content validation of the Vienna post-exertional malaise questionnaire: an iterative mixed-methods study.
items.abstract: Objectives Post-exertional malaise (PEM) is a multidimensional exertion-response pattern involving diverse triggers, variable onset, and prolonged recovery. This study developed and content-validated the Vienna Post-Exertional Malaise (VPEM) Questionnaire, a patient-reported outcome measure assessing functional decline, recovery, crash-associated symptoms, and pacing adaptations in ME/CFS. Methods An iterative mixed-methods instrument-development study combined quantitative ratings and qualitative feedback across sequential evaluation cycles. An initial 13-item draft, informed by existing PEM, fatigue, and functional-capacity instruments and consensus literature, was evaluated by individuals with ME/CFS or Post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCS) using Likert ratings, open-ended feedback, and interviews. Quantitative data were summarised descriptively, and qualitative data were analysed using deductive-inductive structuring content analysis. Revisions were documented in revision matrices. The revised instrument was evaluated by an interdisciplinary expert panel using domain-level and item-level ratings of relevance and clarity. Results Twelve individuals with ME/CFS and one individual with PCS fulfilling ME/CFS criteria evaluated the questionnaire. Ratings showed high approval for length (92.3%) and terminology (76.9%), while completeness and clarity were more heterogeneous. Qualitative findings identified ambiguities in distinguishing PEM from non-specific fatigue, missing trigger domains, and insufficient representation of intra-individual variability. After revision, the expert panel (n = 11) rated PEM coverage as complete or largely complete (100%) and the multidimensional structure as suitable or very suitable (90.9%). Item-level ratings showed high relevance (S-CVI/Ave = 0.96), whereas clarity ratings were more variable (S-CVI/Ave = 0.82). Conclusions The VPEM Questionnaire operationalises PEM as multidimensional post-exertional deterioration. Findings support initial content and face validity, warranting further psychometric validation.

items.title: Bioinformatic analysis of ACAD9 genetic variability.
items.abstract: Mitochondrial diseases (MD) are a heterogeneous group of disorders with a diagnostic rate often below 50%, mostly due to the difficulty of interpreting Variants of Unknown Significance (VUS). ACAD9 is a nuclear gene that encodes a mitochondrial protein involved in fatty acid β-oxidation and the assembly of respiratory complex I. This study aimed to refine the classification of ACAD9 missense VUS through an integrative computational approach combining in silico, evolutionary and structural analysis. A gene-specific dataset of missense pathogenic, benign and uncertain significance variants was curated from public databases (HGMD, ClinVar, GnomAD, UniProt or LOVD) and in-house sequencing data. Thirty-five in silico pathogenicity predictors were retrieved from the dbNSFP v5.3 and benchmarked using the datasets. Predictor performance was evaluated using 10 metrics and the top predictors were integrated with evolutionary conservation (ConSurf), structural modelling (PyMOL, HOPE) and thermodynamic stability analysis (FoldX) to re-evaluate 17 VUS. Predictor performance for ACAD9 variants varied significantly. Because no statistically significant differences were detected among the ten highest-ranked predictors, ClinPred, MetaRNN, PHACTboost, MutationTaster and REVEL were selected as the top stability-informed predictors. The integrative predictive and structural analysis reclassified 8 variants as "likely pathogenic" and 5 as "likely benign", while 4 remained classified as VUS due to conflicting evidence. A gene-specific, multi-layered computational strategy substantially improves VUS classification in ACAD9. These in silico findings provide strong, albeit non-definitive, evidence to guide diagnostic efforts. It should be complemented with functional validation, which remains essential to confirm pathogenicity.

items.title: Systolic pressure gradient across myocardial bridge mediates the effect of bridge depth on clinical symptoms.
items.abstract: The relationship between myocardial bridging (MB) morphology and function and the pathways to clinical symptoms remained unclear. This study investigated the association between delta coronary computed tomographic angiography-derived fractional flow reserve (ΔCT-FFR) and angina-equivalent symptoms in left anterior descending MB without coronary atherosclerosis using photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT). This retrospective cohort included 180 patients with deep MB (depth > 2 mm) and no plaques. All underwent PCD-CT angiography. CT-FFR was computed by machine learning; systolic (ΔCT-FFRsys) and diastolic (ΔCT-FFRdia) trans-bridge pressure gradients were derived. MB depth and length were measured. Associations with symptoms were assessed by logistic regression and mediation analysis. Symptomatic patients (n = 81) had greater depth (median 3.30 mm vs. 2.45 mm), longer length (mean 36.06 mm vs. 26.10 mm), higher ΔCT-FFRsys (3.81% vs. 1.62%) and ΔCT-FFRdia (3.45% vs. 2.15%) than asymptomatic patients (n = 99) (all p < 0.001). Multivariable analysis identified depth (OR = 1.77, 95% CI: 1.27-2.46, p = 0.001) and ΔCT-FFRsys (OR = 1.16, 95% CI: 1.05-1.27, p = 0.002) as independent predictors. Mediation analysis indicated that ΔCT-FFRsys significantly mediated the effect of depth on symptoms (indirect effect = 0.1881, 95% CI: 0.1023-0.2897). MB depth and ΔCT-FFRsys were independent risk factors for symptoms, and ΔCT-FFRsys appeared to mediate the morphological-clinical symptoms link. These findings suggested that integrated assessment, particularly ΔCT-FFRsys, might be a new non-invasive imaging biomarker for clinically identify symptomatic MB and understand its potential pathogenic mechanisms. Question The precise relationship between myocardial bridging morphological and functional features and clinical symptoms, and whether underlying key mediating factors exist, remains currently incompletely determined. Findings Depth, length, and systolic trans-bridge pressure gradient of myocardial bridging independently predicted symptoms, with the gradient significantly mediating the relationship between morphology and clinical presentation. Clinical relevance Noninvasive assessment of depth and systolic trans-bridge pressure gradient can assist in identifying patients with symptomatic myocardial bridging, serving as potential imaging biomarkers and providing insights into the underlying pathophysiology of symptom presentation.

items.title: Effect of household sanitation on child undernutrition and health indicators: evidence from Pakistan.
items.abstract: Poor sanitation is a major public health issue linked to significant health outcomes. Several studies have associated sanitation with undernutrition and diarrhoea. Improved sanitation, however, is determined by household decisions, which may induce endogeneity that has been insufficiently explored in most of the previous literature. We assessed the effects of improved sanitation on children's height-for-age, weight-for-age, and weight-for-height z-scores, and diarrhoea. Using an instrumental variable approach, our findings demonstrated that improved sanitation was found to have a positive and significant impact on anthropometric indices, mainly height-for-age and weight-for-age. Conversely, no significant impact was identified on weight-for-height and diarrhoea. The heterogeneity analyses add value to the literature, showing that girls, children older than two years, and children with uneducated mothers significantly benefit from improved sanitation as compared to boys, children younger than two years, and those with educated mothers, respectively. Our results suggest that policies that enhance access to sanitation can be effective in reducing undernutrition.

items.title: Public Participation in U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Advisory Committees: A Qualitative Analysis.
items.abstract: Importance The FDA frequently solicits public input to inform advisory committee meetings reviewing new drug applications. Although intended to enhance transparency and incorporate patient perspectives, the content of these submissions has not been well described. Objective To characterize public comments to FDA advisory committee meetings and examine the values and considerations expressed. Design Qualitative study using inductive content analysis with an iterative coding framework. Comments were coded by one reviewer and independently double-coded for a random subset; disagreements were resolved through discussion (Light's kappa = 0.81). Setting Public comments associated with FDA advisory committee meetings for five new drug applications reviewed between January 2020 and December 2024. Participants A random sample of 600 public comments from the five products with the highest public engagement: (1) sodium phenylbutyrate-taurursodiol for ALS; (2) teplizumab for type 1 diabetes; (3) midomafetamine (MDMA-assisted therapy) for PTSD; (4) delandistrogene moxeparvovec for Duchenne muscular dystrophy; and (5) eflornithine tablets for pediatric neuroblastoma. Main outcome measures Stakeholder role, stance regarding drug approval, and thematic content. Results Submissions were most commonly from caregivers or immediate family members (31.5%), individuals without disclosed roles (20.0%), friends or extended family (18.5%), and patients (17.2%). Most comments supported approval (90.2%), with few neutral (7.8%) or opposing (1.3%) views. Four themes emerged: (1) experiential considerations; (2) evidentiary considerations, including clinical trial data and personal observations; (3) regulatory and policy considerations, such as urgency of access; and (4) values-based considerations, such as therapeutic hope and autonomy. Conclusions and relevance Public comments were overwhelmingly supportive of approval, reflecting experiential, evidentiary, policy, and values-based considerations. Strengthening mechanisms for synthesizing public input may enhance transparency and confidence in the FDA regulatory process.

items.title: Psychometric performance of the OECD Patient-Reported Indicator Surveys Patient Questionnaire (PaRIS-PQ) among adults with chronic conditions in Norway.
items.abstract: Purpose The OECD Patient-Reported Indicator Surveys (PaRIS) initiative aims to provide standardised, internationally comparable patient-reported indicators for people living with chronic conditions receiving primary or generalist ambulatory care. This study evaluated the psychometric performance of the multi-item scales in the Norwegian PaRIS Patient Questionnaire (PaRIS-PQ). Methods Data were drawn from the 2023 Norwegian PaRIS Main Survey. Respondents aged ≥ 45 years with at least one self-reported chronic condition were included. Measures were PROMIS Global Physical Health, PROMIS Global Mental Health, and WHO-5 Well-Being Index as patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs); the Person-Centred Coordinated Care Experience Questionnaire (P3CEQ) as a patient-reported experience measure (PREM); and the Porter-Novelli Scale (PNS) and self-management confidence as capability-related measures. Analyses assessed structural validity, internal consistency reliability, measurement invariance, item functioning, and construct validity. Results Of 8,683 respondents, 6,691 reported at least one chronic condition. PROM scales performed best, with acceptable internal consistency (α = 0.80-0.89) and strongest confirmatory support for PROMIS Global Physical Health (CFI = 0.992, RMSEA = 0.080). The PREM (P3CEQ) showed weaker performance, with suboptimal fit for the total scale (CFI = 0.818, RMSEA = 0.132), limited scalar invariance, and low internal consistency for the care coordination subscale (α = 0.61). Capability-related measures showed mixed performance. Metric invariance was supported across all tested models, whereas scalar invariance was less consistent. Construct validity findings were consistent with expectations. Conclusion PROM scales showed the most consistent psychometric support. PREM and capability-related measures were more heterogeneous and require cautious, scale-specific interpretation, especially in subgroup comparisons and when used as latent measures. Evaluation and refinement of weaker experience- and capability-related measures is warranted.

items.title: Increases in high-frequency cannabis use among pregnant women in the United States during 2010-2019 and 2021-2023.
items.abstract: Adverse outcomes associated with cannabis use in pregnancy are affected by frequency of maternal cannabis use. This study examines time trends in frequency of cannabis use among U.S. pregnant women. This study used data from the National Survey on Drug Use and Health. Participants included pregnant women aged 18-44 from 2010 to 2019 (n = 7,310), and 2021-2023 (n = 1,992). A multinomial regression model assessed time trends in low-moderate versus high-frequency cannabis use (< 15 versus [Formula: see text]15 days in the past month) from 2010 to 2019, controlling for age, education level, income, marital status and race/ethnicity. From 2021 to 2023, we examined the prevalence of low-moderate versus high-frequency cannabis use and whether use was reported as "recommended by a healthcare professional". From 2010 to 2019, high-frequency cannabis use in pregnancy increased from 1.15% to 3.43% (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) for increase per year = 1.10, 95% CI = 1.02-1.18), while low-to-moderate frequency cannabis use remained stable (1.76% in 2010, 1.93% in 2019; aOR = 1.04, 95% CI = 0.97-1.10). From 2021 to 2023, over half of pregnant women who used cannabis reported high-frequency use (4.31% high, versus 2.36% low-moderate). From 2021 to 2023, 15% of pregnant women reporting low-moderate cannabis use, versus 35% with high-frequency use, reported that cannabis use was recommended by a healthcare professional. High-frequency cannabis use during pregnancy increased among U.S women while low to moderate use of cannabis in pregnancy remained stable. From 2021 to 2023, one-third of pregnant women who used cannabis frequently reported that their use was recommended by a healthcare professional.

items.title: Criteria-led discharge in paediatric inpatient care in Switzerland: a quality improvement study of implementation, safety and satisfaction.
items.abstract: Paediatric hospitals have high admission rates and short lengths of stay, leading to a high turnover. The discharge process is challenged by delays and a lack of standardisation. Criteria-led discharge (CLD) has been proposed to overcome these challenges. CLD enables nursing staff to safely discharge patients once predefined clinical criteria are met, reducing reliance on physician review and minimising delays. We introduced CLD on a paediatric ward and evaluated its implementation in a quality improvement study pre- (December 2023-March 2024) and post-implementation (December 2024-March 2025). Outcomes were assessed using retrospective electronic health record data and surveys. The primary outcome was patient safety, measured by 14-day readmission and complication rates. Secondary outcomes included efficiency and patient flow, measured by length of stay, time of day at discharge and discharge delays, as well as patient, caregiver and staff satisfaction. A total of 355 eligible admissions (202 pre-, 153 post-implementation) were included into the analysis in three diagnostic groups: 122 bronchiolitis, 135 pneumonia and 98 asthma. 14-day readmission rates were comparable between CLD (3.2%), standard discharge (SD) (3.4%) and post-implementation SD (4.5%) cohorts. Patient, caregiver and staff satisfaction was high. Conclusions CLD is non-inferior in terms of safety compared to standard discharge. It subjectively improved discharge efficiency and positively impacted workload distribution while maintaining high patient, caregiver and staff satisfaction. CLD is a promising tool to facilitate discharges in paediatrics. Local adaptation and quality control are necessary for successful implementation. What is known • Criteria-led discharge (CLD) increases standardisation, safety and efficiency in discharges from hospital. What is new • CLD is a safe method to discharge children from inpatient paediatric wards. • CLD may decrease stress of ward staff and enhance efficiency in paediatric hospitals.

items.title: Development and Psychometric Evaluation of the Self-Efficacy for Cooking Healthy Meals Scale in the Teaching Kitchen Multisite Trial (TK-MT).
items.abstract: Objective To develop and evaluate a scale measuring self-efficacy for overcoming barriers to preparing healthy meals at home. Design Cross-sectional data were analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis comparing 1 and 2-factor structures. Setting Teaching Kitchen Multisite Trial. Participants Adults with overweight or class I-II obesity (n = 169; mean age, 46 years; 79% female; 38% Hispanic, 10% Black, 23% Asian). Variables measured Self-Efficacy for Cooking Healthy Meals, addressing contextual barriers and resource constraints. Analysis Confirmatory factor analysis was performed using maximum likelihood estimation with robust errors; fit was evaluated with multiple indexes; internal consistency was assessed with Cronbach α. Results The 2-factor model fit better than the 1-factor model; the indexes were borderline (SBχ²[43] = 82.9, root mean squared error of approximation = 0.074, Comparative Fit Index = 0.91, Tucker-Lewis Index = 0.88). Reliability was acceptable for contextual barriers (α = 0.79) but lower for resource constraints (α = 0.68). Conclusions and implications In this preliminary analysis with a predominantly female, educated, higher-income sample, the scale showed borderline-to-adequate psychometric properties; validation in larger, more diverse samples is needed.

items.title: Development and Feasibility of In Situ Simulation for Pressure Injury Prevention in Intensive Care.
items.abstract: Objective To develop, validate and test in situ simulation scenarios aimed at pressure injury (PI) prevention for nursing professionals working in an intensive care unit (ICU). Design A multi-method study is planned across four phases. Methods Conducted at a high-complexity Brazilian university hospital, this four-phase study: (1) development of simulation scenarios and checklists; (2) content validation by 11 experts (CVI/MKC); (3) pilot testing with 12 nursing professionals; and (4) ICU-based educational intervention. Scenarios were grounded in international guidelines and the NLN/Jeffries Simulation Theory. Feasibility was assessed via metrics of acceptability, appropriateness, adoption and fidelity. Results Two evidence-based simulation scenarios and checklists were developed for registered nurses and nursing technicians, achieving high content validity among 11 experts. The in situ intervention reached 83% of the unit's nursing staff, demonstrating strong operational feasibility and acceptability. Beyond education, the scenarios served as a diagnostic tool, successfully identifying critical practice gaps, notably in Braden Scale utilization, pressure redistribution and the execution of standardized preventive measures. Conclusion The scenarios demonstrated satisfactory content validity and proved feasible for use in ICUs. In situ simulation showed potential to support continuing education actions, promote critical reflection on clinical practice and identify gaps in care processes related to PI prevention. Implications for practice In situ simulation can contribute to strengthening continuing health education, support the review of care practices and favour the implementation of evidence-based preventive measures for PI prevention in intensive care. Patient or public involvement No patient or public involvement in the development of this study. Trial registration https://ensaiosclinicos.gov.br/rg/RBR-4xc2sk8.

items.title: Pesticides and Hypospadias in Southern Brazil: An Ecological Study.
items.abstract: Rio Grande do Sul ranks among the Brazilian states with the highest pesticide consumption and one of the highest prevalences of hypospadias, a congenital anomaly often associated with prenatal exposure to endocrine-disrupting chemicals. We assessed the relationship between prenatal pesticide exposure and hypospadias risk through an ecological study of 1 776 670 live births in the state from 2010 to 2022. Using a spatial Bayesian hierarchical model, we examined associations between hypospadias and municipal-level indicators: relative crop area, pesticide sales, and probability of pesticide detection in water samples. The prevalence was 4.69 cases per 10 000 live births, with 10 municipalities at high risk and 15 at low risk. Higher risk was associated with tobacco cultivation. Sales of metaflumizone and Melaleuca alternifolia were associated with increased risk, while detection probabilities of alachlor and DDT showed the largest estimated effects, although these estimates were accompanied by substantial uncertainty. While causal inference is not possible in this ecological design, findings generate hypotheses for future research on prenatal pesticide exposure. Considering other environmental risk factors may further clarify hypospadias etiology. Identifying modifiable determinants is key to guiding interventions and public policies to reduce this condition's burden, particularly in rural areas and agricultural populations.

items.title: Colleague-Perpetrated Workplace Bullying Among Nurses: Experiences and Perceived Implications for Mental Health and Professional Functioning-A Qualitative Study.
items.abstract: Introduction Workplace bullying is a persistent problem in nursing that may adversely affect nurses' mental health, professional functioning and quality of patient care. This study aimed to explore Slovenian nurses' experiences of colleague-perpetrated workplace bullying, its perceived organisational contributors, implications for mental health and professional functioning, and nurses' responses and perspectives on prevention. Methods A qualitative descriptive study was conducted using semi-structured interviews with 20 nurses employed in different healthcare settings in Slovenia. Study participants were recruited through purposive sampling. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim and analysed using Braun and Clarke's six-phase thematic analysis. Results Through thematic analysis, four main themes were identified: (1) nurses' experiences of workplace bullying; (2) the impact of workplace bullying on mental health; (3) the impact of workplace bullying on professional functioning; and (4) nurses' responses to bullying and prevention strategies. Nurses described workplace bullying as a common and persistent phenomenon characterised by verbal abuse, humiliation, social exclusion and hostile communication. Bullying was perceived to negatively affect psychological well-being through increased stress, anxiety, emotional exhaustion, reduced self-confidence and difficulties detaching from work. Discussion and conclusions Workplace bullying remains an important occupational challenge with substantial implications for nurses' mental health and professional functioning. Healthcare organisations should prioritise comprehensive bullying prevention strategies, supportive leadership and psychologically safe work environments to protect nurses' well-being. Patient or public contribution No patients or members of the public were involved in the design, conduct, analysis or interpretation of this study, or in the preparation of this manuscript. As the study population consisted of registered nurses and nursing professionals rather than patients or members of the public, this study aimed to give voice to nurses' own experiences of colleague-perpetrated workplace bullying as the primary contribution to the research process.

items.title: Target Trial Emulation: Considerations for Physical Therapy Research.
items.abstract: Randomized clinical trials (RCTs) are considered the ideal method for assessing the effectiveness of physical therapist interventions. However, RCTs are resource-intensive and usually take several years to complete, often providing insights well after they are needed to inform practice. Due to the constantly evolving nature of physical therapy, study designs are needed that can more rapidly generate evidence that can be used to guide clinical care. Target trial emulation (TTE) provides a framework that improves researchers' abilities to draw causal inferences from observational data, by specifying protocol components of a hypothetical RCT and emulating those components with observational data elements. By leveraging data generated through routine care encounters, TTE allows researchers to examine the effectiveness of interventions as they are being used in clinical care - enhancing researchers' abilities to generate evidence when it is most needed. However, TTE has not been used extensively among physical therapy researchers, potentially due to a lack of familiarity with this concept or challenges related to the way physical therapy is delivered or the types of data generated during physical therapist encounters. In this manuscript, the authors provide an introduction to the TTE framework, using an ongoing study examining the effectiveness of remote therapeutic monitoring as a case example. The authors also discuss considerations and challenges associated with TTE studies within the context of physical therapy and recommend strategies for addressing these challenges. They also discuss how TTE studies can be enhanced through the addition of implementation-focused data collection and conclude with a discussion of limitations associated with TTE studies.

items.title: Psychological well-being as a relational and institutional process: a PERMA-informed focus group study with Chinese undergraduates.
items.abstract: Purpose This study explored how undergraduates understood, experienced, negotiated, and sustained psychological well-being in everyday university life at a public university in Southwest China, using PERMA as a sensitising framework. Methods Between 20 December 2024 and 20 January 2025, six in-person semi-structured focus groups involved 36 purposively selected undergraduates aged 18-22 years across four year levels. Discussions were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, anonymised, translated into English, and checked for conceptual accuracy. Reflexive thematic analysis used PERMA flexibly rather than as a fixed coding structure. The lead researcher coded and developed themes, with a second researcher contributing reflexive review and analytic discussion. Results Five PERMA-informed themes were generated: lived positive emotion, sustained engagement, relational growth and agency, meaning and purpose, and perceived accomplishment and mastery. Although broadly aligned with PERMA, the themes showed that well-being was interconnected and shaped by relational, academic, and institutional conditions. Accomplishment extended beyond achievement to competence development, task completion, problem-solving, contribution, and recognition of effort. Conclusions The findings extend applications of PERMA by showing how its elements were interconnected and sustained through relational and institutional processes. Student flourishing was shaped not only by individual experiences but also by relationships, opportunities for participation and competence development, and institutional recognition.

items.title: When Do Child Behaviour Problems Warrant Paediatric Management, and What Is Needed to Do This Successfully? Results of a Delphi Study.
items.abstract: Aim Developmental-Behavioural problems represent the most common reason for referral in Australian outpatient paediatric practice. While paediatricians consider behaviour a part of developmental assessment, it is unclear to what extent they then go on to manage problem behaviours themselves. To clarify this question, this study examines (1) properties of child behaviour that warrant ongoing medical care, (2) supports considered necessary to do this work effectively and (3) whether these supports are available in current practice. Methods These questions were examined by expert consensus (Delphi) methodology, comprising two rounds of surveys. The survey population was members of the Australasian Society for Developmental Paediatrics (ASDP). Results A total of 228 completed responses were received to the first survey round, with a high level of consensus achieved. Behaviours considered appropriate for medical assessment and intervention were those potentially causing either direct or indirect harm for the child and/or others. There was strong agreement regarding support services considered necessary for good clinical practice both from within and outside of health services. In current clinical practice, these supports were commonly not available. In the public health system compared to private practice, needed supports were less available. Conclusions Management of behaviour is part of Developmental Paediatrics. Paediatricians have a clear understanding regarding behavioural properties that justify active intervention. There is agreement regarding supports needed to do this work successfully. These supports are not often available in clinical practice, most notably within the public health system. This is problematic for the well-being of the children seen.

items.title: Burden of Albuminuria in US Adults and its Association with Obesity, Sex and Mortality: A Cross-sectional Analysis of NHANES 2003-2020.
items.abstract: Albuminuria is an early marker of kidney disease diagnosis, severity and progression. Obesity, a major public health concern in the United States, may contribute to the development of albuminuria; however, the obesity-albuminuria relationship remains incompletely defined. We hypothesized that albuminuria is more prevalent in obese individuals and is associated with poor survival. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of NHANES survey cycles from 2003 to 2020, with linked mortality data through 2016. The study included 59,717 participants aged ≥18 years with available urinary albumin creatinine ratio (uACR) and BMI ≥18 kg/m2. BMI was categorized into normal weight, overweight and obese. Albuminuria was defined as UACR ≥30 mg/g and categorized into three severity grades (mild, moderate, and severe). Logistic regression models were used to assess the association between obesity and albuminuria, and adjustment by sociodemographic and clinical factors was assessed. Survival across albuminuria severity grades was examined. Among individuals with albuminuria the prevalence of obesity was significantly higher than those without albuminuria (40.2% vs 32.9%; p<0.001). Individuals with albuminuria were relatively older and had higher prevalence of diabetes and hypertension as compared to the no albuminuria group. Obesity was significantly associated with higher odds of albuminuria (OR 1.36; 95% CI 1.23-1.50) when controlling for sociodemographic and clinical factors. We also observed higher odds of albuminuria in individuals who were males (OR 1.58, 95% CI 1.37-1.82), ages 18 to 44 years (OR 1.46, 95% CI 1.26-1.68), and ages 45 to 64 years (OR 1.79, 95% CI 1.49-2.14). The Individuals with albuminuria had poorer survival, with stark decline in a stepwise manner across albuminuria severity grades. Obesity is strongly associated with albuminuria in U.S. adults. Albuminuria is linked to survival disadvantage, underscoring the importance of screening among individuals with obesity and early initiation of nephro-protective therapies in individuals with albuminuria.

items.title: Partner, advisor, advocate, mentor: A typology of collaborative roles for patients and those with lived experience in health systems.
items.abstract: IntroductionAs patient engagement has evolved, a range of longitudinal collaborative partnerships between patients, family caregivers, and health systems decision-makers has emerged. These roles carry many different labels, and there is no consensus on definitions or terminology. The objective of this study is to propose empirically-based role definitions to describe longitudinal partnerships between people with lived experience and health systems.MethodsWe analysed survey and interview data to examine how patient partnership roles are defined by those with lived experience engaged in longitudinal partnerships with Canadian health organizations ( n = 603 survey respondents, n = 35 interviewees), and by staff and decision-makers in those organizations ( n = 25). Through inductive analysis, we identified key elements, sources of variation and terminology considerations, developing a typology of roles to describe the concept of "patient partner".ResultsIn our typology of roles, "Partner" could describe those deeply embedded in organizations, who participate actively in decision-making on multiple issues, representing both their own lived experience and the priorities of a broader community. We suggest "Advisor" to describe members of networks who engage episodically on multiple projects over time, offering perspective and input when requested, drawing mainly on their own lived experience. Working within and outside the health system, "Advocate" could define those who work independently to achieve particular outcomes, sometimes by disrupting dysfunction in the healthcare system. We offer "Mentor" to express the role of supporting other patients in their health or engagement journeys based on one's own lived experience.DiscussionThe proposed terms and definitions will be useful to describe the diverse activities and approaches of longitudinal collaboration. These can be used as the starting point in dialogue within and between patient partners and organizations to create engagement-specific role definitions, and to clarify the expectations, responsibilities, and intended outcomes of engagement. We present these definitions for clarity, without endorsing any particular form of engagement.

items.title: Aging Service Organizational Capacity to Deliver Evidence-Based Depression Programs: A National Survey.
items.abstract: BackgroundIntegration of mental health programs within community-based, social or aging service organizations has been recommended to serve more older adults with depression.ObjectiveThe purpose of this study was to obtain input from aging service organizations across the United States regarding their consideration and resource needs for implementing a lay-led program for depression ( "Do More, Feel Better," DMFB).MethodsAn online survey distributed via email inquired about perceived need and consideration regarding DMFB, existing resources, and resource needs.ResultsAmong 242 respondents across 42 states, perceived need for community-based depression services was high (8.7/10), and almost all reported they would consider implementing DMFB (94%). Most had some resources in place to support DMFB (e.g., technology, staff, experience with other evidence-based programs), but most indicated need for key program-specific resources, with the most critical resource needs being funding, dedicated personnel, and training (e.g., depression identification, DMFB delivery, and emergency management).

items.title: The Struggle for Nursing Professionalization in Indonesia: Colonial Era to Reformasi.
items.abstract: Political constraints and professional aspirations have shaped the history of nursing in Indonesia. This study traces this history from the end of the Dutch colonial period to the Reformasi period. This narrative history draws on published scholarship, statutory texts, and contemporaneous Indonesian press reporting. However, under Guided Democracy and the New Order, corporatist control of professional associations left them no route to legislation, and ministerial decree fixed their status. The fall of the New Order restored freedom of association. It produced a legislature with a genuine power of initiative, although regime change was a necessary condition and not a sufficient one. The Indonesian National Nurses Association (PPNI) used that opening across three parliamentary terms, combining insider lobbying of Commission IX with mass mobilization, including a demonstration by thousands of nurses at the parliament building on May 21, 2013, and secured passage on September 25, 2014. The Law No. 38 of 2014 concerning Nursing is the first Indonesian statute to define nursing as a profession and to establish education standards, registration, and licensing for nurses. Under this law, nurses gained authority to treat common illnesses only where no physician is posted and under a government assignment, and the proposed independent council was placed under another council shared with other health professions. The history examined here has implications for understanding how professional recognition is achieved in low- and middle-income countries where colonial medical hierarchies have never been fully dismantled.

items.title: Developing indicators of watershed health through public consultations and positing the use of ecological place-based approach in watershed management planning
items.abstract: Watershed health assessment is essential in the identification of issues and in the development of a plan to find solutions to issues. Watershed health is assessed based on a suite of watershed health indicators (WHI) often selected by technical experts. Stakeholders’ input into the selection of WHIs is necessary. Additionally, the importance of each indicator varies in different areas of a large watershed due to differences in ecological factors. The Red Deer River Watershed Alliance (RDRWA) conducted public consultation workshops at three locations that corresponded to natural regions (ecological land units) within the Red Deer River watershed, Alberta, Canada. Participants were asked, “What are your watershed issues?” Similar issues were grouped together and placed under a corresponding group of watershed health environmental indicators used by the RDRWA and the Government of Alberta. Non- environmental issues turned out to be social and institutional issues and these were classified based on the subject or topic that emerged from the process of grouping similar issues together. Issues were analyzed and comparisons were made between locations. Nine environmental indicator groups, three of which were new, and a new set of eight social and institutional indicator groups were identified. Natural regions influenced environmental indicators and, to a lesser extent, social and institutional indicators. Using natural regions within a large watershed is an ecological place-based approach that groups together land areas and their communities that have similar environmental issues. This approach, in combination with the use of WHIs developed by stakeholders, will provide the basis of a comprehensive watershed health report and a management plan in the future. This approach can be replicated in other places in the world that practice participatory watershed management planning.

items.title: Digital Game Addiction and Empathy Levels in Primary School Children: A Cross-Sectional Study Using Mediation and Hierarchical Regression Analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Introduction: Digital game addiction has emerged as a growing public health concern due to its potential implications for children’s psychosocial development. Empathy, a key component of socio-emotional functioning, may be associated with patterns of digital gaming; however, the nature of this relationship remains complex and may involve multiple interacting factors. items.title: ProtLink: Sequence and Multispecies Graph Context for Protein Interaction Prediction
items.abstract: Predicting protein-protein interactions (PPIs) from sequence alone is difficult, while known interaction networks may provide informative biological context. We introduce ProtLink, a sequence-conditioned graph-learning framework that combines frozen ESM-2 representations with protein interaction topology and orthogroup-mediated connections between species. We compare sequence-only models, GraphSAGE, a homogeneous graph transformer, and a heterogeneous graph transformer (HGT) for human PPI prediction. In an initial edge-level comparison, three-layer multispecies HGT with ESM-2 650M features achieves an average precision (AP) of 0.980 under random negative sampling, compared with 0.951 for the homogeneous transformer; its AP decreases to 0.878 with two-hop-preferred negatives. In controlled three-seed experiments, three-layer full-graph HGT obtains an AP of $0.9701\pm0.0022$, exceeding an orthogroup-only model ($0.9435\pm0.0094$). The corresponding two-layer comparison shows little additional benefit from non-human PPI edges, consistent with the greater message-passing depth needed to transmit their information. For human proteins excluded from training interactions, multispecies HGT achieves $0.8335\pm0.0094$ AP versus $0.6482\pm0.0052$ for a sequence-only pair model. These results identify the value, depth dependence, and limits of evolutionary graph context while distinguishing prediction of held-out edges from generalization to held-out proteins.

items.title: Learning Actionable Information Landscapes for Multimodal Active Sensing in Hawkmoths
items.abstract: Animals integrate information across sensory modalities to guide exploration, suggesting that they maintain internal estimates of where actions are expected to reduce uncertainty. However, how such action-conditioned information maps are learned from multimodal sensory experience remains unclear, as previous studies have been largely confined to unimodal sensing frameworks. We introduce a multimodal predictive-coding framework for learning uncertainty-reduction maps from visual and mechanosensory observations in hawkmoth flower interaction tasks. A variational generative model trained on simulated environments recovers modality-specific information landscapes over the action space, capturing how visual patterns, surface geometry, and mechanosensory cues shape the value of exploratory actions. These learned maps are consistent with several features of hawkmoth behavior, including nonzero tracking offsets, probing along visual patterns, and geometry-dependent exploration. Applying the model to behavioral data from flower tracking and nectary search, we find that natural trajectories tend to occupy regions of high uncertainty reduction in these learned maps. Building on these observations, we develop an uncertainty-gated lexicographic algorithm that switches between information gathering and reward exploitation based on perceptual uncertainty. In nectary search, uncertainty gating improves learning relative to exploit-only, $ε$-greedy, fixed-time, and uncertainty-calibrated non-lexicographic controls, with better generalization and robustness to sensory and curvature shifts. These results link information landscapes learned through generative modeling to biological sensing and embodied exploration.

items.title: Perception, Not Reasoning, Limits Visual Theory of Mind
items.abstract: Vision-language models pass text-based false-belief probes at near-human levels but drop by over twenty percentage points on abstract panels the moment the same problem is conveyed visually. The consensus diagnosis is conceptual, prescribing new belief-reasoning modules. We argue the dominant bottleneck is perceptual: not what the model cannot reason about, but what it cannot see. We propose a five-condition dissociation protocol that holds the reasoning task constant while varying perceptual fidelity from visual only to text only, and quantify the result with the Perceptual Contribution Ratio, the share of the visual-to-text gap a given fidelity closes. We test this on two kinds of scenes: abstract 2D panels in the Heider--Simmel tradition, and naturalistic 3D game scenes from MuMA-ToM and MindPower. The evaluation covers seven VLMs and roughly 159,000 API calls. Ground-truth scaffolds substantially close the gap in every setting, and on the abstract panels and MuMA-ToM they match or exceed the text-only reasoning. Whereas scaffolds built by automatic parsers, including frontier VLMs, fail. The most common error in the visual-only condition is \emph{reality bias}, which accounts for 60\% of false-belief failures. Models report where an object actually is, not where an absent agent believes it is. This points to a perceptual front-end that fails to track which agents were present at each moment. Under the evaluated protocol, structured visual scene-state extraction, rather than belief inference, is the dominant bottleneck for visual ToM.
