items.title: NeuroHorizon: Long-Horizon Forecasting of Neural Population Activity with Hierarchical Memory
items.abstract: Long-horizon forecasting of neural population activity tests whether a model has captured dynamics that remain predictive well beyond the observed history. Prediction quality typically declines as the horizon grows, yet neither short-horizon accuracy nor teacher-forced evaluation, which supplies the true activity preceding each predicted step, reveals how well models sustain predictions from an initial history alone. We compare direct multi-step prediction and autoregressive rollout on spiking recordings across horizons and introduce NeuroHorizon, which pairs event-based spike encoding with a causal decoder for population firing rates. Its hierarchical prediction memory keeps recent predictions at full temporal resolution and compresses earlier ones into segment summaries, giving the decoder both local detail and longer-range context. Under teacher-forced training this memory holds ground-truth activity, whereas during rollout it holds the model's own predictions. To reduce this mismatch, we train with scheduled sampling, progressively exposing the decoder to its own predictions. From 500 ms of macaque motor-cortex activity, NeuroHorizon achieves the highest forward-prediction score among the evaluated autonomous models at all four horizons from 100 to 1000 ms, and its per-bin predictions remain above a mean-firing-rate baseline across nearly the full 1 s window. Complementary experiments on macaque sensorimotor and mouse multi-region recordings show that performance generally increases with model and data size, alongside improved prediction after cross-subject pretraining and fine-tuning. Together, these results clarify how forecasting performance changes across horizons and offer an effective approach to long-horizon forecasting of neural population activity.

items.title: Pixels over Symbols: Sensory Realism Improves Behavioral Alignment in Models of Cognition
items.abstract: Computational models of cognition have traditionally relied on abstract symbolic inputs that approximate sensory experiences with simplified vector representations. This simplification reflects historical computational constraints and a long-held assumption that the details of sensory realism are incidental to the study of cognitive processes. Recent advances have enabled the development of sensory-realistic models capable of performing diverse cognitive tasks, yet whether sensory realism meaningfully shapes cognition has not been formally established. We address this gap through a large-scale empirical comparison of abstract and sensory-realistic neural network models trained on a battery of memory-dependent decision-making tasks. Our results show that sensory-realistic models mirror human behavioral response patterns significantly more than their abstract counterparts, though a substantial gap to human internal behavioral consistency remains even for the best tested models. By analyzing the internal dynamics of these systems, we find that the learned recurrent weights are not the main source of this divergence. In fact, frozen abstract-trained weights driven by sensory-realistic inputs recover the human consistency of sensory-realistic models. The resulting dynamics are also within the seed-to-seed variability of sensory-realistic models. Together, our findings argue that across a broad set of visual working-memory tasks, sensory realism accounts for a substantial portion of the model-human behavioral agreement, more than the choice of sequence architecture and comparable to the choice of vision encoder. These results suggest that findings obtained from abstract task models in neuroscience should be more carefully interpreted in light of their potential behavioral limitations.

items.title: Same Contacts, Different Rooms:Meeting Format Shapes LLM Group Influence Beyond Pairwise Contact Counts
items.abstract: Simulations of LLM agent collectives usually summarise interaction as a pairwise contact network. We test that summary with a contact-matched intervention: the members, their initial stances and every pairwise contact count stay fixed while the meetings are reorganised, and each member gives a one-step support readout after reading the arguments of everyone present. Across six open-weight LLMs and 14 debate topics, merging triads into five-person meetings (resize) moves group support more than reshuffling who meets in triads (regroup), although both move the same 60 dyadic exposures. The root-mean-square change is 4.36 versus 2.59 percentage points (pp), larger for resize in all six models and in 81 of 84 model-topic cells. Resizing also has a consistent direction: it amplifies the initial majority of the merged members by 1.72 pp, in every model, whereas regrouping has no direction (<= 0.03 pp). A contact network cannot represent regrouping at all, yet pairwise rules applied meeting by meeting explain up to 76% of its effect, and with identical weights they raise resize R^2 by 0.51-0.58 for two models. We show that the gap between the two placements is an exact Jensen gap of the sigmoid readout, bounded by how much a member's predicted logits vary across meetings; this dispersion tracks the gap with log-log r=0.97 and tells a modeller when contact counts are a safe summary. Meeting format is a first-class variable for LLM social simulation.

items.title: Constraining Cosmic Deceleration using the Solar System
items.abstract: We investigate whether Solar System dynamics can provide independent constraints on the present day cosmological deceleration parameter $q_0$, offering a complementary approach to conventional cosmological probes. By relating cosmic acceleration to a weak Hooke type radial perturbation, we derive bounds using planetary perihelion precession, trans-Neptunian objects, and Oort cloud dynamics. We obtain relatively robust planetary bounds of $|q_0|\lesssim 10^9$, while the outer Solar System yields potentially stronger, albeit more model dependent, constraints approaching $10^5$. Through Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation and sensitivity analyses, we explore the statistical robustness of these estimates and their dependence on orbital measurements. Finally, we demonstrate how future precision astrometry and outer planet missions could improve these limits by several orders of magnitude, establishing Solar System dynamics as a complementary laboratory for probing cosmological acceleration.

items.title: Is price-impact decay statistically identifiable by propagator estimation? Diffusive prices force the inferred kernel to be transient and fine-tuned
items.abstract: Despite the long memory of market-order flow, price dynamics remain diffusive---a seemingly paradoxical coexistence known in econophysics as the diffusivity puzzle. The propagator model has long been regarded as a promising solution: price impact decays in time, finely balanced against the order-flow memory, and propagators inferred from data have been reported to be consistent with this fine balance. Here we prove a no-go theorem: asymptotic impact decay is not statistically identifiable by propagator estimation, since for diffusive prices the fine-tuned decay is returned whether or not the true impact decays. It rests on universal theorems for the Wiener--Hopf deconvolution by which propagators are inferred under long-memory order flow: (i) the inferred propagator is necessarily transient, even when the true impact is permanent; (ii) under a mild condition, it decays with the fine-balance exponent, fixed by the order-flow autocorrelation alone. The fine-tuned decay is thus a property of the deconvolution, not evidence of impact decay. We demonstrate this with an exactly solvable null model that retains order splitting and the square-root law but whose impact is strictly permanent: the inferred propagator shows an artificial fine-tuned decay although the true impact never decays. Nonlinear propagator estimation, being of Wiener--Hopf type, is subject to the same theorems whenever true metaorders have long memory.

items.title: Evidence for Ambipolar Diffusion from Ion-Neutral Velocity Drift in HH 212
items.abstract: We present the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array Band 7 observations of the hyperfine structure of C$^{17}$O (3-2) and the H$^{13}$CO$^{+}$ (4-3) molecular line emissions of the Class 0 protostellar system HH 212 at $\sim$ 44 au spatial resolution. Radiative transfer models interpreted in the framework of non-ideal MHD of the envelope allow us to estimate an envelope mass of $M_{env}\sim0.12\,M_\odot$ and a mass infall rate of $\dot{M}_{env}\sim4.4-5.7\times10^{-6}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, consistent with values reported in the literature. The models also reveal a systematic radial velocity drift between the neutral tracer (C$^{17}$O (3-2)) and the ionized species (H$^{13}$CO$^{+}$ (4-3)) of $0.1-0.3$ km s$^{-1}$, exceeding the spectral resolution of 0.105 km s$^{-1}$ and consistent with possible ambipolar diffusion in the envelope. The ambipolar diffusion fraction, $f_{AD}\sim 0.1-1$, and the Hall parameter, $β_{i,H_2}\gg1$, indicate partial ion-neutral decoupling, with non-ideal effects becoming more significant toward the inner regions. In the envelope, our analysis shows that rotational energy decreases from $\sim 50\,\%$ of the gravitational energy at $R_{cen}$ to $\sim 25\,\%$ at $2R_{cen}$ and $\sim4\,\%$ at 1100 au. In contrast, for $B_0=1$ mG, magnetic energy increases from $\sim 0.4\,\%$ of the gravitational energy at $R_{cen}$ to $\sim2.6\,\%$ at $2R_{cen}$ and $\sim20\,\%$ at 1100 au. The drift velocity expected from radial force balance is consistent with the modeled drift velocity within $\sim300-400$ au of the central source but is lower at larger radii. These results are consistent with a scenario in which ambipolar diffusion leads to partial ion-neutral decoupling, allowing neutrals to move faster than ions within the envelope.

items.title: Telling coordination from coincidence: a no-interaction twin for collective systems
items.abstract: Measures of emergence based on information theory or causal closure ask whether a group variable has a predictable law of its own, but not whether that law was produced by the members' interactions: the centre of mass of non-interacting random walkers passes the standard criterion $Ψ$. We introduce the interaction share S, the fraction of the forecast error of a system's no-interaction twin (the same members with every interaction removed) that the real group law eliminates, and a projected estimator with expectation zero without interaction. For Gaussian forecasts, $-\frac{1}{2}\ln(1-S)$ is the expected Kullback-Leibler divergence of the real group law from the twin's. S is exactly zero for the centre of mass of linearly coupled walkers, and a machine-checked proof extends this to any pairwise force obeying Newton's third law. Across magnets, oscillators and flocking models it rises from 0 to about 1 where collective order appears. With time-shifted virtual groups and positive controls, it separates real fish schools (0.54-0.91, 17 recordings, two species) from groups that never interacted (-0.10 to 0.07), and it falls to zero when zebrafish are placed in the dark. In 221 mouse brain areas and in US stock markets the shares are small (about 1-3%) and were confirmed in pre-registered tests on unseen data. For linear forecasts the share is a memory gap, computable from two autocorrelation curves without fitting a twin; it matches measured shares (Spearman 0.97) and predicted fresh markets within 0.004. All code, data pipelines and hashed pre-registrations are public.

items.title: From Exo-Earth Detection to Atmospheric Characterization: Enabling Phase-Dependent Molecular Detection SNR in EXOSIMS
items.abstract: Detection and characterization of Earth-like worlds is a primary science goal for the upcoming NASA flagship Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). The HWO mission will be the first of its kind to specifically search for Earth-like worlds around Sun-like stars and characterize their atmospheres to identify potential biosignatures. A mission with such ambitious science goals thus requires equally robust and physically realistic simulation tools. In this work, we extend the realism of the EXOSIMS framework by incorporating phase-dependent biosignature detectability. We use the spectral retrieval tool rfast to determine the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) required to detect atmospheric O2 and H2O as a function of planetary phase and incorporate these requirements directly into EXOSIMS characterization integration-time calculations. Although the required molecular detection SNR decreases toward increasingly crescent phases, successful molecular detections are concentrated at intermediate phase angles, demonstrating the competing effects of molecular information content and direct-imaging observability. Relative to fixed characterization thresholds of SNR = 5 for H2O and SNR = 8.5 for O2, the phase-dependent treatment increases mean molecular detection yield by 76.8 percent for H2O and 29.7 percent for O2. Ultimately, we provide a framework that improves simulation fidelity, increases the realism of EXOSIMS as we expand to assess additional biosignatures in future work, and marries detection and characterization in yield modeling as we look to the future with HWO.

items.title: Climate-Based Modeling of Invasive Species Impact on Urban Green Infrastructure Using CLIMEX and Remote Sensing Data
items.abstract: The pace at which invasive alien species are established and spread is becoming a threat, especially to urban ecosystems, due, in part, to the variability of climates, urban growth, and fragmentation of habitats. These biological invasions are highly dangerous to urban green infrastructure (UGI), which sabotages biodiversity, ecological services, and ecological resilience in the long term. A unravelled modelling approach to employ the CLIMEX model of species distribution as well as the spatial analysis of ecosystems via remote sensing to observe invasion risk zones and map them in the fast urbanising landscapes was created in this work. The climatic suitability of chosen invasive species in the current and future climate conditions under parameters serving as temperature, precipitation, and humidity was simulated with the help of the CLIMEX model, and the land cover dynamics and vegetation indices (as well as the urban heat islands) were measured with the assistance of remote sensing data (Sentinel-2 and ModiS) measurements. It was possible to integrate these datasets using a GIS based multi-criteria methodology to create an Invasion Risk Index (IRI) to predict ecologically sensitive regions. The findings indicated that areas with an average rainfall, increasing temperatures, and discontinuous vegetation shows high ecological suitability of the invasive species, and this would be more so at the urban fringes, transport corridors, and industrial areas. These findings underscore the synergistic role of climatic and anthropogenic factors in shaping invasion dynamics and highlight the necessity for adaptive urban planning that incorporates ecological modeling outputs. The proposed framework offers a robust, scalable approach for predicting biological invasions, guiding urban biodiversity conservation strategies, and supporting policymakers in developing climate-resilient, biodiversity-secure urban ecosystems.

items.title: Art therapy sebagai pendekatan kreatif dalam konseling untuk mengurangi kecemasan
items.abstract: Kecemasan pada remaja merupakan masalah kesehatan mental yang kompleks, dipicu oleh faktor akademik, sosial, dan lingkungan, memerlukan intervensi efektif seperti art therapy. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengkaji efektivitas art therapy dalam mengurangi kecemasan remaja melalui Systematic Literature Review (SLR) dengan menganalisis studi terbitan lima tahun terakhir dari database seperti Google Scholar. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa art therapy (melalui lukis, musik, atau tari) signifikan menurunkan kecemasan, terutama pada remaja dengan Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) dan tekanan akademik, serta kelompok rentan seperti pasien kanker dan lansia. Efektivitasnya bervariasi tergantung durasi intervensi, metode, dan dukungan lingkungan. Simpulan penelitian ini menegaskan bahwa art therapy merupakan pendekatan terapeutik yang menjanjikan untuk mengelola kecemasan remaja, meski diperlukan adaptasi metode sesuai kebutuhan individu.

items.title: The resource elasticity of control
items.abstract: Abstract The ability to determine how much the environment can be controlled through our actions has long been viewed as fundamental to adaptive behavior. While traditional accounts treat controllability as a fixed property of the environment, we argue that real-world controllability often depends on the effort, time and money we are able and willing to invest. In such cases, controllability can be said to be elastic to invested resources. Here we propose that inferring this elasticity is essential for efficient resource allocation, and thus, elasticity misestimations result in maladaptive behavior. To test this hypothesis, we developed a novel treasure hunt game where participants encountered environments with varying degrees of controllability and elasticity. Across two pre-registered studies (N=514), we first demonstrate that people infer elasticity and adapt their resource allocation accordingly. We then present a computational model that explains how people make this inference, and identify individual elasticity biases that lead to suboptimal resource allocation. Finally, we show that overestimation of elasticity is associated with elevated psychopathology involving an impaired sense of control. These findings establish the elasticity of control as a distinct cognitive construct guiding adaptive behavior, and a computational marker for control-related maladaptive behavior.

items.title: Modelling location-invariant orthographic processing with artificial and natural language corpora
items.abstract: Previous research indicates that readers may construct a location-invariant letter string representation before associating it with a lexical representation. In neural network modeling, this is achieved with a two-stack model in which a hidden layer first learns to map location-specific letter representations into word-centered positions. Then, another stack is trained to map them into lexical representations. However, the model has been validated only in one language (French). In this study, we replicated the model with a Finnish language corpus having substantially more resembling words (KISSAA, KISSAN, KISSAT) and with modern and accessible programming tools. To gain insight into the model’s coding principles, we also trained the model with random letter strings, analyzed the model’s hidden layer activation patterns, and conducted an error analysis. The results indicated that random letter string training leads to superior letter identity and position coding. However, the natural corpus with many close words leads to a more fine-grained mapping from word-centered letter string representations to lexical representations. Finally, bigram coding may emerge in weights connecting hidden to output nodes. We conclude that the one- or two-stack model seems a potent candidate for developing a universal and comprehensive connectionist model of reading.

items.title: Recognizing fallacious reasoning in deontological arguments
items.abstract: Abstract Deontological arguments, in the broad sense, are those that refer to properties of choice options other than their consequences, such as whether the option is an act or omission. These arguments are often used to justify public policies, such as those concerning vaccination. In principle, some of these arguments could lead to outcomes worse than those of utilitarian choices, i.e., choices designed to yield the best expected consequences. Arguments for deontological choices ought to explain why it is better to make outcomes worse. We suggest that political arguments attempting to do this are usually fallacious. We list several categories of such informal fallacies, and we report two demonstrations in which we ask whether people without special training can distinguish types of such reasoning. People seem generally weak at this task, although those who are more inclined to accept the standards of actively open-minded thinking (AOT) do better, possibly because both AOT and fallacy classification require meta-cognitive competence. Performance may also be improved by more thorough instructions about the task. The idea of requesting justification for making things worse is a new method for empirical research on moral judgment and for instruction in argumentation. It is also a new kind of thought experiment for philosophical argument.

items.title: Gaze reinstatement during working memory for natural scenes
items.abstract: Abstract The information we hold in mind with working memory (WM) may propagate beyond the cortex and out to the peripheral motor system. For instance, directionally biased hand and eye movements can express simple visuo-spatial features during WM maintenance. If such sensorimotor inflections are a form of WM representation, they may also express more multifaceted and task-adaptive information than just spatial location. Here, we ask whether gaze patterns carry item-specific detail about complex stimuli held in mind, and whether gaze prospectively adapts to the behavioral task demands. To do this, we tracked human eye movements (male and female) during WM for naturalistic images, and we manipulated which image features were most task-relevant (visual or semantic). In two experiments, we found that the eyes moved in complex, item-specific spatiotemporal sequences during WM maintenance. Delay period gaze patterns retraced the scanpaths from stimulus encoding, echoing the ‘gaze reinstatement’ that aligns with neural pattern reactivation during long-term memory retrieval. Therefore, gaze patterns during WM may reinstate visual encoding processes for maintenance. We also used time-resolved representational similarity analyses, guided by convolutional neural network modeling, to test the specificity of WM gaze patterns across a trial. We found that gaze representations were more distinct when the task prioritized visual detail, and also ramped up in anticipation of the WM probe. Therefore, oculomotor WM signals are malleable to when and how the content will be used. These results suggest that the earliest levels of visual processing reflect prospectively-oriented and functionally flexible WM content representations. Significance The eyes are an outwardly accessible extension of the brain. They are the first stop for visual processing, but may also offer a rich window into underlying cognition. For instance, pupil dilation can reflect changing cognitive load, and eye movement biases can reflect basic spatial information about content held in mind with working memory. Working memory is a critical neuro-cognitive function, but its physiological bases remain under debate. Here, we show that eye movements code for more than simple spatial WM, and instead express intricate patterns that read out the complex, real-world stimuli held in mind. This work shows how cognitive states influence oculomotor functions, and also advances theories of WM representation to include the earliest stages of sensory processing.

items.title: Sleep-like slow waves in wakefulness index post-stroke behavioural alterations
items.abstract: Increases in high-amplitude, low-frequency EEG oscillations during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep serve as markers of neuronal silencing, which disrupts functional connectivity and is associated with a loss of awareness and responsiveness. Cortical slowing likewise occurs during wakefulness, upon sleep deprivation, and accompanies performance deterioration. Recent work has revealed similar oscillations (termed 'sleep-like slow waves') following stroke in brain regions close or connected to a brain lesion, offering a plausible but untested mechanism for stroke-related behavioural impairment. Here, we simultaneously recorded EEG and behavioural performance while 30 unilateral stroke patients (12 left hemisphere, 18 right hemisphere) and 27 age-matched healthy adults completed a computerised perceptual decision-making task. Stroke patients had predominantly middle cerebral artery strokes (n=25), with a small subset of posterior cerebral artery (n=4), and anterior cerebral artery/middle cerebral artery (n=1) lesions. Sleep-like slow waves occurred more frequently in stroke patients relative to healthy controls, with limited spatial specificity when comparing patients with left and right lesion sites (more slow waves ipsilateral of the lesion). Furthermore, there was a significant correlation between slow wave occurrence and the accuracy and speed of perceptual reports in stroke patients, suggesting that variations in the occurrence of slow waves may contribute to cognitive heterogeneity post-stroke. As sleep-like slow waves predict deficits in perceptual decision-making following stroke, they represent a plausible mechanism of post-lesion functional network dysfunction extending beyond the damaged regions, thereby contributing to broader cognitive impairments.

items.title: Cognitive Inception: Agentic Reasoning against Visual Deceptions by Injecting Skepticism
items.abstract: As the development of AI-generated contents (AIGC), multi-modal Large Language Models (LLM) struggle to identify generated visual inputs from real ones. Such shortcoming causes vulnerability against visual deceptions, where the models are deceived by generated contents, and the reliability of reasoning processes is jeopardized. Therefore, facing rapidly emerging generative models and diverse data distribution, it is of vital importance to improve LLMs' generalizable reasoning to verify the authenticity of visual inputs against potential deceptions. Inspired by human cognitive processes, we discovered that LLMs exhibit tendency of over-trusting the visual inputs, while injecting skepticism could significantly improve the models visual cognitive capability against visual deceptions. Based on this discovery, we propose \textbf{Inception}, a fully reasoning-based agentic reasoning framework to conduct generalizable authenticity verification by injecting skepticism, where LLMs' reasoning logic is iteratively enhanced between External Skeptic and Internal Skeptic agents. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first fully reasoning-based framework against AIGC visual deceptions. Our approach achieved a large margin of performance improvement over the strongest existing LLM baselines and SOTA performance on AEGIS benchmark.

items.title: Trust Modulates Speech Entrainment: Enhanced Cortical Tracking for Low-trust Speakers
items.abstract: Trust is a critical component of human communication, providing a foundation for understanding, information exchange, and social coordination. Much of the research on trust in speech communication has focused on how vocal characteristics impact perceived trustworthiness. However, little is known about how trust in a speaker affects the neural processing of speech. Here, we demonstrate a two-stage experimental framework to study that question using noninvasive EEG. First, participants engage in a trust-building stage, where they play an investment game with fictional characters, each paired with a distinctive voice and trustworthiness level (i.e., frequency and magnitude of lies). Next, participants engage in a story-listening stage, in which they are presented with stories from the same characters. Data acquired from 20 young adults confirm a statistically significant correlation between the perceived and actual trustworthiness of the fictional characters. Cortical speech tracking was quantified using a temporal response function analysis on the EEG data. We found that the trustworthiness established during the trust-building stage influenced the cortical tracking of speech in the subsequent story-listening stage, with lower trustworthiness corresponding to a stronger cortical tracking of speech. Interestingly, trustworthiness selectively modulated tracking strength, with no statistically significant changes in the spatial and temporal temporal response function dynamics.

items.title: Test-retest reliability of resting-state functional connectivity: a methodological investigation with implications for aggression research
items.abstract: Abstract The temporal stability of resting-state functional MR connectivity (rsfMRc) is a fundamental methodological consideration for longitudinal neuroimaging research, yet systematic evaluations across clinically relevant time frames remain limited. This study examined test-retest reliability of rsfMRc over short-term (1 hour) and medium-term (1 month) intervals in 34 healthy young adult males across three sessions. Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and matrix-wide reliability metrics were calculated to evaluate temporal stability across major brain networks, and associations between stable connectivity patterns and aggression measures were examined. Overall reliability showed moderate values (mean ICC = .557) with significant network-specific variation. Salience Network regions, particularly the supramarginal gyrus, and lateral parietal regions of the Default Mode Network demonstrated the highest stability (ICC > .600). Matrix-wide analyses indicated high consistency in connectivity rankings (Kendall's W = .798). Among the 23 most temporally stable regions, several showed systematic associations with both reactive and proactive aggression. These findings reveal substantial heterogeneity in rsfMRc reliability across brain networks and measurement intervals, providing empirical guidance for researchers planning longitudinal connectivity studies. Network-specific considerations are critical in study design, and identifying stable connectivity patterns offers a foundation for biomarker development, while regions with poor reliability may require alternative acquisition strategies.

items.title: SpatialImaginer: Towards Adaptive Visual Imagination for Spatial Reasoning
items.abstract: Spatial intelligence, which refers to the ability to reason about geometric and physical structure from visual observations, remains a core challenge for multimodal large language models. Despite promising performance, recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) often exhibit fragile reasoning traces in spatial intelligence tasks that involve consistent spatial state recognition. We argue that these failures stem from a mismatch between the spatial recognition mechanism and the text-only reasoning behavior of these MLLMs. Effective spatial reasoning requires low-level geometric structure to be faithfully preserved and updated throughout the reasoning process, whereas textual representations tend to abstract away precisely these critical details. To address this issue, we propose SpatialImaginer, a unified multimodal generation framework that integrates textual reasoning with visual imagination. Our framework adopts a divide-and-conquer strategy, using text chain-of-thought for high-level semantic planning and the visual imagination for geometry-sensitive state transformation and consistency preservation. To support this capability, we further introduce a difficulty-aware data engine with closed-loop verification to train the model to invoke visual imagination selectively when stable spatial state tracking is required. Extensive experiments on diverse spatial intelligence benchmarks show that SpatialImaginer achieves state-of-the-art performance and substantially improves robustness on complex multi-step spatial reasoning tasks.

items.title: SwimmingIndividuals: A high-performance agent-based model for marine ecosystems
items.abstract: Abstract Mechanistic models are essential for projecting ecosystem responses to novel conditions, yet the application and biological realism of agent-based models (ABMs) has often been limited by computational constraints. This paper introduces SwimmingIndividuals , an open-source agent-based model (ABM) framework that advances our ability to simulate complex biological processes at large ecological scales. The software’s main contribution is its suite of mechanistic sub-models that govern the full life cycle of each agent, including physics-based visual predation, adaptive behaviors such as diel vertical migration, and a flexible bioenergetics engine with multiple taxa-specific equations. These detailed biological processes are made computationally tractable for large populations through a hybrid CPU/GPU architecture written in the Julia language. We demonstrate the framework’s capabilities through three targeted simulations. The model successfully reproduced complex ecological phenomena as emergent properties, including diel vertical migration, cetacean diving patterns, size-based trophic dynamics, population-level growth curves, and stock-recruitment relationships. Furthermore, long-term simulations generated realistic population dynamics and quantified the impacts of different fishery harvest control rules. By coupling high-resolution biological realism with technical scalability, SwimmingIndividuals provides a powerful and flexible tool for a wide range of ecological inquiries. It can be used to conduct in-silico experiments into the ecosystem-scale impacts of environmental disturbances, test fundamental ecological theory, and evaluate the efficacy of complex, ecosystem-based management strategies. This framework advances our ability to build a more mechanistic understanding of marine ecosystem resilience in a changing world. Author Summary To understand and predict how marine ecosystems function, we need to account for the decisions and life histories of the individual animals within them. We have developed a new open-source software tool, SwimmingIndividuals , that acts as a “virtual laboratory” for marine ecology and fisheries science. This software allows us to create large, realistic simulations with millions of virtual organisms, from multiple taxa and species, each with its own unique set of biological traits. These modeled animals make decisions based on their internal state (e.g., hunger) and their perception of the surrounding environment, such as light and temperature. By simulating these individual actions at scale, our software allows us to see emergent, complex, ecosystem-level patterns, like population dynamics and food web structure. SwimmingIndividuals provides the scientific community with a powerful tool to investigate fundamental biological questions, explore “what-if” scenarios for fisheries management, and forecast how marine life might respond to future environmental changes.

items.title: A mosaic of bacterial communities and their functional potential across Antarctic moss, lichen and soil
items.abstract: Antarctic cryptogams and soils harbour diverse microbial communities that are fundamental to nutrient cycling and ecosystem resilience. However, the functional roles of these communities are not yet fully understood. This study investigated the bacterial communities associated with the moss Andreaea regularis, the lichen Usnea aurantiacoatra and adjacent soils in Antarctica. Metagenomic analysis revealed clear host-dependent structuring of microbial communities, with moss and soil supporting diverse and metabolically versatile assemblages, while the lichen harbored a smaller and more specialized bacterial community. Community composition exhibited significant variation among substrates, with U. aurantiacoatra dominated by Pseudomonadota and a narrow set of cyanobacteria (particularly Leptolyngbyales), whereas A. regularis and soils contained richer, more even assemblages dominated by Pseudomonadota, Actinomycetota and Cyanobacteriota. Functional profiling revealed that soil bacteria possessed the broadest metabolic potential, including a complete nitrogen cycle and multiple nutrient uptake pathways, whereas the lichen microbiome showed the most reduced representation of important metabolic pathways.

items.title: Unique and novel methanotroph taxa from the tropics: taxonomic novelty and a gateway to methane mitigation and valorization applications
items.abstract: Methanotrophs represent a distinctive group of microorganisms characterized by their specialized metabolic pathways, unique morphological traits, and diverse taxonomic classifications. These bacteria play a crucial role in the global methane cycle by oxidizing methane, a potent greenhouse gas, thereby contributing to climate regulation. Over the past decade, our research group has made significant strides in exploring methanotroph diversity, particularly within the Indian subcontinent. We have successfully identified and described several novel species and two new genera of methanotrophs isolated from rice fields and wetland ecosystems in India. These discoveries mark the first and only documented methanotrophs from India, highlighting the untapped microbial diversity of these habitats and underscoring the importance of regional studies in global microbial taxonomy. To facilitate these findings, we developed a modified cultivation technique that has proven instrumental in isolating and characterising these elusive organisms. This innovative approach has not only expanded the known diversity of methanotrophs but also opened new avenues for their application in biotechnology. The unique physiological traits of these Indian methanotrophs hold promise for biotechnological innovations, including methane mitigation strategies, biofertilizer development, and bioconversion processes. As climate change continues to pose significant challenges, the valorization of methanotrophs through sustainable technologies presents a compelling opportunity. Our ongoing research aims to harness these microorganisms for environmental and industrial applications, positioning methanotrophs as key players in the pursuit of climate resilience and ecological sustainability.

items.title: Assessing the adaptation between recreational fisheries development and aquaculture efficiency in multifunctional freshwater fisheries systems: Evidence from China
items.abstract: Abstract To examine the synergy quality and potential mismatch risks between production and recreational functions during the multifunctional transformation of freshwater fisheries, this study constructs a composite index of recreational fisheries development using panel data from 29 Chinese provinces during 2008–2023. Freshwater aquaculture efficiency is measured using a benevolent cross-efficiency model incorporating both desirable and undesirable outputs. An integrated adaptation model is then employed to capture the spatiotemporal differentiation of the adaptation relationship between the two systems, while Random Forest and SHAP methods are applied to identify nonlinear effects and threshold characteristics of key drivers. The results indicate that: (1) both recreational fisheries development and aquaculture efficiency increased steadily over the study period, whereas the composite adaptation index remained at low-to-medium levels with limited stage-wise improvement, suggesting that efficiency gains have not been effectively translated into recreational advantages; (2) the adaptation pattern exhibits pronounced regional differentiation and path dependence, characterized by persistently higher levels in central China, gradual improvement in eastern China, increasing polarization in western China, and consistently low and weakening adaptation in northeastern China; and (3) the driving mechanisms are markedly nonlinear, with water environmental pressure and tourism reception intensity acting as key constraints. Specifically, water quality pressure shows an inverted U-shaped effect with clear thresholds, while tourism intensity exerts a sustained inhibitory impact. This study provides empirical evidence for incorporating adaptation relationships into fisheries transformation assessments and for region-specific optimization of industrial structure and spatial allocation.

items.title: Persistent male survival advantage in a protogynous hermaphrodite fish
items.abstract: Abstract In many polygynous species, males face stronger intrasexual competition, higher energetic demands, and lower survival than females, especially under resource limitation or environmental stress. Such sex-specific vulnerabilities are expected to intensify with climate change. Yet, in sequentially hermaphroditic systems, where individuals change sex during their lifetime, how sex and sex change shape survival remains largely unexplored. We studied sex-specific survival and growth in the haremic protogynous cleaner wrasse Labroides dimidiatus across eight reefs around Lizard Island, Great Barrier Reef. We tracked a total of 731 adult fish (individually recognizable through marking or idiosyncratic color patterns) over two years. This period included the 2024 El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO), which caused a temporary 1-degree increase in water temperature, severe coral bleaching, and coral mortality at Lizard Island. Contrary to expectations from dioecious systems, terminal-phase males exhibited higher survival than initial-phase females under both normal and in particular ENSO conditions. While male mortality was not affected, female mortality more than doubled during the event, indicating greater physiological or energetic vulnerability. A partial explanation for the overall higher female mortality is their generally faster growth rate, which declined in both sexes during the ENSO event. Our findings challenge existing assumptions of male-biased mortality in polygynous species and highlight that sex and sex change fundamentally shape demographic responses to climate extremes.

items.title: Alpine wetland degradation reshapes the balance between hydrolytic and reductive soil nitrogen cycling enzyme potentials on the Qinghai–Tibetan Plateau
items.abstract: Abstract. Alpine wetlands on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau are increasingly degraded, threatening soil nitrogen (N) cycling and ecosystem functioning. However, how degradation restructures enzyme-mediated soil N cycling and its functional balance remains poorly understood. To address this gap, we conducted a three-year field investigation across four degradation stages (non-degraded, lightly degraded, moderately degraded, and heavily degraded wetlands) in the Gahai Wetland. We quantified four key soil N-cycling enzymes, namely urease, protease, nitrate reductase, and nitrite reductase, and developed a nitrogen cycling functional balance (NCFB) index to assess shifts in the coordination between hydrolytic and reductive functions. Degradation-induced drying and nutrient depletion reduced soil water content, soil organic carbon, total nitrogen, ammonium availability, and microbial biomass N, while increasing soil temperature and nitrate accumulation. Degradation increased urease and nitrate reductase activities but decreased protease and nitrite reductase activities, indicating enzyme-specific restructuring of soil N cycling. Most enzyme activities peaked in mid-growing season, whereas nitrate reductase peaked later. Soil N cycling shifted from a relatively coordinated state in non-degraded wetlands toward greater functional imbalance in degraded wetlands. This reorganization was strongly modulated by hydroclimatic variability, with drier conditions amplifying degradation, induced divergence in enzyme activities. Redundancy analysis and piecewise structural equation modeling showed that soil water content, organic carbon, inorganic N availability, and microbial biomass N were the primary regulators of enzyme variation and N-cycling functional imbalance. Overall, this study provides new insight into mechanisms of soil N-cycling destabilization in degraded alpine wetlands and informs wetland restoration under a drier future climate.

items.title: Three New Species of Thelymitra (Diurideae, Orchidaceae) Endemic to Aotearoa New Zealand
items.abstract: Abstract Three new species of sun orchid ( Thelymitra ) endemic to Aotearoa New Zealand are here described: T. palustris , T. scabrifolia and T. semaphora . The morphological distinctiveness of these three species has been acknowledged for decades; however, their taxonomic status has remained unresolved. Evidence from existing karyological data, recently generated DNA sequence data ( LFY and ycf 1) and morphological studies from historical and fresh collections are used here to support their formal description. Both T. palustris and T. semaphora are restricted to wet habitats north of Auckland (North Island). Thelymitra scabrifolia inhabits mostly scrub, with a similar northern North Island distribution, but it has been found also in Manawatāwhi / Three Kings Islands and historically in Otago (South Island). All three species are polyploids and are of conservation concern.

items.title: Tree species mixing shifts community-level leaf economics trait composition and functional diversity in phosphorus-limited plantations
items.abstract: Understanding how tree species mixing alters community-level functional strategies is critical for managing phosphorus-limited plantations, yet empirical evidence linking species composition to community functional composition remains scarce. Here, we investigated whether increasing tree species diversity shifts the community-weighted position on the leaf economics spectrum (LES) and enhances functional diversity in planted forests. We measured five leaf functional traits (specific leaf area, leaf dry matter content, leaf nitrogen,leaf phosphorus, and N:P ratio) across 54 plots, comprising monocultures, two-species mixtures, and three-species mixtures in the Yellow River Floodplain, China. Community-weighted means, non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS), functional dispersion (FDis), and structural equation modeling (SEM) were used to evaluate trait responses to species mixing and environmental gradients. Leaf phosphorus increased from 0.253 in monocultures ( n = 33) to 0.337 in two-species ( n = 15) and 0.467 in three-species mixtures ( n = 6; +84.6%; bootstrap 95% CI = 0.161–0.262). The three-species result should be interpreted with caution given the small sample size and limited species combinations. Functional diversity (FDis) increased from 0 in monocultures to 0.954 in two-species and 1.233 in three-species mixtures ( p < 0.001). NMDS revealed that mixed stands exhibited distinct community functional composition and occupied a significantly broader functional space than pure stands. SEM further demonstrated that the canopy–soil structure gradient (PC2) irectly and negatively associated with leaf phosphorus concentration ( β = −0.693, p < 0.001) and indirectly associated with it via decreased species richness, with the model explaining 67.5% of the variance in LTP. Collectively, our findings confirm that species mixing shifts the community-level leaf economic trait composition—particularly along nutrient-related dimensions—and enhances functional diversity in P-limited plantations, providing robust quantitative evidence that trait-based indicators can effectively guide biodiversity-oriented forest management in nutrient-poor alluvial soils.

items.title: Can't see the forbs for the grasses – Forb ecology in Indian grasslands
items.abstract: Grasslands are one of the world's most widespread and diverse ecosystems. However, ecological research in grasslands has largely focused on grasses and woody plants, while forbs, which are non-graminoid herbaceous plants, are often overlooked despite their considerable contributions to biodiversity and ecosystem functioning of grasslands. In this review we synthesize current knowledge on the ecological roles of forbs in Indian grasslands by merging evidence from the global literature with 31 studies conducted across diverse Indian grassland ecosystems. Global studies demonstrate that forbs mainly contribute to species richness, pollination, nutrient cycling, ecosystem resilience, and post-disturbance recovery, whereas Indian research has primarily documented forbs within floristic assessments or medicinal uses, with relatively few studies unambiguously investigating their functional roles. Despite their ecological and livelihood importance, forbs remain comparatively understudied in grassland disturbance research, particularly in relation to how their functional traits and species-specific strategies influence persistence and recovery under repeated disturbances such as grazing. This review emphasizes the need to recognize forbs as distinct functional groups of Indian grasslands and identifies priority areas for future research to support more effective conservation, restoration, and sustainable management of these ecosystems.

items.title: Landscape composition and connectivity explain butterfly use of clear-cuts in contrasting forest-farmland mosaics
items.abstract: Loss and intensified management of meadows, grasslands and open woodlands have caused widespread declines of butterflies in Europe. While historical forests contained dispersed open habitats as a result of windfall, wetlands, and large herbivores, many forests today are more closed and less structurally diverse through most of the forest cycle. However, temporary open habitat created by clear-cuts under rotational forestry may be used by butterflies, with their use potentially depending on connections to more permanent open habitats. In Sweden, where more than half of the land area consists of production forest with few naturally open areas, clear-cuts are ubiquitous and can provide habitat for species associated with open habitats and forest edges. We compared butterfly communities at the centre of 120 forest clear-cuts in two different Swedish regions, one with a forest-dominated landscape with little grass- and farmland (Dalarna), and one with a forest-farmland mosaic landscape (Scania). The main objective was to evaluate how butterfly use of transient, open clear-cut habitat depends on successional stage and landscape context. We combined the survey of 120 clear-cuts in 2018, 2019 and 2020 with landscape analyses. We used (i) a dbRDA to understand the drivers of community structure; (ii) GLMs to investigate the landscape and local drivers of farmland and grassland butterfly indicators; and (iii) joint species distribution models to understand how traits and phylogeny mediate species’ responses to local and landscape variables. All 14 species of the Swedish farmland indicator, and 9 out of the 12 grassland indicator species, were observed in the 120 surveyed clear-cuts. The butterfly communities differed markedly between the regions, but also with respect to the area of clear-cuts and farmland in the surrounding landscape. Most importantly, clear-cuts were used by many grassland and farmland butterfly species, with their occurrence and abundance associated with the composition of the surrounding landscape. This indicates that clear-cuts may provide functional habitats for some butterfly species, depending on their ecological requirements and the broader landscape context. Body size and larval host-plant type partly explained butterfly species distributions in clear-cuts. Our results demonstrated that use of clear-cuts is filtered by life-history traits, with the proportion of roads also associated with the occurrence of several species, highlighting the role that landscape-wide management could play for butterfly conservation even in production forests. Hence, while clear-cuts are known to have negative consequences for forest biodiversity, we show that their ubiquitous use in modern forestry could have positive incidental consequences for butterflies, with these effects depending on the broader landscape context.

items.title: Global urban tree leaf area under climate change: divergent projected trajectories and the limits of space-for-time inference
items.abstract: Abstract Urban trees moderate city climates, yet how their leaf-area density relates to projected future climates is poorly constrained globally. We fitted a Random Forest model to monthly temperature and precipitation normals and the multi-year mean leaf area index (LAI) derived from a satellite-informed machine-learning urban tree product across 21,590 urban cells, then projected end-of-century change under six Shared Socioeconomic Pathways. Leave-one-continent-out validation gave $$R^2 = 0.846$$ (95% CI $$0.813$$ – $$0.873$$ from spatial-block resampling), but that spatial skill does not transfer to time: driven by observed reanalysis anomalies over exactly the satellite record, the same relationship reproduces neither the magnitude nor the pattern of observed change ( $$\rho = +0.087$$ ). The response variable is itself a machine-learning product built from overlapping climate predictors, so the spatial fit is not independent evidence of that relationship either. Under modified Mann–Kendall tests with false-discovery-rate control, 19.8% of cells greened and 5.3% browned during 2000–2022, roughly half the browning obtained without those corrections. Global mean change is positive under all scenarios, yet 32.6% of cells decline under SSP5-8.5, with declines concentrated in tropical humid cities and gains at high latitudes. Two further results bound them: 10.6% of cells fall outside the fitted climate domain under SSP5-8.5, and four algorithms agree on the sign of change at only 68.1% of cells. We report these as changes implied by transferring a spatial relationship into future climates, not forecasts: the zonal contrast is the most reproducible result across the evaluated algorithms; cell-level magnitudes and city orderings are not.

items.title: Expanding the frontiers of Amazonian archaeology into the forest
items.abstract: Growing interest in long-term human history of Amazonia reflects the recognition that pre-colonial Indigenous societies shaped food-rich and persistent landscapes - an understanding that holds crucial implications for the region's socio-environmental conservation and sustainability. We integrated archaeological, archaeobotanical, paleoecological, and ecological approaches to investigate how and when the cultural landscapes of the Ponta da Castanha archaeological site, located within a highly heterogeneous forest mosaic in the Tefé National Forest (middle Solimões River basin, Amazonas, Brazil), were constructed. Going beyond settlement-centered perspectives, we approached living plant communities as cultural artifacts. We combined ceramic-based cultural chronologies and analyses of charred plant remains with phytolith, soil, and floristic analyses across five cultural landscapes recognized by local inhabitants: two Brazil nut ( Bertholletia excelsa ) stands, one Amazonian oil palm ( Elaeis oleifera ) stand, a transitional forest, and a mature forest. These five landscapes underwent highly dynamic and localized landscape transformations during at least five pre-colonial occupations that lasted over 3200 years. Phytolith signatures, archaeobotanical records, floristic compositions, and soil profiles indicate the introduction, promotion, and cultivation of crops, such as maize and squash, along with fire-based management and landscape clearing over time. These practices are evident from the earliest phase of occupation (Flona occupation, ca. 3200 - 2000 cal yr BP), despite low ceramic densities. The use of Brazil nut is documented since the beginning of human occupation, but the current dense Brazil nut stands seem to be a post-colonial phenomenon. Evidence of Amazonian oil palm use dates from the Late Tefé occupation (ca. 700–350 cal yr BP). Palm enrichment in the mature forest occurs throughout human occupation, intensifies during the Late Tefé occupation, and declines in the post-colonial period. By using a multi-proxy approach and integrating local perspectives, rooted in the inextricability of nature and culture, our study offers a practical framework for environmental archaeological research in tropical regions that expands and refines archaeological sampling and reveals the long-term, diverse, and place-specific landscape transformations that shaped today's heterogeneous forests in Amazonia.

items.title: Two Decades of Landscape Connectivity Science: a Bibliometric Analysis of Thematic Structure, Temporal Trajectories, and the Ecological Security Divide
items.abstract: Landscape connectivity is a central organizing concept of spatial ecology and conservation, but the breadth of systems, methods, and disciplines invoking the term obscures its intellectual structure. This study maps that structure empirically to reveal the field’s principal divisions and their trajectories. I applied bag-of-words multivariate clustering, redundancy analysis (RDA), random forest machine learning, and multivariate trajectory analysis to 6,280 landscape-connectivity papers from the Web of Science Core Collection, examining hierarchical clusters at five levels (2, 3, 6, 12, and 18 clusters). The deepest division in the field is not methodological but framework-based: a compact, rapidly growing cluster of “ecological security pattern” planning papers—concentrated in China and built on a state-led, source–corridor–node, composite-index idiom—separates from the rest of connectivity science, distinguished by a random forest with 97.7% accuracy on words including ECOLOGICAL, SECURITY, SOURCES, CORRIDORS, PATTERN, and CHINA. Finer partitions resolved a coherent methodological core of cost-distance/resistance modeling and graph-theoretic network analysis, alongside applied bodies spanning forest fragmentation, urban green infrastructure, freshwater barriers, road ecology, dispersal theory, hydrological connectivity, climate-driven range shift, corridor design, wetlands, and large-landscape conservation. Trajectory analysis showed broadly stable thematic structure over time even as the field grew, with the ecological security cluster youngest and most rapidly emerging and the resistance/network core most lexically stable. The deepest fault line in connectivity science is one of national research framing rather than methodological dispute—a structural feature with direct implications for how the field develops.

items.title: Biological legacy of large-scale coastal reclamation: Potential oxygen demand from pre-existing benthic biomass
items.abstract: Coastal-enclosure assessments commonly emphasize external organic loading, sediment processes, and hydrological exchange but rarely account for living benthic biomass that may become a transient internal organic load after habitat conversion. Omitting this pool may leave early post-closure oxygen budgets incomplete, particularly where water exchange and oxygen renewal are restricted. We evaluated this biological legacy in Saemangeum, Korea, using a three-step analysis: (1) estimating the pre-closure benthic carbon inventory and its complete-decomposition oxygen-demand upper bound; (2) using reanalyzed laboratory data to assess the temporal plausibility of rapid biomass loss and field-observed intertidal macrofaunal deficits to constrain potential demand; and (3) comparing the field-constrained estimates with standing dissolved-oxygen inventories across three effective receiving-water volumes. The compiled inventory contained 9,384 t C and yielded an all-component upper bound of 25,023 t O 2 ; excluding the transferred bacterial estimate reduced this value to 14,461 t O 2 . At 120 days after closure, the net biomass-deficit and taxon-resolved minimum-loss estimators yielded potential demands of 3,547 and 4,663 t O 2 , respectively, equivalent to 54.0% and 70.9% of the intertidal macrofaunal upper bound. The corresponding point-estimate demand-to-inventory ratios exceeded one at an effective water volume of 0.35 km 3 but remained below one at 0.83 and 1.27 km 3 . Among the tested assumptions, the inventory upper bound was most sensitive to the transferred bacterial stock, whereas the demand-to-inventory comparison was strongly influenced by receiving-water conditions. The tested alternative allocation and conversion-factor perturbations had smaller effects on the 120-day estimates. Conditional bootstrap intervals quantified sampling uncertainty in station-level means, while separate sensitivity analyses examined selected structural assumptions. These comparisons represent potential demand rather than realized oxygen consumption or predictions of hypoxia. The proposed tiered framework can identify coastal-enclosure projects requiring targeted monitoring and process-based oxygen-budget assessment.

items.title: Loopholes in Australian wildlife, cultural heritage, human tissue and biosecurity laws: four case studies
items.abstract: Abstract We provide a novel investigation into where Australian legislation, meant to mitigate commerce in material cultural heritage, wildlife products and human tissue, clash in both their scope and practical application. Through an exploratory analysis of the legal context surrounding three recent Australian auction house sales and a social media post (demonstrating an example of successful import into Australia of human remains posing clear biosecurity risk), we identify legal loopholes through which these categories of trafficking can converge. In reviewing and discussing related cases, and what precedent their verdicts might establish, we also highlight tangential bodies of legislation that could assist future prosecution of import and export violations where environmental, cultural heritage, human tissue or biosecurity laws are found lacking. We highlight future research directions that should be pursued to quantify how cultural heritage, wildlife products and human remains are sought and sold together in Australia and globally.

items.title: Drilling in ‘paradise’: environmental governance, local communities and oil exploration in the Okavango Delta, Botswana
items.abstract: Abstract Oil exploration in ecologically sensitive landscapes presents significant environmental governance challenges, particularly where extractive development intersects with wetland conservation and community livelihoods. This study examines how international, regional, and national policy and legislative frameworks regulate oil exploration in the Okavango Delta, Botswana, using a qualitative desk-based review of legal, policy, and documentary sources. The findings indicate that Botswana has a comprehensive but fragmented environmental governance framework in which international and regional instruments establish conservation principles and promote transboundary cooperation but depend largely on domestic implementation. National legislation focuses on licensing, environmental impact assessment, and mitigation measures rather than prohibiting exploration in ecologically sensitive areas, while ecosystem-specific policies and wildlife legislation enhance environmental protection through institutional coordination, enforcement, and community participation. The study concludes that the existing governance framework regulates, rather than prevents, petroleum exploration in environmentally sensitive landscapes and recommends strengthening legal safeguards, institutional coordination, and public participation to better balance petroleum development with environmental conservation.

items.title: A participatory framework involving trained citizen scientists and conservationists advances genetic understanding of an endangered carnivore
items.abstract: Although citizen science is increasingly used in biodiversity monitoring, moving beyond passive observation toward the active collection of high-quality biological samples remains a major challenge. To address this, we present a participatory framework originating as a bottom-up initiative, designed to facilitate the active and structured collection of high-quality biological samples. This conceptual framework allows for the development of a genuine partnership where collective field expertise enriches scientific data interpretation to inform conservation policy. Designed to be adapted to a wide range of conservation projects, this participatory framework is particularly effective for monitoring threatened, low-density and cryptic species across large landscapes by combining robust biological sampling with strong social engagement. We illustrate the operational strength of this framework through an eight-year case study mobilizing a network of 274 volunteers trained to collect non-invasive samples from the Eurasian lynx ( Lynx lynx ) in France, 42 untrained volunteers and a scat-detection dog. The sampling expanded across 13 departments, with the network collecting 729 scats with a 45.8% genetic confirmation rate. An anonymous online survey evaluating the human dimensions of the framework showed that despite baseline knowledge, most respondents reported gaining new insights and naturalist skills. Direct contribution to conservation was the primary motivation, and participation strengthened trust in science and data governance. Relationships with project coordinators drove long-term engagement, resulting in high willingness to re-engage in future projects. By co-constructing the research project with civil society from the outset, this framework bridges scientific expertise and local knowledge, addresses critical gaps in our understanding of the genetic health of an elusive species, and strengthens public ownership, social acceptance and scientific credibility of the findings, all of which are essential for successful conservation.

items.title: Acoustic Biodiversity And Ecosystem Integrity: A Normative Legal Approach To Sound Extinction
items.abstract: Acoustic biodiversity understood as the fusion of biological sounds (biophony), geophysical sounds (geophony), and anthropogenic sounds (anthrophony), which together constitute an ecosystem's soundscape represents an increasingly prominent element within the concept of ecosystem integrity, yet remains inadequately protected under existing environmental legal frameworks. This paper addresses the phenomenon of sound extinction )the progressive fading of natural biophonic sounds, driven by multiple causes, most notably anthropogenic noise and habitat fragmentation( as an emerging legal dimension within the field of environmental law, approached from a normative legal perspective. items.title: Technological Frontiers in Animal Ecology and Conservation
items.abstract: The accelerating biodiversity crisis requires innovative technologies to better understand and conserve animal populations and their habitats. This chapter explores how advances in remote sensing, artificial intelligence (AI), genomics, and bio-logging are transforming animal ecology and wildlife conservation. AI-powered remote sensing enables large-scale monitoring of habitat degradation, species distribution, population abundance, and illegal activities such as poaching. Genomic approaches provide non-invasive tools to assess genetic diversity, population connectivity, and detect elusive species. Bio-logging technologies generate detailed information on animal movement, behavior, health, and responses to environmental change. Despite these advances, widespread adoption is constrained by high costs, technical expertise requirements, and challenges in integrating diverse datasets. Standardized, collaborative, and cost-effective approaches are essential to translate these technologies into proactive and effective conservation strategies.

items.title: From welfare to the environment: social policy, natural resources, and ecological sustainability in G20 economies
items.abstract: Ecological degradation has emerged as a critical challenge to achieving sustainable development, particularly in G20 economies where economic growth, social welfare objectives, and environmental constraints frequently interact. Using annual data for 17 G20 countries over 2000–2021, this study examines the effects of social welfare (SCWF), economic policy uncertainty (ECPX), trade openness (TROP), life expectancy (LIEX), natural resource rents (NARN), and tourism (TRSM) on ecological footprints (ECFP). Employing a Pooled Mean Group–Autoregressive Distributed Lag (PMG-ARDL) model, the analysis captures both short-run dynamics and long-run equilibrium relationships while accounting for cross-sectional dependence and heterogeneity across countries. The findings reveal that natural resource rents and social welfare expansion significantly increase ecological footprints, indicating that resource-intensive development and consumption-oriented welfare systems can undermine environmental sustainability. Life expectancy and economic policy uncertainty are negatively associated with ecological footprints. These estimates do not establish causal effects or demonstrate the influence of environmental regulation, which is not measured in the model. Trade openness exerts mixed effects, increasing environmental pressure in the short run but promoting ecological sustainability in the long run, whereas tourism consistently intensifies ecological degradation. These findings highlight the complex trade-offs between economic prosperity, social progress, and environmental protection in G20 economies. From an SDG perspective, the results provide important implications for achieving SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 15 (Life on Land). The study advocates integrated policy frameworks that promote sustainable resource management, environmentally responsible tourism, and balanced welfare strategies to support long-term ecological resilience and sustainable development.

items.title: Critical Raw Materials in the Investment Spotlight: Commitments of Foreign Investors and Azerbaijan’s Regulatory Perspective
items.abstract: In recent years, the primary focus of international political debates has been on raw materials essential for economic development.The demand for raw materials critical to the production of modern technological tools, such as cobalt, platinum and lithium, is increasing globally.In general, the processing, development and production of critical raw materials constitute stages of the supply chain and are carried out over a long period, involving enormous investment.For this reason, the intention of foreign investors to make large profits in a short period of time leads to a careless approach to internationally accepted requirements, such as respect for human life, health and the environment.In particular, the dependence of developing countries' economies on these investments leads to a "turning a blind eye" to such violations in those countries and, as a result, to violations of many international obligations assumed by states.Based on the above, the "sustainable" development of the critical raw materials sector is significant for ensuring the well-being of the local population and protecting the environment.This article examines the obligations of foreign investors in this sector and analyzes, in detail, international experience.At the same time, the Critical Raw Materials Act and other European Union documents, which provide the most detailed regulations in this area, are reviewed with respect to their scope of application, the entities they regulate and the obligations they impose on investors and relevant gaps are identified.Additionally, the article examines the availability of critical raw materials in the Republic of Azerbaijan, the regulation of the investment climate in this area and the legal obligations of foreign investors. items.title: Kelimpahan epifit sebagai indikator dalam indeks ekologi kesehatan lamun: studi kasus Pantai Sanur Bali
items.abstract: Seagrass ecosystems are essential components of tropical coastal environments, providing critical services such as carbon sequestration, shoreline protection, and habitat for marine biodiversity. In Indonesia, these ecosystems face increasing threats from anthropogenic activities, particularly in tourism-heavy regions like Sanur, Bali. While numerous studies have assessed seagrass cover, limited attention has been paid to the role of epiphytic communities as indicators of environmental health. This research addresses this gap by evaluating the ecological health of seagrass meadows through the Seagrass Ecological Quality Index (SEQI) and epiphyte structure across five sites in Sanur. The study aimed to determine how variations in seagrass and epiphyte characteristics reflect broader ecosystem conditions under different environmental pressures. Using a transect-quadrat method, data were collected on seagrass species richness, cover, water clarity, and the percent cover of macroalgae and epiphytes. Epiphytes were microscopically identified and classified. The findings reveal that Thalassia hemprichii, Enhalus acoroides, and Halophila ovalis dominate the region. SEQI scores ranged from 0.5669 to 0.6636, categorizing all sites as having moderate ecological condition. Bacillariophyceae dominance in Samuh reflects healthier conditions, while Cyanophyceae prevalence in other sites indicates eutrophication. This study highlights the utility of seagrass–epiphyte associations as sensitive bioindicators of ecosystem quality. The integration of SEQI and epiphyte analysis provides a cost-effective, scalable approach for monitoring shallow marine environments. These insights contribute to ecosystem-based management strategies vital for the conservation and restoration of coastal habitats in Indonesia.

items.title: Mapping Biodiversity Research on Urban Forests and Green Spaces: Conceptual and Intellectual Structures and Country-Level Collaboration
items.abstract: Research at the interface of biodiversity conservation, urban forestry, and urban green space spans ecology, forestry, landscape planning, environmental management, and public health, making its intellectual structure difficult to apprehend through narrative review alone. This study maps a corpus of 3747 documents published from 2006 to 17 August 2026, retrieved from the OpenAlex API on 13 October 2026 after integrity checking and deduplication. Performance analysis, country-level collaboration networks, lexical co-occurrence on titles and abstracts (abstract coverage 82.6% after supplementation), strategic mapping, thematic evolution, co-citation, and bibliographic coupling were computed with scripts released with the article; stochastic community partitions were evaluated over 200 seeded runs. Across the complete years 2006–2025, retrieved annual output increased at a compound annual rate of 15.89%. The corpus spans 1316 journals and affiliations in 124 countries. China leads publication output, whereas Germany and the USA occupy the strongest brokerage positions in the collaboration network. Author-derived text resolves six lexical clusters (modularity = 0.442), in which health and planning vocabulary joins climate and green-infrastructure terms and carbon vocabulary joins tree and plant species, and co-citation of the 200 most cited references identifies six communities (modularity = 0.507). More than half of the corpus (54.9%) enters only through green-space terms, and removing these documents changes the lexical partition substantially; a replica of a prior green-space mapping shows that urban-forestry terms distinguish the corpus. The mapped literature is increasingly connected to climate, health, and planning agendas.

items.title: The impact of population growth on land-use: a system dynamics model for sustainable land-use planning in the Elgon Region of Uganda
items.abstract: Land-use and land-cover change poses major environmental challenge in regions where population growth increasingly drives encroachment into ecologically sensitive landscapes. This challenge arises from the dynamics of interacting feedbacks among; demographic change, declining household land size, ecosystem degradation, and delayed institutional responses. Previous studies in the context of Uganda, have investigated these factors, either independently or in pairs, but not holistically. This study developed a system dynamics model to examine the impact of population-driven land-use dynamics in the landslide prone Elgon region of Uganda. A System dynamics method was used to simulate long-term system behaviour under alternative policy intervention scenarios for sustainable land-use planning. Results indicate that the steady increase in the number of households and decline in land per household are the dominant drivers of encroachment into wetlands and forests. Population growth drives significant conversion of natural ecosystems, with forest cover declining from 317 km² in 2020 to 247 km² (22.08%) by 2050 under business-as-usual scenario, amidst rising demand for agricultural land, housing, fuelwood, and infrastructure. Wetland follows a similar trajectory, decreasing sharply from 47.7 km² to 28.3 km² (40.67%) over the same scenario. These trends are reinforced by weak institutional capacity, limited enforcement, low community participation, and inadequate coordination among conservation actors, which collectively undermine effective policy implementation. The findings also highlight the risks of business-as-usual land management and underscore the need for strengthened institutional enforcement, and coordinated conservation interventions. By explicitly capturing feedback-driven dynamics and long-term system responses, the model offers a policy-relevant decision-support tool for evaluating alternative interventions and guiding sustainable land-use planning in population-pressured regions.

items.title: Aquatic Animal Health Management through DNA Barcoding and Morphological Identification of Labeo rohita and Cirrhinus mrigala from the River Chenab, Pakistan
items.abstract: The study evaluated genetic and morphological diversity of two economically significant major carp species namely, Labeo rohita, and Cirrhinus mrigala, inhabiting the River Chenab (Chiniot Pull L1, Trimmu Barrage L2 and Head Muhammad Wala L3) Punjab, Pakistan.Fish specimens were identified structurally, and the mitochondrial COI gene sequence was utilized for genetic analysis.MEGA 11 and the K2P model were used to construct Maximum Likelihood (ML) phylogenetic trees.Using an online QR code generator, QR codes were made for accurate fish identification.With an average length of 664 base pairs (bp), 60 mitochondrial COI barcode sequences were obtained.Transitional mutations were more common than transversions.Each species showed one haplotype (H = 1), haplotype diversity (Hd) = 0.00 and nucleotide diversity (Pi) = 0.00 in the analyzed COI region.In nucleotide composition GC content (45.5%) was lower than the AT content (54.5%).The evolutionary tree showed degree of resemblance in the limit of 99% for sequences of Labeo rohita and Cirrhinus mrigala, which grouped in two clades because they were in the two genera but the same family.In the current study, DNA barcoding has demonstrated that it is a reliable approach for species identification.The molecular data generated in this study provides baseline information on species-level identification and intraspecific genetic variation of the examined carps, which may support future investigations of fish health observation, aquaculture management and fisheries monitoring.
