items.title: From detections to demography: methodological challenges and opportunities in survival estimation from automated telemetry networks
items.abstract: Abstract Survival is a fundamental demographic process influencing individual fitness and population dynamics. Automated telemetry systems offer unprecedented opportunities to estimate survival of highly mobile organisms across broad spatial and temporal scales. However, the structure of these tracking networks creates systematic biases that render standard survival models inadequate. Receiver stations are distributed unevenly across landscapes and over time, meaning that individuals taking different movement paths encounter vastly different opportunities for detection. This spatial clustering also creates problematic dependencies: animals detected in receiver-dense areas are more likely to be detected again, while those in sparse areas may disappear from view despite being alive. These observation biases can easily be mistaken for genuine differences in survival, leading to incorrect ecological or conservation inferences. Here, we review the unique challenges posed by automated telemetry data for survival estimation, highlight existing methodological solutions including spatially explicit approaches and modified capture-mark-recapture frameworks, and provide recommendations for advancing this critical application of wildlife tracking networks.

items.title: Morphophysiological development, allometric growth, and early ontogeny of the Amazonian ornamental characid Moenkhausia oligolepis (Günther, 1864)
items.abstract: Abstract This study describes, for the first time, the morphophysiological development, allometric growth patterns, and the main initial ontogenetic events of Moenkhausia oligolepis , a species of ecological and ornamental importance in the Amazon region. Hatching occurred 16 hours after fertilization, under an average temperature of 25.36 ± 0.64°C with a pH of 7.28 ± 1.11. From hatching onward, the larvae were sampled at regular intervals (0–6 hours post-hatching with collections every 2 h; 6–22 h every 4 h; and subsequently, daily collections) for morphological, morphometric, meristic, and histological analyses. Larval development spanned from the vitelline stage to the post-flexion stage (0–30 days after hatching—DAH), with a well-defined sequence of events: mouth opening and initiation of exogenous feeding at 3 DAH, cannibalistic behavior at 4 DAH, notochord flexion at 15 DAH (mean CP = 6.33 ± 0.56 mm), and the larval–juvenile transition at 30 POE with the development of fin rays and the appearance of scales. Allometric analyses revealed positive cephalic growth relative to standard length (b = 1.389 for HL/SL), indicating prioritization of the development of structures associated with feeding and sensory perception. Notochord length and preanal distance showed growth close to isometry relative to standard length, while body height exhibited negative allometry. Histological analysis demonstrated progressive differentiation of the digestive tract, with the presence of a buccopharyngeal cavity, esophagus, segmented intestine (anterior, middle, and posterior regions), and mucosal cells at 3 DAH. Cytoplasmic vacuolization was observed in hepatocytes starting at 23 DAH, associated with the presence of digested material in the intestinal lumen. The secondary lamellae of the gills exhibited evident buds at 4 DAH, and the swim bladder was divided into two regions at the end of flexion (22 DAH). Gonadal evaluation indicated undifferentiated gonads up to 50 DAH and ovarian differentiation at 60 DAH, characterized by the presence of primary meiotic oocytes; testicular differentiation was not observed during the analyzed period. Based on the observed morphological and ontogenetic characteristics, four larval stages were described (yolk sac, pre-flexion, flexion, and post-flexion). The results expand knowledge of the species’ early biology, providing relevant insights for taxonomic, ecological, and conservation studies, as well as for improving management and larviculture strategies for native ornamental fish.

items.title: Characterization of the organelle genomes of mycoheterotrophic Thismia angustimitra and evidence suggesting horizontal gene transfer
items.abstract: Abstract Background Our knowledge about mitochondrial genome evolution in plants is lacking far behind our knowledge of plastome evolution. In heterotrophic plants, it is well-known that plastome degradation and reduced or lost photosynthesis go hand in hand, and there is little if any difference between plastome evolution in mycoheterotrophic and haustorial parasites. The mitochondrial genome appears less affected by a heterotrophic lifestyle, although exceptions occur. In contrast to plastome evolution, mitochondrial evolution may differ between mycoheterotrophic and haustorial parasites, in particular with regards to the occurrence of horizontal gene transfer. However, data from mycoheterotrophs are scarce, and complete mitogenomes are only known from three of ten clades. Results Here we present data from the complete plastome and mitogenome from Thismia angustimitra , representing a fourth clade of mycoheterotrophs. The 18,215 bp plastome is much reduced and includes only few genes. The mitogenome has a multicircular structure consisting of 22 chromosomes with a total length of 422,400 bp. The gene content and the pattern of RNA editing are normal. The mitogenome includes only few repeats and recombinational activity is limited. A search for foreign DNA did not reveal any fungal sequences, and the content of plastid DNA is low. Just a few inserts appear to have originated through intracellular transfer, whereas others most likely stem from horizontal gene transfer. Conclusion The highly reduced plastome of T. angustimitra fits completely the general picture of plastome degradation in heterotrophic plants. Whereas the mitogenome in many aspects appears unaffected by the lifestyle, the recombinational activity is unusually low. Surprisingly, we find evidence of horizontal gene transfer, suggesting that this phenomenon may be more common among mycoheterotrophic plants than previously thought.

items.title: Riverine biogeochemistry from the Andes to the ocean: longitudinal patterns along a Mediterranean Andean catchment in central Chile
items.abstract: Abstract. Rivers act as dynamic connectors between terrestrial and marine ecosystems, transporting and transforming materials along the aquatic continuum. We investigated longitudinal biogeochemical patterns across the Rapel catchment (central Chile) by integrating dissolved organic matter (DOM) characterization, dissolved metals and nutrients, and microbial community profiling from the Andean headwaters to the Pacific Ocean. Headwaters were characterized by low DOC and nutrient concentrations, high protein-like fluorescence, and diverse microbial assemblages dominated by Flavobacterium, Polaromonas, and Rhodoferax. Downstream, agricultural and mining activities increased nutrient and metal concentrations and altered microbial community composition with an increasing prevalence of hgcI_clade. The Rapel Reservoir emerged as a major biogeochemical discontinuity, promoting DOM transformation, restructuring microbial assemblages, and modifying downstream chemical conditions. Overall, tributary inputs, land use, and hydrological regulation disrupted simple longitudinal patterns and generated distinct biogeochemical processing zones. These findings highlight the interplay between downstream transport and local processing in shaping riverine functioning in Mediterranean Andean catchments and provide a basis for assessing future climate and land-use impacts on riverine biogeochemistry.

items.title: Is conservation AI ready? Quantifying the challenges of automated species identification in Colombia
items.abstract: Multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly adopted by conservation organizations to overcome taxonomic bottlenecks. However, its reliability may systematically fail for sparsely documented and recently described taxa. This study evaluates automated species identification using 10,000 research-grade iNaturalist images of Colombian vertebrates across amphibians, birds, fishes, mammals, and reptiles. Testing OpenAI GPT-5.2 with localized prompts but no taxonomic metadata, we found that species-level accuracy scales non-linearly with global photographic representation and decays severely for recently recognized taxa. At the 10th percentile of data availability, predicted accuracy collapsed to 6–12% for most groups, with mammals performing best at 41%. Furthermore, severe taxonomic hallucinations frequently crossed class boundaries, particularly among fishes and reptiles. These findings demonstrate that AI errors are not random, but structurally inherent to the long-tail distributions of training data. While general-purpose AI offers immense value for rapid sorting, its operational integration requires strict safeguards, including forced abstention protocols, geographic filters, and mandatory expert escalation for rare or recently described species.

items.title: Short fire-return intervals modify fuel structure, changing flammability and fire behavior in dry forests of southeastern Australia
items.abstract: Abstract Shortening fire-return intervals are pushing fire-tolerant ecosystems in temperate Australia beyond their ecological limits, producing alternative vegetation states with markedly different composition and structure. While the structural effects of these regime shifts on fire-tolerant eucalypt forests are increasingly documented, their consequences for flammability remain largely untested. We compared fuel structure and load, surface fuel flammability, and modelled point-based fire behaviour between areas retaining a Eucalyptus overstorey under typical fire regimes (reference state) and alternative states in fire-tolerant native forests of southeastern Australia. Fuel hazard was visually assessed using an established field protocol, and surface fuels were sampled for laboratory flammability testing. Point-based fire behaviour was modelled using Vesta Mk2 across five weather scenarios spanning prescribed-burn to extreme wildfire conditions. Fuel hazard scores were significantly higher for surface and elevated strata in alternative states, but higher for near-surface and bark strata in reference states. However, laboratory flammability tests showed that surface fuels from alternative states were less ignitable, combustible, and consumable than those from reference states. Modelled fire behaviour showed consistently taller flames in alternative states across all weather scenarios, though rate of spread was greater only under the most extreme conditions. Spotting distances were consistently higher in reference states. These results show that alternative-state eucalypt forests produce a distinct fire behaviour signature: lower surface fuel flammability, greater flame height, but reduced spotting potential. The landscape-scale implications of this altered fire behaviour for subsequent fire regimes and the persistence of alternative states warrant further investigation.

items.title: Supplementation of Tannin Extracts and Islands of Plant Diversity on Cattle Grazing Brome Grass Monocultures: Influence on Behavior, Welfare, Performance and Health
items.abstract: Beef cattle grazing systems in the western United States often depend on grass monocultures that decline in nutritional quality during summer. As pasture quality decreases, cattle have fewer opportunities for selective foraging, grazing efficiency declines, and producers face increased supplementation costs to maintain animal performance, welfare, and effective pasture use. This dissertation examined whether interventions that provide phytochemicals either as a supplement or through the establishment of taxonomically diverse “hot spots” in otherwise monotonous landscapes could improve cow-calf pair performance and enhance the sustainability of agroecosystems. The study tested two strategies with free-grazing cow–calf pairs: supplementation with tannin extract and establishing of small patches, or “islands,” of diverse, phytochemically rich forage species within bromegrass pastures. Using combined GPS–tri-axial accelerometer collars, pedometers, and machine-learning methods, the study identified cattle behavioral responses to these feeding strategies with high accuracy. The study developed a monitoring system that combined GPS collars, motion sensors, and direct animal observations to classify cattle behavior while grazing. These tools were able to identify important activities such as grazing, resting, rumination, walking, and posture with high accuracy. Moderate tannin supplementation led cattle to graze longer during the evening, drink more water, change between lying and standing postures less often, and use the pasture more evenly than cattle that did not receive tannins. These responses suggest that tannin supplementation can influence grazing distribution and welfare, and may help reduce concentrated grazing pressure in free-grazing systems. Biological measurements also indicated changes in antioxidant activity, rumen microbial processes, and nitrogen use, showing that tannins had an impact on cattle through both behavioral and physiological pathways. When cattle grazed diverse forages in patches embedded in grass, their preference and selection changed over the summer. They did not graze all plants equally; instead, they showed a preference for sainfoin and adjusted their diets over time by mixing different forages. These findings show that diverse forage “hotspots” can expand feeding choices in otherwise monotonous pasture systems. By linking cattle behavior with welfare, performance, and health indicators, this dissertation shows that phytochemical-based strategies offer a practical way to improve grass monocultures during summer as forage nutritive value decline. Rather than relying solely on protein supplementation, integrating moderate tannin supplementation or establishing small patches of plant diversity can help cattle make better use of pasture resources while supporting more resilient and sustainable beef production systems.

items.title: Trends in phytoplankton communities uncovered by the Southern Ocean Continuous Plankton Recorder
items.abstract: Context Phytoplankton communities in the Southern Ocean are shifting as the region experiences rapid environmental change. Aims To investigate long-term trends or changes in Southern Ocean phytoplankton communities, and model abundance patterns of key dominant genera against sampling year and sea-surface temperature (SST). Methods Using 10 years of Southern Ocean Continuous Plankton Recorder (SO-CPR) data within a 15-year period (2007–21), we examined long-term trends in phytoplankton composition, with emphasis on six ecologically important diatom genera (Chaetoceros, Thalassiothrix, Fragilariopsis, Pseudo-nitzschia, Rhizosolenia and Corethron). Key results Overall diatom and dinoflagellate abundances increased significantly across the sampling domain, whereas the diatom:dinoflagellate ratio remained stable, suggesting little change in the relative contributions of these major phytoplankton groups despite increasing overall abundance. Patterns among focal genera differed, with distinct temporal trends and contrasting relationships with sea-surface temperature, indicating ecological differentiation among dominant Southern Ocean diatoms. Conclusions No single genus accounted for the observed increase in abundance, suggesting a community-wide response to environmental change. Implications These results demonstrated the value of long-term CPR observations for detecting trends, natural variability and ecological change in a rapidly warming Southern Ocean.

items.title: Cataxia on the edge: range contraction of endemic montane mygalomorph spiders in a biodiversity hotspot
items.abstract: Context Large shifts in species distributions are projected under future climate scenarios, yet long-term empirical evidence remains scarce, particularly for invertebrates. Aims We quantified changes in occupancy, abundance, and population structure over 22 years for four short-range endemic trapdoor spider species (Cataxia sandsorum, C. stirlingi, C. colesi, C. barrettae) and tested associations with microhabitat, environmental, and disturbance conditions. Methods Presence–absence surveys conducted in 2002 and 2024 across >250 km of replicated traverses were combined with burrow density and microhabitat assessments from 293 quadrats across 17 subpopulations. Species distribution models identified predictors of occupancy and burrow density. Key results All species showed severe contractions, with 49–67% reductions in area of occupancy and >98% declines in burrow abundance. Declines were greatest at lower elevations and in areas exposed to repeated intense fires. These areas also supported fewer juveniles and recruits. Remnant populations persist mostly in cool, moist, high-elevation gullies where orographic cloud, rocky substrates, and microhabitat complexity provide climate buffering and fire refuge. Occupancy and burrow density were strongly associated with topography and fine-scale microhabitat variables. Conclusions Despite historical persistence linked to longevity and deep-burrowing behaviour, these species have declined rapidly over the past two decades. Implications Narrow habitat requirements and limited dispersal capacity render these taxa highly vulnerable to escalating climate and fire pressures. Other co-habiting surface and shallow-burrowing relict taxa may face even greater risk. Urgent conservation action is required, including habitat protection and restoration, microhabitat enhancement, fire-regime management, assisted recolonisation, connectivity management, long-term monitoring, legislative integration, and stakeholder engagement.

items.title: Vertical space use and activity changes with seasonal climate variation in Bengal slow lorises (Nycticebus bengalensis) in Thailand
items.abstract: Abstract Most species are adapted to navigate the seasonal variations that impact their habitat use and behavior. We can use this baseline understanding of their seasonal responses to understand how they may respond to more extreme and unexpected changes. The canopy structure can provide a buffering effect for arboreal species through vertical microclimatic gradients, creating potential microrefugia. In this study we examine how seasonality impacts the activity and vertical space usage of the nocturnal Bengal slow lorises ( Nycticebus bengalensis ) in Northeastern Thailand. We collected behavioral and concurrent climatic data from June 2023 – August 2024 and used Bayesian multinomial logistic models for each season to understand the impact of loris height in the tree, temperature, and relative humidity on behavior. We found that temperature had the strongest negative association with activity levels and verticality across all seasons. When temperatures rose above average, slow loris activity declined, suggesting that the buffering effect of lower canopy layers was limited when temperatures exceeded the thermal neutral zone for this species. The lower canopy is a climate microrefugia for Bengal slow lorises, however it depends on upper canopy connectivity. As global temperatures rise due to climate change, it is essential that we maintain forest canopy structure to preserve these microrefugia, especially for nocturnal species that have no cooler period to utilize.

items.title: Preliminary Monitoring of the Small Mammal Assemblage within the Dr. Howard Reynolds Natural Area, Hays, KS Soon after the Start of Habitat Restoration Activities
items.abstract: The Dr. Howard Reynolds Natural Area at the Sternberg Museum in Hays (Ellis County), Kansas is a living exhibit of mixed-grass prairie on the outskirts of Hays. Restoration of grassland areas within the natural area started in the mid-2010s, and while this 20-acre project is small in comparison to other grassland restorations, it is still an important contributor toward grassland conservation. Seeding of pollinator plots with native forbs, prescribed burning, eastern redcedar removal, and other projects have been conducted on site to create a native mixed grass prairie area. For just over three years, June 2016 through November 2019, we performed mark-recapture surveys to gain an understanding of the small mammal assemblage in the natural area. This study was the first of such efforts at this location. Our study design consisted of four trap-nights per season with up to three seasons per year (May, September, and November). We surveyed the study site using five transects of 20 Sherman live traps each, placed ∼10 m apart. Hispid cotton rat (Sigmodon hispidus) and deer mice (Peromyscus spp.) were the two focal taxa of our statistical analyses, as other taxa were not captured at high enough rates to be tested. Populations observed in four trap years (September and November seasons from 2016 through 2019) showed capture numbers of different species did not significantly change between survey years. Our observations indicate a continued need for sampling of this assemblage to support stronger inferences regarding species population changes in an actively restored area.

items.title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and pathogen spectrum of other infectious diarrhea in Kunming, China from 2011 to 2025
items.abstract: Other infectious diarrhea (OID) is one of the most frequently reported notifiable infectious diseases in China. As the capital of Yunnan Province, Kunming serves as an important regional hub in Southwest China and a gateway to the Greater Mekong Subregion. Its patterns of regional population mobility and local disease transmission are complex and region-specific, making Kunming an informative setting for sentinel surveillance and epidemiological investigations. This study investigated the long-term epidemiological characteristics and pathogen spectrum changes of OID in Kunming from 2011 to 2025. Temporal, spatial, demographic and pathogen-related patterns were assessed using descriptive epidemiological analyses, time-series and trend analyses. Seasonal-trend decomposition using Loess (STL) was utilized to characterize long-term temporal trends and seasonal patterns of OID. Continuous wavelet transform was applied to identify periodic fluctuations and temporal changes in epidemic patterns. The Shannon-Wiener diversity index was used to evaluate changes in pathogen diversity. Joinpoint regression was performed to assess long-term incidence trends across different population groups. From 2011 to 2025, Kunming reported 152,090 OID cases, with a mean annual incidence of 134.3 per 100,000 population (range: 62.7-273.2 per 100,000). Incidence increased significantly over the surveillance period (AAPC = 11.2%, 95% CI 3.5 to 19.3), showing a marked acceleration after 2023. OID cases occurred across all age groups, with those aged 0-4 years accounting for the largest proportion (67.0%, 101,899/152,090), while incidence increased across all age groups (all P < 0.001). Among 38,902 laboratory-confirmed cases, viral infections predominated (99.2%). Rotavirus remained the most prevalent pathogen (69.7%), followed by norovirus (26.7%). Both were mainly concentrated among children aged 0-4 years (89.1% and 72.0%, respectively). Spatially, OID incidence varied across counties and districts, with increasingly synchronized regional increases observed in recent years, particularly after 2024. Our findings from routinely collected surveillance data indicate that OID epidemiology in Kunming has shifted from traditional epidemic fluctuations toward broader structural changes, characterized by expanding affected populations, evolving pathogen composition, and changing spatial epidemic patterns. Although the observed changes in pathogen composition may have been influenced by testing practices, the findings highlight increasing epidemiological complexity and emerging control challenges. Accordingly, prevention strategies should integrate population diversity, spatial differences, and pathogen composition.

items.title: Impact of Honey Bees on Native Bees in Kansas Tallgrass Prairie
items.abstract: Recent studies have shown that honey bees may impact wild bees due to competition over floral resources. In the United States, nearly a quarter of wild bee species face the threat of extinction, and managed honey bees (Apis mellifera) are also experiencing a serious decline. As a result, both wild and managed bee populations are becoming increasingly dependent on the limited native habitats. We investigated the compatibility of beekeeping with pollinator conservation in tallgrass prairie. Tallgrass prairie is home to native plant communities that conserve native organisms but can also provide key floral resources for honey bees in spring and summer. To assess the influence of managed honey bee hives, we compared native bee interactions in areas with and without honey bee colonies, examining their effects on native bee abundance, richness, and overall diversity. We found that overall wild bee abundance and diversity were lower in plots with managed hives. This indicates that managed hives may be exerting a negative influence on native pollinators. Further research is needed to examine these findings and to ensure proper management of managed honey bee and native bee populations in native prairie.

items.title: Seasonal spatio-temporal coexistence of leopard (Panthera pardus) and brown hyena (Parahyaena brunnea) in the hyper-arid landscape of southern Namibia
items.abstract: Abstract Competition and facilitation shape carnivore community structure, exerting top-down effects on subordinate species and prey and influencing spatio-temporal distributions. These dynamics have been widely studied in southern Africa's high-productivity, mesic environments, but remain poorly understood in arid ecosystems, where low predator densities, distinct prey assemblages, and limited resources constrain species occurrence and reshape expected interspecific relationships. In hyper-arid inland Namibia, leopards and brown hyenas co-occur, occupying the apex predator niche left vacant by lions and spotted hyenas. Here, we investigated the pattern of spatio-temporal coexistence between these two competitors, assessing the roles of habitat, prey, and human activity in shaping habitat use and activity patterns. Using two years of camera trapping (71 stations, 533 km² private reserve), we estimated temporal activity patterns and overlap via kernel density functions, and applied multi-species single-season occupancy models to characterize spatio-temporal niches conditional on competitor presence across dry and wet seasons. Temporal overlap remained moderate (dry season: Δ = 0.68, 95% CI = 0.57–0.79; wet season: Δ = 0.68, 95% CI = 0.53–0.82), with different activity rhythms (p < 0.01). Co-occurrence shifted seasonally: leopards and brown hyenas were spatially independent in the dry season but exerted a positive influence on each other's occupancy in the wet season. Prey abundance, distance from water, and topography were the strongest drivers of marginal occupancy. Our findings showed that leopards and brown hyenas may compete for limited resources in hyper-arid environments, coexisting through consistent temporal partitioning, seasonal spatial independence under resource scarcity, and facilitation-driven co-occurrence during productive periods.

items.title: Linking blue finance with ecological condition and coastal tourism under marine warming in Indonesia
items.abstract: Abstract Blue finance aims to sustain coastal ecosystems and tourism, but evaluating its benefits requires compatible financial and environmental records. We examine Indonesian evidence for 2015–2025 using financial reconciliation, ecological comparisons, revenue accounting and retrospective tourism prediction. Six conservation grant packages report cumulative expenditure of 41.10 billion Indonesian rupiah through 2022. Restoration-specific costs and intervention boundaries remain unresolved. At SD Point, raw hard-coral cover is 21.12 percentage points higher at the restoration locality than at the rubble locality, without independent site replication or a verified funding link. Gili Matra person-ticket receipts increased by 66.04% between 2023 and 2024, but tariff and collection changes prevent interpreting this as visitor growth. A completion-report economic model estimates positive returns across twelve protected areas using assumed counterfactual benefits; these differ from measured project effects. Across 24 evaluation months, a seasonal Bali visitor baseline outperforms ridge prediction with or without regional thermal indicators. The evidence supports expenditure accounting, ecological contrasts and revenue trends, while additional ecological benefits, net tourism income and ecological mediation remain unidentified.

items.title: Second-scale periodicity in FRB 20201124A: Coincident with critical rotation measure evolution epochs and its possible implication
items.abstract: Second-timescale periodicity (∼1.7,s) has been reported in the repeating fast radio burst FRB,20201124A at two epochs, MJD,59310 and MJD,59347. We find that these two epochs coincide with the days on which the Faraday rotation measure (RM) of the source passes through the transition between the quasi-steady and the strongly varying phases that are predicted by the magnetar+Be star binary model. To examine whether this coincidence could arise by chance, we re-fitted the secular RM evolution within the same binary framework and estimated the probability of a chance coincidence, ̊m CC Independently, and in order to cross-validate the reported periodicity, we carried out a coherent joint period search on the bursts of the two epochs, assuming a simple linear evolution of the spin period; we obtain P_0=1.70603,s and dot P =6.1 ,s,s-1 at the reference epoch, with a Gaussian significance of and . -10 consistent with the previous measurement. We propose that the two periodic epochs correspond to passages of the magnetar through the decretion disk of the Be-star companion. The captured disk material suppresses low-latitude magnetospheric emission, such that the polar-cap emission dominates and the spin period becomes detectable; alternatively, because the disk material carries substantial angular momentum, accretion increases the magnetic obliquity and thereby amplifies the periodic modulation of the polar-cap emission. The synchronisation between the burst periodicity and the magneto-ionic transition points to a link between burst activity and the dynamical evolution of the source environment. The details of the binary-model fit and of the period search are given in Appendices

items.title: Multifrequency Study of FRB 20201124A with the uGMRT
items.abstract: Abstract We present results from a monitoring campaign of FRB 20201124A using the uGMRT during its active phase between MJD 59342 and 59362. Simultaneous observations in Band 4 (550–950 MHz) and Band 5 (1060–1460 MHz) provide a uniform view of the source activity. The burst activity exhibits a frequency-dependent evolution, with the last Band-5 burst detected on MJD 59358, while Band-4 activity persisted until MJD 59362. We identified burst pairs in the simultaneously observed Band-4 and Band-5 data, with time separations of 31.8 and 52.3 ms. These separations are comparable to the short-timescale component of the waiting-time distribution, which peaks at ∼60 ms, suggesting that the multiband burst pairs may be associated with the same short-timescale clustering process. Contemporaneous FAST observations detected the Band-5 bursts but revealed no strictly simultaneous counterparts to the corresponding Band-4 bursts. These results suggest frequency-dependent burst occurrence and are consistent with patchy spectral occupancy over the 550–1460 MHz frequency range. The detected bursts exhibit diverse temporal and spectral morphologies. Consecutive bursts were observed with separations of 16.7(2)–291.5(6) ms, revealing short repetition intervals and possible subsecond quasi-periodicity. The waiting-time and energy distributions are bimodal, indicating at least two characteristic emission timescales and energy modes. Burst fluences span 1.7(3)–78(3) Jy ms, and the cumulative fluence distribution is well described by a broken power law. These results provide a simultaneous multifrequency view of FRB 20201124A during its 2021 May active episode and support a picture in which the source exhibits complex frequency-dependent activity and broadband emission behavior.

items.title: Dual-channel multi-product formulas
items.abstract: Abstract Product formula (PF) is a promising approach for simulating quantum systems on near-term digital quantum computers. Achieving a desired simulation precision typically requires a polynomially increasing number of Trotter steps, which remains challenging due to the limited capabilities of current quantum hardware. To alleviate this issue, algorithmic error-mitigation techniques such as the multi-product formula (MPF) have been introduced to suppress Trotter errors under restricted hardware resources. In this work, we propose a dual-channel MPF protocol that utilizes the average of a PF and its reversed-sequence counterpart without increasing circuit depth. Our method enables the target simulation precision to be reached with approximately half the circuit depth compared to conventional MPF schemes. This provides substantial error reduction on noisy hardware while implementing a well-conditioned MPF. We also demonstrate our algorithm through numerical simulations under a noise model, showing that our proposal achieves significantly smaller errors.

items.title: Accretion-powered flares from black hole–disc collisions in galactic nuclei
items.abstract: Abstract Black hole impacts on accretion discs in galactic nuclei can power luminous transients, but predicting their observable signatures is challenging because the post-collision flow is highly time-dependent and inhomogeneous. We present a radiative post-processing framework for relativistic hydrodynamics simulations of black hole–disc collisions. Using physically motivated prescriptions for shock heating, optical depth via an eikonal solver, and photon escape fractions that account for photon trapping and diffusion, we predict light curves and spectral energy distributions over a range of disc densities and collision velocities. Our results indicate that the emission is dominated by the long-lived accretion flow onto the secondary black hole, whose mass supply is highly super-Eddington, rather than by cooling of the unbound ejecta. In the parameter range explored, the luminosity is typically of the order of the Eddington luminosity of the secondary and can reach several times this value, and the emission is generically dominated by soft X-rays. We find that lower velocity collisions produce brighter flares, while the disc surface density mainly controls spectral evolution: low-density discs typically produce ∼keV-peaked flares with weak spectral evolution, whereas high-density discs show softer early emission and late-time hardening. A depletion-time estimate calibrated to our results suggests characteristic durations of hours to days for intermediate-mass secondaries, and yields tflare∝PQPE. We discuss implications for QPE-like transients and for the SMBH-binary candidate OJ 287. Our framework does not include radiative feedback on the gas, therefore the luminosities should be interpreted only as baseline estimates of the available power for radiation.

items.title: Nonstabilizerness Mpemba effects
items.abstract: Quantum state preparation can be strikingly counterintuitive: the fastest route to a target state need not start from the apparently closest initial condition. We uncover such a quantum Mpemba effect in the dynamical generation of quantum magic (nonstabilizerness), quantified by the stabilizer Rényi entropy, in $\mathrm{U(1)}$-symmetric random circuits initialized from tilted product states. States with lower initial magic can generate magic faster than states with higher initial magic. The acceleration is not determined solely by the conserved-charge distribution. Two initial-state families with identical initial magic and identical charge distribution exhibit qualitatively different magic-growth dynamics, depending also on the spatial structure of the initial state within each charge sector. Analogous magic Mpemba effects in $\mathrm{SU(2)}$-symmetric circuits and under nonintegrable Hamiltonian dynamics further show that the phenomenon is tied neither to Abelian symmetry nor to random-circuit dynamics, establishing quantum magic as a distinct arena for Mpemba physics.

items.title: Stardust galaxies at z>9: A dust-origin transition behind the excess of UV-bright galaxies
items.abstract: Recent James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations suggest that galaxies at z ≳ 9 may be dominated by low-opacity supernova (SN)-produced dust before efficient interstellar-medium (ISM) grain growth becomes established. Such a transition in the dominant origin and opacity of dust could naturally explain the prevalence of galaxies with extremely low dust attenuation as well as the excess of ultraviolet-bright (UV-bright) galaxies relative to most pre-JWST predictions. We investigated whether this transition, combined with a redshift evolution of the star formation efficiency, can account for these observed properties. We developed a physically motivated attenuation framework combining (i) extinction laws for SN dust processed by reverse shocks, (ii) metallicity- and dust-to-metal-dependent opacity scalings, and (iii) porous radiative-transfer geometries allowing partial UV-photon leakage. Unlike outflow-driven scenarios requiring large-scale gas evacuation, our approach preserves gas reservoirs while reducing the effective UV opacity through dust composition and geometry. We used observed and model-motivated galaxy scaling relations to follow how dust mass, metallicity, gas content, galaxy size, and star–dust geometry regulate the far-UV attenuation as galaxies evolve from an early SN-dominated dust regime towards a later ISM grain-growth regime. We find that the observed relation between far-UV attenuation, A_FUV, and stellar mass, M_̊m star, at z$>9 is best reproduced by an intrinsic FUV dust opacity of κ_ FUV ^ dust ̊m cm^2.g^ -1 $, which is substantially below standard ISM-like values. Within the baseline physical scenario adopted in this work, this low-opacity regime is naturally associated with SN-produced dust processed by reverse shocks and produces very low attenuation even in gas-rich galaxies. It reproduces galaxies with extremely low dust attenuation (GELDAs), which dominate the observed samples at z≳9. Applied to intrinsic UV luminosity functions from semi-empirical and semi-analytic models, our SN-dominated and hybrid attenuation prescriptions suppress mainly the brightest sources, bringing theoretical predictions into agreement with JWST measurements and showing that only modest dust corrections are needed once the intrinsic UV luminosity functions are close to the JWST ones. Our results suggest that the UV-bright galaxy excess at z may reflect a transition in dust origin and opacity during the earliest phases of galaxy evolution. In the most metal-poor systems, the dust content of some GELDAs may trace the chemical 'ashes' of the first stellar generations, potentially including Population III SNe.

items.title: Benchmark for quantum teleportation with nonuniform prior distributions
items.abstract: Quantum teleportation should surpass maximum fidelity thresholds possible with local measurements and classical communications. Benchmarks have been established when states are drawn from a uniform distribution of qubits or coherent states of harmonic oscillators. These are not applicable when there is prior knowledge about the input that skews the distribution. We determine the highest mean fidelity achievable for teleportation of states without using entanglement but drawn from a non-uniform prior distribution, specifically a von Mises - Fisher distribution. Using Bayesian methods, we derive benchmark functions for single qubit teleportation that utilize projective measurement on specific axes on the Bloch sphere. We demonstrate that similar results can be achieved with a coherent spin positive operator-valued measure (POVM), based upon heterodyne detection. These methods are then used to derive corresponding benchmarks for teleporting multi-qubit systems that we model as spin coherent states, covering the full range of particle number $N\in [1, \infty)$. The results show that fidelity thresholds to declare quantum advantage can be significantly higher than is typically assumed with uniform distribution.

items.title: SDSS-V LVM: Revealing the Physical and Chemical Structure of the Helix Nebula
items.abstract: Abstract We present a spatially contiguous spectroscopic analysis of the physical and chemical structure of the Helix Nebula (NGC 7293, PNG 036.1-57.1) using integral-field observations from the SDSS-V Local Volume Mapper (LVM). The nearly complete nebular coverage allows us to map extinction, electron density and temperature, ionisation structure, and chemical abundances within a common dataset. We reconstruct calibrated datacubes from the LVM row-stacked spectra and measure 41 optical emission lines from hydrogen, helium, and collisionally excited ions. The Helix is globally a low-density nebula, with characteristic electron densities of ∼102 cm−3, but shows a strongly structured thermal distribution. Te([O III]) exhibits a U-shaped radial profile, decreasing from the central cavity to intermediate radii and rising toward the outer nebula, while Te([N II]) increases outward and Te([O II]) decreases. These contrasting behaviours show that different diagnostics trace distinct ionisation zones. The spatially resolved abundance analysis yields a near-solar oxygen abundance, 12 + log (O/H) ≃ 8.7, consistent with an approximately chemically homogeneous nebula once ionisation structure is considered. Simulated long-slit extractions show that inferred O/H depends systematically on slit orientation and can remain biased after ionisation correction, demonstrating the importance of spatial coverage in strongly stratified nebulae. We also find sulfur systematically deficient relative to other α-elements, consistent with the planetary-nebula sulfur anomaly. These results highlight the power of wide-field integral-field spectroscopy for linking the thermal, ionisation, and chemical structure of extended planetary nebulae.

items.title: Transitions in the Mass-ratio and Spin Properties of Binary Black Holes in GWTC-5
items.abstract: Abstract We analyze the mass-ratio and effective-spin ( χ eff ) distributions of binary black hole mergers in the latest gravitational-wave catalog, GWTC-5, as a function of primary mass. Using hierarchical Bayesian inference with flexible Gaussian-process population models, we identify four distinct mass regions separated by transitions in both mass-ratio and spin properties. Below ∼18 M ⊙ the population strongly favors equal-mass binaries and exhibits a narrow, symmetric χ eff distribution peaked at positive values. The positive skewness previously reported for the overall population is absent from this low-mass component, and it is most likely associated with higher-mass binaries. In the range 18–30 M ⊙ , the mass-ratio distribution becomes substantially flatter, while the χ eff distribution broadens and shifts to a peak consistent with zero. The region associated with the feature near ≃35 M ⊙ returns to a narrow χ eff distribution consistent with symmetry at zero and strongly favors equal-mass binaries. Above ≃45 M ⊙ , both the mass-ratio and χ eff distributions broaden significantly. The inferred support of the spin distribution converges toward the range expected for binaries containing remnants of previous black hole mergers, making the highest-mass region fully consistent with a star cluster population of hierarchical mergers. The close correspondence between transitions in mass ratio and effective spin suggests that different primary-mass ranges trace distinct formation channels, with isolated binary or triple evolution likely dominating the lower-mass population and dynamical assembly becoming increasingly important at higher masses.

items.title: Depth-reduced quantum simulation of Lindbladian dynamics via adaptive variational quantum trajectory compression
items.abstract: Abstract Quantum simulation of open quantum systems in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era is hindered by the non-unitary nature of dissipative dynamics and the limited quantum resources available on near-term quantum processors, namely restricted qubit counts and noise-limited circuit depths. In this work, we propose an efficient quantum algorithm for simulating Lindbladian dynamics on NISQ devices. For open quantum systems with Pauli dissipations, we first derive a compact and stable mixed-unitary adjoint channel that approximates the target dissipative dynamics and enables ancilla-free implementation through trajectory sampling. To further reduce the circuit depth required for implementing the sampled trajectories, we introduce an adaptive variational quantum trajectory compression framework. In this framework, a depth-adaptive parameterized quantum circuit is trained to approximate repeated Trotterized Hamiltonian simulation operators, which are then used to replace repeated unitary segments appearing in the sampled trajectories. Importantly, the training procedure can also be performed without auxiliary qubits. Numerical simulations of the dissipative quantum XY model and the interacting disordered XXZ chain demonstrate the accuracy and reduced execution gate counts of the proposed algorithm. Our results provide a practical route toward ancilla-free and depth-reduced simulation of open quantum systems on near-term quantum hardware.

items.title: Leptogenesis with a sub-electroweak-scale reheating temperature
items.abstract: We study the generation of the baryon asymmetry of the Universe via leptogenesis during the post-inflationary reheating epoch, considering reheating temperatures below the temperature of sphaleron freeze-out. Within the framework of a monomial inflaton potential during reheating, we analyze three perturbative reheating scenarios in which the inflaton decays into (i) a pair of Standard Model (SM)-like bosons, (ii) a pair of SM-like fermions, or (iii) exclusively into a pair of heavy right-handed neutrinos, which eventually decays into the SM final states after briefly dominating the energy density of the Universe. For each case, we identify the regions of parameter space that successfully reproduce the observed baryon asymmetry consistently tracking the sphaleron interaction rate during reheating, while satisfying existing cosmological constraints. We also highlight the potential of future primordial gravitational wave observations to probe this class of scenarios.

items.title: Relative dispersion and eddy diffusivity in laboratory experiments of β-plane turbulence
items.abstract: We present the first experimental measures of relative dispersion and turbulent diffusion in rapidly rotating turbulence in the zonostrophic regime, i.e. in the presence of instantaneous and dominant zonal jets. Synthetic Lagrangian trajectories are computed from time-resolved experimental velocity fields, from which we measure relative (two-particle) dispersion. Time-based and separation-based statistics are calculated, including the cumulative inverse separation time (CIST), for which analytical predictions exist in the inertial ranges (direct enstrophy cascade and inverse energy cascade) and in the diffusive regime. These statistics show evidence of a transition from a Richardson regime at scales larger than the energy-injection scale, to a diffusive regime, at scales larger than the transitional scale, the scale at which turbulence becomes anisotropic owing to the interaction between turbulent eddies and Rossby waves. The analytical predictions for the CIST allow us to measure the turbulent energy dissipation rate in the Richardson regime and the turbulent diffusivity in the diffusive regime. Our measurements of diffusivity are broadly consistent with predictions from mixing length and zonostrophic theories but suggest a shallower dependence on the energy dissipation rate. This article is part of the theme issue 'Anti-diffusive transport and layering: from sub-cellular to astrophysical scales'.

items.title: Raman-Assisted Multiband Nonlinear Frequency-Conversion Network in a High- Q LTOI Microdisk
items.abstract: Abstract On-chip nonlinear frequency conversion offers a key route to broadband coherent light sources, but spanning telecom, visible, and ultraviolet wavelengths within a single resonator remains challenging. Lithium tantalate-on-insulator, which has recently emerged as a promising material platform for integrated photonics, combines strong Raman activity, a large second-order nonlinearity, broad optical transparency and high resistance to photorefractive damage, thereby attracting increasing attention for on-chip nonlinear frequency conversion. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a Raman-assisted multiband frequency-conversion network in a high-Q lithium tantalate-on-insulator microdisk with a loaded quality factor of 2.48 × 106. Under separately optimized operating conditions, the device produces high-purity single-mode Raman lasing with a threshold of 3.14 mW, a slope efficiency of 32.44%, and a side-mode suppression ratio of 29.5 dB, as well as multiple Stokes lines and an anti-Stokes line. Together, the directly observed Raman fields and the intermediate Stokes fields inferred from energy conservation define a network of cascaded χ(2) pathways that generates near-infrared and visible emission and extends to 312.6 nm in the ultraviolet. These results demonstrate cooperative Raman and second-order nonlinear interactions across widely separated spectral bands in a single microcavity, providing a route to integrated multiband sources and a platform for studying coupled nonlinear dynamics.

items.title: High-precision numerical framework for the time-varying solar neutrino flux with full Earth matter oscillation corrections for global underground laboratories
items.abstract: Solar neutrinos have been studied for over half a century to test both the Standard Solar Model and the electroweak sector of the Standard Model of particle physics. Contemporary experiments are now entering an era of high-precision measurements, demanding corresponding theoretical predictions with sub-percent accuracy to enable meaningful comparison. In this paper, we identify and analyze the essential physical and computational components required to compute solar neutrino fluxes with high fidelity, and present a unified, computationally efficient framework. This framework incorporates: (i) the time-varying Earth-Sun distance; (ii) Earth matter effects modeled using both one-dimensional (1D) and three-dimensional (3D) Earth electron-density profiles; and (iii) a fast, Strang-splitting-based implementation of the Mikheyev-Smirnov-Wolfenstein (MSW) neutrino propagation formalism, enabling rapid, large-scale scans over neutrino trajectories and energy grids. We deliver site-specific predictions for the China Jinping Underground Laboratory (CJPL) and other underground laboratories actively engaged in solar neutrino programs.

items.title: Quantum Estimation Theory with Quantum Noise Control
items.abstract: Quantum estimation theory serves as one of fundamental backbones of quantum Shannon information theory and was mathematically systematized by pioneers of quantum information science. Although its applied research saw limited progress for a long period, the 21st century has witnessed active discussions and numerous fruitful proposals regarding its applications. Notably, the contributions of Monras and Paris represent one of the most remarkable achievements addressing the realization problem of estimation bounds. This paper aims to demonstrate a practical direction for extending their original ideas. Next-generation quantum information mechanisms urgently demand guarantees of quantum advantage unattainable by classical theory, alongside strict real-time processing without delays. By leveraging the concept of generalized heterodyne detection proposed nearly half a century ago, we demonstrate that a scheme based on their results can effectively meet the stringent requirements of near-future information technologies.

items.title: Direct Measurement of Polar Coronal Hole-like Solar Wind in Its Acceleration Phase
items.abstract: Abstract The early evolution of fast polar coronal hole (PCH) solar wind remains largely unconstrained by in situ measurements. In 2025 March, Parker Solar Probe (Parker) at its closest approach of 9.86 solar radii ( R ⊙ ) measured outflow from a large equatorial coronal hole (ECH), which was also measured at 1 au and at intermediate distances by Solar Orbiter (also near its perihelion). At 1 au the stream properties are consistent with PCH properties established by Ulysses. The stream was measured by Parker substantially below the Alfvén surface, with proton temperatures in excess of 2 MK and a speed at ∼10 R ⊙ which was only ∼60% of its asymptotic value. The Solar Orbiter data indicate that the acceleration is largely complete by 60 R ⊙ . Spherically polarized fluctuations in the stream are observed to develop from near-transverse and small-angle at Parker to full reversal “switchbacks” at Solar Orbiter. Comparison of the implied acceleration profile to historical Doppler-dimming measurements suggests that the stream’s low coronal acceleration is similar to that of PCH flows. Consistent with previous work, this acceleration requires significantly more energy than can be provided by the observed thermal pressure gradients, with a significant contribution likely from the abundant Alfvénic fluctuation energy observed at Parker. These observations provide unique constraints on models of the radial evolution of the fastest solar wind, and indicate that these wind streams experience gradual, steady acceleration over their first few tens of solar radii of evolution.

items.title: Magnetic Fields in Massive Star-forming Regions (MagMaR). IX. Radiative Torque Alignment and Disruption in NGC 6334I
items.abstract: Abstract Intense radiation from high-mass stars is expected to significantly affect dust grain alignment and evolution through radiative torques (RATs). We investigate this effect in a massive star-forming region, NGC 6334I, using 1.2 mm dust continuum polarization observations from the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array. The polarization fraction spans from ≲1% to ∼10% and decreases with increasing column density, remaining below 2% in dense cores despite high temperatures (∼100 K), where efficient grain alignment by RATs is expected. We investigate how grain alignment, grain growth, grain disruption, B -field tangling, and local physical conditions affect the polarization properties of MM1, MM2, MM3, and their surroundings. Polarization-angle dispersion shows that B -field tangling contributes to depolarization at moderate densities but cannot fully explain the lowest-polarization fractions. Using RAT-based grain alignment and polarization modeling, we find that reduced alignment efficiency and high optical depth reproduce the low polarization in the densest regions. MM2 shows evidence of grain growth, with maximum grain sizes a max ∼ 0.35 – 1.0 μ m, while MM1 exhibits smaller values of ∼0.35–0.50 μ m. Accounting for optical depth increases the inferred grain sizes in MM1 to ∼1.0–2.0 μ m. Analytical estimates of RAT disruption from the intense outburst suggest that micron-sized grains in high-temperature, moderate-density regions can fragment into submicron grains. Alternatively, high optical depth may also explain the low polarization in the densest regions even in the presence of micron-sized grains. Incorporating the B -field inclination effect indicates a transition from predominantly plane-of-sky fields at low densities to more line-of-sight-aligned configurations at high densities.

items.title: Tidal Love numbers of wormholes as black-hole mimickers
items.abstract: We study the dynamical scalar tidal Love numbers of wormholes that provide viable mimickers for black holes, focusing on thin-shell Schwarzschild and Damour-Solodukhin geometries. Using a matched near- and far-zone expansion, we determine their tidal response in the low-frequency regime. The presence of a long throat introduces an additional characteristic scale and naturally separates the modes into two classes. Super-throat modes probe the global wormhole geometry and are sensitive to both asymptotic regions, whereas sub-throat modes probe only one side of the wormhole and effectively perceive the throat as a black-hole horizon. We derive the scalar tidal Love numbers analytically for both classes of modes and show that their dissipative parts exhibit distinct low-frequency behavior, reflecting whether one or both potential barriers participate in the scattering process. We further find that, as the wormhole approaches the black-hole limit, the super-throat contribution becomes progressively negligible, while the sub-throat response smoothly reduces to that of a Schwarzschild black hole. These results demonstrate that the tidal response of wormholes depends crucially on whether the perturbation probes the global structure of the throat.

We adopt scattering transforms (ST) as our summary statistics sensitive to the non-Gaussian features of foreground residuals and to their correlation with foregrounds tracer maps. items.title: WFST Follow-up of S251112cm: Searching for an Optical Counterpart to a Subsolar-mass Compact-binary Merger Candidate
items.abstract: Abstract Electromagnetic counterparts to gravitational-wave (GW) sources probe the properties, environments, and evolution of compact-object mergers. S251112cm belongs to an emerging class of GW candidates with possible subsolar-mass components. We present an optical counterpart search for S251112cm with the Wide Field Survey Telescope (WFST). The observations began 20.2 hr after the GW trigger and continued for 3 nights, covering approximately 780 deg 2 and 51% of the localization probability in the updated skymap. We searched for newly emerging, rapidly evolving, off-nuclear optical transients and identified four candidates whose host-galaxy distances are broadly consistent with the GW distance estimate. However, all four evolve substantially more slowly than AT 2017gfo, ruling out an AT 2017gfo-like origin and disfavoring their association with S251112cm as rapidly evolving kilonova counterparts. Combining WFST and DECam observations increases the covered localization probability to approximately 67%. Conditional on the counterpart lying within this footprint, we constrain a grid of binary-neutron-star kilonova models. For viewing angles θ obs < 60 ∘ , with the other parameters fixed to the best-fitting values for AT 2017gfo, models with dynamical ejecta mass M dyn ≳ 0.01 M ⊙ or wind ejecta mass M wind ≳ 0.05 M ⊙ are disfavored over most of the covered GW probability. Beyond kilonova models, our phenomenological analysis constrains rapidly evolving optical transients with T rise,1/2 ≤ 2 days to peak absolute magnitudes fainter than approximately −13 mag. To our knowledge, WFST provides the strongest optical constraints to date in the northern sky on possible rapidly evolving counterparts to this new class of GW candidates involving subsolar-mass compact objects. The comparable depths and complementary sky coverage of WFST and DECam extend these constraints across a larger fraction of the localization region at similar sensitivity.

items.title: Searching for Massive Remnant Planetary System Hosts with White Dwarf Gaia XP Spectra
items.abstract: Abstract Remnant planetary systems around massive white dwarfs ( M WD > 0.8 M ⊙ ) are intrinsically rare and remain poorly characterized. As the evolutionary endpoints of intermediate-mass B- and A-type stars, these white dwarfs provide valuable constraints on the formation and survival of planetary systems around higher-mass progenitors. In the absence of large, dedicated spectroscopic surveys, extremely low-resolution Gaia XP spectra provide a powerful means of identifying candidate metal-polluted white dwarfs. We obtained follow-up observations with low-resolution optical spectroscopy ( R = 500–4000) to search primarily for Ca ii H&K absorption in massive, metal-polluted white dwarf candidates selected from Gaia XP spectra to increase the sample of massive remnant planetary system hosts among objects with effective temperatures below ∼15,000 K. We find that Gaia XP spectra recover metal-polluted white dwarfs efficiently, confirming 82% ± 5% recovery of photospheric metals (59 of 72 targets) in high-confidence candidates of our sample (with classifier probability P DZ > 0.65). However, Gaia photometric masses derived from G , G BP , and G RP broadband photometry are not sufficient to identify the most massive systems, as reliable mass determinations require detailed metal-enriched atmospheric fits. We present a selection of cool white dwarfs confirmed to be both massive and metal-polluted, demonstrating that Gaia XP spectra can substantially expand the sample of white dwarf exoplanet hosts. Our search led to the discovery of a new transiting debris system, SDSS J1624+5404, the 21st published system to date and eighth to show periodic transits.

items.title: Radio Quasars in the Cosmic Dawn: A Spectroscopic Sample from the DESI Survey
items.abstract: Abstract We present the largest statistical spectroscopic sample of radio quasars at 4.7 ≤ z ≤ 6.7 to date. These have been selected from a dedicated Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument target program and provide a robust sample to study the influence of radio jets on early quasar evolution. Using low-frequency radio data from the LOFAR Two Metre Sky Survey Data Release 3 at 144 MHz, we identify 83 high- z radio quasars, 26 of which are classified as radio-loud (5%–15% of 646 confirmed high- z quasars, defined as R = F 5GHz / F 4400Å > 10). With radio luminosities of ∼10 25−28 W Hz −1 , the radio emission in all 83 quasars is expected to be jet dominated rather than powered by star formation. Analysis of their rest-frame ultraviolet spectra reveals broadly similar composite spectral properties and C iv velocity shifts compared to radio-nondetected quasars. The radio-detected and radio-loud quasars exhibit slightly smaller Ly α and C iv equivalent widths on average; however, we find no significant evidence (∼1.3 σ ) for a higher fraction of weak-line quasars (∼10% ± 4% versus ∼4% ± 1% for radio-nondetected quasars). We further find that the broad absorption line (BAL) quasars are predominantly radio-quiet, and no correlation is observed between absorption index and radio-loudness, suggesting that radio emission is not produced by the BAL outflows themselves and is a physically distinct phenomenon. Our results demonstrate that powerful radio jets were already well established by z ∼ 5.

items.title: Estimates of Magnetic Field Strength in the Solar Corona Using Observations of Thermal Radio Emission at Low Frequencies
items.abstract: Abstract Measurements of the magnetic field strength in the solar corona at heliocentric distances r ≳ 1.1 R ⊙ , using observations other than transient radio bursts, are rare. Circular polarization observations of thermal bremsstrahlung radio emission at frequencies 1.1 R ⊙ in the solar corona, can be effectively used for this purpose. The thermal bremsstrahlung emission is randomly polarized, but in the presence of a magnetic field, it propagates in two oppositely polarized circular modes whose differential absorption in the medium results in an observable circular polarization. We report a case study of two-dimensional imaging observations of the abovementioned circular polarization in the solar corona at 51 MHz using the Gauribidanur Radioheliograph (GRAPH) and estimates of the associated coronal magnetic field strength. The peak degree of circular polarization ( dcp ), calculated from the observed total and circularly polarized intensity images with the GRAPH, is ≈2.7%. Using ray-tracing simulations, we find that the observed peak dcp corresponds to a radio source located at r ≈ 1.65 ± 0.15 R ⊙ at 51 MHz, and its field strength is ≈ 1.55 ± 0.3 Gauss.

items.title: Effects of Alfvénicity on the compressible energy cascade in magnetohydrodynamic solar-wind turbulence: Evidence from Parker Solar Probe, Solar Orbiter, and WIND observations
items.abstract: The compressible magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) energy cascade in the solar wind is shaped by Alfvénicity, plasma fluctuations, and proton temperature, yet how they regulate the relative contributions of compressible and incompressible energy transfer across heliocentric distances remains poorly understood. We aim to investigate how Alfvénicity, plasma fluctuation amplitudes, and proton temperature regulate the compressible and incompressible MHD energy cascade rates in the solar wind and how the two components of the compressible cascade, the Yaglom-like term and the purely compressible term, respond to changes in plasma conditions. We applied compressible and incompressible exact relations to a large statistical sample of two-hour intervals from WIND (1 au), Parker Solar Probe (PSP; $ 0.75$) or non-Alfvénic ($|σ_c|<0.25$) based on the normalized cross helicity and further separating them by solar-wind speed. The velocity-fluctuation amplitude is found to be the strongest predictor of the compressible cascade rate, łangle|ɛ_c|̊angle, among the variables examined, followed by density and magnetic-field fluctuations. łangle|ɛ_c|̊angle and łangle|ɛ_i|̊angle are tightly correlated across all regimes, with their ratio organized by Alfvénicity and wind speed---non-Alfvénic and Alfvénic fast winds cluster along łangle|ɛ_c|̊angle = łangle|ɛ_i|̊angle---while Alfvénic slow wind shows a systematic excess consistent with internal energy contributions. Across all regimes, the intervals with the largest łangle|ɛ_c|̊angle are systematically the hotter ones, with increases of nearly 1.5 and two decades in Alfvénic slow and non-Alfvénic wind, respectively---a trend primarily carried by the purely compressible cascade---while the dominant Yaglom-like term appears to control the overall cascade magnitude. Our results indicate that Alfvénicity and wind speed govern the efficiency of turbulent energy transfer across heliocentric distances. The tight coupling between compressible and incompressible cascade rates points toward the need for compressible, multi-fluid descriptions to fully capture the turbulent dissipation budget in the solar wind.

items.title: Large Offsets of Double-neutron-star Mergers: Degeneracies and Implications for Host Associations
items.abstract: Abstract The projected offset of a gamma-ray burst (GRB) from its host galaxy is an important diagnostic of its physical origin, where the host associations are usually evaluated through chance-coincidence probabilities. However, as shown by observations, the host associations given by this approach may be ambiguous in some cases. In this work, we revisit the modelling of the offsets of double-neutron-star (DNS) mergers with controlled numerical experiments using Monte Carlo simulations. To isolate the dynamical effects of the second supernova (SN) from uncertainties in the upstream binary evolution, we parametrize the direct progenitor of DNSs and integrate the post-SN trajectories in galactic potentials using galpy . Complementary to previous population synthesis calculations, our Monte Carlo tool, GRB-offset , provides a lightweight framework to identify sensitivities and expose degeneracies in offset modelling. With GRB-offset , we have investigated the following physical ingredients: SN physics (ejected mass and kick velocity), galactic potential (potential shape, galaxy virial mass), DNS birth location, star formation history, and redshift. The offset distributions given by our reference Monte Carlo simulation peak at around 30 and 1000 kpc for the DNSs bound to and unbound from the host galaxy, which sensitively depends on the considered physical ingredients. A given offset can arise from various combinations of these ingredients, introducing substantial degeneracies when interpreting observed offsets. Therefore, an observed offset alone can hardly constrain the properties of the DNS progenitor and of the host galaxies.

items.title: Giant Impacts Preferentially Remove Low-mass Atmospheres: A Generalised Scaling Law for Impact-driven Atmospheric Loss
items.abstract: Abstract Impact-driven atmospheric loss plays a key role in shaping the diversity of planetary atmospheres. However, existing prescriptions for calculating loss from a given impact neglect the critical role of atmospheric mass on loss, and thus often severely miscalculate the extent of loss. Using 3D smoothed particle hydrodynamics simulations, we quantify atmospheric loss during giant impacts onto planets with 1%–20% mass fraction atmospheres and show that less massive (lower-pressure) atmospheres are significantly easier to remove. We derive a new scaling law for atmospheric loss that includes the effects of atmospheric mass and is applicable to collisions between volatile-poor planetary embryos through to super-Earths and sub-Neptunes. Applying our scaling law to N -body simulations of solar system formation, we show that including the coupling between atmospheric mass and loss efficiency results in significantly more atmosphere removal. Substantial atmospheric loss events are common for smaller planets (≲0.6 M ⊕ ), while even roughly Earth-mass bodies lose 30%–100% of their atmospheres through multiple impacts. We also show that atmospheric loss during the Moon-forming impact strongly depends on both the pre-impact atmospheric mass and impact style. For a representative ∼100 bar pre-impact atmosphere, Earth could have lost between 20%–80% of its atmosphere. In any system that undergoes a phase of giant impacts, the atmospheres of its host planets will be unavoidably shaped by the stochasticity of impacts. Our new scaling law can be readily incorporated into models of planet formation and system-wide evolution, offering new insights into the origins of planetary diversity.

items.title: Discovery of Hidden Extragalactic Pulsars in the Parkes Archival Data
items.abstract: Abstract Just over 1% of the known radio pulsar population resides in the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds (MCs), the satellite galaxies that are 50–62 kpc away from the Milky Way. These pulsars are important for constraining the peak of the pulsar luminosity function, and may give insights into neutron star populations formed from stars of different metallicities than the Milky Way. Using search techniques that have proven highly effective at discovering a large number of pulsars in archival data by folding candidates near the noise floor at high harmonic folds, we reprocessed the original Parkes Multibeam MC surveys and discovered six pulsars. Five of these pulsars are located in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC), including one with a spin period of 3.8 s, making it the slowest pulsar known in the MCs. The remaining pulsar was detected toward the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC), and is associated with the Milky Way foreground. Four of the newly discovered pulsars exhibit scintillation, with one showing clear nulling and others showing possible nulling behavior. These discoveries bring the total number of radio pulsars known in the LMC to 49. A luminosity function and duty-cycle analysis of all current MC pulsars shows that they are consistent with Galactic canonical pulsars. Population-synthesis simulations suggest that deeper surveys would reveal many more pulsars in the MCs, including up to a handful of millisecond pulsars, based on the adopted upper limits for their parent populations. Finally, this reprocessing demonstrates the continued importance of reanalyzing archival data, both to improve the completeness of pulsar surveys and detect scientifically valuable objects.

items.title: Dynamically Coupled Three-dimensional Cloud Chemistry in Rapidly Rotating Irradiated Atmospheres: An Application to the Compact White Dwarf–Brown Dwarf System ZTFJ0038+2030
items.abstract: Abstract Clouds and disequilibrium chemistry shape the observable properties of substellar and planetary atmospheres, and JWST time-resolved spectroscopy now enables direct tests of their three-dimensional (3D) structures. We present an update to the 3D atmospheric framework ADAM , coupling the dynamical core to a miniature kinetic chemistry scheme (mini-chem) and a saturation–relaxation-tracer cloud module. Using this framework, we investigate the atmosphere of the brown dwarf orbiting the white dwarf ZTFJ0038+2030 in a 10 hr orbit. The brown dwarf receives stellar irradiation comparable to its internal heat flux, placing the atmosphere in a regime where the circulation is characterized by a standing Matsuno–Gill wave response and equatorial superrotation. Rapid rotation confines these structures closer to the equator, producing more symmetric broadband light curves with smaller hotspot offsets than canonical hot Jupiters, in agreement with recent JWST observations of this system. Circulation-driven disequilibrium chemistry enhances global mean CO and CO 2 while slightly reducing H 2 O, CH 4 , and NH 3 relative to chemical equilibrium. Although most species are globally homogenized, rapid rotation limits global-scale horizontal mixing and allows circulation-driven vertical transport to maintain strong CO and CO 2 inhomogeneities in the photosphere. These chemical inhomogeneities produce asymmetric phase curves in the CO and CO 2 absorption bands, which could qualitatively explain the observed CO 2 light-curve asymmetry. When clouds are included, Na 2 S clouds dominate the photosphere and weaken the large-scale circulation, lowering photospheric CO and CO 2 abundances, while MgSiO 3 and Fe clouds rain out at deeper levels. Because the dominant Na 2 S clouds reside mostly above the quench region, cloud-driven convection has limited impact on the quenched abundances, which are instead regulated mainly by large-scale circulation.

items.title: Stationary Resistive MHD Solutions near an Isolated Three-dimensional Magnetic Null
items.abstract: Abstract Magnetic null points define the topology of magnetic fields in stellar coronae, planetary magnetospheres, and astrospheres and are commonly associated with magnetic reconnection. We investigate the local structure of stationary 3D resistive, incompressible magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) flows in the vicinity of an isolated magnetic null and an isolated velocity stagnation point, assuming that the two nulls are colocated. The governing MHD equations are solved self-consistently using a first-order local expansion of the magnetic and velocity fields about the null. For any given magnetic-null configuration, the equations admit a two-parameter family of stationary solutions, comprising multiple solution branches with distinct velocity topologies. Along these families, the velocity-null polarity can change at bifurcation points where the flow becomes effectively 2.5D. A single magnetic null can therefore support positive-radial, negative-radial, and spiral stagnation flows, with qualitatively different inflow, outflow, and rotational properties. The associated pressure and resistivity distributions are likewise determined self-consistently and vary across the solution family, demonstrating that they are coupled to the flow topology rather than prescribed independently. The generic solutions do not require the velocity and magnetic separatrices to coincide, allowing plasma to cross the magnetic fan separatrix and providing a local reconnective flow. These results demonstrate that, in the presence of nonuniform resistivity, the magnetic topology alone does not uniquely determine the associated stationary flow, pressure, or resistivity structure around a 3D magnetic null, revealing the nonlinear feedback between all macroscopic variables and resistivity. The constant-resistivity field-aligned and spiral field-crossing solutions identified previously are recovered as special cases.

items.title: Unveiling the correlation between the UV 2175 Å dust attenuation bump, PAH emission, and gas-phase metallicity at cosmic noon
items.abstract: The UV 2175,Å attenuation bump is one of the most prominent yet poorly understood features of galaxy attenuation and extinction curves. It is observed from the local Universe up to z∼ 7, but its physical origin remains uncertain. Its main carrier candidate is polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) molecules, which are more prevalent in high-metallicity environments. We present the first systematic study of the relationship between the PAH abundance and the UV attenuation bump in 49 galaxies at cosmic noon (1.5<z<2.7), and we examine its dependence on the stellar mass (M_*), star formation rate (SFR), and V-band optical depth (τ_V). For 19 galaxies, we also explore the role of gas-phase metallicity via oxygen abundance measurements. We measured the UV bump amplitude using VLT/MUSE spectroscopy from the MUSE/HUDF survey. Galaxy properties, including the PAH-to-dust mass fraction q_̊m PAH, were derived via spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting with , combining JWST/NIRCam and JWST/MIRI photometry (λ_ Prospector ̊m rest at z=2). Oxygen abundances were obtained from strong-line diagnostics using Keck/MOSFIRE and JWST/NIRSpec data. We find a positive correlation between the UV bump amplitude E_̊m bump and q_̊m PAH (Spearman ̊ho=0.60); at low q_̊m PAH, UV bumps are rarely detected, supporting PAHs as the primary carriers. Both E_̊m bump and q_̊m PAH correlate with M_*, oxygen abundance, and τ_V, and they anticorrelate with the specific SFR (sSFR), indicating that PAHs and the UV bump are suppressed in low-metallicity, dust-poor, and/or intensely star-forming environments. This is consistent with the destruction of PAHs in regions with limited dust shielding and/or strong radiation fields produced by young stellar populations. A principal component analysis of E_̊m bump, q_̊m PAH, τ_V, sSFR, and oxygen abundance explains 97% of the data variance, supporting previous findings that reported correlations with M_* reflect an underlying correlation with metallicity. Finally, variations in dust geometry can explain the wide range of UV bump amplitudes (sim0-0.5,mag) at high q_̊m PAH.
