items.title: Investigating the relationships between vegetation and climate across China and the regulatory role of terrain conditions
items.abstract: Terrestrial Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) is pivotal to the global carbon cycle, and its response to climate change is strongly regulated by topographic conditions through complex, non-linear mechanisms that remain poorly quantified at macro scales. Integrating multi-source remote sensing data with structural equation modeling (SEM), geographical detectors, and generalized additive models (GAM), this study investigated the spatiotemporal dynamics of GPP and its non-linear responses to coupled climate-topography gradients across China from 2001 to 2020. Results revealed a significant increasing trend in GPP across nearly 80% of China, with precipitation identified as the dominant driver, surpassing temperature and radiation. Topography significantly modulated climate sensitivity by redistributing hydrothermal resources. A distinct transition in dominant limiting factors was observed along the altitudinal gradient, shifting from water-limited ( 3000 m) regimes. Notably, mid-altitude regions (1000–2000 m) exhibited the highest sensitivity to precipitation, representing an ecological "sweet spot". Furthermore, we quantified critical ecological thresholds for climatic drivers, identified saturation points for temperature (~17.4°C) and precipitation (~1974 mm), and an inhibition threshold for solar radiation (>101 W/m²). These findings elucidate the transition mechanisms of climatic constraints and non-linear thresholds in complex terrain, providing robust scientific evidence for region-specific ecosystem and carbon management.

items.title: Biases and gaps in freshwater mollusks research in Latin America and the Caribbean: a multi-decadal bibliometric analysis (1976–2024)
items.abstract: Abstract Freshwater molluscs play key ecological roles in aquatic ecosystems, yet they are among the most threatened and least studied invertebrate groups worldwide. This study evaluates how scientific knowledge on freshwater molluscs is structured across Latin America and the Caribbean, testing the hypothesis that research effort is uneven and shaped by multiple knowledge shortfalls that constrain ecological understanding and conservation planning. We conducted a bibliometric review of peer-reviewed literature indexed in Web of Science, combining systematic screening with quantitative bibliometric analyses to assess geographic coverage, taxonomic focus, research themes, collaboration networks and gender representation in authorship. Our results reveal pronounced Wallacean and taxonomic shortfalls, with research concentrated in a limited number of countries and disproportionately focused on invasive species, whereas many native and threatened taxa remain poorly studied. We also detected thematic gaps related to evolutionary and physiological processes, alongside fragmented collaboration networks and persistent gender asymmetries, reflecting broader shortfalls in biodiversity research. These patterns indicate a mismatch between research effort and conservation priorities in a megadiverse region facing increasing environmental pressures. By identifying critical blind spots in current knowledge, this study offers a regional framework to guide future ecological research, conservation strategies and collaborative initiatives on freshwater mollusc management globally.

items.title: Stony coral symbioses show variable responses to future ocean conditions
items.abstract: Abstract Coral reefs support over a quarter of marine species and nearly a billion people worldwide but are also among the ecosystems most threatened by anthropogenic impacts. There is long-standing debate about whether coral symbioses will be disrupted or respond adaptively under future ocean conditions. Using a factorial 2.5-year future-ocean mesocosm experiment across eight coral species representing the major coral lineages, we tracked symbiont community shifts within replicate fragments from the same individual coral. Some corals exhibited stochastic divergence consistent with dysbiosis, whereas others showed deterministic, thermally adaptive shifts. Heat stress generally reduced symbiont diversity and promoted predictable restructuring, supporting deterministic processes under moderate stress but stochastic dysbiosis under extreme conditions. We propose that adaptive and stochastic responses represent endpoints along a continuum of host-orchestrated symbiont sorting. This study bridges coral reef ecology with broader host–microbiome theory, offering an integrated perspective on how symbiotic systems may respond to environmental change. Teaser Long-term experiments reveal that corals follow distinct paths of symbiont change under heat stress, from adaptation to dysbiosis

items.title: Systematic Comparisons between Long-Read- and Short-Read-Based Amplicon Sequencing to Characterize Mixed Microalgal Communities
items.abstract: Abstract The 18S rRNA gene has emerged as the primary molecular marker for amplicon-based characterization of microalgal communities, including in wastewater treatment systems, yet trade-offs between short- and long-read approaches remain poorly defined. We systematically compared V8–V9 short-read sequencing (SR; Illumina MiSeq), near-full-length long-read sequencing with ss5ss3 primers (LR; PacBio Sequel II), and computationally extracted V8–V9 regions from LR data (LS). In silico evaluation of multiple primer pairs revealed differences in predicted taxonomic recovery, while incomplete reference sequences and taxonomic misannotations complicated performance assessments. In environmental samples, SR and LR captured different aspects of sequence diversity: SR recovered a broader set of sequence variants, whereas the longer LR amplicons retained greater sequence information and discrimination. Truncating LR sequences to V8–V9 collapses distinct ASVs. The taxonomic advantage of LR was classification-workflow-dependent and was particularly apparent at genus and species levels with the eukaryote-focused workflow. Differential-abundance analysis identified species-level Chlorophyta associations in LR, with consistent higher-level taxonomic patterns across periods, whereas SR additionally revealed largely period-specific associations with heterotrophic protists. Despite its finer taxonomic resolution, LR did not provide a clearer whole-community distinction between process performance states (i.e., phosphorus-removal, emphasizing that the sequencing approach should be selected according to the information required.

items.title: When cold-bloods heat up: meta-analytical evidence that climatic variability mediates behavioural fever in amphibians and reptiles
items.abstract: Abstract Fever is an adaptive defence response that enhances immune performance by elevating body temperature above normal values. In ectotherms, fever is expressed behaviourally through the selection of warmer microhabitats following infection, yet its magnitude and determinants vary widely across species and environments. We performed a phylogenetically informed meta-analysis to test whether behavioural fever expression is shaped by climatic thermal variability, pathogen identity and taxonomy in amphibians and reptiles. We predicted that species from thermally variable environments would exhibit stronger behavioural fever than those from stable environments and reptiles would exhibit stronger fever responses than amphibians owing to lower hydrothermal constraints. Across 47 studies encompassing 101 effect sizes, behavioural fever emerged as a widespread but context-dependent response. Behavioural fever was strongest in species from thermally variable habitats, suggesting that thermal opportunity and behavioural plasticity mediate the expression of fever. Contrary to our prediction, amphibians exhibited stronger fever responses than reptiles, possibly reflecting differences in thermoregulatory biology, environmental opportunity or methodological artefacts. Bacterial infections elicited larger body temperature increases than fungal or viral challenges. Our findings demonstrate that temperature is not a background condition for host–pathogen interactions, but an active and environmentally contingent component of immune defence in ectothermic tetrapods.

items.title: Physicochemical, carbohydrate, and ecological profiling of Iranian Sidr (Ziziphus spp.) honey: establishing baseline reference ranges for regional quality and authenticity assessment
items.abstract: Abstract Monofloral honeys, particularly Iranian Sidr honey, are highly valued for their unique sensory and medicinal properties; however, they are also prone to fraud. To address this issue, it is essential to create reference databases documenting the physicochemical and pollinological profiles of these honeys. This study analyzed Sidr honey samples from various regions in Iran to document their physicochemical and pollinological characteristics and to understand how ecological factors impact these properties. The analysis of 25 honey samples revealed that pollen from Ziziphus spp. was predominant, indicating a consistent botanical origin. A significant relationship was found between sugar composition, pH levels, and environmental factors, all of which considerably affect honey quality. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) showed that the first two components explained 50.6% of the total variance, highlighting distinct differences in physicochemical and ecological traits. In the first principal component (PCA1), strong positive correlations were identified among erlose, sucrose, pH, rainfall, and altitude. The second component indicated positive relationships between diastatic activity, phenolic compounds, moisture content, and the fructose-to-glucose ratio. Both PCA and hierarchical cluster analysis revealed that honey samples from the same counties did not cluster together, suggesting that environmental factors create unique physicochemical profiles, influencing both the quantity and quality of honey. These findings could enhance the authenticity and quality control of Iranian Sidr honey, improving its commercial value, competitiveness in international markets, and potential for grading.

items.title: Detoxification enzyme modulation and larvicidal efficacy of Klebsiella pneumoniae (PX652414) and Proteus mirabilis (PZ337687) metabolites in mosquito vectors
items.abstract: Abstract Mosquitoes of the Anopheles , Aedes , and Culex genera serve as vectors for significant human and animal diseases. The increasing prevalence of insecticide resistance, primarily mediated by detoxification enzymes, highlights the urgent need for innovative biocontrol strategies. This study assessed the larvicidal activity of secondary metabolites produced by Klebsiella pneumoniae PX652414 and Proteus mirabilis PZ337687, as well as their impact on esterase and glutathione-S-transferase (GST) enzyme activities in three major mosquito species: An. gambiae s.l., Ae. aegypti , and Cx. quinquefasciatus . Metabolites incubated for three and eight days were individually applied to separate cohorts of mosquito larvae. Larval mortality, lethal concentrations (LCs), and enzyme activities were evaluated following 72 hours of exposure. K. pneumoniae metabolites induced substantial larval mortality across all mosquito species, demonstrated by low LC50 values and decreased esterase and GST activity, particularly in Cx. quinquefasciatus. Conversely, P. mirabilis metabolites resulted in minimal mortality and elevated esterase and GST activity. These results demonstrate enzyme modulation by these metabolites and indicate that K. pneumoniae (PX652414) metabolites may serve as promising agents for integrated vector management.

items.title: Applicability of Sustainable Construction and Environmental Resilience in a Circular Built Environment in Southern Africa
items.abstract: Lately, sustainability has dominated academic, practice and policy discourse. The construction industry is singled out as one of the unsustainable sectors due to its linear methods of extract-use-dispose. Globally, linear construction practices are responsible for approximately 50% of raw material extraction, 36% of all emissions, 40% of energy consumption and 50% of waste resulting in natural resource scarcity and waste management catastrophes. In Africa, only 4% of the waste is recycled, whereas 90% is illegally dumped, and the balance is unaccounted for. Consequently, circular economy (circularity), anchored on reduce, reuse, and recycle principles, is widely perceived as a sustainable alternative to linearity. The primary objective of circularity in the construction industry is to advance sustainability by creating a circular built environment. Closely related to circularity, sustainable construction practices also pursue sustainability. On the other hand, environmental resilience from ecology explores how the natural environment adapts to external stressors, promoting sustainability. Nonetheless, the extent to which sustainable construction and environmental resilience non-conflicting factors jointly influence the attainment of a circular built environment remains unknown. The overarching aim of this study was to develop a tailored model for Southern Africa, demonstrating how sustainable construction, environmental resilience factors, and building lifecycle practices contribute to the region's circular built environment transition. To do so, the study was premised on pragmatic philosophy and adopted an exploratory sequential mixed-method research design. The study was divided into two phases. First, through a Delphi study, 11 purposively sampled circularity experts identified 73 drivers contributing to a circular built environment in Southern Africa. Second, a questionnaire comprising these practices was administered to a purposively random sample of 400 stakeholders in Southern Africa. Only 282 participants fully completed the survey. Data was cleaned and analysed through exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and structural equation modelling (SEM). Results show that, generally, there is an awareness of the sustainability concepts, namely circular economy, sustainable construction, and environmental resilience. However, environmental resilience is the most practiced concept, implying that the environmental-related policies enunciated across the region were bearing fruit. v Furthermore, 15 hypotheses were validated, and the results show that environmental resilience, design, construction, operation, and use practices significantly influenced the circular built environment transition. Sustainable construction only impacted design practices. Surprisingly, the results show that sustainable construction and environmental resilience were unrelated. Unlike environmental resilience, sustainable construction or circularity policies are yet to be fully adopted. In conclusion, the study proposes a Southern Africa Circular Built Environment Framework (SACBEF) that demonstrates the applicability of sustainable construction and environmental resilience practices throughout the design, construction, operation, and use phases. The framework also outlines significant barriers and stakeholders in promoting circularity transition. To the knowledge of the researcher, this study is the first of its kind to adopt a multidisciplinary thinking and explore and validate the relationship between cross-cutting concepts, circular economy, sustainable construction, and environmental resilience in promoting circular built environment transition in Southern Africa. Furthermore, the lifecycle assessment perspective provided an in-depth understanding of which building stages influenced circularity in Southern Africa. Future studies should explore the extent of convergence or divergence between sustainable construction and environmental resilience in promoting circularity.

items.title: Too threatened to try: how extinction risk drives research neglect in rays and skates
items.abstract: Global biodiversity loss demands that research effort be directed towards species most at risk. Yet conservation science is biased by species' accessibility and perceived charisma, raising concerns that threatened species may be overlooked. We apply a structured causal modelling framework to 651 species of rays (superorder Batoidea), a highly threatened yet understudied lineage of cartilaginous fishes, to disentangle the drivers of research effort. We quantify the causal effects of taxonomy, extinction risk, accessibility (range size, depth, economic context, year of description) and charisma (body size, shape, patterning and colouration) on species-level research outputs from more than 7000 publications. Research effort was strongly taxonomically biased, driven by accessibility and charisma, with shallow depth, broad geographic ranges, large body size and distinctive morphologies attracting disproportionate attention. Extinction risk exerted a counterintuitive nonlinear effect: Critically Endangered and Endangered species received significantly fewer publications than Near Threatened and Vulnerable species and were comparable to Data Deficient species. This effect is consistent with a 'Goldilocks' zone in which species are threatened enough to justify research but not so threatened that it becomes prohibitively challenging. Systematic research bias away from the species most in need undermines conservation efforts. Realigning research priorities is essential to combating the biodiversity crisis.

items.title: Phenological divergence between flowering plants and flower-visiting Lepidoptera under climate change across Europe
items.abstract: Climate change is altering life-cycle timing and may disrupt coordinated interactions between flowering plants and flower-visiting insects. Using Global Biodiversity Information Facility observation records from Europe between 2000 and 2024, we compiled a continental-scale phenological dataset covering flowering periods of 707 angiosperm species and adult activity periods of 620 Lepidoptera species. We extracted the 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles and activity-window width and used linear mixed-effects models to analyse spatio-temporal trends. The results showed that plant phenology advanced significantly, with the 10th and 50th percentiles shifting earlier by -0.597 and -0.507 d yr⁻¹, respectively, whereas the 90th percentile showed no significant change; flowering-window width increased by 0.361 d yr⁻¹. By contrast, Lepidoptera phenology advanced evenly across the season, with the 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles shifting by -0.137, -0.153 and -0.155 d yr⁻¹, respectively, while activity-window width showed no significant change. Because flowering plants advanced faster than Lepidoptera in the early and middle season, plant-insect phenological overlap declined at 0.340 d yr⁻¹, indicating increasing mismatch across Europe. Further analyses identified temperature as the dominant driver of phenological advance in both groups, but flowering plants and Lepidoptera differed in their responses to other climatic factors. These results suggest that climate change is weakening phenological synchrony between flowering plants and flower-visiting Lepidoptera, with potential consequences for pollination and ecosystem functioning.

items.title: Genomic mechanisms underlying Bombay duck's rapid population surge
items.abstract: Bombay duck (Harpadon nehereus), once a minor by-catch in the East China Sea, has bloomed into a dominant species, altering marine ecosystems. This study explored the genomic basis of its mysterious recent success via chromosome-level genome assembly, comparative and population genomics. The genome assemblies of H. nehereus and its closely related outgroup species Saurida undosquamis were of good quality, showing a 96.7-96.8% Benchmarking Universal Single-Copy Orthologues completeness. Population resequencing supports a single panmictic population throughout the coast of China. Expanded gene families and genes under intensified and positive selection are related to osmoregulation, hypoxia tolerance, immune function and reproduction. Recent selective sweeps are mostly related to immune response. These molecular signatures are consistent with long-term adaptations to a hypoxic, polluted and fluctuating environment. These findings suggest that species genomically preadapted to environments affected by global change can suddenly become new native invaders.

items.title: When dates disagree: radiocarbon and sighting-based models reveal range-wide variability in great auk ( Pinguinus impennis ) extinction estimates
items.abstract: Methods for inferring extinction are well established for events that either occurred on millennial time scales (e.g. the late Quaternary) or are unfolding in the present. However, these methods employ distinct data types inherent to palaeontological or neontological settings, yielding a potentially disjointed view of the extinction process. We leveraged the historical extinction of the great auk (Pinguinus impennis)-a large, flightless seabird native to the Atlantic-as a test case to assess the effects of using varied data types (286 quality-scored occurrences) and models (Gaussian-resampled inverse-weighted McInerny, Solow and Beet) in inferring extinction across centennial time scales. While the last confirmed great auk was killed in 1844 CE in Iceland, the dynamics of species-wide range collapse in response to differing harvest practices have not been explored. Our sighting-based estimates suggest the species may have persisted a decade longer (1860 CE) in the Northwest Atlantic, highlighting the need for future research on this understudied portion of their range. Radiocarbon-based models estimate extinction later (post-2000 CE) across the species' range, suggesting that inherent uncertainties in radiocarbon dates and their calibration-particularly for marine samples-may constrain their applicability for detailing extinction processes on conservation-relevant time scales.

items.title: Modeling of Current and Future Low Flow Characteristics Under Climate Variability and Water Abstraction: Case of Likhubula River Catchment in Malawi
items.abstract: Abstract Water resources are essential in sustaining ecosystems, agriculture and the ever-growing water demands of human population. However, the delicate balance of water availability for these sectors is increasingly facing unprecedented present and future challenges due to climate change and anthropogenic pressures. This study was aimed at characterizing the current and future low flows under climate variability and water abstraction in the Likhubula River Catchment, key a sub-catchment of the major Shire River Basin in Malawi. The study employs a multi-faceted approach, where trend analysis is conducted using the Mann-Kendall test and the Sens Slope Estimator at α = 0.05 significance level. The SWAT hydrological model was set up for simulating future streamflow conditions and forced with RCP and SSP scenarios. Flow duration curves (FDCs) and low flow frequency curves (LFFCs) were employed to compute low flow indices, including the Q90, Q95, 7Q2 and 7Q10. The SWAT model exhibited a satisfactory performance with an R 2 , PBIAS, NSE and RMSE of 0.98, 3.6, 0.94 and 0.29 respectively during calibration and R 2 , PBIAS, NSE and RMSE of 0.96, -2.4, 0.84 and 0.42 respectively, during calibration and validation. Examination of low flow indices indicated substantial increases in low flow frequencies after 2007 with anticipated further increases in low flow duration, magnitude and frequencies after 2027. The RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 indicate less severe low flows as compared to historical periods. The combinations of RCP and SSP scenarios has shown varying results, RCP4.5 & SSP2 indicating significant improvements, while others (e.g., RCP4.5 & SSP4, RCP8.5 & SSP4) showing potential for highly severe low flows; an indication that climate change and intensification of water abstraction activities have a significant impact on the magnitude, duration and frequency of low flows in the Likhubula catchment. Despite the non-significant increasing trend in rainfall being observed, both significant positive trend in temperature and significant declining trend in streamflow imply radical environmental decision-making calls to deal with uncertain future using the 3-H approach. These findings provide crucial insights for sustainable water resource management as these low flow characteristics are critical for managing water quality and quantity.

items.title: Farmers’ perspectives of how farmer research networks shape behaviour and contribute to agroecological systems change in Eastern and Southern Africa
items.abstract: Introduction Farmer Research Networks (FRNs) are collaborative platforms that bring together diverse stakeholders to co-create knowledge and support agroecological innovation. While FRNs are increasingly recognised for enabling farmers to embrace sustainable practices and strengthen resilience, limited evidence exists on how they influence farmer behaviour and contribute to agroecological systems change. Methods This study draws on a single round of qualitative fieldwork conducted in 2024 with nine FRNs that had been operating since 2015 in Kenya, Malawi, and Uganda, comprising 99 interviews and focus group discussions with 182 farmers, researchers and extension or NGO staff, to examine how engagement in these FRNs shapes farmers’ attitudes, perceptions, intentions, and practices. The Theory of Planned Behaviour, the Model of Justified Behaviour, and the FAO’s 10 elements of agroecology were used as analytical lenses. Results The findings indicate that participants experience FRNs as dynamic learning ecosystems. Farmers linked their involvement in FRNs to stronger positive attitudes toward agroecology, enhanced perceived behavioural control through knowledge and skills development, and evolving subjective norms shaped by collective learning and peer influence. Behavioural intentions were reinforced by ecological awareness, emotional engagement, and future-oriented aspirations. Participants associated their engagement with progress across multiple agroecological dimensions, including soil fertility, system diversity, resilience, social cohesion, and economic agency. These outcomes were driven by participatory experimentation, knowledge co-creation, and relational processes such as trust, solidarity, and inclusive decision-making. However, the findings also reveal important limitations in what FRNs can address. Persistent constraints, including labour intensity, limited access to inputs and locally adapted seed, gender and youth inequalities, weak enforcement of community rules, tensions between short-term livelihood needs and long-term ecological goals, entrenched cultural norms and institutional gaps, often lie beyond the direct influence of FRNs. Discussion Overall, the study demonstrates that agroecological transitions are not linear processes of technology adoption, but socially embedded and contested transformations shaped by multiple factors. While FRNs play a critical role, sustaining and scaling these transitions requires complementary investments beyond the scope of the FRNs.

items.title: Editorial: The science of birding in Africa
items.abstract: Birding in Africa plays an increasingly important role in biodiversity monitoring, conservation planning, and environmental policy. The Research Topic, The Science of Birding in Africa, brings together studies that demonstrate how field observation, citizen science, ecological research, and emerging technologies contribute to evidence-based conservation across the continent. The articles in this collection highlight the scientific value of birding and its growing relevance for national and regional biodiversity frameworks, including protected area management, species-action planning, and community-based conservation.Bird Assemblages, Habitat Quality, and Land-Use Pressures A central theme across the contributions is the need for robust, long-term monitoring systems to inform conservation decisions. African countries face rapid land-use change, climate impacts, and biodiversity loss, making reliable data essential for meeting obligations under the Convention on Biological Diversity, the African-Eurasian Waterbird Agreement, and national red-listing processes.One contribution examines seasonal variation, habitat protection, and disturbance effects on bird assemblages in the tropical Guinea Savanna (Ibrahim et al.). By quantifying how bird communities respond to habitat integrity and disturbance regimes, the authors provide insights directly relevant to landuse planning and protected area management.Another study documents a possible short-term but large-scale range contraction of the Brown-headed Parrot in Malawi (Chirwa et al.). As a cavity-dependent species, its decline signals broader ecosystem changes affecting forest structure and availability of nesting sites. The results highlight the urgency of targeted habitat protection and monitoring of cavity-nesting species.Community engagement and citizen science emerge as powerful tools for conservation in several contributions. The article Capacity building as a pathway to indigenous participation in tropical birding and citizen science (Ivande et al.) shows how inclusive approaches strengthen data quality, build local capacity, and enhance long-term sustainability of monitoring programs.Complementing this, the Opinion article Bridging Citizen Science and Policy for Bird Conservation in Africa (Iniuman et al.) highlights how atlas data can inform national conservation frameworks, guide species assessments, and support environmental decision-making. The authors illustrate how citizenscience generated data, when standardized and validated, can complement professional surveys and fill critical knowledge gaps.Species-specific ecological studies also contribute important insights. The research on nest-site selection and breeding ecology of the Wattled Crane in the Bale Mountains (Desta et al.) provides information essential for managing one of Africa's most threatened crane species. By identifying habitat requirements and breeding constraints, the study supports targeted conservation actions within Ethiopia's protected area network.Threatened species monitoring is further highlighted in the study on critically endangered vultures in N'Djamena, Chad (Djekadjim et al.). By documenting abundance, distribution, and threats, the authors provide urgently needed data for regional vulture conservation strategies. Their findings have direct implications for anti-poisoning campaigns, carcass management policies, and cross-border conservation initiatives.Urban environments, often overlooked in African conservation planning, are addressed in the study Large language models enable large-scale analysis of human-bird relationships in South African cities (Naidoo and Reynolds). By applying artificial intelligence to understand public perceptions and interactions with birds, the authors open new avenues for integrating social data into urban biodiversity policy.The Topic also includes methodological advances that support conservation science. The AfriAtlas R package (Danmallam, Brooks and Ottosson) offers automated visualization tools for African bird atlas data, enabling researchers and policymakers to interpret spatial patterns more efficiently.Complementing this, the study Ecological traits as predictors of avian reporting rates and monitoring gaps using iNaturalist data from Nigeria (Ringim et al.) demonstrates how citizen science platforms can reveal biases and gaps in monitoring coverage.The article Avifauna richness and detection reliability between structured scientific surveys and citizen science data (Afrifa et al.) evaluates the strengths and limitations of different monitoring approaches. Their findings support the integration of citizen science into national monitoring frameworks while emphasizing the continued importance of structured surveys for high-precision assessments.A brief research report on Fire-crested Alethes following humans and Bushbuck in Uganda's Budongo Forest (Freymann and Taylor) offers intriguing behavioural insights with potential implications for understanding human-wildlife interactions in protected forests.Together, these contributions illustrate the breadth and vitality of birding science in Africa. They also reveal that the field is developing at different stages across the continent: some regions continue to emphasize basic ecological research, others are expanding citizen-science participation and its integration into conservation practice. This diversity of approaches reflects both regional priorities and emerging opportunities, making it especially valuable for future editions of this Research Topic to explore how birding science continues to develop, connect, and diversify across Africa. The Topic demonstrates that birding is not only a scientific practice but also a strategic tool for achieving conservation outcomes across diverse African landscapes. We thank all authors for their valuable contributions and the reviewers for their thoughtful evaluations. We also acknowledge the Frontiers editorial team for their support. It has been a pleasure to co-edit this Research Topic, and we hope this collection will serve as a resource for researchers, practitioners, policymakers, and birding communities across Africa.

items.title: Moss Diversity and Soil Nature in Established Plots in the Montane Forest of Mt. Hamiguitan Range Wildlife Sanctuary, La Union, San Isidro, Davao Oriental
items.abstract: The one-way effect of moss diversity on soil properties was investigated using belt transects in two established 1-ha plots located at 920–1,160masl in the montane forest of Mt. Hamiguitan Range Wildlife Sanctuary, San Isidro, Davao Oriental. Moss species were identified, and diversity, dominance, and relative abundance were determined. Soil properties were assessed based on soil type, temperature, moisture, pH, and NPK macronutrient levels. Pearson’s correlation coefficient was used to determine relationships between moss diversity and soil physicochemical parameters. A total of 28 moss taxa from six orders and ten families were recorded, with 20 species identified in Plot 1 and 21 in Plot 2. The mean Shannon diversity index was 1.68, indicating moderately high diversity, while the mean Pielou’s evenness and McIntosh dominance indices were 0.55 and 0.83, respectively. Trismegistia calderensis and Braunfelsia sp. were the most abundant species. Most mosses occurred on epigeous or tree-based substrates rather than on the ground. Both plots had clay loam soil. Mean soil temperatures were 19.7°C and 21.5°C, while soil moisture values were 1.05% and 1.07%, and pH values were 5.4 and 5.3. NPK levels varied between plots. Correlations between moss diversity and soil parameters differed between plots, particularly for NPK. Temperature showed no correlation in either plot. Overall, the findings suggest that moss diversity influences certain soil properties through ecosystem functions rather than solely through direct substrate contact, supporting the ecological and functional importance of mosses in montane forest ecosystems.

items.title: Unstable carbon sink growth in alpine grasslands of the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau
items.abstract: Introduction Alpine grasslands on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau (QTP) are central to regional carbon cycling and climate regulation. Although warming and increasing precipitation have driven widespread greening and greater carbon uptake, it remains uncertain whether these gains are accompanied by greater ecosystem stability. Methods We examined carbon sink capacity and temporal variability using net ecosystem productivity (NEP) and proportional variability (PV), and assessed recovery resilience indirectly using lag-one autocorrelation (TAC) as a conditional proxy. Grasslands were classified into eight types based on the trend directions of NEP, PV, and TAC. Multivariate spatial regressions were used to examine hydroclimatic associations with these trends. Results Annual NEP increased across 81.7% of the grassland area between 2000 and 2024, with significant increases (p < 0.05) across 31.7%. Plateau-scale mean annual NEP increased significantly at 0.553 g C m ⁻² yr ⁻² (p = 0.006). Regional mean PV and TAC also increased, indicating greater temporal fluctuations and potentially slower recovery under the assumptions underlying TAC. Robust sinks (T1), with increasing NEP and declining PV and TAC, covered 20.2% of grasslands, whereas 61.6% belonged to T2–T4, where increasing NEP co-occurred with rising PV, TAC, or both. Vulnerable sinks were the largest category (32.6%) and were concentrated in semi-arid alpine steppes and alpine deserts, whereas robust sinks occurred mainly in eastern alpine meadows. Mean annual precipitation was the strongest predictor associated with NEP trends, and vapor pressure deficit was the strongest predictor associated with PV and TAC trends. Discussion Stronger carbon uptake does not necessarily translate into a more stable ecosystem. Evaluating carbon uptake together with temporal variability and conditional resilience indicators can inform assessments of QTP alpine grasslands under climate stress.

items.abstract: The Children’s Python Antaresia childreni has a widespread distribution throughout inland Australia; yet in NSW, its largely restricted to the north-west. The species is listed as Vulnerable in NSW, it is infrequently recorded and has few recent records from the reserve estate. Here we report on a new record for the species and a valuable addition to records for fauna protected in the Paroo-Darling National Park.

items.title: Exorcising ghosts with gravitational waves
items.abstract: General Relativity (GR) is an effective field theory valid in the infrared regime. Quadratic curvature extensions intended to probe ultraviolet physics generically propagate a massive spin-$2$ ghost and are therefore non-unitary. One route to remove ghost is by enlarging the geometric sector (torsion, non-metricity). We investigate the infrared phenomenology of both the standard (ghostful) and ghost-free fourth-order gravity theories by computing Gravitational Wave (GW) emission and confronting the results with observations such as the orbital-period decay of quasi-stable binaries such as PSR B1913+16 and PSR J1738+0333 and the chirp-mass evolution of GW170817. In the ghostful theory, besides the theoretical inconsistency due to non-unitarity, there are also phenomenological problems: the massless spin-$2$ GW flux cancels the combined GW fluxes of the massive spin-$2$ ghost and massive spin-$0$ scalar in the vanishing-mass limit, so the GR quadrupole formula is not recovered at the leading order. As a result, we obtain the GW constraint on the ghostful theory as $m\gtrsim 10^{-11}~\mathrm{eV}$, where $m$ is the mass of the massive modes. By contrast, the ghost-free theory smoothly reproduces the Newtonian potential and GR quadrupole formulae when the two coupling constants $α_1$ and $α_2$ vanish, independently of the mass $m$. Therefore, GW observations put mass-dependent upper bounds on the size of the coupling constants. For example, if we assume $α_1\simeqα_2$ for simplicity, then we obtain $α_{1,2}\lesssim 4.2\times 10^{83}$ for $m\sim 3\times 10^{-16}\,\mathrm{eV}$ and $α_{1,2}\lesssim 1.3\times 10^{75}$ for $m\sim 10^{-11}\,\mathrm{eV}$. To our knowledge, these are the first astrophysical-scale bounds reported for ghostful and ghost-free fourth-order gravity.

items.title: JWST View of the Supernebula in NGC 5253. II. Nebular Lines
items.abstract: Abstract The nearby dwarf starburst NGC 5253 is dominated by a compact radio-infrared supernebula powered by a very young and bright embedded super star cluster of ∼10 9 L ⊙ . We observed this source and its surroundings over the 5–25 μ m range with the Mid-Infrared Instrument (MIRI) Medium Resolution Spectrometer (MRS) on JWST, and in Paper I presented the JWST view of the region and its continuum features. We now present the more than 70 emission lines of H I , H 2 , and metal ions detected by MIRI/MRS. We derive the extinction by comparing H I recombination lines to the free–free radio continuum and find that it is very flat, i.e., almost independent of wavelength over this spectral range. Nebular conditions are consistent with young (≲5 × 10 6 yr) and very massive stars. All regions show high excitation, but the spatial distribution of the high-excitation lines suggests that photons with energies close to 50 eV are escaping the supernebula core in spite of 35 mag of visual extinction.

items.title: Direct torque detection of crystal chirality
items.abstract: Chirality governs phenomena ranging from chemical reactions to the topology of quasiparticle charge carriers. However, a direct macroscopic probe for crystal chirality remains a significant challenge, especially in time reversal symmetric systems with weak circular dichroism signal. Here, we propose the ``Chiralometer'', a mechanical detection method that probes chirality by driving angular momentum carriers out of equilibrium. Using first-principles calculations and semiclassical transport theory, we demonstrate that a temperature gradient in insulators or an electric field in metals induces uncompensated angular momentum in phonons and electrons, respectively. This imbalance generates a macroscopic mechanical torque ($τ\sim 10^{-11} N \cdot m$) well within the sensitivity of modern torque magnetometry and cantilever-based sensors. We identify robust signatures in chiral crystals such as Te, SiO$_2$, and the topological semimetal CoSi. Our work establishes mechanical torque as a fundamental order parameter for chirality, offering a transformative tool for orbitronics and chiral quantum materials.

items.title: A Census of Na D–Traced Neutral Interstellar Medium and Outflows at 0.6 < z < 4
items.abstract: Abstract We present a statistical census of the Na D–traced neutral interstellar medium (ISM) and outflows in 309 galaxies at 0.6 10 ), and 12% are in lower-mass systems. At high mass, ISM absorption is seen in both star-forming and quiescent galaxies, whereas in lower-mass systems, it is observed only in star-forming galaxies. In massive quiescent galaxies, Na D detectability appears linked to star formation history: it is preferentially detected in older systems with larger 4000 Å breaks and younger, rapidly quenching galaxies with strong Balmer absorption H δ A . We identify Na D outflows in 25 galaxies, revealing a possible dichotomy in driving mechanisms between star-forming and quiescent galaxies. In star-forming galaxies, outflow properties correlate with star formation properties, consistent with a star-formation-driven origin. In quiescent galaxies, however, outflows are not associated with residual star formation and often require more energy than such star formation can provide. Together with the high AGN fraction among outflow-detected quiescent galaxies, this suggests that AGN dominate Na D–traced neutral outflows in cosmic noon quiescent systems. We further identify four quiescent galaxies with possible AGN fossil outflows, suggesting that AGN-driven outflows can persist beyond the active accretion phase and may help maintain quiescence.

items.title: Ly α Radiation Pressure in Dense Star Clusters: Implications for Star Formation and Winds at Cosmic Dawn
items.abstract: Abstract Observations with the JWST in lensed fields have revealed that galaxies at cosmic dawn may concentrate their star formation in highly dense, compact, star clusters. The high columns and low metallicities encountered in their birth environments suggest that Ly α radiation pressure may be crucial to their formation and evolution. In this study, we address this question by postprocessing snapshots from radiation-hydrodynamic simulations of dense star-cluster-forming clouds (Σ * ≳ 10 3 M ⊙ pc −2 ) with a range of dust abundances ( Z d = 0–0.1 Z d,⊙ ) using the colt Monte Carlo code. We infer that Ly α is likely to have mild (∼10%) effects on the gas-to-star conversion efficiencies ( ϵ * ≳ 60%) for Z d ≳ 0.01 Z d,⊙ , and even in dust-free environments, ϵ * ≳ 25%—much higher than the ≲10% values typical of star-forming regions in the local Universe. This is because the densest filaments dominating stellar mass assembly ( n ≳ 10 4 cm −3 ) remain sub-Eddington ( f Edd 1, with noticeable fractions having f Edd ≳ 10, implying that Ly α can launch dynamically significant winds from these systems rapidly (≲4 Myr), with possible implications for ionizing photon escape and galactic outflows. The Ly α force multiplier M F is highly sensitive to Z d , with M F ≲ 3 (≲500) for 0.1 Z d,⊙ (dust-free) environments, respectively. Nevertheless, Ly α dominates over UV and IR radiation pressure at all values of Z d ≲ 0.1 Z d,⊙ , by factors of ∼3–500. Our results suggest that Ly α radiation pressure reinforces the emerging picture of locally efficient, bursty star formation accompanied by rapid outflows in galaxies at cosmic dawn.

items.title: Formation of bound composite vortices of a singly quantized 1 S 0 vortex and half-quantized 3 P 2 vortices in the 1 S 0 - 3 P 2 coexisting phase in neutron stars
items.abstract: Pulsar glitches are believed to originate from the dynamics of quantized vortices in the neutron superfluid interior. The outer core of a neutron star hosts a $^3\text{P}_2$ spin-triplet superfluid, whose half-integer quantum vortices (HQVs) are qualitatively different from the $^1\text{S}_0$ singly quantized vortices (SQVs) in the inner crust. It has recently been proposed that the coupling between these two vortex species gives rise to a large-scale vortex network, providing a candidate mechanism for the diversity of observed pulsar glitch phenomena. Using the Gross--Pitaevskii equations for the $^1\text{S}_0$ and $^3\text{P}_2$ condensates, we perform two-dimensional simulations of one SQV and two HQVs in a coexistence phase near the crust-core boundary, varying the density--density and Josephson coupling constants. We find that the Josephson term, arising from the relative phase between the two condensates, induces a strong attractive interaction between the two HQVs and the SQV, which dominates over the density--density coupling. When pinning potentials are applied to the HQVs and the SQV at spatially separated locations, this attraction is found to be sufficiently strong to drive vortex depinning. These results suggest that two HQVs and one SQV can form a tightly bound composite vortex at the crust-core boundary, with implications for the glitch mechanism in neutron stars.

items.title: The Milky Way’s Missing In-Situ Halo
items.abstract: Abstract The Milky Way’s stellar halo preserves a record of its mass assembly history, encoding accretion events in its structural properties. Among the most prominent of these features is a strong break in the halo density profile at ≈20-30 kpc, long attributed to the apocenter pile-up of stars from the Gaia-Enceladus/Sausage merger. However, whether this interpretation is consistent with state-of-the-art cosmological simulations remains unclear. In this work, we compare the Milky Way’s measured stellar halo density profile between galactocentric radii of 1–100 kpc to those of Milky Way-mass galaxies from the FIRE-2 and Auriga cosmological zoom-in simulation suites, spanning a total of 24 simulated galaxies. We find that simulated halo profiles are significantly steeper than Milky Way measurements within ≈15 kpc, and that profile breaks are rare in simulations and never as strong as the Milky Way’s. Of the three galaxies with statistically significant breaks, only one exhibits a break attributable to apocenter pile-up of an accreted merger remnant. Decomposing the simulated profiles, we find that the accreted halo profiles are broadly consistent with Milky Way measurements, while the in-situ halo dominates within ≈20 kpc and drives the discrepancy. These results raise a compelling question: where is the Milky Way’s in-situ halo? The origin of this tension may reflect systematic biases in current halo measurements, an overproduction of early spheroidal star formation in cosmological simulations, or more fundamental differences in the underlying physics (e.g., dark matter) governing the assembly and structure of the inner Galaxy.

items.title: A Collapsar-disk Origin for GW190814
items.abstract: Abstract GW190814 was a remarkable gravitational-wave (GW) event: a merger between a 23 M ⊙ black hole (BH) and a 2.6 M ⊙ compact object, with an extreme mass ratio that is difficult to reproduce through standard isolated-binary or dynamical formation channels. Recent work has shown that neutrino-cooled collapsar disks can become gravitationally unstable and fragment, producing neutron stars (NSs) or low-mass BHs in orbit around the newly formed central BH. These fragments may subsequently interact, scatter, merge with one another, or inspiral into the central remnant. We explore the possibility that GW190814 originated from such a collapsar-disk fragment merging with the central BH. A key prediction of this scenario is a temporal association with a stripped-envelope supernova preceding the GW event, and we identify the Type Ib supernova candidate SN 2019npv, which occurred inside the GW190814 credible volume approximately 60 days before coalescence, as a possible electromagnetic precursor. Although this delay is too long for a conventional kilonova counterpart, we show that three-body interactions among disk fragments can excite some compact objects to wide orbits and produce merger delays of weeks to months. While GW190814 itself was not expected to produce detectable tidal-disruption-powered emission, future delayed mergers in this channel could generate luminous transients through either reprocessed kilonova heating or shocks driven as merger ejecta collide with the preceding supernova ejecta. Finally, treating SN 2019npv as the electromagnetic counterpart makes GW190814 a bright standard siren and yields H 0 = 71 . 1 − 7.5 + 9.3 km s − 1 Mpc − 1 .

items.title: Wave optics effects from gravitational wave propagation through dark matter halos
items.abstract: Gravitational wave (GW) propagation is usually studied under the geometric optics approximation. However, when GWs propagate through structures of sizes similar to their wavelength, this approximation breaks down. To study this situation, we present a scheme for numerically evolving linearised plane GWs through stationary, spherical astrophysical structures in both weak and strong gravity regimes. Our simulations evolve the full Einstein equations (with all 10 components) for Gaussian, NFW and Burkert potentials. Our simulations show that the scattering of the GWs depends not only on the mass of the lens but also strongly on the gravitational potential distribution of the lens. Among our most important results, we find that the GWs do not propagate along null geodesics when propagating through the Gaussian density, neither in the strong nor weak gravity setting. Another significant finding is that in the strong gravity case of the Burkert potential, the convexity of the wave is flipped when leaving the structure. We compare our results with the linearized scalar wave predictions and find that the difference between these and the exact GW modes are of order one when the wave is inside the central potential. However, the difference reduces to only a few percent when the wave has passed through the structure. Although these effects are small, future GW detectors and Pulsar Timing Arrays (PTAs) could be sensitive to these signals which could thus potentially help in constraining the structure of dark matter spikes or halos.

items.title: Interpretable human-label-free deep learning for real-bogus classification with uncertainty quantification
items.abstract: Time-domain surveys generate large numbers of transient candidates, making real-bogus classification a critical step in automated discovery pipelines. Obtaining reliable human-labeled training sets is costly, while community-provided labels can be noisy and survey-dependent. We aim to develop a real-bogus classification framework for point-like astrophysical transient detections against bogus survey detections, that can be trained without human-labeled data using physically motivated injected transients and bogus-dominated survey data, that remains robust under strong class contamination, and that provides well-calibrated and reliable uncertainty quantification (UQ) suitable for downstream decision-making. We combine simulated transient injections with a heavily contaminated survey class and train a dual-network model using an asymmetric co-teaching strategy for classes with different label-noise levels. We evaluate performance on a labeled benchmark subset and analyze the learned representation with latent-space visualization tools. For UQ, we compare standard approaches (Monte Carlo dropout and deep ensembles) and propose a low-cost hybrid strategy that exploits the dual-network setting to improve calibration. We further extend the evaluation to the light-curve domain to assess recovery of light-curve classes. The method achieves strong real-bogus performance on the labeled subset and remains stable under severe class contamination. It recovers transient light-curve classes with high fidelity, while single-source identification is fundamentally limited by intrinsic ambiguity in light-curve-derived labels. Our hybrid UQ approach achieves competitive calibration relative to substantially more expensive ensemble baselines. Latent-space analyses indicate that uncertainty aligns with the decision boundary and reveal that the model can identify subclasses within the bogus population. Our results show that injection-driven, weakly supervised training can enable scalable and consistent real-bogus classification without human-labeled training data while providing calibrated uncertainties. The methodology is well suited for transfer to forthcoming surveys by rerunning the injection-based training pipeline.

items.title: Unveiling the Milky Way with a Gaia DR3 census of OB-type stars within 2 kpc. I. Tracing local Galactic structure, massive star-forming regions and core-collapse supernova progenitors
items.abstract: Abstract O- and B-type stars are young and hot, thereby serving as vital tracers of the star formation and spiral arm structure of the Milky Way. At the dusk of the Gaia DR3 era, a high-confidence and accurate catalogue appears timely. We have characterized 105,971 OB-type stars (Teff > 10,000 K) within 2 kpc from the Sun, using an astro-photometric Bayesian inference tool. Our map unveils a complex view of the young stellar populations across the thin disk, with prominent large-scale features such as the Cepheus Spur, the Giant Oval Cavity, and a segment the Sagittarius-Carina arm all visible. Their inhomogeneous spatial distribution implies that massive star formation has taken place clustered across a few highly concentrated regions. We find a correlation between the overdensities of OB-type stars and young open clusters, and attribute departure from it to extinction effects. We identify 4200 stars as model-dependent core-collapse supernova (ccSN) or direct-collapse black hole (BH) progenitor candidates, including 6 ccSN progenitor candidates within 125 pc – the maximum radius within which a ccSN explosion could be harmful to Earth’s biosphere – but our analysis suggests none of them exploding within the next 5 Myrs. Finally, we anticipate more evolved OB-type stars to collapse to form BHs within the next 1 Myr than ccSN progenitors will explode, despite the former’s much scarcer number. A possible interpretation is a recent star formation burst in the local Milky Way, consistent with overdensities of ccSN progenitor candidates in Cyg OB2 and the Sagittarius-Carina arm.

items.title: Feature–adaptive fusion in hybrid quantum–classical neural networks for robust biomedical image classification
items.abstract: Abstract Hybrid quantum-classical neural networks provide a promising approach for incorporating quantum circuits into machine learning in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum regime. However, existing hybrid models often rely on fixed or globally shared fusion strategies, which may limit their ability to exploit complementary information carried by quantum branches, especially under distribution shifts. In this work, we propose a Feature-Adaptive Fusion Hybrid Quantum-Classical Neural Network (FAF-HQNN) for biomedical image classification. The model combines a classical deep feature encoder with a variational quantum circuit (VQC) and introduces a feature-adaptive fusion mechanism to dynamically weight classical and quantum predictions. We evaluate FAF-HQNN on two MedMNIST benchmarks, PathMNIST and BloodMNIST, under clean and corrupted test conditions. FAF-HQNN achieves the strongest overall performance on clean data among the compared methods and shows improved robustness under Gaussian, salt-and-pepper, and Poisson corruptions. Further analysis of circuit layout, measurement basis, and depth shows that even shallow variational quantum circuits can provide useful complementary information. These results demonstrate that feature-adaptive fusion is an effective strategy for improving accuracy and robustness in hybrid quantum-classical models for biomedical image classification.

items.title: Mitigating the Timing Impact of Anomalous Pulse Profile Shape Variability in PSR J1713+0747 with Gaussian Component Modeling
items.abstract: Abstract The North American Nanohertz Observatory for Gravitational Waves achieves submicrosecond timing precision for several millisecond pulsars in its pulsar timing array (PTA) with the objective of detecting and characterizing nanohertz gravitational waves. PSR J1713+0747 is one of the most precisely timed pulsars in the array, achieving submicrosecond timing precision. However, in 2021 April, PSR J1713+0747 underwent a sudden and unusual change in pulse shape that disrupted its timing stability. As PSR J1713+0747 is a key contributor to PTA sensitivity, variations in its pulse profile significantly affect the array’s sensitivity to nanohertz gravitational waves. We apply frequency-dependent Gaussian component models to decompose the pulse profile and track the evolution of individual components through the event. This component-level method maintains phase-connected timing across the shape-change event. At the L band, the recovered times of arrival (TOAs) have a median uncertainty of ∼0.47 μ s compared to ∼0.70 μ s for standard template matching. At 820 MHz, where profile frequency evolution is stronger, the recovered TOAs have a median uncertainty of ∼1.63 μ s compared to ∼0.67 μ s for standard template matching. The recovered TOAs achieve timing uncertainties comparable to conventional template matching while allowing data affected by profile variability to be retained in PTA gravitational-wave analyses. These results represent an initial step toward profile-domain timing methods capable of accounting for pulse profile evolution while reducing the need for additional timing model parameters.

items.title: Nucleon effective mass in neutron stars cooling
items.abstract: The cooling of neutrons stars, which are composed of ultra-high-density nuclear matter, strongly depends on the equation of state because the dominant cooling sources are neutrinos produced in their interiors. Here, we investigate the cooling properties of neutron stars, focusing on effective nucleon masses, whose impacts have been recently examined in supernova explosion and proto-neutron star cooling. The uncertainties of effective masses originate from the difference in the attractive interaction of scalar meson and the definition of the Dirac and Landau masses. At first, we employ so-called Walecka models that allow these two masses to be introduced within a unified framework and evaluate the resulting cooling curves. Based on the Walecka model, we compute the emissivity of the neutrons and the direct Urca process and their cooling curves. We demonstrate that the Dirac and Landau masses affect cooling of massive neutron stars, although most previous cooling simulations do not distinguish them. We also perform cooling simulations with two realistic equation of states based on relativistic mean-field (RMF) theory, whose differences arise from properties of only effective masses among characteristic parameters. These results are broadly consistent with those obtained from the Walecka models, indicating that the treatment of effective nucleon masses may be an important source of uncertainty in neutron-star cooling.

items.title: Structured coherence: A modern perspective on optical coherence as a resource
items.abstract: Optical coherence is a well-established branch of physical optics in which the statistical properties of fluctuating optical fields are described in terms of correlation functions over continuous spatial and temporal degrees of freedom (DoFs). Nevertheless, in any practical setting, only discrete DoFs are ever accessible. In these scenarios, the modes are fixed, stable, and deterministic, and partial coherence arises from random relative complex amplitudes, a configuration we refer to as 'structured coherence'. Advances in structured coherence have recently unveiled new conceptual ground in optical communications and information processing in which partial coherence may be preferable to full coherence, which we call a 'coherence advantage'. We formulate structured coherence in terms of coherence matrices to investigate these recent theoretical and experimental breakthroughs. We first review optical fields characterized by a binary DoF via 2x2 Hermitian coherence matrices and introduce key concepts that take on new significance for larger-dimensional modal sets. Next, we examine the structured coherence of two binary DoFs, which can be described by 4x4 coherence matrices. We introduce the concept of coherence rank, entropy swapping, and optical cross-purity. In the perspective outlined here, coherence is viewed as a 'resource', which can be exchanged between DoFs, concentrated into a DoF or into particular modes, or spread over the DoFs. We then examine larger-dimensional modal sets, which allow for more versatile applications in optical information processing. The formulation presented here lends itself particularly to the manipulation of partial optical coherence in integrated photonic platforms, thereby opening myriad avenues for novel fundamental investigations of structured coherence and exploiting the coherence advantage in optical communications and information processing.

items.title: Double gravity-assist rendezvous trajectory to Halley’s comet using deep-space low thrust
items.abstract: The perihelion of comet 1P/Halley in 2061 is an excellent chance to revisit this object of outstanding scientific and cultural relevance. During its 1986 approach to the Sun, it was targeted by several flyby missions. Due to its retrograde, highly-inclined orbit, the relative velocities during the encounter were large, restricting the scientific return due to the short time spent inside the coma. A rendezvous trajectory would overcome this limitation, but the design is challenging due to the limitations of current propulsion technology. Given the lead times of spacecraft development and the long duration of the interplanetary transfer to the comet, it is imperative to start mission planning as soon as possible. We present a novel rendezvous strategy, combining unpowered Jupiter and Saturn gravity-assists with deep-space low-thrust arcs. It minimizes launch energy and propellant budget, constraining the arrival to occur before the onset of high activity. The double flyby strategy reduces the otherwise prohibitive cost of the plane change maneuver. Closed expressions for the optimal flyby geometry, together with an explicit low-thrust transcription technique, reduce the number of design parameter to three, improving computational efficiency. Crucially, this is the first rendezvous mission concept achievable with well-proven technology (standard radioisotope thermoelectric generators and an ion thruster) and compatible with several existing launchers. We describe the trajectory optimization strategy and perform a comprehensive exploration of the design space. Finally, we present two promising proof-of-concept trajectories in detail.

items.title: Impact of heavy modes on primordial black hole formation
items.abstract: Primordial black holes (PBHs) form from rare fluctuations in the high-density tail of the primordial distribution, making their abundance highly sensitive to primordial non-Gaussianity. Heavy fields during inflation can source such non-Gaussianity, producing characteristic signatures widely explored in cosmological collider physics, yet its impact on PBH formation remains largely unexamined. We investigate this question within quasi-single-field inflation (QSFI), the minimal realization that couples a heavy field to the inflaton. Unlike most PBH studies that consider only the bispectrum, the QSFI can generate a sizable trispectrum alongside the bispectrum, allowing us to investigate their combined effects on PBH formation. In our leading-order calculation, heavy-field non-Gaussianities can amplify the high-density tail and substantially enhance PBH production. Within the parameter scan, the largest enhancement occurs at the smallest heavy-field mass and the largest sound-speed ratio considered. The trispectrum contribution can be comparable to that of the bispectrum and may even dominate the total non-Gaussian correction. Our results establish PBH abundance as a novel observational channel for cosmological collider physics, demonstrating how heavy fields during inflation can significantly shape PBH formation.

items.title: A Decade-scale Ionization Echo of Black Hole Accretion in Galactic Nuclei
items.abstract: Abstract Circumnuclear structures in active galactic nuclei (AGN) respond to accretion variability over different spatial and temporal scales, but whether compact narrow-line gas responds on decade timescales has not been systematically established. We use repeat Sloan Digital Sky Survey and Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument spectroscopy of 473 variability-selected galactic nuclei with evidence for recent nuclear brightening. We identify 19 sources whose narrow [O III ] λ 5007 flux increased by more than a factor of 2 over rest-frame baselines of 12.0–20.4 yr, which we term narrow-line ionization echoes (NIEs). In equal-weight stacked spectra, [O III ] increased by 229% ± 22%, while lower-ionization lines remained nearly unchanged or declined, indicating an ionization-dependent response rather than uniform spectral rescaling. The NIE hosts also moved coherently toward higher excitation in optical diagnostic diagrams, with mean increases of 0.46 ± 0.18 dex in log ( [ O III ] / H β ) and 0.58 ± 0.13 dex in log ( [ O III ] / [ O II ] ) . Photoionization models reproduce this evolution with a higher ionization parameter and a harder AGN-like ionizing spectrum at fixed gas abundance. For 13 sources with well-defined mid-infrared (MIR) outbursts, the integrated W1+W2 excess energy correlates strongly with the absolute [O III ] luminosity change ( r = 0.87), linking the dust and narrow-line responses to the same nuclear event. The MIR timescale and spectroscopic baseline constrain the variable [O III ]-emitting gas to characteristic scales of 1.5–5.2 pc. Compact narrow-line gas therefore appears to form an intermediate, decade-scale response layer between the infrared dust echo and the long-lived extended narrow-line region.

items.title: A comparison of particle and fluid approaches for modeling the streaming instability in global patch simulations
items.abstract: Identifying the process relevant to planet formation is still a major task. Mechanisms have been identified that can trap dust and prevent it from migrating inward. A particular hydrodynamic instability, known as the streaming instability, is of high interest because it might cause the formation of dust clumps from which the first planetesimals form. We compared the outcome of nonlinear streaming instability simulations using two fundamental approaches in a more realistic global disk model. The results were not used to identify or disentangle the effect of numerical diffusion in fluid simulations, for instance, or the possibility of crossing particle streams. Instead, they enabled us to determine whether the Lagrangian particle approach is most suitable for numerical studies of the streaming instability. We performed 2D axisymmetric global and isothermal hydrodynamic simulations using the two codes FARGO3D (dust fluid) and PLUTO (fluid and particles) to investigate the temporal evolution of dust scale height, the midplane dust-to-gas ratio, and the maximum dust density, as well as to study velocity distributions and vorticities. For PLUTO particle simulations, we also investigated the influence of the gas Riemann solver and spatial reconstruction orders. Our results from a resolution study of up to 5120 cells per gas scale height indicate convergence between PLUTO fluid and FARGO3D. The two codes yield a Gaussian profile that is dominated by small-scale dust-depleted voids. The particle simulations with PLUTO have not yet converged because a transient midplane dust component persists, indicating the need for an even higher resolution or more particles. A more accurate Riemann solver or a higher-order spatial reconstruction scheme helps to cause the dust density profile to approach the converged structure. At the highest resolution, the maximum dust density in fluid simulations is only 36$%$ of that in particle simulations, which is similar to other code-comparison works. When the streaming instability is studied in a global sense, the choice of the Riemann solver and spatial reconstruction order becomes more important than the approach itself (fluid or particles). When the computational performance of the two dust treatments is included, the fluid approach provides an efficient and suitable tool for streaming instability simulations.

items.title: The Silk Nebula: A Newly Discovered Giant [O iii ] Emission Filament
items.abstract: Abstract We report [O iii ] narrowband imaging of an extremely large-scale nebula, the Silk Nebula, discovered by the Super Wide-Field [O iii] Narrow-band Survey (SWONS), together with multifiber medium-resolution spectroscopic data covering the H α , [N ii ], [S ii ], and [O iii ] emission lines, acquired with the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST) as part of the Medium-Resolution Spectroscopic Survey of Nebulae (MRS-N). Based on 2684 high-quality spectra, we measured its physical parameters, including relative line intensities, radial velocities, and full widths at half-maximum. The [S ii ]/H α ratio of the nebula significantly exceeds the shock-excitation threshold of 0.4. Its location in BPT diagnostic diagrams and spatial morphology of [O iii ] both support the optical emission is dominated by shock-heated gas. The oxygen abundance is near solar and spatially uniform, consistent with a shock propagating into the ambient interstellar medium. Because [O iii ] is the only emission line that clearly traces the nebular morphology, we base our distance estimate exclusively on the [O iii ] kinematics, obtaining a fiducial distance of ∼160 pc. At this distance, the nebula has a physical extent of ∼28 pc along the north–south direction. We suggest that the Silk Nebula is a large [O iii ] filament possibly associated with a supernova remnant, although a diffuse-ionized-gas (DIG) or ionized-bubble origin cannot be ruled out with the present data, and one of the largest angular-scale [O iii ] emission structures documented to date. Future deep X-ray observations and shock-modeling efforts are required to firmly establish its nature.

items.title: A New Method for Constraining 3D Exoplanet Atmospheres: Application to WASP-94A b’s Panchromatic Spectrum
items.abstract: Abstract A growing number of transiting exoplanets exhibit spectroscopic evidence that their leading and trailing limbs differ. Interpreting these observations is now the limiting step. The standard approach of fitting limb-resolved transit depths results in highly anticorrelated transit depths, and treating them as independent measurements can result in strongly biased (3 σ ) retrieved molecular abundances. We present an inference framework that avoids these correlations by using the temporal signature of limb asymmetry instead. This wavelength-dependent shift in mid-transit time, or “time-shift spectrum,” carries the limb-asymmetry information, is measurable from existing light curves with a spherically symmetric transit model, and is uncorrelated with the spherically averaged transit depth. Simultaneously fitting the resulting transmission and time-shift spectrum with an independent atmospheric column for each limb enables the retrieval of limb-resolved properties from two independent measurements. We demonstrate that this approach reduces the mean squared error on the retrieved molecular abundances by factors of ∼30–50 relative to the next best of the alternative approaches currently adopted in the field, and improves retrieved abundance precision by ∼3–6× . We apply the framework to WASP-94A b and present its panchromatic limb-resolved spectrum, spanning 0.8–5 μ m and combining NIRISS/SOSS and NIRSpec/G395H observations. The planet’s morning limb remains aerosol-obscured across this entire range, while its evening limb constrains the abundances of H 2 O, CO 2 , CO, and H 2 S. We measure a limb-to-limb temperature difference of 415 ± 58 K at 1 mbar. This limb-resolved analysis finds [M/H] = +0.32 − 0.11 + 0.11 and C/O = 0.724 − 0.013 + 0.013 , consistent with the host star.

items.title: νGundam: A unified framework for point-redshift and probability-density-function-aware spatial correlation functions
items.abstract: Photometric-redshift uncertainties redistribute galaxy pairs along the line of sight (LOS) and across projected-separation bins, which dilutes spatial clustering measurements. Modern photo-z methods provide full per-object redshift probability density functions (PDFs), but propagating them directly through standard pair-count estimators remains computationally demanding. We present 1.2 ν Gundam a unified framework for point-redshift and PDF-aware spatial correlation functions. Our aim is to propagate radial PDFs at the pair-count level while retaining a common interface for exact, compressed, and stochastic projected-clustering calculations. The code implements four PDF-aware modes: exact empirical-PDF integration on a shared radial grid, Gaussian-mixture (GMM) compression, Monte Carlo (MC) sampling, and a quantile-compression method, 16quant. All modes accumulate pair counts on a resolved $(r_ ,π)$ grid, from which ξ(r_ ,π) and cumulative w_ (r_ ;Π) are reconstructed. We validated these methods with DESI galaxies and CosmoDC2 mocks using pair-level diagnostics, controlled degradation, convergence tests, and an exact-grid benchmark. p p p p The PDF-aware modes produce nearly indistinguishable LOS redistribution kernels, while point-photo-z estimates discard probabilistic pair information. Controlled Gaussian and empirical-PDF experiments show that radial uncertainty mainly redistributes the existing clustering signal to larger π, and that the LOS depth required to recover the truth-redshift projection scales approximately with the effective pairwise radial dispersion. For practical settings, MC, 16quant, and GMM reproduce the exact-grid result with fractional root-mean-square (RMS) residuals below 5%. Applied to DESI red and blue Bright Galaxy Survey samples, MC sampling recovers their spectroscopic clustering shapes and relative amplitudes for r_ p -1 Mpc -1 Mpc , respectively. Projected clustering with redshift PDFs is best understood as a pair-redistribution problem. When propagated consistently, the projected signal can be recovered accurately and efficiently. The LOS integration depth is nevertheless sample-dependent and should be treated as part of the measurement definition rather than as a fixed technical choice.

items.title: Theoretical pulsation properties of RR Lyrae and Type II Cepheids in the JWST and Roman photometric systems
items.abstract: RR Lyrae (RRL) stars and Type II Cepheids (T2Cs) are key standard candles and tracers of old stellar populations. The deep, wide-field capabilities of facilities such as the Space Telescope (JWST) and the Space Telescope will significantly expand their utility as a Population II alternative to classical Cepheids for distance scale calibrations. James Webb Nancy Grace Roman We present theoretical pulsation properties -- including light-curve morphologies, amplitudes, and multi-filter relations -- for RRLs (Z = 0.0001--0.02, M = 0.51--0.80,M_⊙) and T2Cs (Z = 0.0001--0.01, M = 0.495--0.65,M_⊙) to enable detailed studies of Galactic and extragalactic populations. Using already available non-linear convective pulsation models, we converted their predicted bolometric light curves across various chemical compositions and evolutionary stages into the JWST and photometric systems. From these, we derived multi-filter period-amplitude and colour-colour diagrams, alongside period-luminosity and period-Wesenheit relations with explicit metallicity terms. Roman The relations for RRL pulsators display a significantly stronger zero-point metallicity dependence than those of T2Cs, despite having similar slopes. Consequently, T2Cs offer a distance scale indicator that is remarkably robust against metallicity uncertainties. As a preliminary test, we applied our metal-dependent period-Wesenheit relations to a subset of JWST-observed RRLs in the WLM galaxy, deriving a distance modulus of μ = 24.85 ± 0.03 mag (assuming the literature average metallicity). The derived distance to WLM is consistent with most literature values, though slightly shorter than determinations based on classical Cepheids and the tip of the red giant branch. These theoretical relations pave the way for future high-precision distance determinations and asteroseismic diagnostics with JWST and . Roman
