items.title: Comparison of hybrid and standard reconstruction methods on IXPE astrophysical data
items.abstract: A hybrid reconstruction algorithm combines a convolutional neural network (CNN) with standard moment analysis to improve the reconstruction of photoelectron tracks in the gas pixel detectors (GPDs) on board the Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE). The method has been validated on laboratory calibration data, but its performance on astrophysical sources with known polarimetric properties has not yet been systematically characterized. We present the first comparison of hybrid and standard reconstruction methods on IXPE data of astrophysical point sources, with the aim of quantifying the improvement in polarimetric sensitivity as a function of energy. We analyzed two IXPE observations selected to probe complementary regimes: Her X-1, a bright and highly polarized accreting X-ray pulsar used as a quantitative benchmark, and the transient neutron star low-mass X-ray binary XTE J1701-461 in its soft state, a bright source with no detectable polarization used to measure residual systematic effects. For each source, we compared the normalized Stokes parameters, the degree of polarization (PD) and angle (PA), and the detection significance derived from the level 2 event files produced by both pipelines. For Her X-1, the hybrid method yields a consistently higher detection significance at all energies, with a statistically significant improvement above ∼2.83 keV. For XTE J1701-461, both methods yield polarization degrees consistent with zero and significance ratios consistent with unity. items.title: A Global Magnetohydrodynamic Simulation of the Birth and Cannibalism of Homologous Coronal Mass Ejections
items.abstract: Abstract Homologous coronal mass ejections (CMEs) are sequential eruptions from the same active region. They are of particular space-weather interest because they can interact and coalesce into compound ejecta, potentially amplifying their geomagnetic impact. Yet the full chain from recurrent initiation to magnetic merging has not been captured self-consistently in a single global simulation. We present a three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic model that generates three homologous CMEs from a bipolar active region by recurrent photospheric shearing. All three eruptions follow the same initiation mechanism by tether-cutting reconnection within a recurrently formed sigmoid, while the later CMEs propagate significantly faster than the first. We demonstrate that this speed hierarchy arises from progressive coronal preconditioning; preceding eruptions evacuate the overlying corona, reducing both mass loading and ambient drag. The faster, later CMEs catch up with their predecessors, and the compression between them forms inter-CME current sheets. Reconnection within these current sheets then progressively merges the interacting flux systems, completing the cannibalistic process. Synthetic coronagraph images reproduce the apparent coalescence of multiple white-light fronts. This simulation provides the first self-consistent global view of the birth, preconditioning, and cannibalistic interaction of homologous CMEs, bridging recurrent eruption initiation and inter-CME magnetic merging in the near-Sun corona.

items.title: ARRAKIHS: The observability of tidally stripped satellites in a Milky Way-like halo
items.abstract: Current and forthcoming deep imaging surveys are revealing an increasing number of low surface brightness stellar streams around Milky Way-like galaxies. These streams encode information about the orbital evolution and internal structure of their disrupted dwarf galaxy progenitors. We investigate the dynamical evolution and observability of tidal features produced by dwarf galaxies consistent with the cosmological constant and cold dark matter ((Λ)CDM) framework and observations of Local Group satellites. We performed high-resolution N-body simulations of dwarf galaxies orbiting within a static Milky Way-like potential comprising a disc, a bulge, and a dark matter halo. Each dwarf comprised two collisionless components: a Plummer stellar distribution embedded in a cuspy or cored generalised Navarro--Frenk--White dark matter halo. Idealised integrated surface brightness maps were constructed from simulation outputs every (0.5, ) over (10, ), and detectability was quantified through the projected area of progenitor stellar light brighter than a range of limiting surface brightnesses, (μ_ =29)--(32, ), chosen to span depths relevant to the Analysis of Resolved Remnants of Accreted galaxies as a Key Instrument for Halo Surveys (ARRAKIHS), the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), and . The detectability of tidal features depends most strongly on progenitor stellar mass, orbital configuration, parameterised by the eccentricity proxy (e_0), and evolutionary stage. Over the surface brightness range explored, extended tidal debris is predominantly recovered for initially more radial configurations, mainly those with (e_0 ≳ 0.75). In the simulated grid, detectable area is dominated by (M_⋆=10^8)--(10^9,M_⊙) progenitors, whereas (M_⋆=10^6)--(10^7,M_⊙) systems can undergo stripping without detectable debris. The detectable area evolves non-monotonically with time, reflecting the competition between stream formation, phase mixing, and the fading of diffuse debris below the adopted surface brightness limits. items.title: Desynchronization between CME Acceleration and Flare Reconnection
items.abstract: Abstract According to the standard coronal mass ejection (CME) model, both the flare and the CME are a result of the common process of magnetic reconnection. This implies that the CME impulsive acceleration and the flare reconnection should correlate in time. However, observations suggest that this correlation may break for CMEs associated with weak flares. In this work, we aim to find experimental evidence of such desynchronization. For this study, we chose a CME that 1) was associated with a weak B7.1 flare; 2) was continuously tracked from the solar surface up to the outer corona with high-cadence observations; 3) for which X-ray images were available. We measured the CME acceleration profile and compared it with the reconnection signatures: the derivative of the soft X-ray (SXR) emission and the motion of flare ribbons. The studied CME had non-trivial kinematics. It first impulsively accelerated to 440 km s-1 over 20 min, then decelerated to 280 km s-1 over 15 min, and then slowly accelerated up to 660 km s-1 over 2 h. We observed reconnection signatures only during the deceleration and second acceleration phases, suggesting that the main impulsive acceleration occurred without flare reconnection. We interpreted the first acceleration phase as a consequence of the kink instability. As the flux rope rose, it stretched the current sheet below it, which slowed down the CME. Eventually, the reconnection started inside the newly formed current sheet, and the CME started to accelerate again. These results show that CMEs can accelerate significantly without magnetic reconnection and exhibit a complex acceleration structure. This means that different mechanisms play a role in CME acceleration at different stages of its evolution.

items.title: Spatially Resolved Cell-Fate Engineering through Nanoneedle-Mediated Optoporation
items.abstract: The development of advanced tissue models demands spatially resolved control over cell fate to provide deeper insights into complex biological processes, yet precise intracellular manipulation remains a critical bottleneck in cellular engineering strategies. Current approaches for gene delivery struggle in achieving the required localized resolution to control individual cell fate, while optogenetic approaches are constrained by the requirement for complex genetic engineering and limited modes of gene regulation. Here, we show that nanoneedle-mediated optoporation enables spatially resolved intracellular delivery of nucleic acids, locally directing cell fate. Through computational modeling and experimental validation, we investigated the dependence of electromagnetic field enhancement on wavelength, nanoneedle geometry, and porosity. We demonstrated the importance of surface chemistry for optoporation efficiency, achieving optimal transfection performance through thermal carbonization. This approach achieves efficient delivery for propidium iodide, 500 kDa dextran, and siRNA, alongside a 72% mRNA transfection efficiency, resulting in sustained protein expression after 24 h. Selective SNAIL1 mRNA transfection demonstrated localized cell-fate engineering, inducing a targeted epithelial to mesenchymal transition. This porous nanoneedle system presents a versatile and flexible approach for precise genetic manipulation through electromagnetic field tunability, offering new possibilities for studying complex biological processes and disease progression through spatially resolved control of cell fate.

items.title: Gravitationally driven fragmentation and classical turbulence: a quantitative assessment of the spectral analogy
items.abstract: The postinflationary inflaton condensate fragments gravitationally, a process well described by the Schrödinger–Poisson (SP) equations. Under the Madelung transformation the SP system is exactly equivalent to a compressible, inviscid, irrotational self-gravitating fluid in which a quantum potential replaces the thermodynamic pressure. That exact correspondence shows that vortex stretching, viscous dissipation and scale-separated forcing are all absent, so Kolmogorov scaling is not predicted. We then analyse the density-fluctuation power spectrum published by Musoke, Hotchkiss and Easther for the snapshot at which the Universe has grown by a factor of 200 since inflation ended, extracted from their figure with an uncertainty budget, bootstrapped confidence intervals, a scan of the fitting interval, and information-criterion model comparison. Over the decade of wavenumbers immediately above the horizon scale the spectrum follows a power law of slope − 3.73 ± 0.18 , which for that choice of interval is consistent with the − 11 / 3 obtained by transcribing the Kolmogorov spectrum into a three-dimensional spectral density and inconsistent with − 5 / 3 . The agreement is interval-dependent and is not a robust feature of the data: the slope varies between − 3.1 and − 7.4 as the fitting interval is changed, a curved spectrum is mildly preferred, and the scatter is dominated by realization noise rather than by figure extraction. The exponential high-wavenumber tail extends past the Nyquist frequency of the source simulation, so we attach no dissipation-range interpretation to it. The correspondence therefore holds over about 1 decade; we set out the measurements that would make the test decisive.

items.title: A two-dimensional numerical simulation of polarization electric field instability in the mid-latitude ionospheric E region at Wuhan, China
items.abstract: Background Ionospheric E-region irregularities modify local electron density and can affect high-frequency radio propagation, satellite communication, and navigation. Existing theories describe plasma density perturbations produced by electron density gradients and electric fields in sporadic E (ES) layers, but do not fully explain the persistence, propagation direction, and spatial structure of quasi-periodic (QP) echoes. Objective This study investigates the generation and evolution of E-region irregularities under geomagnetic conditions representative of the mid-latitude region at Wuhan. Methods A two-dimensional numerical simulation of E-region polarization electric field instability is conducted with initial perturbations and zonal wind shear. The Flux-Corrected Transport (FCT) and Bi-conjugate Gradient Stabilized (BICGSTAB) methods are used to solve the governing equations. The nighttime irregularity evolution at 100 km is simulated under a specified ionospheric background condition. Results The simulated plasma-density structures and polarization electric fields evolve in space and time. Horizontally distributed ES structures extend along the geomagnetic field and develop into stripe-like thin layers. During the 1,500 s simulation, the maximum polarization electric field reaches approximately 2.2 mV/m. The characteristic spacing of the resulting structures is comparable to the 27.0 km horizontal wavelength of the imposed seeding perturbation. Conclusion Under the prescribed background and perturbation conditions, the simulated ES morphology is associated with the imposed perturbation scale, suggesting a possible link between seeding wavelength and the resulting structure.

items.title: Artifact detection and localization in single-channel mobile EEG for sleep research using deep learning and attention mechanisms
items.abstract: Artifacts in the electroencephalogram (EEG) degrade signal quality and impact the analysis of brain activity. Current methods for detecting artifacts in sleep EEG range from threshold-based algorithms to machine learning approaches, yet applications remain limited for single-channel mobile EEG. We propose a convolutional neural network (CNN) model incorporating a convolutional block attention module (CNN-CBAM) to detect and localize artifacts in sleep EEG using attention maps. We benchmarked this model against 6 other machine learning and signal processing approaches. We trained/tuned all models on 72 manually annotated EEG recordings obtained during home-based monitoring from 18 healthy participants with a mean (SD) age of 68.05 y ( ± 5.02). We tested them on 26 separate recordings from 6 healthy participants with a mean (SD) age of 68.33 y ( ± 4.08), which contained artifacts in 4% of epochs. CNN-CBAM achieved the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (0.88), sensitivity (0.81), and specificity (0.86) among the tested approaches. Under the ideal choice of an attention threshold of 0.66, the attention maps from CNN-CBAM localized artifacts within detected artifact epochs with a sensitivity of 0.61 and specificity of 0.63. This work demonstrates the feasibility of automating artifact detection and localization in wearable sleep EEG.

items.title: Enhanced sampling enables binding site water reorganization in polarizable absolute binding free energy calculations
items.abstract: Abstract Water molecules play a critical role in mediating protein-ligand interactions by forming hydrogen-bonding networks and contributing to ligand solvation. However, their behavior—ranging from rapid solvent exchange to persistent occupancy of buried sites—makes accurate binding free-energy estimation with molecular dynamics challenging. Inadequate sampling of water reorganization can bias computed affinities and obscure key interactions by preventing representative hydration states during calculations. To address this, we employ the polarizable AMOEBA force field together with Lambda-ABF-OPES, an integrated enhanced-sampling framework combining lambda-dynamics, multiple-walker adaptive biasing force, and on-the-fly probability enhanced sampling. AMOEBA provides a polarizable description of protein–ligand, ligand–water, and protein–water interactions, while the dynamic alchemical coordinate and adaptive biasing facilitate exploration of coupled ligand-pocket-solvent configurations during ligand decoupling. This construction allows water exchange, binding-site rehydration and solvent reorganization to emerge along the alchemical pathway without explicitly biasing water-based collective variables. Applied to five protein-ligand complexes spanning buried and semi-buried environments, the approach yields binding affinities in good agreement with experiment and captures relevant water-mediated reorganization to provide reproducible absolute binding free energies.

items.title: From the Rock Floor to the Cloud: A Systematic Review of State-of-the-Art NLP in Battery Life Cycle
items.abstract: This work presents a systematic review of the application of natural language processing (NLP) along the entire battery life cycle, instead of reviewing one stage or method, and introduces a novel conceptual technical language processing (TLP) framework for the European Union (EU)’s proposed digital battery passport (DBP) and other general battery predictions, as the main objective. It follows the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) method and employs three reputable databases or search engines, including Google Scholar, Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers Xplore (IEEE Xplore), and Scopus, searched in October, 2025. The search criteria are ’text’, ’language processing’, and ’battery’, while the exclusion criteria are non-relevant papers and those published before 2017, which were applied to all databases, except IEEE Xplore because it turned up fewer results. Consequently, it assesses 274 scientific papers before the critical review of the final 66 relevant papers. We publicly provide artifacts of the review for validation and possible reproducibility. The findings show that new NLP tasks are emerging in the battery domain, which facilitate materials discovery and other stages of the life cycle. Notwithstanding, challenges remain, such as the lack of standard benchmarks. The proposed TLP framework, which incorporates agentic AI and optimized prompts, may be apt for tackling some of the challenges.

items.title: Integrated computational pipelines using machine learning and deep neural networks for modelling Drosophila cardiac aging and disease classification
items.abstract: Abstract High-speed optical microscopy of Drosophila hearts has become an essential approach for modeling cardiovascular disease and aging. However, manual evaluation of cardiac function is time-consuming, subjective, and error-prone, highlighting the need for reliable computational frameworks. Here, we present an end-to-end dual-modality pipeline that combines segmentation-derived cardiac parameters with ensemble machine learning and raw video-based representations with deep convolutional neural networks. This integrated approach enables automated and quantitative phenotyping of cardiac function across both aging and cardiovascular disease contexts. We evaluated the performance of the pipeline across three biological problems relevant to cardiovascular systems biology: distinguishing between young (1-week) and aged (5-week) hearts, classifying healthy hearts from those carrying the lamin C mutation (LamC G489V ), and identifying phenotypes associated with Ogdh knockdown. Ensemble learning with Random Forest, XGBoost, and Logistic Regression applied to segmentation-derived features achieved accuracies of 82.3% ± 0.6% for aging classification, 79.0% ± 0.4% for lamin C mutant detection, and 98.5% for Ogdh knockdown identification. In parallel, video-based modelling using a custom convolutional neural network and a residual 3D network (R3D-18) yielded accuracies of 89.1% ± 0.5%, 74.0% ± 1.2%, and 93.9%, respectively. By integrating classical feature-based learning with modern deep architectures, this work provides a scalable computational framework for modelling Drosophila cardiac aging and disease. More broadly, the study demonstrates how multimodal machine learning can enhance quantitative phenotyping, minimize human error in analysis, and expedite the application of invertebrate models in systems-level investigations of cardiovascular health and aging.

items.title: Bearing, heading and the perceptual geometry of collective motion
items.abstract: Traditional models of collective motion commonly assume that animals turn to match their neighbours' directions of travel. In the harmonic theory, decisions follow from a neural representation of direction, and a neighbour enters only as a stimulus at a bearing, the direction in which it lies. Here we show that a neighbour's spatial extent allows its orientation to enter through projection geometry alone, and the theory generates a matrix of coupling coefficients indexed by the neighbour's bearing and aspect. Responses to bearing alone form one edge of this matrix, and classical heading matching is a special case on its diagonal, one ray through a two-parameter family. Independently, an animal that responds only to neighbour position, perceived with a delay, acquires an alignment coefficient set by the slope of its distance-weighted attraction profile, so that it can align, anti-align or reverse sign. Alignment need not be a rule to be measured. In schooling fish and walking pigeons with body orientation measured independently of travel, social responses are recovered, including bearing responses in the fish. Heading excess depends on how turning is measured, appearing in the fish with forward but not centred responses and remaining unresolved in pigeons. Controls show why neither outcome identifies a direct alignment rule. In fish recordings with motion-assigned body polarity, heading-dependent structure departs from Vicsek form and fails the coefficient test for a common angular potential. Whether animals align thereby becomes a measurable question, with geometric, perceptual and behavioural origins that can be distinguished.

items.title: REST: Routing with En-route Seating Thresholds for pedestrian accessibility
items.abstract: Public seating can support walking by providing opportunities to rest at useful positions along complete journeys. We introduce a route-based framework that assesses nearby seating, access to everyday destinations, and whether rests are well spaced along routes. One method finds the shortest route that does not exceed a chosen distance without rest; another allows longer stretches but adds a cost expressed as equivalent walking distance. We apply the framework to Mannheim, Germany. With a 1,000 m travel budget and a 500 m limit on walking without an opportunity to rest, 99.5% of older residents in Feudenheim lived within 500 m of a rest, yet only 33.5% could reach at least one destination in each of five categories (food shops, pharmacies, primary healthcare, public transport, and community services) on ordinary shortest routes meeting this limit. Finding alternative routes with sufficiently spaced rests increased this share to 61.4%; allowing longer stretches with an added cost raised it to 76.2%, compared with 89.7% when resting needs were ignored. Across Mannheim, 20.2% of older residents lost access to a reachable category when routes required a resting opportunity every 500 m, versus 7.1% when longer stretches were allowed at extra cost. Compared with the shortest physical distance, the least burdensome routes incurred extra costs from seating gaps: a median of 7.3 m of equivalent walking distance across city areas (90th percentile: 45.9 m). Better-placed seating could reduce this burden without changing street layouts. These measures help planners identify deficiencies, test improvements and guide route choices.

items.title: An analytical framework for atmospheric tides on rocky planets. II. Semidiurnal thermotidal torque
items.abstract: The thermodynamic acceleration induced by atmospheric thermal tides has a major impact on the rotation of temperate rocky planets, where gravitational and radiative tidal forcings are of comparable strength. This acceleration drives planets away from synchronous rotation, thereby affecting their climate, large-scale circulation, and surface conditions. These implications underline the need to better constrain the dependence of the thermotidal torque on the tidal frequency and on the physical parameters characterising the star-planet system, as this relationship remains insufficiently understood. In particular, the role of resonantly excited Lamb waves requires clarification due to its potential impact on Earth's length of day (LOD) during the Precambrian. Building on a previous work, which provided a fully analytical formulation of the atmospheric tidal response of rocky planets, we apply this framework to isentropic and isothermal atmospheres. We perform a comprehensive functional analysis of the resulting torque and compare the analytical predictions with numerical solutions from earlier general circulation model (GCM) studies. The analytical model agrees well with GCM results, accurately capturing the frequency dependence of tidal torque both for paleo-Earth and present-day Earth. More generally, the solutions capture the torque peak near synchronous rotation and the amplification associated with Lamb-wave resonance. Near resonance, the GCM results exhibit a stronger braking torque than accelerating torque. This asymmetry is reproduced by allowing tidal heating to lag behind insolation. The agreement with GCM spectra suggests that thermal tides in the benchmark simulations are driven predominantly by an indirect thermal forcing characterised by a substantial time delay, in contrast to the direct absorption of sunlight that dominates semidiurnal tides on present-day Earth.

items.title: The Composition of M-dwarf Exoplanet Hosts: Atmospheric Parameters and O, Mg, Si, and Fe Abundances from IR Spectroscopy
items.abstract: Determining M-dwarf abundances is an important step to discerning the chemical evolution of the Milky Way and characterizing exoplanetary systems, especially since these objects commonly host small exoplanets. However, a dearth of M-dwarf abundance measurements exist compared to Sun-like stars, partially due to their complicated optical spectra dominated by molecular absorption lines and low luminosities. To overcome these issues, we have obtained high resolution H-band spectra of 40 planet-hosting M-dwarf stars and 2 M-dwarfs in wide binaries with FGK primaries with IGRINS on Gemini South and on the McDonald Observatory 2.7m telescope, and NIRSPEC on Keck. Abundances were derived by comparing each observed spectrum to synthetic spectral grids generated with MOOG and MARCS atmospheric models. Effective temperatures were derived using OH and H$_{2}$O lines and [Fe/H] from Fe I and FeH lines. Both Mg and Si abundances were determined using atomic features. Overall, we find that our abundances are broadly consistent with previous literature M-dwarf abundances. We complemented our abundances analysis with UVW velocities and Milky Way stellar population membership probabilities and identified 2 potential thick disk stars from our kinematic and chemical analysis: GJ 1252 and L181-1 which was a previously known thick disk star. Kinematic stellar population probabilities and a low [Fe/H] abundance makes Kepler 42 a likely thick disk star, although uncertain Mg and Si abundances make classification difficult. Lastly, we have determined Si/Mg and Fe/Mg molar ratios for M-dwarf exoplanet hosts and find the abundance distributions leads to exoplanet core-mass fractions between 20 - 40$\%$.

items.title: The JWST Early Release Science Program for Direct Observations of Exoplanetary Systems IX: A Multi-Wavelength Framework for Source Characterization in JWST Coronagraphic Imaging of the HIP 65426 System
items.abstract: We present an updated analysis of the JWST coronagraphic imaging data of the HIP 65426 system. We aim to search for and characterize potential planetary companions as well as provide updated astrometry and photometry for the known exoplanet HIP 65426 b following updates to the JWST and spaceKLIP pipelines. Our measured photometry and astrometry show significant differences to those in Carter et al. (2023) but are consistent to within $2.2σ$ in separation, $1.5σ$ in position angle, and $3.7σ$ in flux. Our results indicate that pipeline updates have changed the photometry and astrometry significantly in some filters, especially in terms of observed flux. We see the greatest changes in separation in F444W and F1550C, position angle in F250M, and flux in F250M, F300M, F410M, F1140C, and F1550C. The SED of HIP 65426 b remains consistent with a young, giant planet best fit by models with a cloudy atmosphere and an effective temperature estimate of ~1436 K. Using both NIRCam and MIRI data, we identified 21 candidate companion sources in addition to the known planet. Of the 21 sources, 13 were attributed to astrophysical sources with eight background stars, four galaxies, one unknown, and zero planets. While one of these sources was detected in Chauvin et al. (2017), the remaining point sources were undetected in previous ground-based observations, which makes this work an initial epoch of astrometry for these objects. One galaxy in particular appears as a point source in MIRI but is highly extended in NIRCam and exposes a potential drawback to single-epoch MIRI imaging in a blind search for companions.

items.title: Permutation order governs basin entropy in critical one-input Boolean networks
items.abstract: Basin entropy measures uncertainty about a network's long-term behavior. For every critical one-input synchronous Boolean network with $m$ relevant nodes, we show that the permutation structure induced by its feedback loops determines basin entropy, up to a universal error. Although the loops oscillate independently, their relative phases can be offset, producing a deviation from additivity that can grow linearly in $m$. Yet at the ensemble level, a previously derived additive prediction is preserved through the first subleading term, with the discrepancy appearing at order $\ln m\ln\ln m$.

items.title: PINR-ESI: Physics-Informed Self-Supervised Implicit Neural Representation Framework for EEG Extended-Source Imaging
items.abstract: EEG extended-source imaging aims to localize active cortical regions and characterize their spatial extent, yet supervised inverse networks typically depend on synthetic EEG-source pairs and may be sensitive to synthetic-to-real mismatch. We propose a physics-informed self-supervised implicit neural representation (INR) framework for spatial source reconstruction without paired source labels or simulation-based supervised pretraining. The lead field matrix encodes the source-to-sensor volume-conduction model and constrains the INR through agreement between predicted and measured EEG. Cortical current density is modeled as a continuous coordinate-conditioned field. A classical inverse estimate provides warm initialization and spatial constraints on source activity, while patch-integrated projection maps the field to discrete source coefficients for forward modeling. Simulations across varying noise levels, source extents, and source counts showed consistently low spatial dispersion and good localization performance. Quantitative and qualitative evaluations using real EEG recordings from epilepsy patients and intracranial stimulation experiments further supported the feasibility of the framework for source imaging. These findings suggest the potential of physics-informed self-supervised INR for extended-source imaging.

items.title: 3C-guided reflection combined with scenario simulation for humanistic care education among nursing students: a mixed methods study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Humanistic care is essential to nursing practice and directly influences patient outcomes. Since nursing students constitute the future clinical workforce, cultivating humanistic care competencies is an educational responsibility rather than a solely clinical issue. However, current training often faces challenges such as disconnection between theory and practice, highlighting the need for effective teaching models. Based on reflective practice theory, this study evaluates a multicomponent educational intervention integrating 3 C (Context, Content, Course) guided reflection with scenario simulation for humanistic care education among undergraduate nursing students. Methods A sequential explanatory mixed methods design was employed. In the first phase, all seven intact classes of first-year nursing students (total n = 350) from a medical university in Guizhou Province were included and randomly assigned using a random number table at the class level to either the intervention group (4 classes, n = 200) or the control group (3 classes, n = 150). The intervention group received a single, integrated 160-minute classroom-based session consisting of 40 min of theoretical instruction, 40 min of scenario simulation, 40 min of 3 C-guided reflection, and 40 min of summary and assessment activities, whereas the control group received traditional theoretical instruction within a 160-minute session that also included assessment activities. Outcomes were assessed using the Caring Ability Inventory, theoretical knowledge tests, and satisfaction questionnaires. Quantitative outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models accounting for class-level clustering; CAI models additionally adjusted for the corresponding baseline scores. In the second phase, 40 nursing students were purposively selected from the intervention group for semi-structured in-depth interviews, and data were analyzed thematically. Results The intervention group had a higher immediate post-intervention score on the self-report Caring Ability Inventory (CAI) than the control group (adjusted mean difference = 19.68 points, 95% CI 17.04–22.33; standardized effect size = 1.65; P < 0.001). Higher self-reported CAI scores were also observed for the Understanding, Courage, and Patience subscales. The intervention group also had a higher immediate post-intervention theoretical knowledge score (mean difference = 4.80 points, 95% CI 0.72–8.88, P = 0.021). Learner evaluations of the intervention were generally favorable. Qualitative analysis revealed four themes: empathy awakening, cognitive reconstruction through structured reflection, courage cultivation, and conceptual shift toward professional caring. Conclusion This sequential explanatory mixed methods study (a cluster randomized trial plus qualitative interviews) provides preliminary evidence that the multicomponent 3 C-guided scenario simulation model is associated with higher immediate post-intervention self-reported CAI scores and theoretical knowledge scores among undergraduate nursing students following a single-session intervention. Qualitative findings provided complementary insights into students’ experiences; however, the study design cannot establish long-term causality or sustained competency development. The independent contribution of 3C-guided reflection cannot be determined from this multicomponent intervention. The potential role of the “experience–reflection–abstraction” cycle warrants further investigation through multi-center, longitudinal studies incorporating objective behavioral assessments.

items.title: Role of Personality in Conversational Information Seeking
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for information seeking, where users find, compare, and evaluate information through dialogue. In this role, the assistant does more than retrieve or generate content: it shapes how users articulate constraints, ask follow-up questions, verify claims, and decide when an answer is sufficient for action. Yet little is known about how user personality, assistant personality, and task context jointly influence these interactions. We examine personality as a controllable variable in conversational information seeking and study its effects on user behaviour and interaction quality. We conducted a controlled within-subject study in which assistant personality and task type were experimentally varied, while participant personality was measured using Big Five scores. Twenty-six participants each completed three information-seeking tasks under three assistant personality conditions: extraverted, conscientious, and neutral. Tasks covered exploratory travel planning, comparative smartphone shopping, and verification-sensitive health and diet information seeking. Data included conversation logs, behavioural traces, post-interaction questionnaires, an exit questionnaire, and Big Five measures. The assistant conditions were behaviourally distinct: the extraverted assistant produced longer turns, the conscientious assistant elicited higher user word share and more turns, and the neutral baseline fell between them. The strongest effect was a task-by-assistant interaction on trust and delegation, with preferred styles varying by task. No global winner emerged, but participants strongly preferred style choice or adaptation. These findings position assistant personality as a context-sensitive interactional design variable rather than a globally optimisable system property.

items.title: Outcome-aware Evaluation of Recommendation Rankings in Art Therapy Using Multimodal Physiological Utility
items.abstract: Recommender systems are often evaluated using observable behavioral signals as surrogate relevance measures of user experience.However, in well-being and mental health support applications, user experience is inherently non-observable.To address this limitation, we introduce a multimodal physiology-driven framework for evaluating recommendation rankings in art therapy using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) and eye-gaze signals.We define a physiological utility scalar that captures item-level internal response by combining prefrontal hemodynamic responses with attention and engagement dynamics derived from gaze behavior, enabling direct comparison between system-generated rankings and rankings induced by internal user responses.We show that fNIRS-derived utility exhibits moderate alignment with system rankings (Spearman's 𝜌 ≈ 0.40, pairwise accuracy ≈ 0.69), with inter-hemispheric functional connectivity showing the strongest alignment among the evaluated neural descriptors.Gaze-derived utility yields stronger observed alignment (𝜌 ≈ 0.55, pairwise accuracy ≈ 0.75), particularly for attention continuity and engagementrelated representations.Multimodal integration yielded the highest observed agreement between recommendation rankings and physiology-derived utility (𝜌 ≈ 0.61, pairwise accuracy ≈ 0.77).Our findings provide exploratory evidence that multimodal physiological signals may offer complementary information for evaluating recommendation rankings in outcome-sensitive art therapy.

items.title: The Compaction Cliff in Long-Running AI Agent Memory
items.abstract: A safety rule and an episodic log compete for the same tokens in an AI agent's context. When the budget overflows, both are summarized at the same rate; only the rule needs exact wording to remain enforceable. On 20 production agent configurations, Claude Code's /compact prompt on Sonnet 4.6 preserves 53\% of safety rules after one compaction round and 10\% after five. We name this the Compaction Cliff. We address it with Knowledge Triage, a framework that classifies each line of an agent's knowledge base by type and routes each type through its own retention policy. Three deterministic operators implement this triage across the three context-management operations: TypeCompact rewrites items in place under per-type fidelity, TypeDecompose partitions a topic too large to compact safely, replicating in-scope safety rules across partitions, and TypeRetrieve fetches items from external storage with in-scope rules pinned ahead of relevance. On five public corpora, TypeCompact preserves 2--4$\times$ more safety rules than the strongest single-shot LLM compactor at every ratio, with 96\% recall over five rounds. TypeDecompose reaches 0\% locality violations against 93\% under uniform partitioning. TypeRetrieve reaches 100\% recall@50 against 73\% for the best single-shot LLM retriever. On three downstream behavioral benchmarks, we outperform the production Sonnet compactor on medical compliance (paired McNemar $p < 10^{-8}$ on preservation, $N = 200$), the full-policy and hierarchical baselines on retail task pass rate ($p < 0.01$, $N = 115$), and the hierarchical compaction on the airline domain ($p = 0.024$). We release AgentArtifactCorpus (396{,}934 agent configurations from 54{,}628 public GitHub repositories), the classifier, and the reference implementation.

items.title: Do General NLP Embeddings Capture Ontological Reasoning?
items.abstract: General-purpose NLP embedding models perform well on linguistic tasks, but their ability to capture symbolic ontological structure remains unclear. We introduce AVA, a systematic framework for evaluating whether embeddings distinguish logic-sensitive relational semantics in ontologies and knowledge graphs. AVA comprises 171,007 contrastive triplets derived from 163 heterogeneous ontologies using hierarchy inversion, relation substitution, and disjointness injection. Each triplet contains an ontology statement, a semantically equivalent paraphrase, and a logic-sensitive hard negative with contradictory relational meaning. We evaluate more than 25 state-of-the-art embedding models and find substantial limitations: the best model achieves only 0.739 triplet accuracy, while hard negative accuracy falls to 0.135. Fine-tuning improves discrimination by a large margin but transfers poorly to downstream Semantic Web tasks, including taxonomy discovery and ontology alignment. Further analysis suggests that improvements stem partly from perturbation-specific pattern recognition rather than robust ontological understanding. These findings reveal a persistent gap between linguistic representation learning and ontology-level discrimination, challenging the assumption that strong NLP benchmark performance translates to Semantic Web competence.

items.title: E-MODULE BIOLENDO BERBASIS INKUIRI TERBIMBING BERMUATAN POTENSI LOKAL UNTUK MENINGKATKAN BERPIKIR KREATIF DAN KOLABORASI SISWA
items.abstract: This research was motivated by the low creative thinking and collaboration skills of students in science subjects due to the minimal use of digital teaching materials and the lack of integration of local potential in learning. To address this issue, this study aimed to develop the BIOLENDO e-module based on guided inquiry integrated with the local potential of galendo on Ecology and Biodiversity topics. This study employed the Research and Development (R&D) method using the Lee and Owens model with a quasi-experimental Non-equivalent Control Group Design involving seventh-grade students at MTs Darul Ulum, Ciamis Regency. The results revealed that the average N-gain for creative thinking in the experimental class reached 0.514 (moderate category), which was significantly superior to the control class at 0.377 (t=4.005;df=58;p<0.001), with a large effect size (Cohen's d = 1.034). Furthermore, students' collaboration skills showed a marked improvement from an initial baseline of 55.00% to 80.06%, placing it in the high category. Thus, the BIOLENDO e-module is proven to be valid, practical, and effective in enhancing creative thinking skills as well as supporting students' collaborative capabilities. ABSTRAK Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh rendahnya kemampuan berpikir kreatif dan kolaborasi peserta didik pada mata pelajaran IPA akibat minimnya pemanfaatan bahan ajar digital serta belum terintegrasinya potensi lokal dalam pembelajaran. Untuk mengatasi permasalahan tersebut, penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan e-module BIOLENDO berbasis inkuiri terbimbing bermuatan potensi lokal galendo pada materi Ekologi dan Keanekaragaman Hayati yang teruji valid, praktis, dan efektif. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode Research and Development (R&D) model Lee dan Owens dengan desain eksperimen semu Non-equivalent Control Group Design pada peserta didik kelas VII MTs Darul Ulum Kabupaten Ciamis. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan rata-rata N-gain berpikir kreatif kelas eksperimen mencapai 0,514 (kategori sedang), lebih unggul dibandingkan kelas kontrol sebesar 0,377 (kategori sedang), dengan perbedaan signifikan secara statistik (t=4,005;df=58;p<0,001) serta effect size Cohen's d sebesar 1,034 (efek besar). Sementara itu, kemampuan kolaborasi peserta didik meningkat nyata dari kondisi awal sebesar 55,00% menjadi 80,06% pada akhir pembelajaran dan berada pada kategori tinggi. Dengan demikian, e-module BIOLENDO terbukti valid, praktis, dan efektif dalam meningkatkan kemampuan berpikir kreatif serta mengoptimalkan kolaborasi peserta didik.

items.title: Large Language Model as Universal Retriever in Industrial-Scale Recommender System
items.abstract: In real-world recommender systems, different retrieval objectives are typically addressed using task-specific datasets with carefully designed model architectures. We demonstrate that Large Language Models (LLMs) can function as universal retrievers, capable of handling multiple objectives within a generative retrieval framework. To address the model expressiveness and inference efficiency issues of generative retrieval, we propose multi-query representation and transferable discriminative mapping layers to model complex user-item relationships, and incorporate probabilistic sampling to reduce computation costs. Finally, our Universal Retrieval Model (URM) can adaptively generate a set from tens of millions of candidates based on an arbitrary given objective while keeping the latency within tens of milliseconds. Applied to industrial-scale data, URM outperforms expert models elaborately designed for different retrieval objectives in offline experiments and achieves a 3.13% revenue increase on our online advertising platform. URM also demonstrates strong performance in impression and GMV for long-tail and cold-start items.

items.title: FinMamba: Market-Aware Graph Enhanced Multi-Level Mamba for Stock Movement Prediction
items.abstract: Recently, combining stock features with inter-stock correlations has become a common and effective approach for stock movement prediction. However, financial data presents significant challenges due to its low signal-to-noise ratio and the dynamic complexity of the market, which give rise to two key limitations in existing methods. First, the relationships between stocks are highly influenced by multifaceted factors including macroeconomic market dynamics, and current models fail to adaptively capture these evolving interactions under specific market conditions. Second, for the accuracy and timeliness required by real-world trading, existing financial data mining methods struggle to extract beneficial pattern-oriented dependencies from long historical data while maintaining high efficiency and low memory consumption. To address the limitations, we propose FinMamba, a Mamba-GNN-based framework for market-aware and multi-level hybrid stock movement prediction. Specifically, we devise a dynamic graph to learn the changing representations of inter-stock relationships by integrating a pruning module that adapts to market trends. Afterward, with a selective mechanism, the multi-level Mamba discards irrelevant information and resets states to skillfully recall historical patterns across multiple time scales with linear time costs, which are then jointly optimized for reliable prediction. Extensive experiments on U.S. and Chinese stock markets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed FinMamba, achieving state-of-the-art prediction accuracy and trading profitability, while maintaining low computational complexity. The code is available at https://github.com/TROUBADOUR000/FinMamba.

items.title: Exploring Model Invariance with Discrete Search for Ultra-Low-Bit Quantization
items.abstract: As language models continue to grow in size due to their success in a wide range of applications such as conversational agents and coding, there is a pressing need to make them more accessible. A popular technique is to reduce their memory footprint by post-training quantization, where we use fewer bits (e.g., 4--8 bits) to represent the model without retraining it. However, quantizing language models remains a challenging task, especially in the ultra-low-bit setup (e.g., 2 bits). In this paper, we propose InvarExplore, a unified framework that systematically explores different kinds of model invariance to maximize quantization performance. Importantly, InvarExplore features a discrete search algorithm that enables us to explore permutation invariance, which is under-studied as it cannot be optimized with gradient-based methods. Such exploration allows us to take advantage of the synergy between each type of invariance. Our results and in-depth analyses show that InvarExplore is compatible with existing state-of-the-art integer quantization methods, achieving an add-on performance improvement over strong competing methods.

items.title: Towards Comprehensible Recommendation with Large Language Model Fine-tuning
items.abstract: Recommender systems have become increasingly ubiquitous in daily life. While traditional recommendation approaches primarily rely on ID-based representations or item-side content features, they often fall short in capturing the underlying semantics aligned with user preferences (e.g., recommendation reasons for items), leading to a semantic-collaborative gap. Recently emerged LLM-based feature extraction approaches also face a key challenge: how to ensure that LLMs possess recommendation-aligned reasoning capabilities and can generate accurate, personalized reasons to mitigate the semantic-collaborative gap. To address these issues, we propose a novel Content Understanding from a Collaborative Perspective framework (CURec), which generates collaborative-aligned content features for more comprehensive recommendations. CURec first adapts the LLM with recommendation objectives through post-training, equipping it with instruction-following and chain-of-thought reasoning capabilities. Next, we use the LLM-generated features to train the recommender model. Then, we treat the user-item prediction scores produced by the trained recommender model as reward signals to guide RL-based refinement of the LLM, thereby improving the quality of generated reasons and pattern. The corrected reasons are directly integrated into the recommender model to enhance comprehensibility and recommendation performance. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks demonstrate the superiority of CURec over existing methods.

items.title: ELBO TDS : Temporal Distribution Shift Generalization for Industry-Scale Recommender Systems
items.abstract: Temporal distribution shift (TDS) erodes the long-term accuracy of recommender systems, yet industrial practice still relies on periodic incremental training, which struggles to capture both stable and transient patterns. Existing approaches such as invariant learning and self-supervised learning offer partial solutions but often suffer from unstable temporal generalization, representation collapse, or inefficient data utilization. To address these limitations, we propose ELBO$_\text{TDS}$, a probabilistic framework that integrates seamlessly into industry-scale incremental learning pipelines. First, we identify key shifting factors through statistical analysis of real-world production data and design a simple yet effective data augmentation strategy that resamples these time-varying factors to extend the training support. Second, to harness the benefits of this extended distribution while preventing representation collapse, we model the temporal recommendation scenario using a causal graph and derive a self-supervised variational objective, ELBO$_\text{TDS}$, grounded in the causal structure. Extensive experiments supported by both theoretical and empirical analysis demonstrate that our method achieves superior temporal generalization, yielding a 2.33\% uplift in GMV per user and has been successfully deployed in Shopee Product Search. Code is available at https://github.com/FuCongResearchSquad/ELBO4TDS.

items.title: Agent-R1: A Unified and Modular Framework for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have rapidly evolved from single-turn text generators into the foundation of increasingly capable agents. As these agents take on more complex reasoning, decision making, tool use, and long-horizon tasks, reinforcement learning (RL) is becoming increasingly important for shaping their behavior. This shift is especially visible in agentic RL, where models must interact with tools and environments across multiple rounds rather than produce a single standalone response. In this regime, the usual view of a trajectory as one ever-growing token sequence becomes increasingly inadequate: it makes context evolution rigid and creates representation mismatches between rollout and training. This paper presents Agent-R1, a unified and modular framework for agentic RL built around step-level trajectory representation, flexible context management, and layered interfaces for workflows, environments and optimization. The key idea is to treat each interaction step as the basic reinforcement-learning transition, while keeping the optimization layer flexible: once the interaction is modeled at the step level, the framework can support token-level credit assignment, step-level credit assignment, or other compatible designs. These design choices make the framework compatible with a range of optimization strategies rather than tying it to a single algorithm. Together, these components provide a principled, extensible, and reusable substrate for agentic RL.

items.title: PosIR: A Multilingual Benchmark for Diagnosing Position Bias in Information Retrieval
items.abstract: In real-world documents, the information relevant to a user query may reside anywhere from the beginning to the end. This makes position bias -- a systematic tendency of retrieval models to favor or neglect content based on its location -- a critical concern. Although recent studies have identified such bias, existing analyses focus predominantly on English, fail to disentangle document length from information position, and lack a standardized framework for systematic diagnosis. To address these limitations, we introduce PosIR (Position-Aware Information Retrieval), the first standardized benchmark designed to systematically diagnose position bias in diverse retrieval scenarios. PosIR comprises 310 datasets spanning 10 languages and 31 domains, with relevance tied to precise reference spans. At its methodological core, PosIR employs a length-controlled bucketing strategy that groups queries by positive document length and analyzes positional effects within each bucket. This design strictly isolates position bias from length-induced performance degradation. Extensive experiments on 10 state-of-the-art embedding-based retrieval models reveal that: (1) retrieval performance on PosIR with documents exceeding 1536 tokens correlates poorly with the MMTEB benchmark, exposing limitations of current short-text evaluations; (2) position bias is pervasive in embedding models and even increases with document length, with most models exhibiting primacy bias while certain models show unexpected recency bias; (3) as an exploratory investigation, gradient-based saliency analysis further uncovers two distinct internal mechanisms that correlate with these positional preferences. We hope that PosIR can serve as a valuable diagnostic framework to advance the development of position-robust retrieval systems.

items.title: GraFine: Retrieval-Time Refinement for Efficient Graph RAG over Corpus Graphs
items.abstract: Graph RAG on corpus graphs enhances retrieval by leveraging intermediate node content as contextual clues to uncover unretrieved oracle nodes. However, existing methods suffer from two critical blind spots, namely semantically blind graph expansion and topology blind pruning, or else rely on prohibitively slow retrieval and generation interleaving. To address this, we formalize these limitations through an operational taxonomy and propose a retriever design that couples semantics-aware adding with graph-aware pruning under efficiency constraints. We instantiate this design as GraFine, which alternates between two refinement stages: Semantic Proximity eXpansion (SPX) for semantics-aware node addition, and a Graph Smoothing Reranker (GSR) for graph-aware pruning. Experiments on reference networks and text-rich knowledge graphs show that GraFine improves retrieval accuracy and generation quality while maintaining time-efficiency. Furthermore, we introduce Topological Recall (TR), a metric that quantifies the topological proximity between retrieved and oracle nodes. Our analysis using TR confirms that GraFine more effectively steers refinement toward undiscovered oracle nodes by leveraging intermediate contextual clues. Our code is available at this link: https://github.com/asmath472/GraFine.

items.title: Mine and Refine: Optimizing Graded Relevance in E-commerce Semantic Search Retrieval
items.abstract: Embedding-based retrieval (EBR) for large-scale e-commerce search faces three intertwined challenges: graded (non-binary) relevance where engagement signals are noisy and intent-varying while business relevance guidelines admit acceptable-but-not-exact matches, false negatives in hard sample mining, and unstable similarity score separability across relevance levels, the last of which complicates hybrid search score fusion and downstream ranking. We propose Mine and Refine, a two-stage contrastive training framework that addresses all three. A lightweight LLM, fine-tuned with engagement-driven audit, serves as a guideline-aligned scalable labeler throughout training. Stage 1 establishes a robust global embedding space via label-aware supervised contrastive learning; Stage 2 mines hard samples, re-annotates them with the LLM labeler to mitigate spurious negatives, and refines the model through a multi-level extension of circle loss that enforces margin-controlled separation across relevance levels. Deployed in production e-commerce search across multiple product verticals, the approach delivers statistically significant lifts in user engagement and gross order value, and substantially improves retrieval and end-to-end relevance metrics.

items.title: MOSAIC: Unveiling the Moral, Social and Individual Dimensions of Large Language Models
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in sensitive applications including psychological support, healthcare, and high-stakes decision-making. This expansion has motivated growing research into the ethical and moral foundations underlying LLM behavior, raising critical questions about their reliability in ethical reasoning. However, existing studies and benchmarks rely almost exclusively on Moral Foundation Theory (MFT), largely neglecting other relevant dimensions such as social values, personality traits, and individual characteristics that shape human ethical reasoning. To address these limitations, we introduce MOSAIC, the first large-scale benchmark designed to jointly assess the moral, social, and individual characteristics of LLMs. The benchmark comprises nine validated questionnaires drawn from moral philosophy, psychology, and social theory, alongside four platform-based games designed to probe morally ambiguous scenarios. In total, MOSAIC includes over 600 curated questions and scenarios, released as a ready-to-use, extensible resource for evaluating the behavioral foundations of LLMs. We validate the benchmark across three models from different families, demonstrating its utility across all assessed dimensions and providing the first empirical evidence that MFT alone is insufficient to comprehensively evaluate complex AI systems' ethical behavior. We publicly release the dataset and our benchmark Python library.

items.title: DEP: A Decentralized Evaluation Protocol and Toolkit for Large Language Models
items.abstract: With the rapid development of Large Language Models (LLMs), a large number of benchmarks have been proposed. However, most benchmarks lack unified evaluation standard and require the manual implementation of custom scripts, making results hard to ensure consistency and reproducibility. Furthermore, mainstream evaluation frameworks are centralized, with datasets and answers, which increases the risk of benchmark leakage. To address these issues, we propose a Decentralized Evaluation Protocol (DEP), a decentralized yet unified and standardized evaluation framework through a matching server without constraining benchmarks. The server can be mounted locally or deployed remotely, and once adapted, it can be reused over the long term. By decoupling users, LLMs, and benchmarks, DEP enables modular, plug-and-play evaluation: benchmark files and evaluation logic stay exclusively on the server side. In remote setting, users cannot access the ground truth, thereby achieving data isolation and leak-proof evaluation. To facilitate practical adoption, we develop DEP Toolkit, a protocol-compatible toolkit that supports features such as breakpoint resume, concurrent requests, and congestion control. We also provide detailed documentation for adapting new benchmarks to DEP. Using DEP toolkit, we evaluate multiple LLMs across benchmarks. Experimental results verify the effectiveness of DEP and show that it reduces the cost of deploying benchmark evaluations. As of February 2026, we have adapted over 60 benchmarks and continue to promote community co-construction to support unified evaluation across various tasks and domains.

items.title: Eval4Sim: An Evaluation Framework for Persona Simulation
items.abstract: Large Language Model personas, explicit profiles specifying a user's attributes, preferences, and behavioural tendencies, are increasingly used to simulate human conversations for user modelling, social reasoning, and behavioural analysis. Evaluating whether such simulations faithfully reflect human conversational behaviour is critical, yet current practice often relies on LLM-as-a-judge approaches that provide limited grounding in observable behaviour and produce opaque scalar scores. We present Eval4Sim, an evaluation framework that measures alignment between simulated and human conversations across three dimensions: adherence, whether persona traits are recoverable from dialogue via dense retrieval; consistency, whether a persona maintains a distinguishable stylistic identity via authorship verification; and naturalness, whether conversations exhibit human-like turn-to-turn flow via dialogue NLI. Unlike optimization-oriented metrics, each dimension takes a human corpus as a reference baseline and penalizes deviations in both directions, distinguishing insufficient persona encoding from over-optimized, unnatural behaviour. The framework is corpus-agnostic: any persona-annotated conversational dataset can serve as the reference. Evaluated over ten simulation corpora, Eval4Sim surfaces systematic trade-offs invisible to single-score methods.

items.title: Semantic Caching: From Exact Hits to Close Enough
items.abstract: The rapid adoption of large language models (LLMs) has created demand for faster responses and lower costs. Semantic caching, reusing semantically similar requests via their embeddings, addresses this need but breaks classic cache assumptions and raises new challenges. In this paper, we explore offline policies for semantic caching, proving that implementing an optimal offline policy is NP-hard, and propose several polynomial-time heuristics. We also present online semantic aware cache policies that combine recency, frequency, and locality. Evaluations on diverse datasets show that while frequency based policies are strong baselines, our novel variant improves semantic accuracy. Our findings reveal effective strategies for current systems and highlight substantial headroom for future innovation. All code is open source.

items.title: TagLLM: A Fine-Grained Tag Generation Approach for Note Recommendation
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown promising potential in E-commerce community recommendation. While LLMs and Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) are widely used to encode notes into implicit embeddings, leveraging their generative capabilities to represent notes with interpretable tags remains unexplored. In the field of tag generation, traditional close-ended methods heavily rely on the design of tag pools, while existing open-ended methods applied directly to note recommendations face two limitations: (1) MLLMs lack guidance during generation, resulting in redundant tags that fail to capture user interests; (2) The generated tags are often coarse and lack fine-grained representation of notes, interfering with downstream recommendations. To address these limitations, we propose TagLLM, a fine-grained tag generation method for note recommendation. TagLLM captures user interests across note categories through a User Interest Handbook and constructs fine-grained tag data using multimodal CoT Extraction. A Tag Knowledge Distillation method is developed to equip small models with competitive generation capabilities, enhancing inference efficiency. In online A/B test, TagLLM increases average view duration per user by 0.31%, average interactions per user by 0.96%, and page view click-through rate in cold-start scenario by 32.37%, demonstrating its effectiveness.

items.title: ContextClaim: A Context-Driven Paradigm for Verifiable Claim Detection
items.abstract: Automated fact-checking pipelines typically begin with a filtering stage that decides which claims are worth verifying, given that the later evidence retrieval and verification components are expensive to apply at scale. A central task in this stage is verifiable claim detection, which asks whether a statement is in principle checkable against external evidence. Prior work on this task, as well as on the closely related notion of check-worthiness, conditions its decisions only on the claim sentence itself. We argue that this is restrictive, because deciding whether a statement is checkable often depends on identifying the entities and events it mentions, and on whether external information about them is actually available in the first place. Motivated by how downstream verification systems rely on retrieved evidence, we move retrieval upstream into the detection stage and introduce ContextClaim. Given an input claim, the approach identifies entity mentions, queries Wikipedia as a structured background source, and uses large language models to compress the retrieved material into short contextual summaries that are then passed to a classifier. Experiments are conducted on two domains and genres, namely the CheckThat! 2022 Twitter collection and the PoliClaim corpus of political debates, and cover both encoder and decoder only models under fine-tuning, zero-shot, and few-shot settings. The added context yields gains on verifiable claim detection in several configurations, although the size of the improvement varies with the dataset, the backbone model, and the training setup. We further find that the same retrieved summaries are useful beyond detection. Feeding them into a downstream verification model on FEVER improves verification F1. Component level analyses, human annotation, and error inspection further clarify the conditions under which retrieved context helps, and where it does not.

items.title: Culture or cognition?
items.abstract: Abstract Gender languages assign nouns to a category, such as masculine, feminine, neuter or common. Gender assignment is complicated and difficult to learn, as languages do not have specific rules for assigning a noun to one or the other gender. This study looks at gender assignment from the perspective of semantics and lexical semantic evolution, exemplified on the Indo-European family. Gender assignment has a semantic core, in which animate nouns are more likely to be masculine, inanimate nouns feminine and neuter, nature nouns masculine, and culture nouns feminine or neuter. To investigate how these patterns emerge, we study the evolutionary dynamics of these semantic properties on a gender-coded lexical data set for Indo-European. We find that masculine is a stable gender that remains in its semantic category and does not change. Feminine is also a stable category which may get lost or transfer to masculine. Neuter and common are unstable categories, which continuously alter or get lost in gender assignment. In sum, our result shows that the semantic core of gender — affected both by cognitive and cultural factors — remains stable and does not vacillate in evolution.

items.title: Understanding Biodiversity in Acer Forests: From Species Diversity to Sustainable Conservation
items.abstract: The genus Acer comprises more than 110 tree and shrub species distributed throughout the Northern Hemisphere and represents an important component of temperate forest ecosystems. This review evaluates biodiversity patterns, ecological functions, environmental pressures, and conservation approaches associated with Acer forests. A systematic literature search conducted in the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus databases on 20 January 2026, without publication-year restrictions. After screening and eligibility assessment, 688 publications were included and analyzed using bibliometric methods and qualitative thematic synthesis. The literature increased substantially over the last four decades, with climate change, biodiversity conservation, forest dynamics, and sustainable management among the principal research themes. The selected studies covered species and genetic diversity, forest composition and dynamics, associated plant, fungal, and animal communities, environmental change, and conservation and management. Native Acer forests were frequently associated with structurally complex habitats, diverse understory communities, nutrient cycling, and multiple ecosystem functions, whereas habitat loss, fragmentation, climate change, atmospheric pollution, and biological invasions were identified as major pressures. Introduced species, particularly Acer negundo, were also frequently examined in relation to impacts on native biodiversity. Important research gaps concerned poorly studied endemic species, long-term monitoring, multitrophic interactions, and the effectiveness of conservation measures under environmental change. Future research should integrate ecological, genetic, physiological, and remote-sensing approaches to support evidence-based conservation and sustainable management of Acer forests. This review provides a systematic and bibliometric synthesis of the indexed English-language literature retrieved using the specified search strategy and identifies major research patterns, evidence gaps, and conservation priorities relevant to Acer forests biodiversity under environmental change.

items.title: Decompression With or Without Fusion Across Subgroups With Degenerative Lumbar Spondylolisthesis : A Target Trial Emulation.
items.abstract: Background Randomized trials have shown limited benefits and increased risks of adding spinal fusion surgery to decompression for degenerative spondylolisthesis. Decompression with fusion has increasingly been used in the United States. Objective To examine the comparative effectiveness of decompression with fusion versus decompression alone for patient subgroups. Design Cohort study using the target trial framework. Setting Norwegian Registry for Spine Surgery and nested NORDSTEN-DS (Norwegian degenerative spondylolisthesis and spinal stenosis) randomized trial. Patients Adults aged 18 to 80 years with lumbar degenerative spondylolisthesis and symptomatic back or leg pain lasting at least 3 months. Intervention Lumbar spinal decompression surgery with fusion versus lumbar spinal decompression surgery alone. Measurements The primary outcomes were Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) score and reoperation at 12 months. Linear regression models with inverse probability weighting to control for baseline confounding were used to obtain effect estimates with 95% CIs for decompression with fusion versus decompression alone for prespecified subgroups, including sex, age, smoking, body mass index (BMI), back pain intensity, and American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) grade. Results Of 2252 patients, 236 were in the NORDSTEN-DS randomized trial. The mean age was 66 years, and 1576 (70%) women were included. A total of 1446 patients had decompression alone, and 806 had decompression with fusion; respective unadjusted baseline ODI scores were 38.9 (SD, 14.9) and 41.4 (SD, 14.7). At 12 months, the ODI score was 22.3 (95% CI, 15.5 to 29.1) for decompression alone and 20.0 (CI, 13.9 to 26.2) for decompression with fusion; the mean difference was 2.2 (CI, -1.6 to 6.1). In exploratory analyses, the ODI score was worse for decompression with fusion for men with BMI of 30 kg/m 2 or higher. Reoperation risk at 12 months did not differ. Limitation Possible residual confounding. Conclusion Patient subgroups did not have differential effects from the addition of fusion to decompression at 12 months. items.title: Mapping three decades of consciousness research in neuroscience: a scientometric synthesis of intellectual evolution and emerging frontiers.
items.abstract: Over the past three decades, consciousness research in neuroscience has expanded into a broad and increasingly diverse field. Despite significant progress, a quantitative understanding of how these research areas have collectively evolved has remained limited. In this study, we conducted a large-scale scientometric analysis of consciousness research in neuroscience based on 22,836 publications and 639,975 cited references retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection spanning 1998-2025. We identified three major research paths: neural correlates of conscious contents and states, internal awareness and self-consciousness, and integrative approaches bridging these two paths. Emerging hotspots included neural mechanisms of consciousness, subjective experience, disorders of consciousness (DoC), and interoception. Despite increasing boundary-spanning research across different areas, bibliometric connections between DoC and other major topics, particularly subjective experience and interoception, remain comparatively sparse. These findings provide a field-level synthesis of consciousness research in neuroscience, offering a quantitative framework for understanding its development and emerging research directions.

items.title: Exploring resident doctors' experience, attitudes, perceptions and beliefs about the serious incident investigatory process within mental health settings.
items.abstract: Background Serious incidents, such as patient suicide, profoundly impact clinicians. In mental health settings, these events are uniquely distressing. Despite policy shifts towards learning from serious incidents, many doctors report inadequate support and significant emotional distress. Resident doctors, already vulnerable to burnout and emotional exhaustion, are particularly at risk. Aims This study aimed to understand resident psychiatry doctors' experiences of serious incidents. It sought to gather in-depth insights about how resident psychiatrists navigate the serious incident process, and the effect the process has on their professional and personal lives. Method A qualitative study recruited 10 participants via email in 1 National Health Service (NHS) trust. Semi-structured online interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed and analysed using Braun and Clarke's six-phase thematic analysis, employing an iterative, constant comparative approach. Results Descriptive characteristics of the participants are reported. Three overarching themes were identified: (a) when the process becomes the experience, with subthemes focusing on how open and transparent the investigation process was, about communication during the process and how doctors felt the process impacted their clinical role; (b) from theory to practice: when training meets reality. Subthemes here reflected on whether resident doctors felt prepared and knowledgeable about the process. There was also focus on the experience itself being a learning opportunity; (c) the emotional undercurrents: trauma, grief and support. Here the subthemes focused on the emotional toll of an incident and investigation, the grief and wider impact of a patient death and lastly, the need for support to resident doctors including supervisor and peer-to-peer support. Themes are reported accompanied by verbatim quotes from participants. Conclusions Findings confirm prior studies investigating the negative impact of serious incidents on resident doctors' well-being and career confidence, highlighting the need for robust support. The study adds to the literature through emphasising the inadequacy of current support and highlights rectifiable issues such as the need for structured peer support and improved supervisor/resident training for emotional and professional complexities. Future research should compare these findings with experiences under the new Patient Safety Incident Framework (PSIRF) system to assess improvements.

items.title: Exploring the Relationship Between Maternal-Infant (Dyadic) Attachment, Postpartum Depression, and Breastfeeding Self-Efficacy: A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Purpose This scoping review explores intersecting relationships among the concepts of postpartum depression, maternal-infant (dyadic) attachment (or bonding), and breastfeeding self-efficacy within postpartum populations and how often these concept relationships are examined among predominantly historically marginalized populations (non-White, low-income, low education level). Background To address the ongoing public health concern of postpartum depression, we must understand its relationship with dyadic attachment and breastfeeding self-efficacy. Discussion Four studies met inclusion criteria, examining the relationships between the concepts of postpartum depression, dyadic attachment, and breastfeeding self-efficacy. Because these 4 studies had heterogeneous study designs, study measures, and study time points, the exact nature of the relationship between these 3 concepts is difficult to parse. Furthermore, only 1 study evaluated these concepts in historically marginalized populations (low-income). Future research using rigorous study design approaches is warranted. Implications for research and practice While studies found a relationship between increased breastfeeding self-efficacy and increased dyadic attachment, mixed results remain regarding the relationships between postpartum depression and dyadic attachment or breastfeeding self-efficacy. Nevertheless, dyad-focused interventions have shown the potential to improve breastfeeding self-efficacy and dyadic attachment while reducing postpartum depression. The scoping review findings suggest that these concepts collectively need more research attention, given their potential effects on improving maternal-child dyadic outcomes.
