items.title: The Survival Paradox of Close-In Planets Orbiting Red Clump Giants
items.abstract: Close-in planets orbiting core-helium-burning red-clump (RC) giants directly challenge tidal-engulfment theory, which predicts that planets within about 1 au of Sun-like stars should be engulfed during red-giant-branch (RGB) expansion. The existence of such survivors would imply missing physical processes in the late stages of stellar and planetary evolution. Yet only one such "forbidden" planet had been identified to date. Here we report three systems-24 Boo b, HD 12648 b, and TYC 4282-605-1 b-whose host stars are confirmed red-clump giants through asteroseismology, showing that each has already undergone dramatic expansion and contraction following helium ignition. Their planets now reside at orbital separations smaller than the maximum stellar radii attained during the RGB phase, implying that they should not have survived. Among them, 24 Boo b orbits at only 0.183 au with a 30-day period, making it the closest planet known around a red-clump giant. These discoveries demonstrate that this paradox is not an isolated anomaly but signals the emergence of a new class of evolved planetary systems. Their survival defies current models of stellar-planetary coevolution and points to unexplored physics shaping planetary architectures around post-RGB stars.

items.title: Fitting Resonant Exoplanets Orbits. I. Properties and Applications of Fixed-Point Orbits
items.abstract: Intact chains of mean-motion resonances may preserve information about the formation and early dynamical evolution of multiplanet systems. Although most mature multiplanet systems are non-resonant, the resonant fraction may have been substantially higher at young ages. Establishing whether exoplanet data are consistent with a resonant configuration is often challenging because the planetary orbits must be sufficiently well constrained. Moreover, while resonance configurations promote stability, standard orbital fitting methods do not impose such a dynamical constraint, with stability tested only a posteriori. As the first step in a series of papers aimed at favoring stable orbital solutions during the fitting process, we develop a method that restricts solutions to stable fixed-point orbits (fPOs)---coplanar, exactly periodic configurations associated with resonant dynamics. We show that dissipative evolution drive resonant systems toward an fPO state, motivating for fPO-constrained fitting for those planet systems that have avoided large-scale dynamical rearrangements since formation. The fPO model greatly reduces the number of free parameters and yields stable solutions by construction. We determine the best-fitting fPos through $χ^2$ minimization and apply the method to astrometric data for the directly imaged PDS 70 and HR 8799 systems and to radial-velocity data for GJ 876. For HR 8799 we independently recover a previously reported resonant solution, illustrating the fidelity of our method. For PDS 70 we find solutions fall in two groups, with the group where the outer planet c mass exceeds planet b more aligned with previous measurements. Finally, For GJ 876 our fPO fit is on par with previous unconstrained fitting, which strengthens the case that its planets reside deep in resonance.

items.title: Shallow lunar fractures dominate the long-lasting seismic coda
items.abstract: Lunar seismic records are characterized by long-lasting spindle-shaped coda, which has long been considered to be caused by strong velocity contrasts in a continuous-medium lunar crust; however, simulated waveforms could not well match the observation even with unrealistically strong velocity contrasts, demonstrating its mechanism still unsolved. Here we propose a novel model of coda wave generation with random fractures in the lunar crust, where vacuum fractures prevent seismic wave propagation as insulating boundaries, causing strong persistent reverberation in terms of total reflection among fractures. Our model can easily reproduce the typical characteristics of observed Apollo data even using a limited number of simplified fractures in homogeneous matrix, with envelope correlations over 0.9, much higher than previous studies. Numerical simulations suggest that fractures in the uppermost ~1 km of the crust may dominate lunar seismic scattering. This model enables us to investigate the shallow lunar fracture system using seismic data and to suppress seismic coda for detecting critical phases reflected from deep interiors.

items.title: Fractional Orbital Bombardment Systems
items.abstract: We analyze Fractional Orbital Bombardment Systems (FOBS) as a means of delivering nuclear weapons by placing warheads into partial orbits around the Earth, and show that they do not represent a game-changing advance in technology or capability. We consider potential uses of such a weapon, including evading missile defenses and delivering attacks with short warning time. FOBS could underfly current exoatmospheric defenses, but the required payload reduction may not justify its use if other countermeasures are deemed effective. If a FOBS attack could be successfully disguised as a satellite launch, the warning time could be short enough to raise fears of a decapitating strike. The development of such a capability could lead countries to shorten decision-making timelines in a crisis, which would be destabilizing. The US can take steps to ensure that very-short-warning attacks would not succeed, thereby enhancing deterrence during a crisis.

items.title: Life Cycle Sustainability Assessment of Fossil- and Bio-Based Membrane Manufacturing
items.abstract: The transition towards sustainable membrane manufacturing is challenged by its reliance on fossil-based polymers, organic solvents, and generation of large volumes of contaminated water. We combined process simulation, life cycle assessment, and Monte Carlo simulation to identify hotspots in the manufacturing of ultrafiltration hollow-fiber membranes for pharmaceutical applications and evaluate strategies to mitigate impact and reduce waste generation. Process models informed by industry input compared fossil- and bio-based membranes on a cradle-to-gate basis per square meter of membrane produced. Key environmental hotspots include polymer and bore solution preparation, driven by the contribution of polymer and solvent, accounting for 30-80% of total impacts across the categories investigated, and wastewater dilution, driven by the environmental burden of solvent-contaminated wastewater management. Under the modeled conditions, although polymer substitution can reduce environmental burdens, cellulose-based membranes show higher impacts than polysulfone membranes in at least 85% of simulations within each impact category, due to chemical-intensive cellulose modification and regeneration. In contrast, solvent recycling can mitigate solvent- and wastewater-related burdens when combined with reduced water demand, yielding climate change benefits at water demands below approximately 36 L per m2 under the modeled recovery configuration and highlighting its potential to reduce the environmental footprint of membrane manufacturing.

items.title: Sexual Health in Females with Multiple Sclerosis of Reproductive Age.
items.abstract: Purpose of review Sexual dysfunction is highly prevalent among females with multiple sclerosis (FwMS), yet it remains under-recognized and inadequately integrated into routine care. This review examines sexual health in FwMS of reproductive age, with particular attention to assessment, reproductive considerations, and management. Recent findings Sexual dysfunction in FwMS is often multifactorial, with contributions from neurological, physical, psychological, and relationship-related factors. Sexual dysfunction and disease-related factors may indirectly influence sexual activity, conception, and reproductive decision-making. Preconception counselling should incorporate sexual health alongside disease activity and treatment considerations. Evidence regarding sexual function during pregnancy and postpartum in FwMS remains limited. Management is individualized and may include symptom optimization, pelvic floor therapy, exercise, psychological and couples-based interventions, and selected pharmacologic therapies. Sexual health should be incorporated into comprehensive MS care, particularly during reproductive transitions. Prospective studies across preconception, pregnancy, and postpartum periods and randomized trials of interventions in FwMS are needed to guide evidence-based care.

items.title: Examining the Intersection of Quality of Life, Viral Suppression, and Race/Ethnicity Among Women with HIV.
items.abstract: Objectives Quality of life (QOL), which encompasses mental and physical health and socioeconomic stability, is an important determinant of health outcomes. This analysis assessed the relationship between QOL and viral suppression among women with HIV (WWH) in the Women's Interagency HIV Study and differences across race/ethnicity. Design A multi-center, prospective, observational cohort study of women living in the U.S. Methods Longitudinal data over a 5 year period were used to fit generalized mixed effects regression models to assess the relationship between self-reported QOL (single-item; scale of 0-10) and viral suppression ( Results In the cohort sample (n=1,324), on average, the participants were 48 years old (SD = 9.2) and living with HIV while in the study for 16 years. Approximately 90% identified as heterosexual; 70% as Black/African American, 16% as Hispanic, and 11% as White. Roughly 20% of the cohort was not virally suppressed. QOL was positively associated with viral suppression (adjusted odds ratio (aOR)=1.10, 95% CI: 1.04, 1.16). However, the magnitude of this association varied by race/ethnicity, with the highest association among White WWH (aOR=1.36, 95% CI: 1.10, 1.63) and lowest among Black WWH (aOR= 1.08, 95% CI: 1.02, 1.15). Conclusion These findings highlight a positive association between QOL and viral suppression and a moderating effect by race. Future research should assess which specific QOL domains are driving this association to inform tailored interventions.

items.title: Pediatric Epilepsy Surgery: Global Survey of Surgical Approaches.
items.abstract: Background and objectives Pediatric epilepsy surgery is an established treatment, but current global data on surgical practices are limited. This study, conducted by the International League Against Epilepsy Pediatric Epilepsy Surgery Taskforce, provides an updated international overview of surgical approaches and their regional variation. Methods Group-level data were collected from 61 epilepsy surgery programs (49 pediatric-only) across 29 countries on 6 continents. All children and adolescents who underwent epilepsy surgery in 2023 were included. The study was designed to enable direct comparison with the similar survey conducted by the International League Against Epilepsy in 2004. Results The cohort comprised 2427 patients. Resections accounted for 50.6% and disconnections for 23.0% of procedures. Resection rates were highest in Oceania (87.3%) and lowest in North America (40.3%). Resections were 43.0% unilobar-most commonly temporal (39.6%) and frontal (32.7%)-and 9.7% multilobar, with 61.9% involving the posterior quadrant. Hemispheric surgeries comprised 12.9% of all cases (highest in South America: 18.1%). Subcortical procedures (eg, for hypothalamic hamartomas or deep-seated lesions) represented 2.7% (highest in South America: 12.1%). Intraoperative electrocorticography was used in 38.3% of cases, most commonly in Oceania (84.1%) and Asia (85.5%). Minimally invasive techniques were used in 7.7% of cases, with the highest rate in North America (16.9%). Laser interstitial thermal therapy was most common (4.9%), followed by radiofrequency ablation (2.1%), endoscopic surgery (0.7%), and radiosurgery (0.1%). Corpus callosotomy was performed in 5.9% of all cases, and no multiple subpial transections were reported. Neurostimulation was used in 14.7% of patients, highest in North America (35.6%), and included vagal nerve stimulation (11.8%), deep brain stimulation (1.5%), and responsive neurostimulation (1.4%). Conclusion Resections and disconnections, including extensive multilobar and hemispheric procedures, remain the core procedures of pediatric epilepsy surgery. Although minimally invasive and neuromodulatory techniques are increasingly used in selected regions-particularly North America-their global adoption remains limited.

items.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Anterior and Posterior Surgical Approaches for Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy: An Economic Evaluation of a Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract: Background and objectives Surgery for cervical spondylotic myelopathy improves quality of life but remains expensive. We conducted a cost-effectiveness analysis of patients treated with anterior cervical diskectomy/fusion (ACDF), posterior cervical decompression/fusion (PCDF), and laminoplasty (LP) in the Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy Surgical (CSM-S) Trial, a randomized trial comparing surgical approaches for cervical spondylotic myelopathy. Methods In the trial, patients were randomized (2:3) to anterior (ACDF) or posterior surgery (LP or PCDF, at surgeon's discretion). A cost-effectiveness analysis was performed from a societal perspective with a 1-year time horizon, including only US patients as-treated. Cumulative costs were estimated using patient data on utilization and lost productivity using a human capital approach. Direct costs were calculated using 2022 Medicare rates for professional fees and cost-to-charge ratios for hospital services. Quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) were calculated from patient responses to the EuroQol-5-Dimensions instrument at baseline and 3, 6, and 12 months postoperatively. Incremental cost-effectiveness ratio analysis was performed with bootstrapping to address uncertainty. Results Of 163 total patients enrolled in the CSM-S Trial, 153 from the United States (mean age, 62 years; 80 (52%) female) were included as-treated (ACDF = 61, PCDF = 64, LP = 28) in a cost-effectiveness analysis. Economic data were not available for 9 patients. The remaining 144 patients treated (ACDF = 55, PCDF = 61, LP = 28) had cost data through a 1-year follow-up. Mean hospitalization costs were higher after PCDF than ACDF and LP ($33 410 vs $26 468 vs $25 550; P Conclusion In the CSM-S Trial, LP yielded greater 1-year quality-of-life improvements at lower costs than PCDF and ACDF.

items.title: Reading disability in glaucoma: A neglected dimension of visual disability.
items.abstract: Reading disability is a common and clinically relevant, yet under-recognized, functional impairment in glaucoma, with significant impact on independence, daily activities, and quality of life, particularly in an increasingly digital environment. Reading performance is influenced by a complex interplay of visual field loss, reduced contrast sensitivity, oculomotor dysfunction, and cognitive load. Patients typically exhibit reduced reading speed, increased fixation instability, and altered saccadic patterns, even in the presence of preserved visual acuity. The severity and spatial distribution of visual field defects play a key role in determining impairment, as central and paracentral defects may disrupt fixation and letter recognition, while peripheral loss can impair text navigation and eye movement guidance. Additionally, glaucoma therapies may indirectly contribute to reading impairment through detrimental effects on ocular surface health and overall visual quality. Assessment remains challenging due to the lack of standardized, glaucoma-specific tools. Available tests capture complementary aspects of reading function, while patient-reported outcomes provide insight into perceived disability but only partially address reading. Evidence on interventions is heterogeneous. Assistive devices show the most consistent benefits, whereas rehabilitation strategies and emerging technologies remain insufficiently validated, with particularly limited evidence in glaucoma-specific populations. Reading disability represents a rapid and clinically accessible measure of functional impairment that may complement structural and perimetric assessment in glaucoma. Given its impact on quality of life, independence, and near-vision demands in an increasingly digital world, reading performance should be more regularly evaluated in clinical practice, while a better understanding of the underlying mechanisms may help guide targeted rehabilitation strategies.

items.title: A validated antibody toolbox for ALS research.
items.abstract: A substantial fraction of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)-associated proteins remains poorly characterized, in part because of the limited availability of validated research antibodies. We established knockout (KO)-based antibody characterization workflows and demonstrated that widely used antibodies against the major ALS-associated protein C9orf72 lacked specificity (Laflamme et al., 2019). We subsequently scaled this framework to systematically benchmark research antibodies, revealing that up to 61% fail to perform as recommended by manufacturers (Ayoubi et al., 2023b). Here, we extend this approach by establishing the ALS-Reproducible Antibody Platform (ALS-RAP), a comprehensive effort to generate a publicly available dataset of KO-validated antibodies targeting proteins encoded by ALS risk genes. In total, we characterized 303 antibodies against 33 ALS-associated proteins to identify high-quality reagents for use in western blot, immunoprecipitation, and immunofluorescence. Using these antibodies, we profiled protein levels across human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived and primary neurological cell types. These analyses revealed diverse cellular distributions and higher levels of several ALS-associated proteins in glial populations, consistent with emerging evidence for immune contributions to ALS. Together, ALS-RAP provides a validated antibody toolbox and protein expression resource to support the study of ALS-associated proteins.

items.title: Migraine beyond attacks: Insights on the interictal phase.
items.abstract: BackgroundTraditionally, migraine has been characterized by its paroxysmal attacks, with the interictal phase considered to be a symptom-free interval. However, emerging evidence suggests that the "migraine brain" remains in a state of altered neuro-excitability and impaired habituation between attacks, manifesting as debilitating interictal symptoms. This narrative review aims to describe the spectrum of interictal symptoms, their underlying mechanisms, and their impact on the cumulative disease burden, at the same time as exploring the implications for clinical management.MethodsAn extensive literature search of the PubMed database was performed using terms related to the migraine cycle, interictal phase, and disease burden. Original articles published within the last 10 years were prioritized, focusing on clinical trials, real-world evidence, and neurophysiological studies.ResultsInterictal symptoms, including sensory hypersensitivity (photophobia, phonophobia, osmophobia, allodynia), cognitive dysfunction ("brain fog"), vestibular symptoms, and affective dysregulation, affect between 26% and 76% of patients. These symptoms significantly contribute to the socioeconomic burden of migraine, leading to substantial productivity losses (absenteeism and presenteeism) and reduced quality of life. While non-specific preventives often fail to alleviate interictal symptoms, calcitonin gene-related peptide-pathway targeted therapies and onabotulinumtoxinA have demonstrated promising results in reducing the interictal burden, as measured by standardized tools such as the Migraine Interictal Burden Scale (MIBS-4).ConclusionsMigraine management requires a paradigm shift from focusing solely on attack frequency to a more holistic approach that includes the interictal period. Standardizing interictal symptoms definitions and implementing specific outcome measures in clinical practice are essential to restore full functional capacity and provide comprehensive care for patients.

items.title: Motor Response Variability Reflects Recovery Potential After Stroke: A Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation Study.
items.abstract: Background Stroke recovery is highly heterogeneous, and predictive neurophysiological markers of motor outcome are still needed. Although transcranial magnetic stimulation-derived motor evoked potentials (MEPs) are widely used to assess corticospinal integrity, their trial-to-trial variability remains poorly explored and has largely been interpreted as noise rather than a source of clinically relevant information. Methods In this prospective longitudinal observational study, we investigated MEP peak-to-peak amplitude and amplitude variability in 77 patients with subacute stroke assessed at baseline (T0, early subacute phase) and after a 2-month high-intensity daily rehabilitation program (T1), alongside 10 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. MEPs were recorded from both hemispheres at rest. Clinical outcomes were evaluated using the Fugl-Meyer Upper Extremity scale and a Motor Recovery Index. Results Seventy-seven patients with subacute stroke (mean age, 68.5±12.7 years; 41.6% women) and 10 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (mean age, 73.9±4.3 years; 40.0% women) were included. At T0, MEP amplitude was lower in the affected than in the unaffected hemisphere (0.16±0.02 versus 0.38±0.01 mV; P =5.42×10 -10 ), as was MEP variance (0.013±0.002 versus 0.038±0.003 mV 2 ; P =8.43×10 - 12 ). Regarding T1, MEP amplitude increased over time in the affected hemisphere (0.21±0.02 mV; P =0.01), whereas MEP variance remained unchanged ( P =0.55). Importantly, baseline MEP amplitude was strongly associated with motor status at follow-up (Fugl-Meyer Upper Extremity scale at T1; P =9.52×10 - 9 ), but not with the degree of recovery. In contrast, baseline MEP variability was significantly associated with both motor outcome (Fugl-Meyer Upper Extremity scale at T1; P =2.76×10 - 7 ) and the Motor Recovery Index ( P =0.009), indicating a specific link with recovery potential. Conclusions These findings reveal a dissociation between MEP amplitude and variability, suggesting that they capture complementary aspects of corticospinal function. Although amplitude reflects the current functional state of motor pathways, variability appears to index network flexibility and adaptive capacity. MEP variability may, therefore, represent a novel neurophysiological biomarker for predicting motor recovery and guiding personalized rehabilitation strategies after stroke.

items.title: Molecular biomarkers associated with progression and adverse outcomes in human ascending thoracic aortic aneurysm: a systematic review protocol.
items.abstract: Objective This systematic review will identify, classify, and synthesize evidence on molecular biomarkers (circulating, tissue, genetic, epigenetic, proteomic, metabolomic, and inflammatory) associated with the progression and outcomes of ascending thoracic aortic aneurysm (ATAA) in human populations. Introduction ATAA is a heterogeneous condition driven by genetic, epigenetic, inflammatory, proteolytic, and metabolic alterations that are not completely understood. Current management relies mainly on aortic diameter and does not incorporate molecular data. Emerging evidence suggests that circulating, tissue, genetic, epigenetic, metabolic, and proteomic biomarkers may support diagnosis, improve prognostic assessment, identify high-risk patients, and clarify mechanisms of medial degeneration. Existing studies are fragmented and inconsistent, and are based on small observational cohorts, highlighting the need for a rigorous synthesis. Eligibility criteria This review will include observational studies that quantify molecular biomarkers in blood or biopsy samples from adult populations with ATAA. Methods We will search PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Scopus, Web of Science, trial registries, dissertations and theses databases, preprint repositories, and other gray literature sources for eligible evidence from 2015 to the present. Study selection, critical appraisal, and data extraction will follow the JBI methodology. A narrative synthesis will summarize the findings. Where sufficient clinical and methodological homogeneity exists, meta-analysis will be conducted using random-effects models. The certainty of evidence will be assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach adapted for prognostic and etiological research. Review registration PROSPERO CRD420251237933.

items.title: Endovascular Therapy in Intracranial Atherosclerotic Stenosis-Related Large Vessel Occlusion Stroke: A Brief Practice Update and Consensus Statement From the SVIN.
items.abstract: Intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis-related large vessel occlusion (ICAS-LVO) represents a distinct subset of acute ischemic stroke with unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges during endovascular therapy. Compared with embolic LVO, ICAS-LVO is associated with higher rates of reocclusion and the frequent use of adjunctive interventions. This Brief Practice Update summarizes current evidence and expert consensus to guide the identification and management of ICAS-LVO during endovascular therapy. The Society of Vascular and Interventional Neurology Guidelines and Practice Standards committee convened a multidisciplinary writing group of neurointerventionalists to review available literature and define key clinical questions on ICAS-LVO and endovascular therapy. Evidence was appraised using the Society of Vascular and Interventional Neurology framework for Class of Recommendation and Level of Evidence, adapted from the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association. Draft statements were iteratively refined and approved by the Society of Vascular and Interventional Neurology Guidelines and Practice Standards Quality Committee for adherence to internal standards and endorsed by the Society of Vascular and Interventional Neurology Board of Directors. Evidence was derived from randomized trials, multicenter registries, cohort studies, post hoc analyses, and meta-analyses addressing diagnostic features, first-line thrombectomy strategies, and adjunctive therapies in ICAS-LVO. Both stent retriever and direct aspiration approaches are acceptable initial strategies; however, durable recanalization is only achieved in about half of patients. Adjunctive use of intravenous or intra-arterial glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitors, balloon angioplasty, and rescue stenting has demonstrated improved recanalization rates and favorable functional outcomes in observational studies, without increased hemorrhagic complications. However, the quality of evidence remains weak. A summary of recommendations is provided to guide practice in common procedural scenarios. This Brief Practice Update provides evidence-based and expert consensus recommendations for the diagnosis and endovascular treatment of ICAS-LVO. Management should be individualized by incorporating the clinical presentation, imaging characteristics, and operator expertise. While adjunctive therapy may be beneficial in select cases, high-quality randomized trials are needed to define optimal strategies and establish standardized algorithms for this challenging stroke subtype.

items.title: Blind spots in Australian bipolar disorder surveillance: Limitations of population-based and consumer needs surveys.
items.abstract: Population-based surveys provide a critical means of characterising the prevalence, burden, lived experience, service use and unmet needs associated with bipolar disorder, including among people who may not be engaged with formal healthcare services. However, existing Australian survey efforts are often cross-sectional, outdated and affected by important sampling and ascertainment biases. Administrative and linked datasets can provide complementary information on service use and outcomes, but their reach is constrained by the absence of an integrated national data system and their reliance on contact with health and other services. Consequently, current surveillance approaches provide an incomplete picture of bipolar disorder in Australia. Despite its considerable burden, substantial unmet need persists in diagnosis, treatment and service provision, even though many people with bipolar disorder can achieve recovery with timely and appropriate care. In this Perspectives-Viewpoint article, we argue that more inclusive, longitudinal and co-designed national surveillance is needed to accurately characterise bipolar disorder and generate the evidence required to guide investment, service planning and reform.

items.title: Autism screening outcomes in a mental health crisis population: findings from a service evaluation.
items.abstract: We evaluated proportions of autism screening outcomes among adults accessing crisis mental health services in Sussex, UK, and examined associations with quality of life and joint hypermobility as an indicator of physiological complexity. Fifty-five participants (mean age 35.7 years, 56% male, 85% White) completed autism and hypermobility screening questionnaires and the Mental Health Quality of Life Questionnaire. Forty-three participants (78%) scored above screening threshold for autism, although only eight had a prior diagnosis, and 27% scored above the published autistic median. Higher Ritvo Autism and Asperger Diagnostic Scale (RAADS-14) scores were associated with lower quality of life ( p p p = 0.01), suggesting a possible biological contribution to distress. Findings indicate high frequency of possible autism in crisis services and a need for tailored, biopsychosocially informed support.

items.title: KARS1-Related Infantile-Onset Progressive Leukoencephalopathy With or Without Deafness: A Novel Variant and Phenotypic Expansion.
items.abstract: Biallelic variants in the KARS1 gene, encoding lysyl-tRNA synthetase, are responsible for autosomal recessive disorders such as infantile-onset progressive leukoencephalopathy with or without deafness (LEPID; OMIM #619147) and nonsyndromic hearing loss (DFNB89). Common features of LEPID include sensorineural hearing loss, developmental delay, and leukoencephalopathy, but dysmorphic facial features and cardiac anomalies are not commonly reported. This study presents the first documented LEPID case in Iran, expanding the phenotypic and genetic spectrum of KARS1-related disorders. Whole exome sequencing (WES) was performed on a two-year-old Iranian boy from non-consanguineous parents, without a positive history of any neurologic conditions. Identified variants were validated by Sanger sequencing, with familial segregation analysis. Moreover, a literature review of 41 KARS1-related cases was conducted to compare clinical and genetic findings. WES identified two compound heterozygous KARS1 variants (NM_005548.3): c.959G > A (p.Arg320His) and c.2T > C (p.Met1Thr), previously reported and novel, respectively, both of which were classified as likely pathogenic according to the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics criteria. The patient exhibited typical LEPID features (sensorineural hearing loss, developmental delay, seizures, leukoencephalopathy) alongside unprecedented dysmorphic facial features (e.g., synophrys, pointed triangular chin) and cardiac anomalies (pulmonary stenosis, atrial septal defect). Literature review confirmed these dysmorphic features as novel, absent in prior cases, with cardiac involvement in a limited number of patients. This study highlights a novel KARS1 variant and an expanded phenotypic spectrum of LEPID, emphasizing the role of WES in diagnosing rare disorders even in non-consanguineous marriages. These findings advocate for broader phenotypic recognition and functional studies to elucidate KARS1's role in neurodevelopmental, craniofacial, and cardiac abnormalities.

items.title: Repurposing, redefining, and reimagining: A paradigm shift towards person-driven neuroscience in the digital age
items.abstract: The focus of neuroscience has traditionally hinged on collecting quantifiable physiological data that are often distanced from the lived experiences of people. In contrast, qualitative, subjective, and situational information provides rich context, but lacks the empirical precision needed to map to neural processes. To reconcile this gap, we established ‘The Lαβ’ as an interdisciplinary initiative that fuses person-driven experiences, personal reflection, and empirical neuroscience. People engage with their chosen experiences in their chosen settings while wearing a portable EEG headset. Timestamped information is then collected from a variety of sources. We introduce our novel neurotriangulation approach: A person‑driven synthesis of quantitative electrophysiological signals, qualitative observations, and subjective and situational information into a single analytic stream. Our aim is to provide people with opportunities for neuro-self-reflection. We use an ethics-first approach to preserve data sovereignty, privacy, autonomy, and agency for the individual. In this paper, we present real-world case studies to demonstrate our data collection, real-time field analysis, and co-interpretation methodologies. These case studies also underscore the neurotriangulation model as an approach to move beyond reductive, data-centric models toward a person‑driven paradigm. This shift allows neurodata to be more accessible, inclusive, and personally meaningful, while prioritising safety and subjectivity. This has the potential to reshape how we think about neuroscientific applications in fields such as education and training, anthropology, creative arts, wellbeing, and mental health. By repurposing and redefining the use of extant neurotechnology, we are reimagining a future in which our understanding of ourselves is person-driven, reality-based, and ethically sound.

items.title: Neuroscience Research: Before and After the Evolution of Optogenetics
items.abstract: Abstract In an article titled “Thinking about the Brain,” published in a special issue of Scientific American devoted to the Brain in September 1979, Francis H.C. Crick wrote: “Reflecting on itself, the human brain has uncovered some marvelous facts. What appears to be needed for understanding how it works is new techniques for examining it and new ways of thinking about it.” He made several important observations about the technological limitations of the time, noting that electrodes cannot readily distinguish different types of neurons. Light could be an ideal signal to turn firing on and off in an alert animal (Crick 1999; Crick 1979). This conceptual blueprint was eventually realized experimentally through the groundbreaking work of Hegemann, Nagel, Deisseroth, and their colleagues, who harnessed the microbial channelrhodopsins to achieve fast, genetically targeted, light-driven control of neuronal activity (Boyden et al. 2005; Nagel et al. 2002; Nagel et al. 2003). Over the past two decades, optogenetics has become a mainstay of circuit neuroscience and is now emerging as a potential therapeutic approach. In light of the 2026 Nobel Prize awarded to optogenetics, this perspective narrates the evolution of neuroscience research before and after the advent of optogenetics, and summarizes how this technology has transformed our approaches to studying the brain.

items.title: What does green mean? Modelling herbivore foodscapes and resource tracking in forested environments.
items.abstract: The forage maturation hypothesis predicts that herbivores should select plants at intermediate growth stages because they strike a balance between biomass and nutritional quality. Methods for identifying this key stage of plant phenology commonly rely on satellite-based greenness indices and their derivatives. By combining such indices with fine-scale movement data, ecologists have uncovered many novel behaviours and life-history strategies, including 'green-wave surfing' by herbivores. Yet, few studies have evaluated the degree to which greenness indices accurately reflect variation in forage characteristics or their selection by herbivores in forested habitats. We studied relationships among remotely sensed greenness indices, on-the-ground measures of forage biomass and quality and resource selection by white-tailed deer (Odocoileus virginianus), elk (Cervus canadensis) and moose (Alces alces) in the coniferous forests of northern Idaho, USA. We hypothesized that remote-sensing methods for measuring the green wave (i.e. the phenological progression of understory food plants) are not useful in coniferous forests because variation in greenness is driven mainly by conifers. We also hypothesized that patterns of forage selection by large herbivores are not detectable in the forest using greenness indices. We tested predictions derived from these hypotheses using on-the-ground measures of forage biomass and quality and more than 10 years of movement data from GPS collars. Remotely sensed greenness indices explained 2 2 = 0.313; high-quality biomass: adjusted R 2 = 0.174). Moreover, with only one exception (elk selected pixels where the instantaneous rate of green-up was near its peak), greenness indices were among the least useful predictors of selection by large herbivores. Indeed, although all three species selected forage biomass, elk and moose simultaneously avoided greener pixels. Our results indicate that greenness indices are of limited value for predicting variation in forage resources or their selection by large herbivores in forested environments. Despite their intuitive appeal and ease of accessibility, such indices cannot always be substituted for on-the-ground measurements of plant traits that directly influence nutrient intake by herbivores.

items.title: Phenotypic integration and modularity evolve along with plumage coloration across populations in a widespread songbird.
items.abstract: Patterns of interdependence among traits such as phenotypic integration and modularity can have profound evolutionary consequences. Despite their importance in evolutionary theory, large-scale empirical evidence for processes that lead to population divergence in phenotypic integration and modularity across a species range remains rare. Here, we analyze patterns of correlations between plumage color traits sampled from many populations across the global range of the barn swallow (Hirundo rustica). Population divergence in phenotypic integration is associated with both genomic divergence and the evolution of ventral coloration. We also demonstrate that throat coloration acts as a separate module from other ventral plumage patches, and populations with darker throat color exhibit increased modularity. These results provide rare empirical evidence to support the theory that selection on one set of traits can lead to the evolution of modularity. Our study takes a unique, comparative approach that links phenotypic integration and modularity to both phenotypic and genomic divergence among populations within a species known to experience divergent sexual selection pressures. Finally, our study offers insight into the evolution of phenotypic integration and modularity in the context of animal coloration, as well as the structure and function of complex signal traits in general.

items.title: Host species identity drives temporally stable octocoral microbiomes in Florida.
items.abstract: Octocorals are foundational components of Caribbean reef ecosystems, yet their bacterial microbiomes remain poorly characterized compared to scleractinian corals. We present an extensive 16S rRNA gene survey of western Atlantic octocoral microbiomes, characterizing 180 samples from four co-occurring South Florida species over three years: the encrusting species Briareum asbestinum and Erythropodium caribaeorum, and the branching species Eunicea flexuosa and Muricea muricata. Host species identity was the strongest predictor of microbiome composition, explaining 14.4% of bacterial community variation, while temporal and spatial factors contributed less than 2% each. Core microbiome analysis at three prevalence thresholds (80, 90 and 100%) revealed host-specific bacterial associations. All four species harbored largely host-specific Endozoicomonas ASVs as dominant core members, with encrusting species maintaining larger and more taxonomically diverse cores than branching species. Phylogenetic reconstruction placed the dominant Endozoicomonas ASVs among described Endozoicomonas species, three lineages related to E. euniceicola, which was described from Florida octocorals, while the dominant Mycoplasma ASVs were highly divergent from described type strains, suggesting undescribed octocoral-associated lineages. Differential abundance analysis identified only a few significant temporally or spatially variable ASVs, reinforcing overall community stability. These findings demonstrate strong host control over microbial associations and provide a phylogenetic framework for understanding octocoral-bacteria symbioses in the western Atlantic.

items.title: Finding the upsides to living alone: Adaptation and inequality among older U.S. adults?
items.abstract: Objectives This study investigates how the growing population of older Americans living alone adapts to daily life, testing three sociological hypotheses regarding "upsides" to solo living: spending more time outside, spending more time with non-residential ties, and spending more time in organized activities. We also consider whether such adaptations are unequal, investigating potential fault lines across key social categories including race/ethnicity, education, gender, and disability. Methods Using 2003-2019 American Time Use Survey data (N = 83,997), we employed multiple regression analysis to estimate both the likelihood of participation and the duration of time spent in each of these ways. Results Results support the notion of locational and social adaptation: older adults living alone spend significantly more time outside the home and more time with friends and non-residential family than their co-resident peers. However, we found that solo dwellers spend less time in organized activities. Consistent with one dimension of the unequal adaptation hypothesis, several behavioral patterns were stratified by race/ethnicity, with Black older adults standing out from each of the other groups. Discussion Findings point to living alone as a distinct social ecology rather than a simple marker of deficit, with older adults adapting through the reorganization of daily exposure to people and places. This adaptation does not appear strongly structured by most social categories, though strong racialized differences suggest that future research should continue to assess the way diverse older Americans live together and with others.

items.title: Enzyme-Antibiotic Liquid Crystalline Nanoparticles for Enhanced Antibiofilm Activity, Bacterial Clearance, and Accelerated Healing of Infected Wounds.
items.abstract: Biofilm-associated wound infections remain difficult to treat because bacteria are protected within extracellular polymeric matrices that restrict antibiotic penetration, promote antimicrobial tolerance, and delay tissue repair. Here, we developed liquid crystalline nanoparticles (LCNPs) for topical coformulation of gentamicin (GEN) and recombinant human DNase I (rhDNase), combining aminoglycoside therapy with an eDNA-targeting enzyme. GEN + rhDNase-LCNPs were successfully formulated as nanoscale particles with low polydispersity, high encapsulation efficiency, and formulation-dependent in vitro release behavior. LCNP formulation preserved GEN antibacterial activity against planktonic Escherichia coli Xen14 and reduced the MBIC against established biofilms by approximately 4-fold. In a minimum biofilm eradication concentration (MBEC) model, GEN + rhDNase-LCNPs achieved the greatest reduction in biofilm-associated viable bacteria, producing an approximately 6-log reduction compared with untreated biofilm controls and supporting the benefit of combining antibiotic delivery with rhDNase. Notably, GEN + rhDNase-LCNPs markedly suppressed bacterial burden and reduced recoverable bacteria at day 9 to near the limit of detection in a bioluminescent E. coli Xen14 biofilm-associated excisional wound infection mouse model. This antibacterial effect translated into accelerated macroscopic wound closure and improved histological repair, including an approximately 80% reduction in wound gape compared with infected controls. Masson's trichrome staining further confirmed enhanced tissue remodeling, with the collagen-positive wound area increasing to approximately 88% following GEN + rhDNase-LCNP treatment, compared with approximately 21% in infected controls. In conclusion, LCNP-mediated codelivery of GEN and rhDNase improved bacterial clearance, re-epithelialization, and collagen deposition, supporting this platform as a promising topical antibiofilm strategy for infected wounds.

items.title: Conceptual framework for the implementation of the Species Threat Abatement and Restoration metric's threat abatement component.
items.abstract: One important goal of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF) aims to halt extinction of species and reduce extinction risk 10-fold by 2050. To help ensure that the actions taken under the targets of the KMGBF contribute to reducing species' extinction risk, the Species Threat Abatement and Restoration (STAR) metric was designed to enable science-based target setting for species. STAR quantifies the potential contribution of threat abatement actions or habitat restoration to reducing species' extinction risk in an area. To support the effective implementation of STAR, we developed a framework to move from determining the threat abatement component of STAR (STAR T ) using global data to calibrating STAR T using local data to setting targets and calculating realized STAR T scores to measure progress. The framework outlines the specific approaches that can be implemented to calculate these different STAR T metrics. First, estimated STAR T scores use global data to provide an initial indication of the species and threats expected to be present within an area. Then, calibrated STAR T scores involve confirming the local presence of species and threats, and the locally verified data allow for setting robust threat abatement targets, which can be articulated as target STAR T scores. Calibrated STAR T can also inform both reactive and proactive threat management. Finally, changes in threat intensity are then monitored and used to calculate realized STAR T . Achieving realized STAR T requires actors to not only reduce existing threats but also prevent additional threats emerging within the area. This framework provides a means for all potential actors, working across varying spatial scales, to quantify, plan, monitor, and deliver interventions to address species threats and then report the impact of the interventions using a consistent method and metric that are comparable and aggregable across actors and locations.

items.title: Inter-annual variation in fine-scale spatial genetic structure and patterns of density-dependent mating in a population of self-compatible Arabidopsis lyrata.
items.abstract: Background and aims Mating patterns in plant populations are shaped jointly by the local availability and relatedness of potential mates, both of which can vary through time in disturbance-prone habitats. We aimed to investigate how a year-to-year change in local plant densities and spatial genetic structure (SGS) influence opportunities for inbreeding and outcrossing in a predominantly self-compatible population of Arabidopsis lyrata subsp. lyrata located in a fore-dune habitat at Rondeau Provincial Park, Ontario. Methods We mapped plants in 40 patches, each centred on a focal plant, over two consecutive years, quantified SGS with kinship-distance analyses of 27 and 34 focal plants in the first and second years, respectively, and estimated multilocus rates of outcrossing and biparental inbreeding from 128 and 177 progeny, respectively. Key results Across surveyed patches, plant density increased more than five-fold between years, coinciding with a marked decline in fine-scale SGS (Sp = 0.130 in year one; Sp = -0.014 in year two). Despite similar population-wide outcrossing rates in both years (tm = 0.45 in 2021; tm = 0.49 in 2022), outcrossing was positively associated with neighbourhood density in the lower-density year but showed no density dependence when densities were high in the second year. In both years, 15-20% of outcrossed seeds were produced by mating among relatives, indicating substantial biparental inbreeding. Conclusions Our results suggest that recruitment pulses in dynamic dune habitats can rapidly weaken SGS while simultaneously altering the scale at which density governs mating patterns. More generally, they highlight how short-term temporal variation in population size can modulate the local availability and relatedness of mates within plant populations.

items.title: Epicuticular Wax Composition and Wax Crystal Microstructure Shape Oviposition Preference in the Diamondback Moth, Plutella xylostella, on Cabbage.
items.abstract: The diamondback moth Plutella xylostella is a major pest of cabbage and exhibits distinct host preferences among cabbage cultivars. Glossy cabbage cultivars, characterized by reduced epicuticular wax crystal coverage on the leaf surface, are generally more susceptible to oviposition by females than waxy cultivars with normal wax bloom. However, the roles of wax components in shaping oviposition behavior remain unclear. We examined this issue using the waxy cultivar 'Kinkei 201 (Kinkei)' and the glossy cultivar 'YR Yuryoku (YR)'. In two-choice tests, females significantly preferred YR over Kinkei for oviposition. Kinkei leaves were densely covered with well-developed epicuticular wax crystals dominated by n-nonacosane (nC29), whereas YR leaves had sparse, granule-like wax crystals dominated by triacontanal (C30al). Mechanical removal of wax crystals significantly increased oviposition on Kinkei leaves but not on YR leaves. Application of 0.1-10 mg nC29 to wax-removed Kinkei leaves significantly suppressed oviposition and, at higher doses, induced dense wax structures across the leaf surface. Similarly, application of 1 mg nC29 to intact YR leaf surfaces increased nC29 coverage and significantly reduced oviposition. In contrast, application of C30al to wax-removed YR leaf surfaces produced sparse wax structures and did not affect oviposition. These results suggest that oviposition deterrence is associated with dense nC29-associated wax structures rather than simply with the presence of epicuticular wax itself. Differences in oviposition preference between the two cabbage cultivars may reflect variation in both epicuticular wax composition and wax crystal microstructure, although their relative contributions remain unclear.

items.title: A Deep Phylogenetic Split Between Short- and Long-Wavelength-Tuned Visual Systems in Surgeonfishes (Acanthuridae)
items.abstract: The light environment, coupled with ecology, is widely thought to drive visual adaptation, creating species-specific visual niches. However, coral reef ecosystems experience continuous spatiotemporal variations in light conditions, and mechanisms such as phenotypic plasticity may be essential for coral reef animals to adjust to such changing sensory requirements. It remains unclear how widespread colour vision plasticity is, or the extent to which ecology and phylogeny drive plasticity in coral reef fishes. Using a comparative transcriptomic approach across 22 species, we aimed to investigate visual plasticity within a prominent coral reef fish family, surgeonfishes (Acanthuridae), in response to changes in the light environment throughout development and across seasons in adults. Surprisingly, we uncovered a deep phylogenetic split (~42 mya) in visual opsin gene expression profiles, with Nasinae expressing a shorter-shifted palette than Acanthurinae, which coincides with the divide between water-column and benthic-feeding modalities during the speciation of their last common ancestor. However, opsin gene expression showed little variation in response to seasonal or ontogenetic shifts in the light environment, nor in the broad functional feeding groups extant species from both subfamilies fall under. Thus, the invariable visual gene expression observed in present-day surgeonfishes appears to be dictated by phylogenetic inertia, despite rapid diversification into a range of ecological niches. This suggests that spectral tuning into two main modalities, short and long, reduces the need for visual plasticity, allowing larger and more mobile coral reef fishes to conduct visually guided behaviours across the entire range of light environments they encounter.

items.title: Resurrecting host–microbiome interactions: combining resurrection ecology and microbiome transplants to test temporal local adaptation
items.abstract: Host-associated microbiomes can influence fitness, respond rapidly to environmental change, and potentially contribute to host adaptation. Yet, determining whether host–microbiome associations evolve adaptively over ecological timescales remains challenging because historical host genotypes and their associated microbial communities are rarely available for experimental comparison. Resurrection ecology offers a means of recovering historical host genotypes from dormant propagules, while microbiome transplantation provides an experimental approach for testing the effects of microbial communities on host performance. Combining these approaches could enable direct tests of temporal local adaptation in host–microbiome associations. Freshwater Daphnia provide a promising model because their dormant eggs can persist in lake sediments, allowing historical host genotypes to be resurrected. However, the microbiota associated with dormant eggs may originate from multiple sources, including ancestral hosts, lake water, and surrounding sediment, complicating the recovery of historically associated microbial communities. We outline a framework combining sediment archives, host resurrection, microbiome characterisation, and reciprocal transplantation experiments to test whether historical and contemporary hosts perform better with microbiomes from their respective time periods. We discuss the conceptual predictions, methodological challenges, and experimental controls required to distinguish temporal local adaptation from microbial environmental effects, host-genotype specificity, and changes in community composition. This framework could extend resurrection ecology beyond host evolution to experimentally investigate the historical evolution of host–microbiome interactions.

items.title: Artificial Intimacy: How AI-Mediated Closeness Reshapes Human Mating Psychology
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly expanding into domains traditionally reserved for human intimacy, including emotional companionship, romantic interaction, and sexual engagement. Although research on AI companions has grown rapidly, existing explanations remain fragmented across attachment theory, relationship science, human–AI interaction, and communication research, with limited integration into a broader evolutionary framework. To address this gap, we introduce the Artificial Intimacy Model (AIM), an integrative theoretical framework that proposes that Artificial Intimacy is best understood as a transformation of the relational ecology within which evolved psychological mechanisms operate. AIM explains how AI companions create novel relational environments characterized by persistent availability, adaptive responsiveness, reduced relational constraints, and fundamentally asymmetric interaction while engaging existing psychological mechanisms. These transformed relational conditions systematically engage existing attachment and mating systems under evolutionarily novel informational conditions, influencing relational decision making, mating effort allocation, relationship expectations, and broader sociosexual orientations. The model further explains how the technological amplification of evolutionarily familiar relational cues may reshape the operation of established psychological mechanisms without altering their underlying functional architecture. By integrating evolutionary psychology with attachment theory, relationship science, and human–AI interaction research, AIM provides a unified explanatory framework linking environmental transformation to psychological mechanisms, behavioral consequences, and broader sociosexual dynamics. Finally, the model generates explicit, empirically testable propositions and establishes a cumulative research programme for investigating how Artificial Intimacy may reshape human relational behavior as AI companions become an increasingly prominent component of contemporary social life.

items.title: Infrastructure, Environmental Risk, and Youth Enterprise Livelihood Sustainability in a Rapidly Urbanizing African City: Evidence from Hawassa, Ethiopia
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid pace of urban growth in African secondary cities affects the context of young people’s entrepreneurial activities, but enterprise and urban infrastructure policies remain largely disconnected. This study analyzes the relationship between infrastructure, environmental, and market factors and enterprise livelihood sustainability for youth-owned micro and small enterprises (MSEs) in Hawassa, Ethiopia. Using a concurrent mixed method approach, a survey of 252 MSE managers was supplemented by 12 key informant interviews, two municipal interviews, and observations from 12 MSE production sites. The binary logistic regression model was used to determine the relationship between livelihood sustainability, measured as an upward trend in enterprise net monthly income, and selected infrastructure, environmental, and market factors. Availability of medium water (OR = 3.293, p = .005) and retailer (OR = 6.151, p = .004) were positively related to livelihood sustainability, whereas high natural-disaster challenges (OR = 0.256, p = .004) and medium resource pressure (OR = 0.252, p = .014) were negatively associated with it. The negative relationship of sanitation is analyzed carefully since some enterprises might invest their own money in these facilities. The findings link enterprise performance with urban expansion, wetlands, stormwater, and urban ecology in Hawassa. The research presents a model that connects urban infrastructure with enterprises and suggests that utilities, drainage, climatic robustness, provision of serviced space, and market linkages should be regarded as productive elements of urban economic policy.

items.title: Effect of inter and intra specific Plant Densities on Yield Performance of Broad Bean (Vicia faba L.) at Jarte District, Western Oromia Ethiopia
items.abstract: Abstract In the study area the yield of faba bean crop was declined mainly due to improper plant density, and biotic factors. The field experiment was conducted to evaluate the effect of inter and intra row spacing on the yields of faba bean crop. The field experiments consist of 16 treatment combination having four inter-rows spacing (20, 30, 40 and 50 cm) and intra-row (10, 15, 20 and 25 cm) spacing of Dagaga variety of faba bean. The treatment was arranged as Randomized Complete Block Design (RCBD) and replicated three times. The analysis of variance was revealed that the main effect of inter and intra row spacing was showed significant difference on days to 50% flowering, days to 90% maturity, pod length, hundred seed weight and harvest index of faba bean, but plant height, number of pods per plant, and number of seeds per pod was non significantly affected. The longest pod length per plant (8.55 cm and 8.67 cm) were recorded at 13 cm intra and 50 cm inter row spacing. Similarly, the maximum number of pods per plant and number of seeds per pod was recorded at 13 cm intra and 50 cm inter row spacing. Maximum seed yield 4117.11 kg/ha and 3853.17 kg/ha was recorded at 40 cm inter and 10 cm intra row spacing, respectively. But the lowest grain yield 3386.22 kg/ha and 3378.25 was obtained at 50 cm and 13 cm inter and intra row spacing respectively.Therefore, it can be recommended that sowing faba bean crops at 40 cm inter and 10 cm intra-row attain maximum and economic yield at the study area and similar agro ecology.

items.title: A nocturnal guild with a diurnal exception: Diel activity and temporal overlap among riparian mesocarnivores and their small mammal prey in southern Africa
items.abstract: Abstract Temporal partitioning of activity is a key mechanism facilitating coexistence among ecologically similar species and structuring interactions between predators and prey. Yet, within Africa this has been examined almost exclusively among competing mesocarnivores, rarely extending to their small mammal prey. This study used camera-trap data collected across ten riparian sites spanning multiple biomes in South Africa and Namibia (2017–2024) to characterise diel activity patterns of eight mesocarnivore and small mammal taxa, quantify temporal overlap both among co-occurring mesocarnivores and between mesocarnivores and their small mammal prey, and assess whether activity timing within each taxon was spatially consistent across sites. Seven of eight taxa were classified as nocturnal; only Slender mongoose was strongly diurnal. Pairings involving Slender mongoose consistently showed low overlap with other mesocarnivores (Δ̂ = 0.18–0.38), while overlap among the remaining nocturnal mesocarnivores was moderate to high (Δ̂ = 0.70–0.84). Overlap between mesocarnivores and murids ranged from low (Slender mongoose, Δ̂ = 0.23) to high (Serval, Δ̂ = 0.86), broadly reflecting differences in dietary reliance on this prey group among predator species. Activity timing was spatially consistent across sites for three of four taxa assessed, with Water mongoose showing comparatively lower consistency. These findings indicate that temporal partitioning operates unevenly within this mesocarnivore guild, it is shaped in part by species-specific dietary relationships with prey, and, for most taxa, appears resistant to variation in local site conditions. This study extends existing understanding of African mesocarnivore temporal ecology to include predator–prey dynamics within riparian systems, a habitat and interaction type that has received limited prior attention in the region.

items.title: Testing an AI-Driven Sound Management Technology for Autistic Individuals With Decreased Sound Tolerance in Virtual Reality Environments.
items.abstract: Purpose The current study tested the acceptability and perceived benefit of a developing auditory technology for Autistic individuals with decreased sound tolerance (DST) as part of an iterative design process. Methods Twenty Autistic youth and adults (ages 12 to 47 years) with DST evaluated an auditory technology that detects aversive sounds and automatically activates one of three sound management techniques. Sound management interventions included active noise cancellation (ANC), masking, or an AI-based selective filtration feature. Participants rated their comfort during a series of auditory trials in virtual reality (VR) environments and provided feedback on the technology. Results Participants reported greater comfort when using the technology to manage aversive sounds compared to hearing the same sounds unaltered. Their feedback supported the utility of the technology and underscored the importance of flexible, customizable sound management solutions. Participants also offered actionable suggestions for design improvements to guide further development. Conclusion Findings provided preliminary support for the acceptability and perceived benefit of a responsive, customizable auditory technology that includes AI-based sound detection and AI-based selective filtration. All tested interventions improved comfort relative to unaltered sound for Autistic participants with DST. Ongoing user testing and feedback will continue to guide the technology's development.

items.title: Improving the subtyping of gamblers by gambling type.
items.abstract: In gambling research, gambling subtypes have traditionally been used to distinguish between games of skill or competition and games of chance. The former are referred to as strategic games, whereas the latter are classified as non-strategic games. Despite their similarities, individuals who engage in strategic and non-strategic gambling exhibit distinct characteristics. Consequently, a substantial body of research has examined how gamblers differ according to the types of gambling activities in which they engage. These differences in gamblers' profiles have important implications for the clinical assessment and treatment of individuals with gambling problems. Nevertheless, heterogeneous classification methods have been used to define gambling subtypes, compromising the comparability and reproducibility of research findings and hindering the implementation of evidence-based recommendations for the regulation, prevention, and treatment of gambling disorder.

items.title: Transient Alerting Effects of Karolinska Sleepiness Scale Ratings on Physiological and Driving Performance Indicators.
items.abstract: The objective of this study was to determine whether subjectively rating sleepiness on the Karolinska Sleepiness Scale (KSS) gives rise to an alerting effect and, if so, how long it persists. Data from five driving simulator studies involving 83 participants were pooled. Time-locked trajectories of blink duration, blink closing velocity, heart rate, electroencephalographic (EEG) parietal α and frontal θ power, and lateral lane position variability were analysed around each KSS rating using linear mixed-effects models with condition-specific KSS baselines, a transient post-rating component, a late post-rating offset, and time-on-task terms. Immediately after the rating, several indicators shifted in an alerting direction: blink duration and standard deviation of lateral position (SDLP) decreased, blink closing velocity and heart rate increased, and parietal α power generally decreased. Frontal θ showed a more condition-dependent response. The estimated duration of the transient component was indicator dependent, ranging from 40 s for heart rate to the upper bound of the 120-s analysis window for SDLP. These findings have practical implications for driver sleepiness detection system development, validation protocols, and type-approval processes that rely on KSS as a reference measure. If ratings themselves are associated with short-lived physiological or behavioural changes, the timing and modality of KSS administration become important for ensuring valid ground truth labels. Future studies with control conditions, randomized or jittered rating times, and real-road data are needed to determine whether the rating-associated changes are causal and generalisable.

items.title: Understanding the role of social support and depression among women and MSM living with and without HIV in the MACS/WIHS combined cohort study.
items.abstract: Although virally suppressive antiretroviral therapy has transformed HIV into a chronic, manageable condition, people living with HIV continue experiencing elevated depression rates. This study investigated differences in social support and depressive symptoms between men who have sex with men and women, both living with and without HIV. Using data from the Multicenter AIDS Cohort Study/Women's Interagency HIV Study Combined Cohort Study ( N = 2,537), depressive symptoms were evaluated via the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale and social support via the modified Medical Outcomes Study Social Support Survey. Regression models adjusted for income, age, race, ethnicity, and HIV serostatus. No significant differences between MSM and women in levels of total social support ( p = 0.657), instrumental support ( p = 0.307), or emotional support ( p = 0.901) were found. Women reported significantly higher levels of depressive symptoms than MSM ( p = 0.046). Total, instrumental, and emotional support showed strong negative associations with depressive symptoms ( p < 0.001). Interaction models revealed that the protective buffering effect of support appeared consistently across groups. Targeted clinical interventions and longitudinal research are urgently needed to bolster emotional and instrumental support systems, particularly for women and lower-income individuals facing disproportionately elevated depression risks.

items.title: Cultural and lived experiences of menopause among women from Global Majority backgrounds in Western countries: a qualitative systematic review.
items.abstract: Menopause is increasingly recognised as a significant stage of the female reproductive cycle; however, the experiences of women from Global Majority backgrounds (GMB) remain underrepresented within menopause research. To address this gap, this systematic literature review explored how women from Global Majority backgrounds living in Western countries perceive and experience menopause, and how cultural, social and structural factors shape these experiences. Multiple databases were searched in November 2025 for qualitative studies, or mixed-method studies with extractable qualitative findings. Eligible studies were appraised using the CASP qualitative checklist, and findings were synthesised using thematic synthesis. Fifteen studies conducted in US, Canada and Australia, involving women from East and Southeast Asian, South Asian, African American, Hispanic/Latina and Aboriginal backgrounds were included. Six interrelated themes were identified: menopause as a culturally constructed concept; as an embodied and identity-disrupting experience; the influence of social and gendered expectations; cultural and intersectional variation; coping strategies and healthcare navigation; and menopause as a potentially transformative life stage. Experiences were shaped by interactions among cultural beliefs, migration histories, family and community expectations, language barriers, socioeconomic circumstances and healthcare encounters. While some women described stigma, loss and disruption, others experienced greater freedom, resilience and personal transformation. These findings support the need for culturally responsive, intersectional menopause care that avoids cultural assumptions, attends to women's own understandings and treatment preferences, and strengthens clinicians' cultural awareness. Further research should include underrepresented groups and examine whether culturally adapted resources improve healthcare access, experiences and outcomes.

items.title: Reading comprehension, vocabulary knowledge, and compound morphological awareness in grade 2 Chinese children: a two-wave longitudinal study.
items.abstract: Research has established links between morphological awareness (MA) and Chinese reading, but the prospective association between reading comprehension and later MA remains less understood. This two-wave study examined longitudinally adjusted associations among reading comprehension, vocabulary knowledge, and compound MA. We assessed 143 second-grade students at two time points and the complete-case path analyses included 142 children. Hypothesized and reverse path models were estimated across three progressively adjusted covariate specifications, together with a concurrent-outcomes model. Indirect associations were evaluated using 5,000 bias-corrected bootstrap resamples.T1 reading comprehension, T2 vocabulary, and T2 compound MA were positively correlated. In Specification 1, both the hypothesized T1 reading comprehension → T2 vocabulary → T2 compound MA ordering (β = .070, SE = .032, 95% BC CI [.020, .148]) and the reverse ordering (β = .047, SE = .026, 95% BC CI [.010, .113]) yielded positive indirect associations. The indirect-association point estimates in Specification 2 were numerically lower under broader covariate adjustment, and in Specification 3 the bootstrap intervals for both orderings approximately spanned zero. The concurrent-outcomes model showed a significant residual association between T2 vocabulary and compound MA (standardized association = .265, p = .001). Reading comprehension, vocabulary, and compound MA showed close longitudinally adjusted associations. However, because both directional orderings were compatible with the data and the T2 constructs were measured concurrently, their temporal ordering cannot be determined. These findings may inform future longitudinal and intervention research.

items.title: A little-known perspective on the I-squared statistic.
items.abstract: The I-squared statistic has become hugely popular in meta-analysis. Motivated by the recent statement that 'Informally, it can be considered to reflect the extent to which confidence intervals displayed in a forest plot do not overlap with each other', this short note formalises this perspective. The insights provided by our analysis lend further weight to the interpretation of the I-squared statistic as a measure of inconsistency. This perspective reminds us that visual inspections of forest plots are vitally important when assessing between-study variation.

items.title: Because You Know They Like Me So: Examining the Accuracy of Dyadic and Triadic Meta-Liking Judgments in Initial Social Encounters.
items.abstract: Knowing who likes whom is essential for predicting others' behavior and navigating social interactions. We examined whether people can accurately assess whether other people like each other and which cognitive heuristics underlie these triadic meta-liking perceptions, replicating previous results by Kenny et al. (1996). In a generalized round-robin study, unacquainted participants ( N = 403, 74.3% female, M age = 23.3) interacted and judged how much they liked others, were liked by others, and believed others liked each other. Analyses using the Triadic Social Relations Model revealed that judges somewhat agreed on who is liked and who likes whom, had some insight into who is generally liked and who likes whom, and relied on perceived reciprocity and assumed agreement, which were partially true. Beyond this, others were more accurate about how much one is liked, while one's own and others' perceptions about how much one is liked aligned to a certain degree.

items.title: The Role of the Disintegration Trait in Everyday Situation Perception.
items.abstract: The Disintegration trait reflects the proneness to psychotic-like experiences and behaviors (PLEBs) in the general population. We examined its links to momentary situation perception using the DIAMONDS taxonomy. In an experience sampling method study and a diary study ( N total = 1,350 participants, n total = 28,114 episodic measures), we found that Disintegration (beyond the HEXACO traits) was associated with more intense perceptions of situations in everyday life across all DIAMONDS characteristics (except Positivity). This applied in particular to unpleasant and stimulating aspects of situations. This pattern aligns with the conceptualization of Disintegration as a tendency toward illusory perception-seeing, thinking, and feeling connections among objectively unrelated phenomena (false-positive detection errors)-and trait activation theory. Proneness to PLEBs thus help explain how individuals in the general population perceive situations.

items.title: Women's Voices Against Patriarchal Violence: Rights, Resistance, and Womanhood in Kadınlar Dünyası (1913).
items.abstract: This study examines how Ottoman women articulated and challenged patriarchal domination in Kadınlar Dünyası (1913). Drawing on qualitative document analysis of its first 100 issues (820 pages), four themes emerged: naming oppression and rights deprivation, domestic and public manifestations of violence, exclusion from education and employment, and resistance through rights claims and redefining womanhood. Situated within the constitutional transformations following 1908, these discourses expose the tensions between proclaimed liberty and persistent male authority. The findings demonstrate how contributors transformed critiques of gendered domination into claims of dignity, equality, and public participation, highlighting the journal's significance in Ottoman women's history.

items.title: Illness Identity in Type 1 Diabetes: A Nine-Year Longitudinal Perspective in Belgian Youth.
items.abstract: This study offers a unique long-term perspective on the development of illness identity in young individuals with type 1 diabetes and examines how this process relates to their psychological and diabetes management outcomes over time. From a seven-wave longitudinal study, spanning 9 years, data was used from 403 Dutch-speaking adolescents and emerging adults with type 1 diabetes (ages 14-25 years at baseline). The group-level development of illness identity was examined using multivariate latent growth curve modeling, and distinct developmental trajectory classes of illness identity were identified through multivariate latent class growth analysis. Mean differences in depressive symptoms, self-reported management, and hemoglobin A1c across these classes were evaluated using the Bolck-Croon-Hagenaars method. At the group level, small but significant changes were observed with youth reporting more acceptance, enrichment, and engulfment, and less rejection over time. Next, five distinct trajectory classes were identified, each displaying unique developmental patterns of the illness identity dimensions. Youth in these classes differed substantially in their experience of depressive symptoms, self-reported management, and hemoglobin A1c over time. This study demonstrates the heterogeneity in how young individuals with T1D develop their illness identity and how these differences are tied to meaningful variation in psychological and diabetes-related functioning. These findings support illness identity as a clinically relevant target to inform holistic, person-centered care for individuals with type 1 diabetes.
