items.title: Time to untether transitional care from hospital quality: Healthcare utilization following discharge from a Department of Veterans Affairs hospital among community-dwelling older persons.
items.abstract: Background Thirty-day performance measures (e.g., unplanned readmissions), designed to evaluate inpatient care, were neither designed to reflect the experience of patients transitioning from hospital to home, nor the impact of transitional programs to improve postdischarge outcomes. Objective To identify transitional care outcomes by examining a range of postdischarge encounters and mortality. Methods This retrospective observational cohort (October 2022-September 2023) included community-dwelling patients ≥65-years-old, discharged from 120 Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) hospitals to home after medical or neurological admissions. The outcomes, assessed 30- and 90-days postdischarge were: mortality; planned and unplanned readmissions; observation stays; Emergency Department (ED) visits at VA or non-VA hospitals; and number of days in acute care. Results Among 99,778 patients, 71.1% had no acute care utilization within 30 days postdischarge; 49.9% in 90 days. Unplanned readmissions occurred in 14.4% (N = 14,400) at 30 days; 27.5% (N = 27,386) at 90 days. Mortality occurred in 1.8% (N = 1750) within 30 days; 5.6% (N = 5624) within 90 days. Mortality was highest among patients with unplanned readmissions: 30 days, 6.1% (882/14,400); 90 days, 13.1% (3599/27,386). Planned readmission mortality rates were 30 days, 5.8% (59/1017); 90 days, 9.6% (258/2692). Half of patients who died within 30 days postdischarge did so after an unplanned readmission (50.4% [882/1750]); 35.0% (613/1750) had no acute care utilization. Among N = 94,154 patients who survived 90-day postdischarge, 11.2% spent ≥10 days in acute care settings. Conclusions These findings support using the number of days in acute care within 90 days postdischarge as a transitional outcome. Thirty-day readmissions do not capture the full scope of postdischarge healthcare utilization and mortality among community-dwelling older adults.

items.title: Changes in Social Wellbeing Among Older Adults With Limited Prognosis: Results From a Nationally Representative Cohort.
items.abstract: Background Physicians use clinical prognostic estimates to identify medical tests and treatments likely to benefit patients within their lifetime. Poor social wellbeing is associated with mortality, but it is unclear if prognostic indices can identify older adults at risk for worsening social well-being. We examined associations between a mortality prognostic index and social wellbeing at baseline and over 2 years to inform care priorities in the context of a limited prognosis. Methods Data from the National Social Life, Health and Aging Project (NSHAP) Round 4 (2021-2023) and Round 4.2 (2024) included 1630 older adults. Social measures included loneliness, living alone, and at least monthly volunteering, socializing, and attending community groups and religious services. Scores of 8 or higher on the Lee Index (range: 0-26) indicated high mortality risk. Survey-weighted logistic regressions adjusting for sociodemographic and health covariates were used to compare baseline and 2-year changes in social wellbeing in the high versus low mortality risk group. Results Participants had a mean age of 70.3 years, and were 54% female, 62% White, 20% Black, and 14% non-Black Hispanic. At baseline, higher mortality risk participants had poorer social wellbeing on all measures except socializing. Among those not lonely at baseline, 24.2% of higher versus 15.6% of lower risk participants became lonely at follow-up (aOR 1.47; 95% CI: 1.01-2.14). Among those socializing at least monthly at baseline, 19.0% of higher versus 12.3% of lower risk participants transitioned to less-than-monthly socializing (aOR 1.60; 95% CI: 0.97-2.65). Higher risk participants had larger declines in all measures of social wellbeing at follow-up. Conclusions Older adults with higher mortality risk had poorer social wellbeing at baseline and were more likely to become lonely and decrease social participation at follow-up. Prognostic information may help clinicians avoid low-value medical interventions while prioritizing interventions to support meaningful social connection.

items.title: Explanation of the ergonomic components of safety shoes based on the experience of industry workers.
items.abstract: Objectives . Safety shoes are essential for worker protection, yet ergonomic shortcomings may reduce usability and lead to non-compliance. This study aimed to identify ergonomic components of safety shoes based on industrial workers' experiences. Methods . A qualitative content analysis was conducted using semi-structured interviews with 30 industrial employees in Kerman, Iran, with at least 1 year of safety shoe experience. Participants were purposively selected, and interviews continued until data saturation. Data were analyzed using open, axial and selective coding based on Graneheim and Lundman and on Corbin and Strauss, and used investigator triangulation to ensure trustworthiness. Results . Five primary categories and 14 subcategories affecting safety shoe use were identified: musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs), negative effects on performance, skin and thermal discomfort, difficulties with shoelaces and donning/doffing, and individual feelings. These factors contributed to reduced usability and effectiveness, as shown in a paradigmatic model. Conclusion . Key usability-enhancing factors include appropriate alignment of upper and sole dimensions with foot anthropometry, reduced steel-component weight, greater material flexibility, softer and more breathable lining, effective adjusters (e.g., laces or zippers) and consideration of user preferences and safety culture. Manufacturers and occupational health professionals should prioritize these user-centered features to improve comfort, compliance and workplace safety.

items.title: Modeling the cost-effectiveness of NVX-CoV2705 and the public health impact of vaccination for the prevention of seasonal COVID-19 in the US.
items.abstract: Background Older adults and those with comorbidities have increased risk of severe disease and mortality from COVID-19. This analysis estimated the cost-effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccination versus no vaccination in the US and potential impact of increased vaccine coverage. Research design and methods A Markov-based model was updated using the latest epidemiology and vaccine reactogenicity data. Cases, costs, and outcomes for individuals aged 18-64 with ≥1 comorbidity and ≥65 years were estimated for NVX-CoV2705 (Nuvaxovid) versus no vaccination from a third-party payer perspective. Scenario analyses considered the societal perspective and analogous comparisons for BNT162b2 (Comirnaty), mRNA-1273 (Spikevax), and mRNA-1283 (mNEXSPIKE). Results were scaled for public health impact analyses. Results Base-case results associated NVX-CoV2705 with fewer cases (0.0447), hospitalizations (0.0037), and deaths (0.0004) per person on average. NVX-CoV2705 yielded an ICER of $9,840/QALY gained, reflecting fewer QALYs lost (0.0039) alongside increased direct costs ($38.09) per person. Differences for mRNA vaccines were driven by price and reactogenicity. Increasing vaccine coverage by 5-15 percentage points resulted in 114-341 hospitalizations and 11-33 deaths averted per 1,000,000 individuals. Conclusions NVX-CoV2705 was predicted to be cost-effective over no vaccination. This analysis included a more granular approach to modeling reactogenicity events, an important consideration in vaccine cost-effectiveness analyses.

items.title: Primary Prevention Needs to Reduce Family Violence and Sexual Violence Among Older Adults: A Culture-Centered Study in Aotearoa New Zealand.
items.abstract: Family and sexual violence are significant public health issues in Aotearoa New Zealand, but research examining prevention strategies is limited. Grounded in Dutta's culture-centered approach, this study examines the primary prevention needs of older adults to reduce family violence and sexual violence in Aotearoa New Zealand as part of a broader project that is co-developing a prevention framework among high-risk groups. Through 63 interviews with older adults in Aotearoa New Zealand, participants expressed the central role of whānau (extended family) and community in reducing violence against older people through strengthening relationships, as well as the importance of education in increasing awareness of violence prevention throughout the lifespan. The findings disrupt singular, individualistic approaches to violence prevention by emphasizing responsibility, solidarity, and connection.

items.title: The TOGETHER Model: A Next-Generation Integrated Framework for Communication in Healthcare.
items.abstract: Communication is a core clinical competence that directly impacts treatment adherence and patient outcomes. Although excellent communication, coaching, and educational frameworks have been developed, they often operate in isolation, leaving clinicians to navigate between disparate approaches without a unifying reference. The TOGETHER Model is introduced in this study as a conceptual proposal that integrates and synthesizes established evidence-based communication practices and professional coaching methods into a coherent and operational framework for patient-centered care, further grounded in recognized psychological theories. TOGETHER Model translates theoretical constructs into eight practical domains: "trust building and relationship," "open communication," "goal setting," "explanation," "treatment options and shared decision-making," "humanity," "education and empowerment," and "review and follow-up." Each domain is associated with practical professional actions and essential competencies, providing clinicians with structured yet flexible guidance that can be integrated across diverse care settings and patient journeys. The model is designed to be modular and scalable, supporting its use in medical education and continuing professional development. Operational applications include structured training curricula, simulation-based assessments, AI-enhanced digital platforms, and organizational toolkits for implementation and change management. Beyond education, the model offers a pathway for embedding communication competence into accreditation systems and quality standards, thereby aligning professional development with broader institutional and policy goals.

items.title: dsRNA: mechanisms of gene expression regulation, disease pathogenesis, and therapeutic potential.
items.abstract: Double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) has long been recognized as a viral pathogen-associated molecular pattern that activates innate immunity. However, dsRNA is increasingly recognized as a regulatory RNA species involved in RNA homeostasis, gene expression, and cell fate determination. In this review, we discuss canonical dsRNA-dependent mechanisms, including RNA interference (RNAi), with particular emphasis on nuclear RNAi, and dsRNA-sensing networks, together with broader RNA-RNA duplex-associated regulatory processes. We also consider structurally distinct RNA-DNA hybrids that functionally converge with dsRNA-responsive innate immune pathways. We further examine how dysregulation of dsRNA production, processing, sensing, and clearance contributes to cancer, autoimmune disorders, and neurodegenerative diseases, and how these mechanisms can be therapeutically exploited. Collectively, these insights establish a conceptual framework for understanding the roles of dsRNA in physiological regulation, disease pathogenesis, and therapeutic applications.

items.title: Prevalence and factors associated with intrapartum and immediate postpartum obstetric complications in Ethiopia: a secondary analysis of a national longitudinal survey.
items.abstract: Background Most maternal deaths in Ethiopia occur during childbirth and the immediate postpartum period, yet population-level evidence on intrapartum and immediate postpartum complications and their determinants remains limited. In particular, the roles of intimate partner violence (IPV) during pregnancy and pregnancy complications have been underexplored. Objective To determine the prevalence and factors associated with intrapartum and immediate postpartum obstetric complications in Ethiopia. Methods We conducted a secondary analysis of the Performance Monitoring for Action Ethiopia (PMA-E) longitudinal survey (October 2019 and September 2020) using a two-stage stratified cluster sampling design. Multilevel modified Poisson regression analysis was used to estimate adjusted prevalence ratio (aPR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results A total of 2558 women were included in the analysis. The prevalence of intrapartum and immediate postpartum complications was 37.6% and 31.6%, respectively. Rural residence (aPR = 1.72,95% CI: 1.34-2.20), intimate partner violence (IPV) during index pregnancy (aPR = 1.31,95% CI: 1.14-1.50), pregnancy complications (aPR = 1.78, 95% CI: 1.55-2.06), and nulliparity (aPR = 1.30, 95% CI: 1.07-1.58) were associated with intrapartum complications. Factors associated with immediate postpartum complications were complications during pregnancy (aPR = 1.65, 95% CI: 1.40-1.93) and prolonged labour (aPR = 1.34, 95%CI: 1.14-1.57). Childbirth at health facility was associated with a lower prevalence of immediate postpartum complications (aPR = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.70-0.98). Conclusion Intrapartum and immediate postpartum obstetric complications are common in Ethiopia. IPV during pregnancy, pregnancy complications, and nulliparity were associated with intrapartum complications. Pregnancy complications and prolonged labour were associated with a higher prevalence of immediate postpartum complications, while health-facility childbirth was associated with a lower prevalence.

items.title: A comparative analysis of the disease burden attributable to high BMI in Asia, Europe and Africa.
items.abstract: Objective To comprehensively assess and compare the disease burden attributable to high BMI and its epidemiological trends across Asia, Africa and Europe from 1990 to 2023. Design A secondary cross-sectional and temporal trend analysis of data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 study. Setting Countries and territories in Asia, Europe and Africa. Participants Population-level data from the GBD 2023 study covering the three continents. Results In 2023, Asia recorded 2 877 582 deaths (95 % uncertainty interval (UI): 1 465 996-4 507 685) and 120 182 714 Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALY) (56 308 955-186 506 210) attributable to high BMI, with age-standardised death and DALY rates of 30·83 (14·87-49·89) and 1253·75 (573·14-1984·15) per 100 000, respectively. Europe recorded 1 675 848 deaths (791 226-2 558 882) and 49 401 025 DALY (20 994 181-77 166 219), with corresponding rates of 52·52 (24·64-80·78) and 1824·14 (773·31-2872·71). Africa recorded 1 092 682 deaths (621 669-1 602 027) and 40 278 756 DALY (21 676 314-59 084 575), with rates of 88·74 (48·06-134·85) and 2746·12 (1445·93-4106·26). From 1990 to 2023, the estimated annual percentage change (EAPC) and average annual percent change (AAPC) in age-standardised burden indicators showed a consistent upward trend across all three continents. High BMI primarily contributed to mortality and DALY through CVD and diabetes and kidney diseases. Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) projections indicate a continuing increase in the high BMI-related disease burden over the next 17 years. Conclusions High BMI poses a significant and growing disease burden in Asia, Europe and Africa, a trend projected to persist. Implementing region-tailored interventions is crucial.

items.title: Retrospective Study of Implementation and Outcomes of a Non-Cryopreserved Autologous Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation Program for Patients With Hematologic Malignancy in a Resource-Limited Center in Chile.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND Autologous hematopoietic progenitor cell transplantation (ASCT) is the standard treatment for many hematologic malignancies, and is usually performed with cryopreservation. However, many centers in resource-limited settings perform ASCT without cryopreservation. This retrospective study evaluated the feasibility and outcomes of implementing a non-cryopreserved ASCT program for hematologic malignancy in a public health system hospital in Chile, located far from the capital city and without local cryopreservation facilities. MATERIAL AND METHODS A retrospective study of consecutive peripheral blood ASCT procedures was performed at Hospital Base Valdivia in patients older than 15 and younger than 62 years, between June 2018 and July 2024. Data were extracted from patients' medical records. Overall survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and hazard ratios, and 95% confidence intervals were calculated using univariable Cox proportional hazards models. RESULTS A total of 140 patients underwent ASCT: 81 with multiple myeloma, 31 with Hodgkin lymphoma, and 28 with non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Mobilization failure occurred in 4 patients. There was no transplant-related mortality or graft failure. Median time to neutrophil engraftment was 10.9 days, and median time to platelet engraftment was 12.3 days. Febrile neutropenia occurred in 45% of patients. Overall survival at 6 years was 83% for the entire cohort, and 96%, 88%, and 76% for non-Hodgkin lymphoma, Hodgkin lymphoma, and multiple myeloma, respectively (P=0.41). CONCLUSIONS In this retrospective single-center public-hospital experience, non-cryopreserved ASCT was feasible without local backup cryopreservation facilities, and was associated with acceptable engraftment, early transplant-related mortality, and encouraging survival outcomes.

items.title: The Nature of Pediatric Complaints in the Post-Disaster Setting: Two Natural Disasters and Two Extensive Relief Efforts.

Providers labeled each diagnostic code as either acute, chronic or undecided. These labels were assessed for interrater reliability using the Fleiss kappa and presentations in the post-hurricane setting were described and compared to controls utilizing a Chi-Square analysis. When unanimous agreement was not obtained, majority consensus was utilized. Results The TCH ED totaled 3,587 patients, the MPERT totaled 3,015 and the DMAT totaled 202 patients. items.title: Stable Iodine Knowledge and Preferred Information Sources Among Parents in Fukushima Prefecture After the 2011 Nuclear Disaster.
items.abstract: Background Knowledge regarding stable iodine prophylaxis among populations affected by the Fukushima nuclear accident remains poorly characterized. We assessed knowledge levels and preferred information sources among parents of thyroid examination participants aged ≤18 years. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional descriptive study (April 2019 and December 2022) among parents of thyroid examination participants. Knowledge was assessed using 3 items: role recognition, distribution method awareness, and effectiveness duration (score 0-3). Preferred information providers for future emergencies were collected. Results Among 1,116 participants (mean child age 12.3 years, 8.1-11.8 years post-disaster), the mean knowledge score was 1.66/3 (SD = 0.97). Only 22.1% showed high knowledge (score = 3), while 42.1% had low knowledge (score 0-1). Although two-thirds (67.8%) correctly recognized stable iodine's role, distribution method awareness was most limited: 54.3% lacked awareness of how stable iodine is distributed. Regarding effectiveness duration, 51.2% correctly answered. Health professionals were largely preferred as information providers (90.5%). Conclusions Substantial knowledge gaps existed regarding stable iodine prophylaxis, particularly distribution methods. Health professionals, as the most trusted information source, may play a key role in addressing these gaps by communicating preparedness information to communities.

items.title: Integrated survey of Taenia solium endemicity, schistosomiasis, scabies, and Guinea-worm disease in northern Namibia.
items.abstract: Background During a Mass drug administration (MDA) campaign for schistosomiasis using praziquantel in Namibia in 2019, three cases of serious neurological adverse events were observed due to neurocysticercosis caused by the parasite Taenia solium. To have a better understanding of T. solium endemicity, and to prevent and minimize adverse events in future disease control campaigns, the Ministry of Health and Social Services of Namibia decided to conduct field surveys, and take the opportunity to integrate schistosomiasis, scabies, and Guinea-worm disease (GWD) surveillance. Methods In July 2024, ten survey teams were deployed to the five regions selected as high-risk (Kavango West, Ohangwena, Omusati, Oshana and Oshikoto), using the World Health Organization (WHO) Risk Classification tool for T. solium. Stool and urine samples were collected and analyzed using Kato-Katz and urine filtration, interviews were undertaken relating to GWD and clinical assessments conducted for scabies. Geographical variations in parasite distribution were evaluated for each species using the design-adjusted Rao-Scott second-order chi-square test of independence. Results Roaming pigs and deficient sanitation were confirmed in all regions (61% of the households reported not having a latrine). Laboratory analysis of 4880 stool samples confirmed the presence of T. solium in all regions except Oshana. Only Ohangwena, with a positivity rate of 0.6%, reached the threshold suggested by the WHO to trigger a public health program. However, T. solium was also present in another three regions below the WHO threshold, and while it was not detected in Oshana, it was detected in nearby villages in Ohangwena and Oshikoto. The analysis of 4876 urine samples showed the prevalence of schistosomiasis was only above the threshold to trigger MDA in Kavango West (9.98% for Schistosoma haematobium, and 1.65% for S. mansoni). The overall prevalence of scabies was 1.9% and below the suggested level to justify MDA in all regions. Three households in Ohangwena, near the border with Angola, reported having seen GWD in humans or dogs. Conclusions The results provide updated information on T. solium and schistosomiasis endemicity and will guide future disease control efforts, including the prevention, early identification and management of praziquantel-related adverse events.

items.title: Isolation and characterization of Candida palmioleophila from poultry slaughterhouse wastewater: a first report from Brazil.
items.abstract: Environmental fungi are increasingly recognized as emerging pathogens and potential agents for biotechnological applications. Candida palmioleophila, an ascomycete yeast originally isolated from soil, has demonstrated resistance to fluconazole and capacity for bioremediation of fats and pharmaceuticals. The Brazilian poultry industry produces large volumes of wastewater, which can serve as a reservoir for fungal species with pathogenic and environmental importance. In this study, we performed a fungal screening of wastewater from poultry slaughterhouses. Wastewater samples were collected from a poultry slaughterhouse in São José do Vale do Rio Preto, Rio de Janeiro. Fungal isolation was performed using Sabouraud Dextrose Agar supplemented with antibiotics. Only yeasts were obtained and identified by polyphasic taxonomy. Species identification of both isolates were confirmed by MALDI-TOF MS and ITS sequencing, and the antifungal susceptibility of the strains was evaluated using the Vitek2 system. Physicochemical parameters of the effluent were measured. Candida species were identified and their susceptibility profile described: C. palmioleophila (resistant to fluconazole) and C. parapsilosis (susceptible to all antifungals tested). Physicochemical analyses revealed moderate effluent characteristics, potentially favoring yeast survival. This study reports the first isolation of C. palmioleophila from poultry slaughterhouse wastewater in Brazil, providing phenotypic, proteomic, and molecular characterization of the isolate and expanding the knowledge of fungal diversity in poultry slaughterhouse wastewater. These findings highlight the value of a One Health perspective for monitoring fungal diversity in wastewater and identifying microorganisms of potential biotechnological interest.

items.title: Eight anthropometric indices, including relative fat mass, and CPI-defined periodontal status: A nationwide cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Objectives To compare the associations of eight anthropometric indices with Community Periodontal Index (CPI)-defined periodontal status in a nationally representative sample of Korean adults. Materials and methods This cross-sectional study analyzed 33,310 adults aged 19-79 years from the 2010-2018 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. Each index was standardized within sex. Survey-weighted ordinal logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) per 1-SD increase for a three-level outcome (CPI 0-2, CPI 3, CPI 4). Differences between indices were assessed with bootstrap ratios of ORs. Restricted cubic spline, subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed. Results Seven of the eight indices were associated with worse CPI-defined periodontal status in the fully adjusted model. ORs were 1.166 (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.121-1.214) for relative fat mass (RFM), 1.151 (1.113-1.190) for body mass index, 1.149 (1.106-1.194) for waist-to-height ratio, 1.140 (1.100-1.182) for waist circumference and 1.030 (0.986-1.076) for a body shape index. The ratio of the RFM OR to the ORs for body mass index, waist-to-height ratio, waist circumference and body roundness index ranged from 1.014 to 1.024, and no upper 95% confidence limit exceeded 1.04. Associations of body mass index, waist circumference, waist-to-height ratio, body roundness index and RFM were stronger in women than in men. Conclusions RFM showed the largest point estimate, but the differences among indices of central adiposity were small, and no index was clearly superior in this cross-sectional analysis. Clinical relevance Body mass index and waist-based indices that account for height, including RFM, were modestly and consistently associated with CPI-defined periodontal status in Korean adults, but none performed meaningfully better than the others. These cross-sectional associations do not support the use of any single anthropometric index for periodontal screening.

items.title: Mapping bacterial bile amidation across the bile salt hydrolase family
items.abstract: Evaluating enzyme activity and specificity in complex microbiomes is challenging. The recent discovery that bacterial bile salt hydrolases (BSHs) also function as transaminases in the human gut microbiome highlights what remains to be disentangled, even within one of the most extensively studied microbiomes. BSHs as transaminases can conjugate bile acids with bioavailable amines to produce bacterial bile amidates (BBAs). The implications of BBAs for human health are rapidly evolving, but our understanding of which BSHs produce which specific BBAs remains limited. Here, we connect BSH sequence and function by evaluating the transaminase activities of 115 BSHs and reveal distinct amine specificities using molecular networking. Additionally, we identify enzymatically generated BBAs distributed across life-stage, tissue-, and disease-specific human samples by mining public metabolomics repositories, highlighting the previously unrecognized catalytic diversity of BSHs and their potential relevance to human health.

items.title: Memories of Angering Events: Word Count Analysis of Linguistic Content of Autobiographical Recall of Angering Events
items.abstract: The current research explored the language individuals use to describe their memories of times they experienced intense anger. Word count analysis of these memories was conducted using the Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count program (LIWC; Pennebaker et al., 2022). Angry memories were compared with neutral memories (Study 1) and fearful, sad, anxious, and disgust memories (Studies 2 and 3). These latter comparison conditions were useful as they compared discrete emotions that were similar to anger in negativity and arousal. Some of the most consistent and striking differences were that angry memories, as compared to other memories, included: more social words (personal pronouns, social processes, affiliation, males, females); more words relating to agency/coping potential (clout, drive, power); more words related to justification (moralization, politeness); and more words related to conflict (conflict, communication). These results suggest that angry memories exhibit unique linguistic characteristics.

items.title: Computational Link Between Motivational Factors and Cognitive Deficits in Depression
items.abstract: Abstract Background Cognitive deficits are a common symptom of depression and contribute significantly to the disabling effects of the disorder. Experimentally, they are observed as increased reaction times, increased error rates, and deficient performance adaptation after making errors or receiving adverse feedback, in multiple cognitive paradigms. In the current theoretical study we aimed to address the cause of these cognitive deficits. Methods We constructed computational models of optimal resource allocation in two cognitive tasks – Delayed Match to Sample (DMS), and Eriksen Flanker (EF). The models explicitly link performance feedback values and beliefs about task controllability with measures of cognitive performance including accuracy, reaction times, and post-error improvement in accuracy (PIA). We then introduced depression-related motivational changes – altered control belief and feedback values (representing learned helplessness, anhedonic valuation and negative bias) – to see if these factors can account for deficits in cognitive performance. Results In the DMS task, altered control belief and lower valuation of correct performance accounted for decreased accuracy and decreased PIA. In the EF task, altered control belief and lower correct performance valuation could explain increased response times, decreased accuracy and decreased error-related negativity (ERN) signal. Increased valuation of adverse feedback, on the other hand, was linked to increased accuracy and the ERN signal. Furthermore, in the EF task, different combinations of depression-related motivational factors led to different patterns of cognitive performance, which could offer a basis for stratification. Conclusions Our models offer an explicit computational and algorithmic bridge between the known depression-related motivation factors (learned helplessness, anhedonic valuation) and commonly observed cognitive deficits (increased reaction times, decreased performance accuracy, worse post-error adaptation), which contributes towards a better understanding of depression.

items.title: Distinct neurodevelopmental signatures of sex-specific transcriptome-based polygenic risk scores for depression
items.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) impacts females and males differently and post-mortem gene expression profiling reveals distinct transcriptomic signatures of the disorder in each sex. Using genes that are transcriptionally altered in MDD in both sexes, we recently developed a novel transcriptome-based polygenic risk score (tPRS), which had sex-specific associations with brain structure and depressive symptoms in both adolescents and adults. Identifying the neurodevelopmental signatures of genetically-induced shifts toward a depression-like brain transcriptome in each sex during a crucial stage, when sex differences in MDD vulnerability initially manifest, could provide useful information about the developmental pathways of early MDD risk. Leveraging sex-specific MDD gene expression data, we sought to develop female- and male-specific tPRSs (tPRS-F and tPRS-M, respectively) and evaluate their impact on regional cortical thickness, cortical surface area, subcortical volume, and depressive symptoms at baseline and 2-year follow-up in a developmental sample of 5002 adolescents (46.6% female, aged 8.9-11.0). In males, tPRS-M was associated with higher depressive symptoms at both timepoints and thicker left posterior cingulate at follow-up. In females, tPRS-F was associated with lower volumes of the right accumbens area, right caudate, and bilateral hippocampi at follow-up. Subcortical volumes of the right caudate and right hippocampus further mediated an indirect effect of tPRS-F on depressive symptoms. For each sex-specific PRS, no effects emerged in the opposite sex. Our findings suggest that sex-specific depression-like shifts in gene expression may contribute to unique vulnerability phenotypes for future MDD risk via distinct mechanisms in each sex.

items.title: Physiological Representation of Social Evaluation: Modeling Human Eye Movements, Pupillary, and Neuronal Responses to Faces.
items.abstract: Face-based social evaluations are ubiquitous and consequential, yet it remains unclear how these evaluations are represented in spontaneous physiological responses. Across four studies (222 participants: 142 females, 57 males, 23 unreported; 503 neurons), we used a data-driven modeling framework to examine how facial appearance shapes eye movements, pupillary responses, and neuronal activity during face viewing. We asked what these responses reveal about the underlying social evaluations. Pupillary responses and hippocampal firing during saccades were driven by facial variation associated with an integrated combination of valence and power evaluations; fixation duration on the eyes and hippocampal firing during fixations were more selectively tuned to threat-related evaluations; amygdalar firing primarily tracked approachability-related valence. A prospective validation study confirmed that novel faces synthesized along these modeled directions elicited the predicted physiological responses in new participants. We also found evidence of individual differences: social anxiety selectively heightened the sensitivity of pupillary responses to face evaluations. These findings suggest that distinct physiological responses across attention, autonomic arousal, and medial temporal lobe activity reflect distinct but related facets of face-based social evaluation.Significance Statement Everyday social decisions hinge on split-second impressions of unfamiliar faces. When we see a face, we instantly judge the person's likely intention (positive ↔ negative valence) and social influence (high ↔ low power). Across four complementary studies, we show that these evaluative processes are reflected in physiological responses to faces across overt attention, autonomic arousal, and subcortical neuronal firing. Different physiological systems reflected partially distinct but related facets of social-evaluative meaning, including integrated valence-and-power, threat-related, and approachability-related evaluation.

items.title: Mindfulness and Creativity in Workplace Contexts: A Critical Narrative Review of an Emerging Field
items.abstract: The relationship between mindfulness and creativity in workplace settings has attracted growing interest, yet empirical research in this area remains fragmented and at an early stage of development. Given this emerging status, the present article offers a critical narrative review aimed at mapping the current evidence and identifying conceptual and methodological gaps to guide future research. A structured literature search, preregistered in PROSPERO (CRD42024627551), was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science up to February 2025, following PRISMA guidelines, and was updated in September 2026 using the same search strategy and eligibility criteria. Five studies met the inclusion criteria. The included studies were heterogeneous in design, intervention characteristics, and outcome assessment, supporting a narrative rather than quantitative synthesis. The findings suggested possible relationships between mindfulness-based interventions and creativity-related outcomes, including creativity and problem solving, as well as related processes such as emotion regulation, working memory, cognitive flexibility, and coping. Building on these findings, the review integrates the available evidence with the broader theoretical literature to outline a preliminary integrative conceptual framework linking cognitive, affective, and motivational processes that may explain how mindfulness relates to creativity at work, while identifying key conceptual and methodological gaps to guide future research.

items.title: From Frege to ChatGPT: Compositionality in Language, Cognition, and Deep Neural Networks
items.abstract: Compositionality has long been considered a key explanatory property underlying human intelligence: arbitrary concepts can be composed into novel complex combinations, permitting the acquisition of an open ended, potentially infinite expressive capacity from finite learning experiences. Influential arguments have held that neural networks fail to explain this aspect of behavior, leading many to dismiss them as viable models of human cognition. Over the last decade, however, modern deep neural networks (DNNs), which share the same fundamental design principles as their predecessors, have come to dominate artificial intelligence, exhibiting the most advanced cognitive behaviors ever demonstrated in machines. In particular, large language models (LLMs), DNNs trained to predict the next word on a large corpus of text, have proven capable of sophisticated behaviors such as writing syntactically complex sentences without grammatical errors, producing cogent chains of reasoning, and even writing original computer programs -- all behaviors thought to require compositional processing. In this chapter, we survey recent empirical work from machine learning for a broad audience in philosophy, cognitive science, and neuroscience, situating recent breakthroughs within the broader context of philosophical arguments about compositionality. In particular, our review emphasizes two approaches to endowing neural networks with compositional generalization capabilities: (1) architectural inductive biases, and (2) metalearning, or learning to learn. We also present findings suggesting that LLM pretraining can be understood as a kind of metalearning, and can thereby equip DNNs with compositional generalization abilities in a similar way. We conclude by discussing the implications that these findings may have for the study of compositionality in human cognition and by suggesting avenues for future research.

items.title: Playful but Persuasive: Deceptive Designs and Advertising Strategies in Popular Mobile Apps for Children
items.abstract: Mobile gaming apps are woven into children’s daily lives, including those of children too young to recognize commercial intent. When apps embed manipulative interfaces or heavy advertising, they place young users in environments that conflict with their right to play and to protection from exploitation, contributing to prolonged screen time, disrupted self-regulation, and accidental in-app purchases. We examined 20 popular, free-to-download children’s mobile games in German-speaking regions using persona-based cognitive walkthroughs to assess the prevalence of deceptive design patterns and advertising. Despite platform policies and EU frameworks such as the General Data Protection Regulation and the Digital Services Act, every game contained deceptive design patterns that can nudge, confuse, or pressure children, with a median of 5.5 distinct patterns per app. Advertising was nearly ubiquitous (90%), predominantly non-skippable, and deeply intertwined with deceptive patterns throughout gameplay. We discuss what these findings imply for HCI research on ethical game design, platform responsibility, and regulatory enforcement in the EU.

items.title: Behavioral and Neural Measures of Auditory Distraction Are Not Associated with Tinnitus Severity
items.abstract: Individuals with chronic tinnitus perceive a phantom sound that imposes either a bothersome and irrepressible distraction throughout waking hours or a relatively mild nuisance that often fades into subliminal awareness. The difference in tinnitus salience may reflect a general difference in inhibitory control over any distracting sound, whether externally or internally generated. To test this hypothesis, we investigated neural and behavioral signatures of external auditory distraction suppression in participants with chronic tinnitus that had mild or bothersome tinnitus but were otherwise matched for age and hearing loss. Participants in both groups underwent behavioral and EEG testing that asked them to report on a target stream of amplitude modulated tones that switched from a random arrangement to a repeating sequence. Using additional sounds that imposed varying levels of distraction, we documented neural and perceptual suppression of auditory distractors. Behaviorally, participants with mild versus bothersome tinnitus showed comparable reductions in accuracy in the presence of varying distractor loads. Neural synchronization to the target stimulus change rate provided a useful proxy for distraction effects but did not differ between tinnitus groups. Likewise, no group differences were observed in the neural synchronization to modulation rates of the target or distractor stimuli. Our results build on work showing that individuals with tinnitus perform as well as individuals with normal hearing on listening tasks in noisy environments and expand this observation into the neural representation of sounds. Suppression of the internally generated phantom percept does not appear to be linked to general deficits in suppressing distractors.

items.title: Development of preservice teachers’ competence in lesson planning: Analyzing learning opportunities, pedagogical content knowledge, and lesson-planning skills
items.abstract: Structured Abstract Background Teacher education aims to support preservice teachers in becoming competent lesson planners. However, it remains unclear how opportunities to learn (OTL) in university-based teacher education are related to their pedagogical content knowledge (PCK) and lesson-planning skills as facets of professional competence. Aims We examined two forms of OTL—content-related OTL in university coursework and in-school OTL during teaching practice—and related them to preservice teachers’ PCK and lesson-planning skills. Research questions focused on differences in lesson-planning skills across teacher education stages (RQ1), links between teaching-practice OTL and lesson-planning skills (RQ2), and the mediating role of PCK between coursework-related OTL and lesson-planning skills (RQ3). Sample We designed a cohort-sequential study with annual assessments throughout a five-year initial teacher education program. The sample comprised 441 preservice secondary school teachers of German in Germany, of whom 85 provided repeated measurements. Methods PCK and lesson-planning skills were assessed via standardized tests. The lesson-planning assessment used text-vignette items that captured decision-making in three planning situations. OTL were measured using self-report inventories. Results Lesson-planning skills were higher at later stages of teacher education (RQ1). More planning-related teaching-practice activities were associated with higher lesson-planning skills (RQ2). Evidence for PCK as a mediator of the relation between content-related coursework OTL and lesson-planning skills was mixed (RQ3). Conclusions University-based teacher education appears to support the development of preservice teachers’ lesson-planning skills. Lesson-planning skills were associated with both content-related coursework OTL and in-school teaching-practice OTL. PCK and lesson-planning skills were strongly correlated but theoretically and empirically distinct. Findings on mediation are tentative due to measurement limitations.

items.title: Narrative exposure therapy for post-traumatic stress disorder and appetitive aggression among soldiers retiring from active service in Uganda
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Narrative exposure therapy (NET) is a form of treatment for trauma disorders, particularly in individuals suffering from complex and multiple traumas. It is an evidence-based trauma-focused therapeutic approach designed to help individuals process and manage experiences of trauma, especially in the context of cumulative or complex trauma. Information on the effectiveness of narrative exposure therapy in managing post-traumatic stress disorder and appetitive aggression among retiring soldiers is limited. This study aimed to determine the effectiveness of narrative exposure therapy as a form of treatment for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and appetitive aggression (AA) among soldiers retiring from active service in Uganda. Methods : An interventional study was conducted among 70 retired Uganda People’s Defence Forces (UPDF) soldiers who had earlier been screened for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and appetitive aggression at Gaddafi Barracks in Jinja District, eastern Uganda, in preparation for retirement. At baseline, participants underwent narrative exposure therapy comprising eight 90-minute sessions delivered biweekly over four months. Sessions were conducted either at nearby barracks or within participants’ homes or community settings after retirement. Following completion of the four-month intervention period, participants were reassessed for PTSD and AA at endline. Results : Mean PTSD scores decreased from 19.96 (SD = 15.00) at baseline to 13.93 (SD = 8.96) at endline, representing a mean reduction of 6.04 points. This reduction was statistically significant, t (55) = 3.57, p < .001, indicating a significant decline in PTSD symptom severity following the intervention. Similarly, mean appetitive aggression scores decreased from 34.11 (SD = 6.59) at baseline to 10.39 (SD = 4.09) at endline, representing a mean reduction of 23.71 points. This reduction was statistically significant, t (58) = 20.29, p < .001, indicating a substantial decrease in appetitive aggression following narrative exposure therapy. Conclusion : Narrative exposure therapy demonstrated effectiveness in reducing symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder and appetitive aggression among retiring soldiers in Uganda. These findings support consideration of integrating narrative exposure therapy into the UPDF retirement process prior to community reintegration.

items.title: Psychological determinants of shared decision-making at the end-of-life: development of a structured observation tool
items.abstract: Abstract Background There are currently no tools available for observing the psychological processes that guide shared decision-making at the end of life. Objectives This article aims to formalize a methodological framework for the design of an exploratory scientific study based on participant observation by psychologists. The main objective of the tool is to enable the observation of the psychological distress of patients and the psychological experiences of all those involved in shared medical decision-making (patients, relatives, professionals) during the end-of-life decision-making process. Methods An observation tool for psychologists in palliative care was developed through an integrative methodology based on a structured review of the literature. A preliminary version of the observation tool was submitted to 11 expert psychologists practicing in end-of-life care, via the Delphi method. Quantitative and qualitative analyses of the comments and content of individual and group interviews were conducted. Statistical analysis focused on measures of central tendency, dispersion, and distribution. Results The final version of the observation tool comprises 57 items. The tool was applied in 54 palliative care cases; 44 complete data sets were obtained. Statistical analysis demonstrates good acceptability, feasibility, and reliability of the tool. Conclusion The tool enables psychologists to observe shared decision-making by focusing on the psychological determinants of the process. Without any psychometric ambitions, the observation tool is designed to facilitate participant observation in a psychological context and adequately fulfils the objectives for which it was developed.

items.title: Development and preliminary feasibility of Healing Minds Through Play: a multi-stakeholder-informed CBT–DBT-informed psychoeducational game for early adolescent counselling sessions in Malaysia
items.abstract: Abstract Background Adolescent mental health is increasingly recognised as a critical public health issue, particularly as many mental disorders begin in early adolescence. In Malaysia, findings from the 2023 National Health and Morbidity Survey (NHMS) revealed significant prevalence of depressive and anxiety symptoms among adolescents. Objective Despite the growing need for early intervention, many adolescents struggle to actively engage in their first counselling session due to stigma, fear of being judged, and difficulty expressing emotions. In practice, this often manifests as silence, minimal responses, and prolonged pauses, which delay therapeutic alliance formation and therapeutic engagement. Method This study aimed to develop and assess the early feasibility of Healing Minds Through Play, a CBT–DBT-based psychoeducational Snakes and Ladders game designed to support early engagement and emotional expression among adolescents. The study employed a Research and Development (R&D) approach encompassing needs analysis, prototype development, expert validation, and a pilot feasibility test. The needs analysis involved 101 respondents, while the pilot test was conducted through individual counselling sessions lasting 45–60 minutes with adolescents aged 10 to 19 years in real-world settings. Findings : Preliminary results indicate that the prototype is easy to use, positively received, and demonstrated potential in mitigating communication barriers and enhancing readiness to communicate during early counselling sessions. Future Research : Further studies are recommended to develop a hybrid digital version incorporating interactive boards, DBT audio, CBT animations, and multilingual support to enhance inclusivity. Conclusion The game-based approach creates a clinically-informed, less intimidating medium ,thereby strengthening the foundation for early rapport between adolescents and mental health professionals. As a low-cost, culturally adaptable psychoeducational tool, Healing Minds Through Play has the potential to contribute meaningfully to the achievement of SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being), SDG 4 (Quality Education), and SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities) by improving access and early engagement in adolescent mental health services.

items.title: SAVEstate: A Method for Documenting Player Reflection in Digital Games
items.abstract: In recent years, interest in eudaimonic player experiences (PX) - concerning reflection, meaning-making, and personal growth - has increased. However, most games user research methods are not well-suited to study eudaimonic PX, as they have been developed to evaluate features of hedonic PX, such as flow, immersion, and playability. To more deeply explore eudaimonic PX, we require methods that can 1) investigate how moment-to-moment PX shapes player reflection and 2) explore how players reengage and reinterpret their experiences longitudinally. In this paper, we present SAVEstate , a method that uses documentation as a means of studying player reflection. SAVEstate consists of two phases: reflection-in-action and reflection-on-action, which allow researchers to probe players’ in-situ reflections and how they reengage with their gameplay, respectively. Using SAVEstate, we were able to observe in-situ meaning-making and connect it to post-game reflection-on-action, and view synchronous sensemaking across multiple participants. We also developed an open-source desktop application for researchers to adapt in their own SAVEstate deployments. We discuss implications for how researchers might use SAVEstate to conduct future research in meaningful PX.

items.title: Order-Bound companionship: The Practice of Emotional Labor in Professional Game Companionship
items.abstract: Labor in platform gig economy increasingly involves services involving relationship that demand significant emotional investment. Grounded in China’s unique socio-cultural and multi-platform context, this study explores professional game companionship, an under-explored digital labor practice. Through interviews with 22 game companionship practitioners, we used a micro-level perspective to relational gig work to analyze how workers navigate intimate boundaries and stakeholder networks. We found that companions adopt an "order-bound" mechanism: performing immersive deep acting during paid sessions, followed by complete emotional disengagement post-order. We also identified a tripartite companion-centric network featuring scenario-based performances with clients, competitive-symbiotic peer relations, and interdependent governance with companionship clubs. Furthermore, significant identity fluidity exists, with individuals frequently transitioning between companion, client, and club operator roles. We provide implications for future labor governance and platform designs for intimate digital work that explicitly account for institutionalized boundaries and gig workers’ shifting psychological needs.

items.title: "Dragon Slayer Becomes the Dragon": How Players Perceive and Respond to Inequality in the Game World of Whiteout Survival
items.abstract: Inequality in real-world societies are associated with psychological distress and behavioral consequences. However, less is known about whether similar dynamics emerge when inequality exists within virtual environments or make-belief worlds. As online games increasingly constitute meaningful social spaces, it becomes critical to examine how players perceive and react to structural and resource differences online to optimize their experiences. This study studies perceptions of inequality in the online simulation game "Whiteout Survival," using semi-structured interviews and think-aloud gameplay walkthrough protocols. By focusing on players’ interpretations of resource distribution, ranking systems, gaming mechanisms, and in-game social dynamics, our analyses revealed that players’ attitudes on inequality vary according to their relative status: those occupying lower positions often criticize unfair structures, yet as they acquire stakes through resource accumulation or social integration, many defend the same systems they previously opposed. These shifts reveal how hierarchies reproduce position-dependent evaluations of fairness. The consequences of inequality on player actions depended on the transparency of game mechanisms, the structure of community hierarchies, and differential social capital. This work shows how human social perception and consequent actions are transformed when enacted in virtual processes in make-belief.

items.title: Diagnosing Performance in Invasion-Based Esports: The Esports Performance Screening (EPS) Framework
items.abstract: Coaching in esports continues to become more common, yet conceptual tools for coaches to analyse performance breakdowns in esports remain limited. Existing approaches lack a way to distinguish between mental errors (i.e., mistakes relate to strategy and tactics), and physical slips (i.e., motor execution). This paper introduces the Esports Performance Screening (EPS) framework, that integrates several frameworks and models from sport and computing science which can be used to analyse mental and motor performance in esports. The EPS framework organises performance into five interconnected levels: strategy, tactics, tasks, actions and operations. Across these levels, teams pursue forms of superiority that influence transitions between stability and instability during invasion-based esports competition. The framework supports two complementary modes of screening use: diagnostic during reflective review and real-time screening during live play. Through illustrative esports scenarios, we demonstrate how instability can originate at different hierarchical layers and how misattribution of failure can obscure underlying causes. The purpose of the EPS framework is to help coaches systematically diagnose performance breakdowns, and act as heuristics to aid gameplay analysis during a match. The paper contributes a theoretically grounded, title-agnostic esports framework to support systematic performance analysis and pedagogical development in invasion-based esports.

items.title: Scientific Understanding Across Disciplines: In Varietate Concordia?
items.abstract: Abstract Understanding is a generally acknowledged aim of science, but the way in which understanding is pursued and criteria for when it is achieved differ widely across scientific disciplines. This paper offers a comparative analysis of this disciplinary variation, aimed at revealing differences as well as commonalities in methods and criteria for achieving understanding. Starting-point is the contextual theory of scientific understanding (De Regt 2017), which was developed to accommodate contextual variation in criteria for understanding. While De Regt’s work focused on historical variation and used mainly case studies from the history of physics, the current paper applies the contextual theory to disciplinary variation. We present brief descriptive accounts of how understanding figures in nine scientific disciplines: mathematics, theoretical physics, astrophysics, chemistry, geoscience, biology, neuroscience, psychiatry, and the engineering sciences. Subsequently, we compare and evaluate these accounts in light of the contextual theory of scientific understanding.

items.title: Breaking boundaries: fungi in the “rhizoctonia” complex occur systemically in three European orchid species
items.abstract: Mycorrhizal fungi are an important component of the root microbiota in most land plants as they play fundamental roles in plant nutrition and health. Orchids, one of the largest plant families, are particularly dependent on mycorrhizal fungi for seed germination and plant development. Orchid mycorrhizal (OrM) fungi identified in the roots of most green orchids belong to the ‘rhizoctonia’ complex, a polyphyletic group of Tulasnellaceae, Ceratobasidiaceae, Serendipitaceae and Sebacinaceae (Agaricomycotina), and are generally assumed to colonize their host from soil, where they live as saprotrophs. However, some rhizoctonia OrM fungi were rarely detected by metabarcoding in soil around orchid roots, and we have tested the hypothesis that these fungi may use adult orchid plants as a habitat by colonizing not only their roots, but also other organs. The occurrence of OrM rhizoctonias inside roots, stems and leaves of three terrestrial orchid species ( Spiranthes spiralis , Serapias vomeracea and Neottia ovata ) was investigated by metabarcoding. In all orchid species, a broad majority of putative OrM fungi found in roots was also detected in either stems or leaves of the same plant. Putative OrM fungi were also detected in the capsules of all three species and in seeds of S. spiralis . Systemic occurrence of mycorrhizal fungi in plants is a novel finding. In particular, identification of OrM symbionts in all orchid tissues raises important questions on the plant-fungus relationship in the aerial organs.

items.title: Consistent efficiency of horticultural intercropping: a quantitative synthesis
items.abstract: Abstract Agroecosystem diversification through intercropping is a strategy to mitigate biodiversity loss and enhance ecosystem services while maintaining or improving productivity, resource-use efficiency, and pest regulation. Although field crop intercropping has been well studied, horticultural intercropping remains less explored, despite its relevance for food security. Our study aims to address this gap by assessing the overall efficiency of horticultural intercropping through a quantitative synthesis of global experimental data. In addition, we examine how system design, management practices, and species characteristics influence land-use advantage. Our primary finding is that horticultural intercropping is advantageous compared with monocultures, providing the first large-scale, global quantitative evidence of a land-use advantage in horticultural systems. Overall, the mean Land Equivalent Ratio was 1.41, indicating that monocultures would require 41% more land than intercropping to achieve the same yield, with values exceeding 1 in over 90% of the experimental observations. Additive intercropping and species combinations that include trees or nitrogen-fixing species were particularly efficient, a pattern consistent with ecological interactions such as niche complementarity and facilitation. Notably, the benefits of intercropping decreased with insecticide use, suggesting that this input may suppress indirect positive effects of plant associations, corroborating the recommendation of intercropping for low-input agriculture. In this context, intercropping research holds potential to address some of the persistent challenges in diversification, such as optimizing systems without relying on chemical inputs. To realize this potential, we suggest a deeper investigation into the underlying ecological mechanisms and the use of complementary indices for productivity assessments. The consistent land-use advantage of horticultural intercropping across varied contexts, as identified in this study, supports the productive viability of agroecosystem diversification.

items.title: Agrobiodiversity dynamics in traditional socioecological systems: An agent‐based model approach on the role of kinship systems and variety transmission
items.abstract: Abstract Context : Agrobiodiversity depends on multiple interconnected socioecological processes. The loss of crop diversity represents a critical challenge for global food security and for the resilience and adaptation of small‐scale farming communities to climate change. However, the role of kinship and the transmission of variety in the formation of agrobiodiversity have not been systematically addressed. Objectives : Our objective was to examine how kinship and transmission of varieties influence the dynamics of the diversity of cassava ( Manihot esculenta) in traditional socioecological systems. Methods : We employed an agent‐based model to simulate the vertical diffusion of cassava varieties by considering different postmarital residence norms, variety of transmission rules and two marriage norms (Endogamy and Dual Organization). Results : The model successfully captured the expected loss of diversity over time, while also demonstrating that social norms slow down this process. We further showed that the interaction between postmarital residence rules and variety transmission consistently impacts diversity patterns between groups and clans. Conclusions : By showing how the transmission of varieties' dynamics shapes ecological outcomes, this work underscores the central role of human social institutions in sustaining agrobiodiversity. Moreover, our study highlights the importance of exploring, both ethnographically and theoretically, the complementarities between horizontal and vertical transmission. items.title: Reproduction and the Environment in Southeast Asia: A Scoping Review of Anthropogenic Environmental Change and Sexual and Reproductive Health
items.abstract: ABSTRACT While often neglected, sexual and reproductive health (SRH) is a significant dimension of the health implications of global anthropogenic environmental change, including climate change. However, literature on the topic is scarce and largely neglects low and middle‐income countries (LMICs) and regions such as Southeast Asia. We thus aimed to synthesize the literature connecting anthropogenic environmental change and SRH in Southeast Asia. We conducted a scoping review, searching five databases systematically, and inductively synthesized findings. We included 45 eligible sources of 2764 screened, and generated 5 themes pertaining to pollution; nutrition; gender‐based violence; changes in ways of life; and infectious diseases. Regional patterns of environmental change were presented as forces influencing SRH (e.g., fertility and pregnancy outcomes); increasing gendered vulnerabilities (e.g., in extreme‐weather events); and potentially disrupting reproductive plans, attitudes and access to services. Region‐specific factors such as the large‐scale expansion of plantation agriculture, pollution due to agricultural and industrial developments, and heightened susceptibility to extreme‐weather events given the tropical climate were associated with worsened SRH outcomes. This highlighted the need for further research, particularly of ethico‐political considerations.

items.title: Class-wide sequence, structural, and docking-profile diversity of insect odorant receptors and structural specialization of Orco
items.abstract: Abstract Insect olfaction is facilitated by a heterotetrameric odorant receptor–odorant receptor co-receptor (OR-Orco) complex, which is distinct from that of vertebrate ORs. However, extensive sequence divergence and lineage-specific expansion have complicated large-scale comparisons of OR repertoires across insects. Here, we integrated sequence similarity, structural similarity, and molecular docking to analyze ORs from 115 insect species. Across this class-wide sampling, OR repertoire size was associated with adult diet, larval diet, and habitat, but not with circadian rhythm. We developed a “trunk–branch” network framework to classify ORs according to sequence and structural similarity and used large-scale molecular docking to derive comparative docking profiles. Despite marked differences in sequence-and structural-community composition, almost all sampled orders contained ORs assigned to all six docking-profile communities. Holometabolous insects showed higher OR sequence-community diversity than non-holometabolous insects, and docking-profile composition differed between extant lineages whose order-level origins predate or postdate the end-Permian mass extinction. Most notably, we identified a highly conserved extracellular β-sheet in Orco that restricts ligand access to the binding pocket and may contribute to its reduced capacity to bind natural odorants. The emergence of Orco represents a key evolutionary transition from homomeric receptors to heteromeric OR–Orco complexes, and our results suggest that this transition may have been accompanied by pronounced specialization of the extracellular domain and binding pocket. Together, these analyses provide a class-wide framework for comparing insect OR diversity and generate testable hypotheses for future experimental and evolutionary studies.

items.title: Repurposed smart tuna-fishing buoys provide real-time intelligence for marine conservation and ocean observation
items.abstract: Abstract End-of-use echosounder buoys developed for industrial tuna fishing offer a largely untapped opportunity to expand ocean monitoring using existing fisheries technology. Here we present a technology-transfer and pilot feasibility study testing whether repurposed smart-buoys can operate as short-term autonomous platforms for marine conservation monitoring and ocean observation. Through Satlink project ReCon, refurbished buoys were deployed in fixed-point and drifting configurations across one shelf technical test area, two coral reefs, and two seamount/pinnacle systems in the Western Indian Ocean (WIO) region (Bazaruto Archipelago, Mozambique). Fixed-point acoustic record spans ranged from 51.5 to 96.2 h per site. Across fixed-point and drifting configurations, the exported dataset contained 393 time-stamped acoustic records and 1,281 depth-layer relative acoustic biomass/backscatter observations, with buoy position and acoustic data transmitted by satellite (via INMARSAT) to shore-based systems. Integration with the long-term BCSS Ocean Observatory time-series provided concurrent weather and oceanographic context across > 20 in-situ variables, while scuba-based megafauna surveys recorded 14–20 megafauna taxa per site as biological context for the acoustic records. The pilot time-series captured consistent diel structure, with 20–40% higher nocturnal relative acoustic biomass/backscatter values, alongside exploratory temporal co-occurrences with cooler bottom-water pulses, transient chlorophyll-a increases, and site-level differences in megafauna assemblage structure. While these short time-series cannot be used to infer ecological baselines, reef health, fishing impacts, environmental drivers, or absolute biological biomass, they demonstrate the capacity of repurposed smart-buoys to generate high-frequency acoustic and contextual ecological information in data-poor and remote marine regions. Our study establishes a practical pathway for integrating recovered fishing infrastructure into marine observatories, while highlighting the need for longer deployments, broader replication, quantitative habitat characterization, and independent biological calibration before robust ecological inference can be made.

items.title: GPS-tracking provides novel insights into the age-specific migration behaviour of an endangered migrant seabird in the Afro-Palearctic flyway
items.abstract: Abstract Background Migration is a complex behaviour, requiring individuals to integrate genetic, environmental and social information to reach distant goals, with important consequences for individuals, populations and communities. However, despite its ecological importance, our understanding of the development of migration behaviour across an organism’s lifetime is lacking for most taxa. Recently, developments in bio-logging have enabled us to track juveniles of many species during their first migrations, improving our understanding of migration ontogeny. The Baltic Lesser Black-backed Gull ( L. f. fuscus ) is a long-distance migratory seabird inhabiting the eastern Afro-Palearctic flyway that has undergone recent, dramatic declines. However, determining the drivers of these trends is hindered by poor understanding of fine-scale space use, particularly during the non-breeding period. Methods Here we fitted GPS-tags to a total of 70 adult and 39 juvenile Baltic gulls from 19 Swedish colonies to examine age-related differences in movement behaviour during autumn migration. Results We observed clear differences in the autumn migration behaviour of adult and juvenile Baltic Gulls. Adults tended to migrate further than juveniles, with a much higher probability of crossing the Sahara. They also completed their migrations faster despite similar flight speeds between age classes, with observed differences in overall migration speeds resulting from longer and more frequent stopovers in juveniles. Moreover, migration routes showed equivalent directness between age classes, with a notable lack of exploratory movements by juveniles. Conclusions GPS-tracking of adult and juvenile Baltic Gulls revealed little evidence of exploratory behaviour, providing limited support for the exploration-refinement hypothesis during neonatal migration. Combined with latitudinal differences in migration destinations between age classes, our work suggests that learning and development of this long-distance migration requires multiple annual cycles to complete. Additionally, we identify several key stopover and wintering sites used by Baltic Gulls during the non-breeding period, facilitating the identification of potential threats across the species’ life cycle.

items.title: Reindeer habitat selection and movement change with cumulative impacts from mining and wind power development
items.abstract: Industrial expansion often occurs in landscapes already affected by multiple disturbances, leading to cumulative impacts on biodiversity and local communities. With the societal pressure for an rapid ‘green transition’, land-use changes intensifies, yet most impact assessments remain local and project-based, disregarding cumulative impacts. We conceptualized and disentangled key dimensions of cumulative impacts and integrated them within habitat selection, calving site selection, and movement analyses in a case study of reindeer and Sámi reindeer husbandry in Scandinavia. Using GPS data collected before, during, and after the construction of four wind power plants, we quantified the effects of mining, wind power development, and other infrastructure across snow-free seasons and behavioural processes. We found strong avoidance of mines and wind power plants, with zones of influence extending up to 5-10 km at landscape scale and up to 5 km at patch scale. Impacts were strongest during calving but also present in summer and autumn. Wind power plants affected movement by acting as semi-permeable barriers, with reindeer avoiding crossing them and moving faster and more directionally near turbines during construction. At patch scale, cumulative impacts of several wind power plants were evident during calving. Our results highlight the need for regional and integrative land-use planning that accounts for cumulative impacts from multiple existing and planned developments. The framework we present here provides a general approach to quantify zones of influence and cumulative impacts of multiple features and infrastructure types across landscapes and ecological processes.

items.title: Spatial patterns of mosquito communities and monkey malaria vectors in a tropical riverine forest in Sabah, Malaysian Borneo
items.abstract: Abstract Background Understanding how vector ecology intersects with host behaviour is essential for predicting zoonotic malaria risk in tropical ecosystems. In Malaysian Borneo, zoonotic transmission of simian malaria parasites such as Plasmodium knowlesi is shaped by interactions among mosquito vectors, non-human primate reservoir hosts, and human activities across heterogeneous landscapes. However, fine-scale spatial structuring of mosquito communities within tropical riverine forests remains poorly characterized. Methodology/Principal Findings We conducted a two-year mosquito survey (November 2016–October 2018) in a lowland riverine forest along the Menanggul River, Sabah, Malaysian Borneo. Mosquitoes were sampled on 44 nights using CO₂-baited light traps repeatedly deployed across horizontal (0 m, 250 m, and 500 m from the river) and vertical (ground and canopy) gradients, yielding 244 trap collections. A total of 9,928 mosquitoes were collected, dominated by Culex spp. (91.4%), whereas Anopheles spp. were rare (153 individuals; 1.5%). Female Anopheles mosquitoes (n = 57) were more frequently detected near the river and tended to occur more often in ground traps. Zero-inflated negative binomial generalized linear mixed models based on the female mosquito dataset revealed significant effects of river distance and trap height on mosquito abundance, while short-term microclimatic variation showed little explanatory power. The Anopheles assemblage was dominated by Anopheles balabacensis , a recognized vector of simian malaria parasites in Sabah. Molecular screening detected simian Plasmodium DNA in two An. balabacensis individuals, including P. knowlesi , together with other simian Plasmodium species. Conclusions/Significance Our findings suggest that river-edge habitats may function as localized contact hotspots where mosquito vectors, primate reservoir hosts, and human activities repeatedly overlap in space and time, potentially facilitating zoonotic malaria transmission even when vector densities are low. These results support the growing view that zoonotic malaria risk in tropical landscapes is shaped less by overall vector abundance than by fine-scale ecological overlap among vectors, wildlife, and humans. Author Summary Zoonotic malaria caused by monkey malaria parasites such as Plasmodium knowlesi has become an important public health concern in Malaysian Borneo. Transmission occurs when mosquito vectors feed on both infected non-human primates and humans, but the ecological conditions that increase opportunities for such contact remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated mosquito communities in a tropical riverine forest along the Menanggul River in Sabah, Malaysia, an area where wildlife, human activities, and ecotourism frequently overlap. Over a two-year period, we repeatedly sampled mosquitoes across different distances from the river and at both ground and canopy levels. Although mosquitoes capable of transmitting simian malaria were relatively rare, they were detected more frequently near river edges and in ground-level traps. We also detected simian Plasmodium DNA in two Anopheles balabacensis mosquitoes, a major vector of zoonotic malaria in Sabah. Our findings suggest that river-edge habitats may act as localized “contact hotspots” where vectors, primate hosts, and humans repeatedly overlap in space and time, potentially increasing opportunities for zoonotic malaria transmission even when overall vector abundance is low. These results highlight the importance of considering wildlife ecology, human behaviour, and landscape structure together when assessing and managing zoonotic disease risk in tropical forest systems.
