items.title: Ruptured INfrarenal abdominal AneurySm: aortiC repair using the ENduranT Endograft. The R.IN.AS.C.ENT.E. Study.
items.abstract: Ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (rAAA) represents a vascular surgical emergency with high mortality. Endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) using the bifurcated Endurant stent graft system is widely employed; however, data specifically addressing its performance in infrarenal rAAA remain limited. We conducted a retrospective, multicenter study including 121 patients with confirmed infrarenal rAAA treated exclusively with bifurcated Endurant II or IIs (Medtronic Inc., Minneapolis, Minnesota) devices across 5 Italian tertiary vascular centers from January 2014 to October 2024. Primary endpoints were technical success and 30-day all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included long-term survival, incidence of endoleaks, and reintervention rates. Patients receiving alternative stent grafts or hybrid procedures were excluded to ensure cohort homogeneity. A total of 121 patients were enrolled during the study period. The cohort had a mean age of 75.3 ± 8.2 years, with 91.7% male predominance. Technical success was achieved in 96.7%. The 30-day mortality rate was 15.7%. Multivariate logistic regression identified abdominal compartment syndrome (ACS) (odds ratio [OR], 29.8; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.8-317.7; P = .005) and use of an aortic occlusion balloon (AOB) (OR, 16.4; 95% CI, 2.5-106.2; P = .003) as independent predictors of early mortality. At a median follow-up of 33.6 months (interquartile range, 4.9-72.3), 5-year survival was 65.4%, freedom from any endoleak was 92.6%, and freedom from reintervention was 91.6%. Late type Ia endoleaks occurred in 2.5% of patients. In this large, strictly defined infrarenal rAAA cohort, bifurcated Endurant stent grafts demonstrated high technical success and favorable early and mid-term clinical outcomes, including in patients with hostile neck anatomy. Early identification and management of ACS and judicious use of AOBs may improve survival. These findings reinforce current EVAR-first guidelines and emphasize the importance of device-specific outcome assessment in emergent rAAA repair.Clinical ImpactThis multicenter study provides one of the largest device-specific evaluations of bifurcated Endurant stent grafts for infrarenal ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms in a rigorously defined Italian cohort, demonstrating high technical success (96.7%) and low 30-day mortality (15.7%) despite a high prevalence of hostile neck anatomy (54.5%). Abdominal compartment syndrome and the use of an aortic occlusion balloon emerged as independent predictors of early mortality, highlighting the critical role of perioperative management. Mid-term outcomes were favorable, with a 5-year survival rate of 65.4%, a low incidence of type Ia endoleak (2.5%), and high freedom from reintervention (91.6%). Overall, these findings support the use of Endurant devices in emergent settings for anatomically suitable patients and reinforce EVAR-first strategies in the management of ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms.

items.title: Perceived Causes of Fertility Challenges and Utilization of Infertility Treatment Modalities: Insights from U.S. Black Women.
items.abstract: To qualitatively explore what Black women themselves perceive as the causes of their fertility challenges and examine the treatment modalities utilized to address infertility. The study included 40 Black women aged 25-45 years, with a history of fertility challenges, residing in the United States, who completed the Fertility Equity Study between 2021 and 2023. Participants completed a survey and up to two semi-structured interviews to discuss their fertility journeys and perceived causes of fertility challenges. We examined and synthesized participant perceptions about the causes of their challenges in conceiving or maintaining a pregnancy. Frequencies and percentages were calculated for each common cause of fertility challenges and treatment modalities used. Participants described five common perceived causes of their fertility challenges: (1) clinically diagnosed reproductive health conditions (n = 26; e.g., fibroids, oligospermia); 2) age (n = 7); (3) unknown causes (n = 6); (4) structural issues (n = 4; e.g., limited access to Black donor sperm); and (5) stress (n = 4). Nearly half of participants (n = 19) only used medically assisted reproduction (MAR), whereas one-third (n = 13) had a history of using both MAR and holistic approaches (e.g., herbal teas). None of the participants who only used holistic fertility treatment modalities attributed their fertility challenges to reproductive health conditions. This study reflects the nuanced ways that Black women conceptualize their fertility and the antecedents to fertility challenges. These results reflect the need to integrate holistic and spiritual approaches into fertility care and MAR to appeal to the needs of Black women and families navigating infertility.

items.title: Women-Focused and Sex/Gender-Related Cardiovascular Research Funding under Canada's Sex- and Gender-Based Analysis Policy from 2000 to 2024.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death among women, yet women have historically been underrepresented in cardiovascular research. Whether Canada's sex- and gender-based analysis (SGBA) policies have shifted funding toward women-focused and sex/gender-related cardiovascular research remains unclear. To examine time trends in Canadian Institutes of Health Research (CIHR) investment in women-focused cardiovascular research and assess changes associated with milestones for CIHR SGBA policy implementation, including mandatory application-level requirements in 2010 and grant criteria assessed by reviewers in 2018. We conducted a longitudinal study using CIHR funding data from fiscal years (FYs) 2000 to 2024. Women-focused cardiovascular research projects were identified through terminology searches in titles, keywords, and abstracts. Annual FY funding proportions were analyzed using interrupted time series segmented regression with interruption points in 2010 and 2018. Among 17,168 cardiovascular research grant records, 11.3% were women-focused research. These grants received 11.9% of total funding over the 25-year period. Funding increased before 2010, declined during 2011 and 2017, and accelerated after 2018. Segmented regression showed a small immediate increase in 2010, followed by a negative post-2010 trend and a significant positive quadratic trend after 2018. Application-level SGBA requirements had limited influence on national health research investment patterns, yet more recently reviewer-level assessment aligned with increased investment in women-focused research. Strengthening SGBA implementation will require consistent monitoring of sex- and gender-disaggregated data to assess patient outcomes and impact.

items.title: The role of methionine-driven epigenetic modulation in the regulation of health and disease: a comprehensive review.
items.abstract: Methionine, a sulfur-containing essential amino acid, plays a pivotal role in epigenetic regulation through its involvement in one-carbon metabolism and as a precursor to S-adenosylmethionine (SAM), the universal methyl donor. This review explores how methionine availability dynamically influences DNA and histone methylation, non-coding RNA expression, and RNA modifications, ultimately shaping gene expression, cellular identity, and developmental outcomes. Emerging evidence suggests that balanced methionine intake is critical for maintaining epigenetic homeostasis. At the same time, both deficiency and excess can disrupt this equilibrium, contributing to diseases such as cancer, metabolic disorders, neurodevelopmental abnormalities, and cardiovascular dysfunction. Methionine deficiency is shown to impair DNA and histone methylation, alter non-coding RNA profiles, and compromise stem cell pluripotency and neurogenesis. Conversely, excess methionine can trigger aberrant hypermethylation, genomic instability, and metabolic imbalances, with links to oncogenic transformation and accelerated aging. Notably, methionine restriction (MR) enhances stress resilience, promotes healthy aging, and reduces tumor progression by reprogramming the epigenetic landscape. This review highlights methionine's dualistic nature, both as a crucial epigenetic regulator and a potential contributor to disease when imbalanced. It also underscores the need for context-specific dietary strategies and further research into the intricate interplay between methionine metabolism, gene regulation, and long-term health outcomes. Understanding these molecular mechanisms may unlock novel nutritional and therapeutic approaches for disease prevention and epigenetic reprogramming.

items.title: Sense of Agency and Negative Emotional Experiences Among Stroke Survivors: A Patient Journey Map Based on Qualitative Research.
items.abstract: To explore stroke survivors' experiences of sense of agency and negative emotions during recovery, and to develop a patient journey map. Stroke can disrupt perceived control and cause emotional distress, but how these experiences relate during recovery remains unclear. Descriptive qualitative study nested within a longitudinal study. Purposive maximum variation sampling recruited 13 stroke survivors from a tertiary hospital in Henan, China. Sampling was guided by changes and fluctuations in sense of agency scores across four assessments, from before discharge to six months afterwards. Retrospective semi-structured interviews were conducted six months after discharge. Data were analysed using content analysis and a preliminary stage-theme framework. Reporting followed COREQ. Three themes and 12 subthemes were identified: illness shock, loss of sense of agency and distress marked by doubts and worries; further loss of sense of agency, intensified negative emotions and passive coping; and rebuilding sense of agency, alleviation of negative emotions and active coping. Physical limitations, disrupted roles, unclear information, rehabilitation setbacks and unmet support needs accompanied loss of agency and distress. Meaningful functional gains, clearer illness understanding, motivation and supportive relationships helped participants rebuild agency. Stroke survivors described loss and rebuilding of sense of agency alongside changes in negative emotions and coping. The patient journey map highlights opportunities for continuous, individualised support during recovery. Nurses should assess agency and emotional distress throughout recovery, particularly during care transitions and setbacks. Understandable information, meaningful goals, feedback on progress and patient participation may support agency. Withdrawal should prompt exploration of emotional concerns and practical barriers rather than assumptions about motivation. No patient or public contribution.

items.title: Determinants of optimal number of ANC visits among women of reproductive age in Uganda using modified poisson GLM regression analysis.
items.abstract: Antenatal care (ANC) is a critical maternal health intervention that contributes to the prevention of maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality through early detection and management of pregnancy-related complications. Although Uganda has achieved high coverage of at least one ANC visit, continuity of care remains suboptimal, with many women not completing the recommended number of ANC visits. This study examined the determinants of optimal ANC utilization among women in Uganda using nationally representative data from the 2024 Uganda Malaria Indicator Survey (MIS). A cross-sectional secondary analysis was conducted using data from the 2024 Uganda MIS. The study included 3,477 women aged 15-49 years who had a live birth within the five years preceding the survey. Optimal ANC utilization was defined as attendance of at least four ANC visits during pregnancy. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize participant characteristics, while Multiple Correspondence Analysis (MCA) explored underlying patterns among categorical determinants. Associations between explanatory variables and optimal ANC utilization were assessed using survey-weighted modified Poisson regression with robust variance estimation. Crude and adjusted prevalence ratios (PRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported. Logistic regression was performed as a sensitivity analysis. Overall, 77.7% (n = 2,702) of women reported attending four or more ANC visits during their most recent pregnancy, while 22.3% (n = 775) attended fewer than four visits. MCA revealed a clear socioeconomic gradient, with optimal ANC attendance clustering among women with higher educational attainment, greater wealth, urban residence, and higher media exposure. In the adjusted modified Poisson model, educational attainment and region of residence were the only factors independently associated with optimal ANC utilization. Women with secondary education (APR = 1.12, 95% CI: 1.03-1.21) and higher education (APR = 1.15, 95% CI: 1.03-1.29) were significantly more likely to complete at least four ANC visits compared with women with no formal education. Regional disparities were also observed, with women residing in Northern Uganda (APR = 1.20, 95% CI: 1.11-1.30) and West Nile (APR = 1.26, 95% CI: 1.17-1.36) demonstrating higher prevalence of optimal ANC utilization compared with women in the Buganda region. More than three-quarters of Ugandan women achieved the minimum recommended four ANC visits during pregnancy; however, important disparities remain. Educational attainment and region of residence were the principal determinants of optimal ANC utilization at the population level. Efforts to improve maternal healthcare utilization should prioritize female education and strengthen region-specific maternal health strategies.

items.title: Detection and whole-genome characterisation of Regana virus in the bicoloured shrew (Crocidura leucodon) from Graubünden, Switzerland.
items.abstract: Orthonairoviruses are of medical and veterinary importance, but the genetic diversity and geographic distribution of shrew-associated orthonairoviruses remain unclear. Shrews are increasingly recognised as hosts for diverse orthonairoviruses, including Regana virus (REGV), which has been reported in the bicoloured white-toothed shrew (Crocidura leucodon) in Germany and the Czech Republic. We examined archived shrew specimens collected in Graubünden Canton, Switzerland, between 2005 and 2006 using nested reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction, metagenomic next-generation sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, pairwise sequence comparison, and protein feature annotation. Nairoviral RNA was detected in three C. leucodon from Luzein and Malans, whereas four Sorex araneus and one Neomys anomalus tested negative. Complete or near-complete REGV genome sequences were recovered from the three positive animals. Swiss REGV variants clustered with REGV from Germany and the Czech Republic across the S, M, and L segments. RdRp amino acid identities were 98.8-98.9% among Swiss variants and 92.1-95.6% between REGV Np12 and German or Czech variants. Comparative protein analyses identified conserved viral ovarian tumour protease catalytic residues, similar glycoprotein precursor organisations, and nairovirus-like nucleoprotein motifs. These findings document REGV in C. leucodon in Switzerland and expand the known geographical and genetic ranges of REGV in European shrew populations.

items.title: Values and trade-offs in responsible antibiotic behaviour and sustainable access: protocol for a comparative mixed-methods empirical ethics study in Sweden, Italy, and Bulgaria.
items.abstract: Antibiotic resistance arises through biological evolution but is also shaped by behavioural, sociocultural, and institutional factors. Promoting responsible antibiotic behaviour requires understanding how members of the public and relevant stakeholders perceive antibiotic use, stewardship, access, and responsibility, and the values and trade-offs that shape their decisions. This study aims to investigate these factors across three national contexts and to develop context-sensitive recommendations and a methodological framework for future research. This protocol describes an ongoing comparative mixed-methods empirical ethics study conducted in Sweden, Italy, and Bulgaria from May 2025 to April 2028. The study comprises three connected components: semi-structured online interviews with 16-20 participants from four stakeholder groups in each country; a general-population survey incorporating a discrete choice experiment, with a minimum of 350 respondents per country; and iterative normative analysis using reflective equilibrium. The 3D Value Framework informs the interviews, which examine stakeholders' reasoning about sustainable antibiotic access, stewardship, responsibility, and preparedness. Interview findings, relevant literature, and previous research will inform the survey attributes and scenarios. The survey will examine public preferences and trade-offs concerning antibiotic treatment, responsible behaviour, and sustainable access, alongside antibiotic knowledge, trust, prosociality, biospherism, gender-related perspectives, social norms, and values. The empirical findings will be interpreted in relation to ethical theories of justice and personal and collective responsibility. A One Health perspective informs the overall study. By bringing stakeholder reasoning and public preferences into dialogue with normative analysis, the study will examine how responsibility for preserving antibiotic effectiveness and sustainable access should be understood and distributed between individuals and institutional actors. It will also address the ethical implications of trade-offs between present and future access and the distribution of associated benefits and burdens. This empirical ethics approach is expected to support a context-sensitive account of justice and responsibility and to inform ethically justified antibiotic stewardship, policy, and communication. Not applicable.

items.title: Protocol for the GAPA person-centred dental care at home intervention: a substudy within a cluster randomised controlled trial in Swedish home care.
items.abstract: Oral health is essential to healthy ageing and closely linked to well-being, social participation, and quality of life. Frail older adults are at high risk of oral diseases, yet oral health is often insufficiently integrated into home care. Care staff frequently report limited competence and unclear routines, while older adults wish to participate actively in decisions about their oral health. GAPA Person-Centered Dental Care @ Home (Dental PCC@Home) is a co-designed model developed with older adults, significant others (informal caregivers), municipal care staff, and dental professionals. This substudy evaluates if Dental PCC@Home will promote oral health, participation, and self-determination among older adults living with complex care needs. Dental PCC@Home is embedded within the parent GAPA cluster randomised controlled trial. Decisions about dental care are guided by a patient decision aid and discussion of needs expressed by the older adult or identified by care staff. Participation in the substudy is voluntary. Eligible intervention-group participants are offered a patient decision aid to support decisions about whether and how to receive dental care, followed by one of four pathways: online dental consultation, mobile home dental care, a dental clinic visit, or declining dental care. Eligible control-group participants receive standard care. Oral health and quality-of-life assessments are conducted at baseline and at six and twelve months; cognitive function is assessed at baseline only. Co-primary outcomes are changes in oral health status (ROAG) and oral health-related quality of life (GOHAI) from baseline to twelve months. General health-related quality of life (EQ-5D-5 L) is a secondary outcome. Quantitative analyses will account for clustering and repeated measurements. Semi-structured interviews with older adults, significant others, and care staff will explore experiences of care, decision-making, and implementation and will be analysed using qualitative content analysis. This project will generate evidence on a new cross-organisational model designed to improve access to oral health care for frail older adults living at home. By integrating dental care into existing care processes and offering flexible care pathways, the model has the potential to strengthen autonomy, reduce inequalities, promote health and, when indicated, address oral diseases earlier in home care. The findings may inform future practice, policy development, and person-centred approaches to oral health in ageing populations. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06310798. Registered on March 13, 2024.

items.title: Mental Health Stigma in Primary Care: Association with Participation in a Behavioral Health Training Program.
items.abstract: Stigmatized attitudes toward behavioral health disorders among primary care providers (PCPs) remain a persistent barrier to the delivery of high-quality, equitable care. Reduced clinician stigma is essential to improving mental health access and patient outcomes. To evaluate whether participation in a structured behavioral health training program is associated with lower mental health stigma among PCPs, and to examine the association between stigma and the socioeconomic disadvantage of practice location. Cross-sectional observational study. The study included 154 licensed PCPs (MD, DO, NP, PA) from urban, suburban, and rural settings in the USA in 2024. The sample comprised 75 alumni of the Train New Trainers Primary Care Psychiatry Fellowship, a 1-year structured continuing educational program, and 79 non-alumni PCPs who had not completed a similar program. Participation in the Train New Trainers Primary Care Psychiatry Fellowship and practice location disadvantage, as measured by the Area Deprivation Index. Mental health stigma was assessed using the 15-item Opening Minds Stigma Scale for Health Care Providers, with subscales for attitude, disclosure and help-seeking, and social distance. PCPs who completed the fellowship reported significantly lower total stigma scores (p < 0.0001), less agreement with stigmatizing attitudes (p = 0.0002), and lower stigma related to disclosure and help-seeking (p = 0.0001) compared with non-alumni. Practice in socioeconomically underserved areas was not associated with differences in stigma levels. Participation in a targeted primary care-based behavioral health training program was associated with significantly lower mental health stigma among PCPs. These findings highlight the potential importance of behavioral health training as a factor associated with clinician attitudes and support further prospective research evaluating the impact of such programs.

items.title: Stakeholder Perceptions for the Development of Gabapentinoid Deprescribing Clinical Guideline: A Functional Role Theory Approach.
items.abstract: Gabapentinoids are increasingly prescribed for a range of indications, despite growing concerns about their long-term safety and limited evidence of effectiveness for off-label use. While deprescribing is a recognised strategy to mitigate medication-related harm, clear tapering guidance for gabapentinoids is lacking. To explore consumer and healthcare professional (HCP) perceptions of the need and scope of a gabapentinoid deprescribing clinical guideline. An exploratory qualitative study was conducted using semi-structured interviews. A total of 25 participants were interviewed, comprising 13 consumers and 12 HCPs (e.g. general practitioners, pharmacists, neurologists). Reflexive thematic analysis was applied, guided by functional role theory, to examine stakeholders' perceptions of their own and others' roles in gabapentinoid deprescribing and expectations, to inform subsequent guideline development. Gabapentinoid deprescribing was viewed by stakeholders as a holistic, system-wide activity involving not only prescribers but also allied health professionals. All stakeholders identified a need for guideline recommendations that reflect this complexity and inclusivity. Consumers experienced fragmented care, partly because both they and GPs were left to navigate the deprescribing process without formal guidance. HCPs identified divided responsibilities between prescribers initiating and those tasked with deprescribing, leading to subsequent challenges, particularly for GPs in managing long-term effects. HCPs valued promoting a 'prescribing continuum' over adopting dichotomous roles that separate prescribing from deprescribing. Consumers, including carers, expressed a desire to be central in both the development of guidelines and the process of deprescribing. Stakeholders articulated the need for a deprescribing guideline that addresses the realities of gabapentinoid use in practice. Gabapentinoid deprescribing guidelines should be co-designed with consumers and inclusive of diverse HCPs, addressing role ambiguity and supporting continuity of care. Consumers expressed desire to be actively involved in guideline development and HCPs recognised the need for coordinated care and shared accountability across the healthcare system.

items.title: Sleep position and sleep apnea in newborns.
items.abstract: Public health measures recommend that babies sleep supine, but at all other times of life this can worsen sleep apnea. To examine associations between infant sleep position and the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), we studied polysomnograms of neonates with repaired myelomeningocele, who are often positioned nonsupine during wound healing, and of neonates without congenital anomalies who were recovering in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). We evaluated sleep apnea severity, as reflected by the AHI, in different positions as recorded during polysomnograms from three cohort studies of infants in NICUs. Participants included 173 infants with myelomeningocele (multiple hospitals) and 88 NICU recovery infants across two single-center cohorts. The myelomeningocele cohort was subdivided by repair type (postnatal, open fetal, and fetoscopic surgery groups). We evaluated AHI in different sleep positions using generalized estimating equations to account for repeated measures. Among 261 neonates, AHI was similar between supine and nonsupine positions in the NICU recovery, postnatal myelomeningocele, and open fetal myelomeningocele groups (adjusted analyses, all p > 0.33). In contrast, the fetoscopic myelomeningocele group had substantially lower AHI when supine (7.94, 95% CI 4.95-12.75) compared to nonsupine (22.1, 95% CI 14.02-35.01; p < 0.001). Surprisingly, sleep apnea in neonates requiring NICU care may not be exacerbated by supine sleep, with possible exceptions in some specific conditions. Although we did not study healthy newborns, we speculate that obligate nasal breathing in neonates may protect against worsening of sleep apnea when supine. "Back to Sleep" remains life-saving and appears unlikely to increase sleep apnea risk. Public health measures to prevent SIDS recommend that babies sleep supine. The degree to which sleep position influences sleep apnea in infants is unclear. We had a unique opportunity to study the position dependence of sleep apnea for neonates in the NICU setting, who sometimes sleep in nonsupine positions. As studies at older ages widely show sleep apnea to be worse supine than nonsupine, we hypothesized that we would find the same in neonates. Study results suggest that sleep apnea severity in neonates who require NICU care is not exacerbated by supine sleep. "Back to Sleep" remains a life-saving intervention for infants upon discharge to home and, moreover, does not appear to increase risk for sleep apnea.

items.title: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Relationship Education Within a Nurse Home Visiting Program to Improve Mental Health and Prevent Substance Use Among First-Time, Low-Income Mothers.
items.abstract: To study home visiting programs augmented with relationship education addressing maternal depression (MD), substance use (SU), and self-harm ideation (SHI). We performed a secondary data analysis of a three-wave longitudinal randomized controlled trial of the Nurse-Family Partnership (NFP) program. In Oregon, 238 low-income, first-time pregnant mothers were randomized to a standard or augmented program where trained nurses integrated the Within My Reach curriculum and intimate partner violence screening and referral with the NFP workflow one-on-one at home visits. Nurses maintained good fidelity in the augmented program, tailored training to clients' immediate needs, and were advised not to share with the staff in the standard program. At pregnancy, 1-year, and 2-year follow-ups, research assistants interviewed mothers with the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (including an SHI item), Alcohol Use Disorder Identification Test, and Drug Abuse Screening Test. Multilevel models and generalized estimating equations with the wave-intervention interactions were performed for MD, SHI, and SU, adjusting for race/ethnicity, age, education level, and nativity status. Depressive symptoms (25%), SU (36%), and SHI (6%, 7%, 9% across 3 waves) were common. Compared with the standard program, the augmented program indicated a stable romantic relationship with the child's father (66% vs. 50%, p = 0.01) and reduced depressive symptoms at the 1-year follow-up (p = 0.02) but did not reduce depressive symptoms, SHI, or SU over the two years. The findings can guide pragmatic research identifying mechanisms of change and integrating partner engagement, co-parenting, and targeted approaches to depression, SHI and SU into real-world home visiting services. items.title: Racial and Ethnic Disparities in Stroke Among Hypertensive Adults by Antihypertensive Medication Use in the United States.
items.abstract: Despite improvements in hypertension management, racial and ethnic disparities in stroke persist. Whether intervention intensity modifies stroke disparities remains unclear. We analyzed 10,005 adults aged ≥ 20 years with hypertension in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey from March 2013 to March 2020. Stroke history was self-reported. Antihypertensive therapy was categorized as untreated, monotherapy, or combination therapy. Multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical variables and included a race/ethnicity × medication group interaction term. Outcomes were reported as odds ratios (OR) and accompanying 95% confidence intervals (CI). 5% of the studied population reported a history of stroke. After full adjustment, current smoking (OR = 1.80, 95% CI 1.27-2.56), history of cardiovascular disease (OR = 2.38, 95% CI 1.70-3.35), and Medicaid insurance (OR = 3.06, 95% CI 1.40-6.68) were independently associated with stroke. Descriptive differences in stroke prevalence varied across race/ethnicity and antihypertensive medication categories; however, the race/ethnicity x medication interaction was not statistically significant (p = 0.346). Among untreated participants, predicted stroke prevalence was 3.5% in Black participants and 2.8% in White participants, compared to 7.0% and 6.8%, respectively, among those receiving combination therapy. Compared with White participants, Asian participants demonstrated lower odds of stroke on combination therapy (adjusted OR 0.23, 95% CI 0.06-0.96) compared with untreated individuals (adjusted OR 0.49, 95% CI 0.22-1.09). Hispanic participants demonstrated lower odds of stroke relative to White participants across medication categories (adjusted OR = 0.57, 95% CI 0.37-0.90 combination therapy vs. adjusted OR = 0.66, 95% CI 0.48-0.92 untreated). Stroke prevalence differed by race/ethnicity and antihypertensive medication category; however, no statistically significant evidence was found that treatment intensity modified racial/ethnic disparities. Larger longitudinal studies incorporating blood pressure control, medication adherence, and hypertension severity are needed to better understand the relationship between antihypertensive treatment intensity and racial/ethnic differences in stroke risk.

items.title: Genetic subtyping of MASLD reveals a glucose-lowering axis linked to GCKR alternative splicing.
items.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a global metabolic condition with a complex relationship to type 2 diabetes. Yet human genetic studies suggest the existence of a MASLD subtype with favourable glycaemic effects, raising a clinically important question: how can hepatic steatosis coexist with improved glycaemic outcomes? We aimed to determine whether MASLD comprises genetically distinct subtypes with divergent glycaemic consequences, and to define the genetic basis of a glucose-lowering MASLD subtype. We integrated genetic and triglyceride-related metabolomic profiles to cluster 18 established MASLD-associated variants and construct mutually adjusted partitioned polygenic risk scores (PRSs) in the UK Biobank. We tested associations with hepatic biomarkers, liver outcomes and type 2 diabetes, and replicated glycaemic findings in an independent Chinese cohort (the Taizhou Longitudinal Study [TZL]). We prioritised candidate loci using colocalisation and fine-mapping and performed allele-specific functional assays and structural modelling to investigate the underlying mechanism at the lead locus. Partitioned PRSs revealed bidirectional glycaemic axes: one PRS lowered fasting glucose and type 2 diabetes risk, whereas the remaining PRSs increased both, despite all associating with higher liver injury markers and adverse liver outcomes. The divergent glycaemic effects were replicated in the TZL. To pinpoint the genetic basis of the glucose-lowering axis, colocalisation and fine-mapping prioritised GCKR rs1260326 (C>T) as a shared MASLD-type 2 diabetes signal and the lead cis-pQTL for circulating glucokinase regulatory protein (GKRP). Functional experiments showed that the rs1260326 T allele promotes exon-15 skipping in GCKR, reduces the abundance of full-length GKRP and yields a truncated protein. In silico structural modelling suggested that the truncated GKRP isoform may have reduced binding affinity for glucokinase, although this predicted effect requires experimental validation. MASLD comprises genetically distinct subtypes with opposing glycaemic and type 2 diabetes risk profiles. Within the glucose-lowering subtype, rs1260326-mediated alternative splicing of GCKR provides a potential mechanistic link to reduced GKRP abundance and glycaemic protection. These findings support a more granular view of MASLD heterogeneity and may inform future subtype-specific risk stratification and prevention.

items.title: Paediatric Nurses' Experiences of Grief in Palliative and End-of-Life Care: A Qualitative Study.
items.abstract: To explore Australian nurses' experiences of grief in paediatric palliative and end-of-life care, its impact on professional practice and their utilisation of supports. Qualitative Interpretive description study. In-depth, semi-structured, online interviews were conducted with ten Australian nurses experienced in palliative and end-of-life care in paediatrics. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed and analysed using constant comparative thematic analysis. The COREQ checklist guided reporting. Six interconnected themes were identified, reflecting the evolving and pervasive experience of grief: 'exposure to grief'; 'impact on personal life'; 'impact on professional role'; 'coping with grief'; 'workplace supports'; and 'reflection, growth and adaptation'. Findings suggest that grief is an under-recognised psychosocial phenomenon and potential occupational hazard in paediatric palliative and end-of-life care. Nurses valued informal supports, including peer support and compassionate leadership, more than formal debriefing. Barriers to organisational support persisted, yet many nurses reported increased resilience and growth through reflection. Grief is an intrinsic yet often overlooked aspect of paediatric end-of-life care. Context-sensitive, individualised supports and compassionate leadership can foster openness and reflection, recognising grief as both a natural process and potential occupational hazard and support nurses' resilience and long-term wellbeing. Acknowledging grief as a potential occupational hazard and psychosocial phenomenon requires organisational accountability and a systemic approach at leadership and policy levels. This aligns with clinical governance standards and occupational health principles while affirming nurses' right to emotional safety at work. When supported through compassionate leadership and open emotional dialogue, grief may become a source of personal and professional learning and resilience. By acknowledging nurses' experience of grief, this study highlights the need for formal adjustments in policy frameworks, supervision and education at all levels to ensure safety, quality and staff support through competencies in grief and trauma management. The authors followed the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ). No patient or public contribution was made.

items.title: Effect of non-surgical periodontal treatment on platelet activation in patients with periodontitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Platelets of the patients with periodontitis were seen to be hyper- reactive and formed more platelet- leukocyte complexes. It is unknown if improved periodontal condition affects platelet activation. Hence, the objective of this systematic review and meta - analysis was to pool the available data and explore the effect of non- surgical periodontal treatment on platelet activation. The systematic review and meta - analysis was registered with the PROSPERO with the registration number-CRD42024623817. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs), Quasi-experimental, Cohort and Case-control studies evaluating the effect of periodontal treatment on platelet activation among individuals with periodontitis were included. A systematic search was carried out on 5 major databases. Cochrane's ROB tool was used for quality assessment of the RCTs. Database search yielded 321 studies, among which 162 were from Embase, 49 from PubMed, 59 from Scopus and 51 from Web of Science. Seven studies met the inclusion criteria and were therefore included. 2 studies with common interventions and outcomes at 3 months were used for meta - analysis. Pooled P-selectin levels were similar before and after non-surgical periodontal treatment (mean difference 17.1; 95% CI [-25.11, 59.31]), with very low certainty. Within limits of our review, the available evidence regarding the effect of non-surgical periodontal treatment on platelet activation remains limited and uncertain.

items.title: Cardiovascular disease in diabetes mellitus: beyond atherosclerosis and heart failure.
items.abstract: The global burden of diabetes mellitus continues to grow, now affecting one in nine adults. In people with diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, and considerable focus has been placed on reducing the incidence of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and heart failure over the past few decades. Due to reductions in the prevalence of some major risk factors, improved control of other risk factors and improved therapeutic agents, mortality attributed to atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease has declined. Meanwhile, the decline in mortality attributed to heart failure has stalled. However, beyond atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and heart failure, many other cardiovascular diseases are responsible for morbidity and mortality. We provide a comprehensive narrative summary of the association between diabetes mellitus and the most common cardiovascular diseases as reported by the 2023 Global Burden of Disease study. The evidence indicates that diabetes mellitus is a risk factor for atrial fibrillation, infective endocarditis, hypertensive heart disease, intracerebral haemorrhage and aortic stenosis. We also discuss the available evidence for the effects of incretin hormone mimetics, such as glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists, and of sodium/glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors for each of these cardiovascular diseases. This Review underscores the multifaceted link between cardiovascular disease and diabetes mellitus, highlighting that integrated strategies are required to effectively reduce the global burden of both conditions.

items.title: Heterogeneity of microbiome responses to menopausal hormone therapy among perimenopausal women.
items.abstract: Menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) alleviates climacteric symptoms, yet its microbiome-wide effects and efficacy determinants remain unclear. Here we show that oral estradiol/dydrogesterone, given for 6 months to 356 perimenopausal women, improved neuroendocrine, metabolic and symptom outcomes and induced site-specific microbial remodeling. Vaginocervical and urinary niches showed the most pronounced restructuring, with moderate oral and minimal gut changes. MHT increased vaginocervical Lactobacillus crispatus and reduced Gardnerella vaginalis. Higher baseline vaginocervical L. crispatus predicted greater postintervention vaginocervical and urinary colonization and superior Female Sexual Function Index improvement. Baseline vaginocervical community types determined differential outcomes: G. vaginalis-dominated individuals shifted most toward healthier communities, whereas diversified individuals improved least. MHT efficacy also varied according to baseline gut community type: Phocaeicola vulgatus-dominated women exhibited greater hormonal responsiveness, superior clinical outcomes and were more likely to achieve 4-week rapid clinical remission than Prevotella copri-dominated women. These findings support a precision MHT framework integrating gut and vaginocervical community typing for personalized care. Chictr.org.cn ID: ChiCTR2100049768 .

items.title: Development and validation of a questionnaire on food knowledge and perception of the Mediterranean diet: the ICARO food knowledge questionnaire.
items.abstract: Adherence to the Mediterranean diet has significantly declined over the last decades, particularly among younger generations, due to socioeconomic factors, increased consumption of ultra-processed foods and limited awareness of its positive effects on health. Addressing these barriers necessitates the enhancement of nutritional education and improved access to healthy food options. This study aims to develop and validate a comprehensive questionnaire, the ICARO-Food Knowledge Questionnaire (I-FKQ), to assess food knowledge related to the Mediterranean diet among children, adolescents, and adults. In the context of the ICARO Study, we recruited a sample of 46 parents (for children), 111 adolescents, and 164 adults, from November 2023 to July 2024. Content validity was established through a review by an expert panel, which refined the questionnaire. Assessments of face validity indicated that the I-FKQ is manageable and user-friendly for online administration. Item analysis demonstrated acceptable difficulty and discrimination indices. High test-retest reliability was observed, with strong correlations in scores between the two testing occasions, indicating robust temporal stability. All constructs of the questionnaire demonstrated adequate Cronbach's α and Pearson's correlation coefficients. The overall internal consistency of the questionnaire was acceptable (Cronbach's α = 0.848), although Section 2 showed slightly lower reliability (Cronbach's α = 0.662). Construct validity, evaluated only in adults, was supported by expected differences in scores according to educational level. The I-FKQ demonstrated satisfactory overall psychometric properties and reliable temporal stability. However, while fundamental reliability and face validity parameters were confirmed across multiple age groups, construct validity was established exclusively within the adult population. This specific lack of structural validation currently restricts the full applicability of the instrument in pediatric and adolescent groups. Consequently, pending further psychometric evaluation in younger demographics, the I-FKQ is best suited to support educational and public health initiatives targeting adult populations.

items.title: Loss to follow-up in people living with HIV in Spain: Early disengagement, migrant status, and detectable viral load.
items.abstract: Loss to follow up (LTFU) among people living with HIV is a major clinical and public health challenge, as it is associated with increased risk of onward transmission and higher mortality. Understanding the characteristics of people who are lost to follow-up is essential to improve continuity of care and inform targeted retention strategies. We conducted a retrospective observational study in the Infectious Diseases Unit of Hospital Clínico Universitario de San Juan (Alicante, Spain). We included 209 adults diagnosed with HIV since 2016 and recorded sociodemographic, clinical and virological variables. LTFU was defined, according to GeSIDA criteria, as the absence of clinical visits for ≥12 months. We used bivariate analyses, multivariable logistic regression, and Kaplan-Meier curves to explore factors associated with LTFU and estimate time to LTFU. Overall, 23.9% of patients (n=50) were LTFU. Compared with retained patients, those LTFU were younger (30.5 vs 34.0 years; p=0.016), more frequently of non-Spanish nationality (29.8% vs 14.1%; p=0.010) and less likely to have a stable partner (12.3% vs 29.2%; p=0.008). Detectable viral load at the last visit was the variable most strongly associated with LTFU (52.4% vs 16.5%; p<0.001). In the multivariable model, non-Spanish nationality (OR 2.84; 95% CI 1.21-6.62; p=0.016) and detectable viral load (OR 5.90; 95% CI 2.40-12.50; p<0.001) remained independently associated with a higher odds of LTFU. The probability of remaining in care at 1, 3 and 5 years was 86.0%, 74.5% and 70.2%, respectively. The LTFU rate in our cohort is comparable to that reported in similar high-income settings. Younger age, non-Spanish origin and detectable viral load at last visit were associated with a higher likelihood of LTFU, with a substantial proportion of events occurring early after entry into care. These findings identify young people of non-Spanish nationality with detectable viraemia as a priority group for targeted HIV retention interventions.

items.title: Acral melanoma: a unique subtype requiring unique solutions.
items.abstract: Acral melanoma (AM) is a 'rare-by-rare' melanoma subtype arising on the volar skin of the palms, soles, or nail apparatus. Unlike sun-exposed cutaneous melanoma (CM), AM has a low mutational burden but extensive structural genomic alterations, including clustered copy number events ('hailstorms'/tyfonas) that contain amplification of oncogenes such as CCND1 and TERT. Mechanical stress and distinct clonal evolution, with late, often subclonal, MAPK mutations, may mediate AM development and progression. Nevertheless, AM management is largely extrapolated from CM. Benefits of immunotherapy and targeted therapies remain unclear due to limited trial enrollment and under-representation of diverse patient populations. In this review, we integrate current knowledge with critical challenges in AM research and outline priorities to accelerate AM-specific discoveries and treatments, close critical knowledge gaps, and improve patient outcomes through global collaboration.

items.title: Pharyngotonsillitis, aphthous stomatitis, and adenitis precede familial Mediterranean fever by two decades.
items.abstract: Familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) and periodic fever, aphthous stomatitis, pharyngitis, and cervical adenitis (PFAPA) syndrome share innate-immune features, but population-level data on oropharyngeal morbidity before FMF recognition are lacking. To examine the magnitude, timing, specificity, and treatment burden of a PFAPA-like oropharyngeal phenotype in patients later diagnosed with FMF. Population-based matched case-control study in Leumit Health Services, Israel. FMF patients with colchicine dispensing (n = 3324) were matched 1:4 by birth year and sex to 13,296 controls. Oropharyngeal diagnoses, tonsil/adenoid surgery, antibiotic dispensing, and ear, nose, and throat (ENT) visits were compared across windows up to 20 and 10 years before diagnosis (30-day blackout), using streptococcal, hypertrophy, and non-ENT negative controls with false discovery rate (FDR) adjustment. A PFAPA diagnostic code was recorded in 2.6% of FMF patients versus 0.1% of controls (odds ratio [OR] 25.4, 95% confidence interval 14.3-48.5). Up to 20 years before diagnosis, future FMF patients had more acute tonsillitis (35.6% vs. 27.2%; OR 1.48, 1.37-1.61), viral-labeled tonsillitis (OR 2.65), oral aphthae (OR 1.72), and cervical lymphadenitis (OR 1.62; all q < 0.05); associations persisted after diagnosis. Streptococcal sore-throat coding was not increased (lifelong OR 1.03, 0.94-1.14). Antibiotic dispensing and ENT visits were increased; tonsillectomy alone was more frequent (OR 2.51), although surgical comparisons did not survive FDR correction. FMF is associated with a non-streptococcal, PFAPA-like oropharyngeal phenotype detectable years before diagnosis. Recurrent pharyngotonsillitis with aphthae or cervical adenitis, without demonstrated streptococcal disease, may be a clinical cue to consider FMF in at-risk populations.

items.title: Distinct DAXX effector modules separate H3.3 nucleosome assembly from ERV repression.
items.abstract: Endogenous retroviruses (ERVs) can compromise genome integrity when expressed, and cells have evolved chromatin-based pathways to repress their transcription. The histone H3.3 chaperone DAXX localizes to a subset of ERVs embedded in KAP1-SETDB1-associated heterochromatin and contributes to their repression. Here, we define distinct DAXX determinants that support H3.3 deposition versus ERV repression. Using complementary biochemical and genetic approaches, we identify a conserved basic patch within the DAXX histone-binding domain that engages DNA, promotes H3.3 nucleosome assembly in vitro, and is required for H3.3 enrichment at DAXX-bound ERVs in cells. Despite failure to deposit H3.3, DAXX with substitutions in this basic patch retains localization to ERVs and preserves repression, indicating that H3.3 deposition is dispensable for DAXX-dependent ERV repression. In contrast, disruption of the DAXX C-terminal SUMO-interacting motif impairs DAXX-dependent ERV repression and SUMO-dependent effector engagement, including MORC3 recruitment. These findings define separable outputs downstream from DAXX recruitment, uncoupling nucleosome assembly from ERV repression and placing SUMO-dependent effector engagement within the broader KAP1-SETDB1-centered ERV repression network.

items.title: Factors associated with HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis awareness and use among women aged 40-65 years in South East England: an analysis of the 'Health Counts 2024' survey.
items.abstract: HIV diagnoses are increasing among women in the UK. Granular data on midlife women's (women aged 40-65 years) knowledge about, and access to HIV Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP), an effective chemoprophylactic strategy for HIV, is lacking. Data from a 2024 population health survey of an English city (Brighton & Hove) were analysed to describe the sexual health behaviours of midlife women (cis and transgender), and to investigate whether sociodemographic and/ or sexual behaviour factors were associated with PrEP awareness and use. Among the 3,335 midlife women, 30.4% (1,013) were aware of PrEP and 1.2% (12) had used or were using PrEP. Poor PrEP awareness was associated with older age; heterosexual identity; not living with a long term physical or mental health condition; Asian or Asian British ethnicity; not having received a university-level education; having had fewer sexual partners and never having had an HIV test. National disaggregation of the sociodemographic and sexual behaviour associations with PrEP awareness among midlife women, and an understanding of how this translates to PrEP use is required to enable better targeting of HIV prevention interventions.

items.title: Psychotropic Polypharmacy in the Texas Department of Criminal Justice.
items.abstract: Psychotropic polypharmacy can result in adverse effects, but its application in correctional settings is poorly understood. We assessed rates of psychotropic polypharmacy in the Texas Department of Criminal Justice (TDCJ), the largest U.S. state prison system. This retrospective cohort study included all individuals incarcerated in TDCJ in 2022 and 2023. International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) codes and prescriptions were extracted from electronic medical records. Outcomes were the proportions of people with depressive, bipolar, and schizophrenia spectrum disorders prescribed zero, one, two, three, or four or more psychotropic medications. Among people with depressive disorders (N = 14,903), the percentages of persons prescribed zero, one, two, three, and at least four medications were 16.8, 36.8, 33.3, 10.5, and 2.5, respectively. For bipolar disorders (N = 7,139), the percentages were 14.4, 19.1, 39.6, 20.4, and 6.4. For schizophrenia spectrum disorders (N = 9,421), the percentages were 8.6, 21.5, 42.9, 20.9, and 6.0. Within each diagnostic category, differences in frequencies of polypharmacy were statistically significant (p < .001). Multivariable logistic regression (odds ratio (OR), 95% confidence interval (CI)) found that individuals with bipolar disorders (2.40, 2.25-2.56), schizophrenia spectrum disorders (2.81, 2.65-2.98), two concurrent disorders (3.48, 3.10-3.90), and three concurrent disorders (4.48, 2.62-7.63) had increased odds of being prescribed multiple medications compared with those with depressive disorders. In conclusion, psychotropic polypharmacy was prevalent in Texas prisons. Further research is needed to determine appropriate levels of polypharmacy in this setting.

items.title: From vaccines to vaccination: Recognizing the social domain of vaccinology.
items.abstract: Vaccinology has expanded considerably in recent decades through new platforms, delivery technologies, regulatory science and applications beyond infectious diseases. Most of this growth has followed one direction, enlarging the range of products and targets included in vaccine science. This commentary argues that a second direction of expansion deserves explicit recognition: from the vaccine as a biomedical product to vaccination as a social practice. Alongside basic vaccinology, which asks whether a vaccine works, and programmatic vaccinology, which asks whether vaccination can be delivered, social vaccinology asks how vaccination interacts with society, including institutions, policies, public trust and public discourse. The idea has deep roots. The early formulations of the discipline by Bruce Dull in 1971 and by Jonas and Darrell Salk between 1977 and 1984 already included the technical, administrative and social aspects of vaccination programs, and the term social vaccinology was proposed in 2012. Recent experiences with HPV vaccination in Japan and with childhood immunization policy in the United States show how vaccination outcomes depend on this domain, and work on vaccine hesitancy and communication points in the same direction. Recognizing social vaccinology within the field would have implications for research agendas, the training of vaccinologists and scientific publishing.

items.title: A Bayesian Optimized Biquad Filter-Burg Model for Real-Time EEG Phase Estimation
items.abstract: Real-time phase estimation on stimulus-aligned transient EEG is critical for closed-loop neuromodulation systems targeting the theta-band, yet most real-time phase estimation methods have been developed and validated on resting-state, high-fidelity signals in the alpha band. Recent work has pursued deep learning architectures, while individualized classical bandpass filter tuning remains underexplored. This study characterizes the spectral and temporal properties of non-anticipative bandpass filtering and demonstrates the performance gains achieved through individualized tuning. We present a Bayesian-Optimized Biquad Filter-Burg (BOB) model evaluated on EEG recorded during peripheral vibrotactile stimulation of the left median nerve (theta, N=20 healthy subjects) and on resting-state recordings from the Max Planck Institute's LEMON dataset (alpha, N=20 healthy subjects). BOB was benchmarked against the Deep Dual-Branch Complex Neural Network (DBCNN), EEG Phase Prediction Network (EPN), Phastimate, and Phase Estimation with Autoregressive Padding (PEAP) under matched testing conditions: channel selection, individualized optimization, evaluation time points, and an offline reference phase obtained through zero-phase filtering and the Hilbert transform. Under these testing conditions, BOB achieved matched or better performance than these models at a fraction of the calibration time.

items.title: The impact of M dwarf stellar convection on exoplanetary atmospheric signatures. A 3D radiation-hydrodynamics simulation analysis for high-resolution spectroscopy
items.abstract: M dwarf stars represent prime targets for the detection and characterization of small, temperate exoplanets; however, their complex activity and convective surfaces pose significant challenges for high-resolution spectroscopic studies. This work aims to investigate the impact of stellar convection on high-resolution spectroscopic observations of M dwarf stars and develop an integrated approach combining 3D radiative hydrodynamical simulations, spectroscopic modeling, and transit analysis to mitigate stellar noise. We employ 3D radiative hydrodynamical simulations of M dwarf stellar convection to generate synthetic spectra. We compare the synthetic spectra to actual observations of GJ 3470. We model a high-resolution transit sequence of the Neptune-size GJ 3470 b, including centre-to-limb variations (CLVs) and the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect (RME), and process the sequence via principal component analysis (PCA) to de-trend stellar effects. Comparison of synthetic spectra with actual observations shows that current H2O line lists remain inaccurate, with modest agreement in line strength and position for the chosen K-band interval. During the transit of GJ 3470 b, the amplitude of CLVs+RME is comparable to exoplanet signals. Current PCA can in principle de-trend such effects, but its behaviour is highly dependent on the copresence of telluric and planetary signals. While we are able to correctly detect the exoplanet with no evident bias from stellar residuals, this result is limited to a narrow spectral interval and a specific orbital configuration. This study demonstrates that 3D radiative hydrodynamical simulations are essential for accurately modeling convection-induced spectral variability in M dwarfs. Our integrated framework establishes a foundation to obtain unbiased measurements from future ELT observations of exoplanets orbiting M dwarfs.

items.title: Constraining Ganymede's Interior Structure and Bulk Composition from Its Present-Day Magnetic Field Strength
items.abstract: Ganymede is the only Solar System satellite with a global magnetic field driven by a core dynamo. Although its small moment-of-inertia (MoI) factor indicates a differentiated structure of a metallic core, rocky mantle, and outer hydrosphere, its exact bulk composition and layer thicknesses remain highly uncertain. We developed a comprehensive, long-term thermochemical evolution model that couples thermal history with magnetic field generation. Building upon previous theoretical frameworks, this study systematically evaluates how diverse chondritic precursor compositions constrain Ganymede's internal thermochemical evolution and core solidification processes. Based on interior structures initially permitted by a wide range of chondritic compositions and geodetic constraints, we applied the observed equatorial surface magnetic field strength ($\sim$719 nT) as a dynamic filter. Our evolutionary simulations demonstrate that while magnetic dynamos can operate under entire melting, Fe-snow, and FeS-layer regimes, the requirement to sustain the observed field strength strongly restricts the viable interior models. Satisfying this constraint preferentially requires a relatively large core radius and a specific, non-eutectic bulk core sulfur concentration. Consequently, this coupled thermochemical approach highlights the main novelty of this study: characterizing the hydrosphere's density serves as an independent constraint to break the structural degeneracy of Ganymede's bulk composition. Our model indicates that L and CI chondrites yield parameter spaces capable of sustaining comparable field strengths under a low-density hydrosphere scenario (1,200 kg m-3), whereas the H chondrite composition can satisfy this criterion under a high-density scenario (1,300 kg m-3). These predictions provide a critical framework to be tested by the JUICE mission arriving in 2031.

items.title: On the Detectability of Compact Multi-Planet Systems via Gravitational Microlensing
items.abstract: Compact multi-planet systems orbiting ultracool dwarfs, such as TRAPPIST-1, may be a major population of terrestrial worlds with poorly constrained demographics. Individual close-in planets are expected to escape microlensing detection, but whether a compact system can produce a detectable collective signal remains to be quantified. We calculate the microlensing signal from each TRAPPIST-1 planet, and of all seven combined, if the system were a lens toward the bulge. For a 0.09 $M_\odot$ lens at 4 kpc, $R_E \approx 1.21$ AU, placing the planets at $s = 0.010$--$0.051~θ_E$, 12--63 times interior to the lensing zone. We measure each signal as the residual after fitting a single-lens model, which accounts for the barycentric dipole. Because the quadrupole term cancels between the two images to first order, the residual scales as the octupole ($q s^3$), reaching $|δA / A| \sim 10^{-6}$. The seven planets combined yield $Δχ^2 \sim 10^{-3}$ even at 1~mmag precision, five orders of magnitude below the standard detection threshold. Detection requires increasing all planet masses by a factor of $\sim$300, whereas the resonant chain loses its guarantee of Hill stability at a factor of $\sim$7. Only a lens within $\sim$15 pc of the source or the Sun places the outer planets in the lensing zone. The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is therefore not expected to detect a TRAPPIST-1-like system through microlensing, whereas its transit channel in the same fields can detect such planets in large numbers, marking a sharp boundary in the Galactic census between microlensing and transit sensitivity.

items.title: Missing Outer Rings in the exoALMA Sample: Physical Mechanisms Suppressing Dust Ring Formation Despite Strong Pressure Bumps
items.abstract: The exoALMA survey has revealed candidate gas pressure bumps at radii beyond the observed millimetre continuum discs in several protoplanetary systems, raising the question of whether these regions could host undetected dust structures. We investigate this for nine of the exoALMA discs by reconstructing gas surface density profiles from midplane pressure gradient measurements derived from $^{12}$CO and $^{13}$CO ALMA Band 7 observations. We evolve the dust using DustPy across a grid of turbulence and fragmentation parameters ($α\in \{10^{-4}, 10^{-3}\}$; $v_\mathrm{frag} \in \{1, 10\}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$), followed by radiative transfer calculations with RADMC-3D to give predictions for the continuum emission. We find that the dominant outcome across the explored parameter space is efficient outer dust trapping, leading to prominent outer continuum rings that should be detectable at ALMA Band 7, in tension with the observations. The $^{13}$CO-based reconstructions almost universally produce detectable outer rings, whereas the $^{12}$CO-based reconstructions show more variation. We further test delayed formation of the outer pressure bump and enhanced outer-disc turbulence as possible suppression mechanisms of ring formation. Enhanced turbulence weakens the predicted outer continuum emission most effectively, although the efficiency of the mechanism depends on the system explored and on where the turbulence transition is placed. Delayed bump formation generally does not prevent rapid outer dust accumulation.

items.title: From Earth's Harshest Landscapes to Lunar Horizons: Engineering NEA Telescopes for Extreme Environments
items.abstract: Near-Earth Asteroids (NEAs) represent both a scientific opportunity and a potential threat to human civilization. While current survey programs have successfully detected most large NEAs, a significant observational gap remains for objects smaller than approximately 140 m, which can still produce regional-scale devastation. Ground-based surveys are intrinsically limited by atmospheric conditions, weather, and solar avoidance constraints, which leave a significant fraction of near-Sun objects difficult to detect. In particular, Earth-based observatories remain largely blind to objects approaching from the Sun-ward direction, reducing available warning times. Future lunar observatories offer a promising solution to this limitation. A telescope operating on the Moon could enable observations of regions inaccessible from Earth, provide enhanced sensitivity, and significantly improve early detection capabilities. However, the lunar environment imposes severe engineering constraints, including thermal cycling, dust contamination, radiation exposure, and autonomous operation requirements. We propose the AMAS(Atacama-Mongolia-Antarctica-Sahara) project, an international initiative using Earth's most extreme environments as analogue sites for future lunar astronomical facilities. By deploying and testing specialized NEA survey telescopes in these environments, key technologies for future lunar observatories can be validated under realistic operational conditions. This paper presents the scientific rationale, engineering challenges, site selection strategy, and long-term roadmap toward a global Earth-Moon network for planetary defense.

items.title: Up in smoke: carbon-destruction in the terrestrial planet-forming region of a young Class I disk
items.abstract: Earth's surface and deep mantle are strongly depleted in carbon compared to the Sun. Sublimation of solid carbonaceous material in the inner midplanes of young disks could cause this depletion. We study such thermal processing in HOPS-68, a Class I protostar with a rich hydrocarbon spectrum. A companion paper has shown that it is recondensing refractory dust from a hot inner disk region, and that oxygen-bearing species are tracing a warm (300-500 K) molecular layer entrained in a disk-wind. In this work, we analyze the carbon species in the JWST spectrum of this source using local thermal equilibrium slab models. We detect warm (~400 K) HCN and C2H2 at the base of a disk wind, as well as colder (~40 K) C4H2, CH3, and CS in the outer disk or outflow cavity wall. Additionally, 13CCH2, CH4, and C6H2 are detected, while ALMA observations reveal C2H tracing the outflow cavity walls. We suggest that in a "refractory carbon destruction zone" in the inner disk, carbon-bearing species are released from the grains, possibly contributing to the observed carbon depletion of Earth. The disk wind then redistributes carbon carried by HCN and C2H2 from the inner disk to the colder outer disk, where UV-induced gas-phase reactions with C2H in the outflow cavity walls could produce the aliphatic carbon chains seen. This result implies that the Warm Carbon Chain Chemistry (WCCC, e.g. N. Sakai & S. Yamamoto 2013) might trace outflows rather than infall. The formation of aliphatic chains in the disk wind could promote the abundant aliphatic organics found in meteorites and asteroids.

items.title: Galaxy Luminosity Function of the Coma Cluster from Deep u ′ − g ′ − r ′ Wendelstein Imaging Data
items.abstract: Abstract We derive the g ′ -band galaxy luminosity function (GLF) of quenched resolved galaxies in the Coma cluster from a deep-imaging survey with ≈1.5 deg 2 around the cluster center. The data set comprises deep u ′ -, g ′ -, and r ′ -band data obtained with the Wendelstein Wide Field Imager on the 2.1 m Fraunhofer Wendelstein Telescope reaching median 3 σ surface brightness limits in 10″ × 10″ boxes of ( 30.0 u ′ , 29.6 g ′ , 28.7 r ′ ) mag arcsec − 2 . We measure structural parameters across a large dynamic range in galaxy brightness ( − 24.5 g ′ mag ⪅ M ⪅ − 11.3 g ′ mag ), from the brightest cluster galaxy to low-luminosity dwarfs, including compact dwarf galaxies and ultradiffuse galaxies. We automatically identify more than 6000 cluster member candidates based on their membership on the quiescent sequence in the u ′ − g ′ versus g ′ − r ′ color–color diagram. The structural parameters of bright galaxies are obtained via isophotal modeling, and fully automated parametric image fitting for faint ones. Injection-recovery tests and two identically analyzed reference fields provide statistical corrections for completeness and contamination, yielding a representative GLF that reliably probes the faint end and may serve as a benchmark for future studies. items.title: Development of a biopsychosocial hybrid intervention to support patients following a complex lower-limb trauma : the PROMOTE study.
items.abstract: Aims Complex lower-limb trauma is associated with substantial long-term physical and psychological morbidity. Access to integrated psychological support remains inconsistent. This study describes the development of Pain Rehabilitation to Optimize Major Orthopaedic Trauma REcovery (PROMOTE), a theory-based, hybrid (website plus one-to-one support) biopsychosocial intervention. Methods Development followed the Medical Research Council framework for complex interventions and is reported in accordance with the GUIDance for the rEporting of intervention Development (GUIDED) checklist. This included: 1) an evidence review to identify modifiable psychosocial risk factors and theoretical models; 2) content coproduction with an expert advisory group including multidisciplinary clinicians and patient representatives, alongside independent patient interviews; and 3) iterative development and user testing of a low-intensity, scalable intervention. The intervention integrates the Common-Sense Model of Self-Regulation with cognitive behavioural therapy. Results PROMOTE comprises four brief healthcare professional contact sessions delivered over eight weeks and an interactive, personalized website. The website is structured into five sections: 1) psychoeducation about the injury, pain, stress, and recovery; 2) cognitive behavioural techniques; 3) coping strategies; 4) recovery planning; and 5) a personalized profile. Content includes multimedia resources, interactive exercises, and personalized feedback. Iterative feedback from patients and clinicians led to improvements in navigation, language, pacing, and engagement. Conclusion PROMOTE is a coproduced, theory-informed, scalable biopsychosocial intervention designed to address unmet psychological needs following complex lower-limb trauma. The intervention was evaluated in a feasibility randomized controlled trial to assess acceptability and engagement.

items.abstract: Retrospective cohort study to investigate which factors most reliably distinguish incidental GAD65-antibodies (iGAD65) from true GAD65-antibody neurological disease (tGAD65). 167 adults with positive serum and CSF GAD65-antibodies (> 0.02 nmol/L by radioimmunoassay) were classified as tGAD65 or iGAD65, with diagnostic performance of paraclinical parameters compared in discovery and validation cohorts. items.title: Impacts of mutation accumulation and order on tumor initiation revealed by engineered murine colorectal cancer organoids.
items.abstract: Tumorigenesis typically follows a multi-hit trajectory, driven by accumulating oncogenic mutations. Colorectal cancer (CRC) has long served as a paradigmatic model of multi-hit tumorigenesis, characterized by adenoma-carcinoma transition accompanied by acquisition of specific oncogene and tumor suppressor mutations. However, how the temporal order of early mutations influences CRC initiation remains poorly understood. To address this, we established a CRC tumorigenesis model using murine intestinal organoids. By introducing defined combinations of key CRC driver mutations ( Kras , Apc , and Trp53 ) in distinct orders, we systematically investigated how the order of mutation accumulation affects tumor initiation. Our results reveal that the mutation accumulation confers growth advantages in both in vitro and in vivo models. Strikingly, mutation order also influenced the tumorigenic properties of the organoids. Whereas organoids with Trp53 loss before or after Apc loss similarly affected organoid phenotypes in vitro or tumorigenicity in immunodeficient mice, organoids with Trp53 loss preceding Apc inactivation exhibited reduced tumor-forming potential in immunocompetent mice, likely due to their distinct immunological features. Collectively, our study reveals a critical role of ordered mutation accumulation in CRC initiation, an insight that may hold clinical relevance.

items.title: Memory flows: geometry and dynamics of sequential retrieval in input-driven Hopfield networks
items.abstract: Associative memory models classically describe retrieval as convergence to stored patterns, but the theory of sequential retrieval remains comparatively limited. We develop a two-timescale input-driven Hopfield network in which fast associative retrieval is modulated by a slow feedback variable evolving over a prescribed memory-transition graph. This yields autonomous, graph-constrained transitions while preserving analytical tractability. Using slow-fast and geometric singular perturbation theory, we characterize memory fixation via memory manifolds and identify the geometric regions that govern stability loss and escape from retrieved memories. We further derive reduced slow dynamics and explicit criteria for transition onset, self-sustained retrieval, and collapse, expressed through escape times, gain thresholds, and fixed points. Together, these results provide a tractable framework for analyzing feedback-driven sequential retrieval in Hopfield networks.

items.title: Qualitative results in proficiency testing: a systematic review of evaluation practices and error integration.
items.abstract: Proficiency testing and external quality assessment (PT/EQA) are essential for reliable laboratory diagnostics, however evaluation of qualitative results remains poorly standardized. This systematic review examined how qualitative PT/EQA performance is evaluated and reported across life science domains, with emphasis on performance criteria, acceptance rules, and error handling. Searches of MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection identified 178 eligible studies published between 2016 and 2025. Evaluation practices varied considerably. Binary thresholds were used in 86 % of studies and were most often defined by program organizers (52 %) or formal standards (24 %), while 49 % did not report a formal acceptance criterion. Certified reference material use was explicitly reported in only 2 % of studies, whereas a reference method or independent procedure to establish or verify the target or assigned value was identified in 62 %. Across all included studies, 92 % reported errors, 74 % distinguished between error types, and 33 % considered differences in error consequences. Only 6 % explicitly weighted errors by severity or used risk-based prioritization (e.g., assigning greater weight to false-negative than false-positive results). No single diagnostic field consistently showed a more developed approach to incorporating errors into performance evaluation; instead, examples across fields illustrated approaches that considered how results are used, what consequences errors may have, how results are interpreted, and what actions follow. Overall, qualitative PT/EQA evaluation remains highly variable across studies. Clearer reporting of expected results, acceptance criteria, statistical methods, and error consequences may improve comparability and help laboratories interpret and use PT/EQA results for quality improvement.

items.title: Neoadjuvant Therapy in Mohs Surgery: A Scoping Review of the Literature.
items.abstract: Background Neoadjuvant therapies are increasingly used before Mohs micrographic surgery (MMS) to shrink tumors and reduce defect size, tumor and surgical invasiveness, and reconstruction complexity. Data on neoadjuvant agents used before MMS, their efficacy, and tolerability are limited. Objective The aim of this study was to analyze the literature regarding neoadjuvant therapies in MMS, protocols, outcomes, and tolerability. Methods A scoping review of PubMed, Embase, and Scopus was conducted on July 8th, 2025. Articles related to systemic or local chemotherapeutic and immunotherapeutic agents used neoadjuvantly in MMS were included. Results Thirty-three studies, including 303 patients, met inclusion criteria. Reports of neoadjuvant vismodegib, sonidegib, and imiquimod in basal cell carcinoma support reduction of the final defect and organ preservation. Reports of neoadjuvant imatinib for dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans show reduction in tumor size. Case reports demonstrated benefits from neoadjuvant talimogene laherparepvec in squamous cell carcinoma and pembrolizumab for desmoplastic melanoma and sebaceous carcinoma. Conclusions Neoadjuvant therapy can be used before MMS to shrink tumors, decrease surgical defects, and improve cosmetic, functional, and disease outcomes. It should be considered for locally advanced tumors or when preservation of tissue and anatomic function is critical. Larger studies are needed to confirm whether neoadjuvant therapies improve surgical and cosmetic outcomes and reduce recurrence and metastasis.

items.title: Health, Justice, and Community: Findings from Rhode Island's Health and Justice Research Symposium.
items.abstract: On April 17, 2026, the Center for Health and Justice Transformation (CHJT) convened the Rhode Island Health and Justice Research Symposium at Brown University. The event united researchers, clinicians, community advocates, policymakers, and people with lived experience of the criminal legal system to share findings, build connections, and identify shared priorities. This article synthesizes the proceedings of the symposium along five themes: Evidence-Based Interventions, Pressing Tensions, Existing Barriers, Open Questions, and Shared Vision. Across all five, a single thread recurred: Rhode Island's position as a national innovator in carceral health rests not on the agility afforded by its comparatively small size, but on its collaborative relationships and institutional capacity.
