items.title: Metagenomic and metabolomic analysis of a bryozoan-associated microbial complex from the Hanjiang River, China
items.abstract: Abstract Background Bryozoans are ancient colonial animals that have existed for over 470 million years and are widely distributed across aquatic environments. Recently, many spherical colloids (average diameter≈1 meter in diameter), containing bryozoans and diverse microorganisms, were found in the Hanjiang river in China. In this study, we investigated these bryozoan-dominated microbial complexes using metagenomic sequencing, metabolomic profiling, and complementary approaches. Results The results revealed that the microbial structure dominated by bryozoans included eukaryotes such as fungi, microalgae, as well as prokaryotes such as bacteria, and acellular entities such as viruses. All members form a highly integrated consortium that collaboratively maintains community function and stability, which displayed the shape and structure of a regular microbial complex and increased in size. Additionally, the results suggested the predominately presence of Proteobacteria were particularly abundant and are known to produce bryozoans in response to bryozoan signals. Interesting, it was implied that a decrease or even a loss in virulence occurs when pathogenic microorganisms become members of the complex. This is the first study focusing on the composition and metabolites of the unusual microorganism complex. The results discovered the close and intriguing connections within the microbial communities dominated by the ancient organism bryozoan through multi-omics technologies. It showed that both eukaryotes and prokaryotes can coordinate, thereby forming a stable composite structure.

items.title: Homogeneización estacional en las comunidades de aves del Área Metropolitana de Buenos Aires, Argentina, debido a la urbanización
items.abstract: 1. Las ciudades ubicadas en regiones templadas suelen mostrar una estabilización estacional de recursos para las aves. Esta estabilización ha sido asociada a una menor variación estacional en las comunidades de aves. Sin embargo, este tipo de análisis es escaso en la Región Pampeana.2. El objetivo de este estudio fue analizar la variación estacional de la riqueza y la composición de aves a lo largo del gradiente urbano-rural del Área Metropolitana de Buenos Aires, la segunda más grande de Sudamérica. Se realizaron conteos de aves en transectas durante las etapas reproductiva (primavera-verano) y no reproductiva (otoño-invierno) en cinco niveles de urbanización.3. La riqueza de aves mostró una relación negativa con la urbanización en la etapa reproductiva y fue máxima en niveles poco urbanizados durante la etapa no reproductiva. El cambio en la riqueza de especies entre estaciones fue máxima en el sector rural y no presentó cambios significativos en el sector poco urbanizado. El cambio de composición de especies entre etapas fue máximo en el sector rural y mínimo en el sector moderadamente urbanizado.4. Implicancias. Los resultados apoyan la idea de una homogeneización estacional de las comunidades de aves en áreas urbanas. Este trabajo mostró cambios estacionales en el sector más urbanizado, lo cual demuestra que el efecto homogeneizador de la urbanización sobre las comunidades de aves no es lineal.

items.title: PENERAPAN MODEL KOOPERATIF TIPE NUMBERED HEAD TOGETHER DALAM MENINGKATKAN HASIL BELAJAR PENDIDIKAN PANCASILA MURID KELAS IV
items.abstract: The learning outcomes of fourth-grade students in Pancasila Education at UPTD SD Negeri 074048 Luaha Bouso were still low because previous learning tended to be teacher-centered, resulting in limited student activity, collaboration, and participation. This study aimed to describe the implementation of the Numbered Head Together (NHT) cooperative learning model and to determine the improvement of students' learning outcomes in Pancasila Education after its implementation. The study employed Classroom Action Research using the Kemmis and McTaggart model and was conducted in two cycles. Each cycle consisted of planning, action, observation, and reflection, with two meetings in each cycle. The subjects were 19 fourth-grade students in the 2025/2026 academic year. Data were collected through observations of teacher and student activities, learning outcome tests, documentation, and field notes, and were analyzed descriptively using qualitative and quantitative approaches. The NHT implementation involved heterogeneous group formation, assigning numbers to group members, presenting questions or tasks, group discussion, random number calling, presentation of answers, and reinforcement. The findings showed that teacher activity increased from 58% in Cycle I Meeting I to 90% in Cycle II Meeting II, while student activity increased from 57.69% to 94.23%. Learning outcomes also improved, as indicated by an increase in the mean score from 62.68 in Cycle I to 80.63 in Cycle II and classical mastery from 47.37% to 84.21%. Therefore, the implementation of NHT improved student participation and learning outcomes in Pancasila Education.

items.title: Picloram-Induced Embryogenic Callus Formation and Proliferation from Nucellar Embryo of Mandarin ‘Berastagi’ (Citrus reticulata Blanco)
items.abstract: Mandarin ‘Berastagi’ (Citrus reticulata Blanco) is a key horticultural commodity in North Sumatra, Indonesia, with increasing demand for high quality, genetically uniform planting material. Biotechnological approaches, somatic embryogenesis, hold particularly significant potential enhancing propagation efficiency and crop quality. This study aimed to determine the optimal culture medium and picloram concentration for the induction and proliferation of embryogenic callus from nucellar explants of Mandarin ‘Berastagi’ in vitro. Two experiments were conducted: (1) induction of embryogenic callus from nucellar embryos isolated from young fruits (60–70 days after anthesis) cultured on different basal media supplemented with varying picloram concentrations, and (2) proliferation of embryogenic callus on media containing different carbohydrate concentrations. The Murashige and Wetmore (MW) medium supplemented with 1.5 mg/L picloram resulted in the highest callus induction rate (37.8%) and largest mean callus diameter (17.8 mm). For proliferation, MW medium containing 4% sucrose produced the best response, with an average callus diameter of 14 mm and 96% of explants developing globular stage somatic embryos. These results establish an efficient somatic embryogenesis protocol that can support large-scale propagation and future crop improvement programs in Mandarin ‘Berastagi’.

items.title: Helminth Fauna of the Caucasian Toad, Bufo verrucosissimus (Pallas, 1814) (Amphibia: Bufonidae), Collected from Türkiye
items.abstract: This study presents a helminthological investigation of 35 individuals (13♀♀ and 22♂♂) of the Caucasian toad, Bufo verrucosissimus (Pallas, 1814), collected from Artvin and Mersin provinces in Türkiye during 2024–2025. Six helminth species were identified: 1 species of Cestoda (Nematotaenia dispar (Goeze, 1782) Lühe, 1899), 4 species of Nematoda (Rhabdias bufonis (Schrank, 1788); Aplectana acuminata (Schrank, 1788) Railliet and Henry, 1916; Oxysomatium brevicaudatum (Zeder, 1800); Oswaldocruzia filiformis (Goeze, 1782)), and 1 species of Acanthocephala (Pseudoacanthocephalus caucasicus (Petrochenko, 1953)). This is the first helminthological study of B. verrucosissimus in Türkiye, and N. dispar and O. brevicaudatum represent new records for the host.

items.title: Can interspecific competition explain the absence of saline species in freshwaters? A test using water beetles
items.abstract: Abstract The habitats a species occupies are not determined solely by its environmental tolerance, because biotic interactions can further restrict its realised niche. This mismatch between fundamental and realised niches is well documented in saline-associated aquatic insects, many of which tolerate freshwater conditions in the laboratory yet are largely confined to saline waters in nature. We tested whether interspecific competition could contribute to the absence of the halophilic diving beetle Nebrioporus baeticus in freshwater. We compared its response to restricted food availability with that of the freshwater-associated N. clarkii under freshwater conditions, using single- and mixed-species treatments. Survival was monitored over a 30-day period, while feeding behaviour was assessed on days 1 and 7 based on feeding time and the number of contacts with the food resource. Contrary to our expectations, the halophilic beetle was not competitively disadvantaged by the freshwater congener. Interspecific coexistence instead had a transient negative effect on the feeding behaviour of the freshwater species, but not of the halophilic species. These findings suggest that competition alone cannot explain the absence of halophilic species from freshwater habitats, indicating that other factors are likely involved (e.g., predation pressure, parasitism, or other biotic interactions).

items.title: Thermal ecology drives alternate responses to rising temperatures in Caribbean anoles
items.abstract: Rapidly rising temperatures threaten populations of ectothermic animals worldwide, with the greatest impacts predicted in the tropics—hotspots for biodiversity. Ectotherms can respond to warming through two primary compensatory responses: behavioral thermoregulation, which buffers exposure to extreme temperatures; and heat tolerance increases via plasticity, adaptation, or both. The relative contribution of these responses is predicted to depend on ecological context, but whether these principles can anticipate organismal responses to contemporary warming remains largely untested. Here, using a decadal resurvey of anole lizards from Hispaniola, Jamaica, and Puerto Rico, we show that simple principles of thermal ecology can reliably anticipate organismal responses to rising temperatures. Species occupying thermally heterogeneous open/edge habitats, such as dry forests, behaviorally thermoregulate and have shown little to no increase in heat tolerance over the past decade. By contrast, species from thermally homogeneous closed-canopy environments are poor thermoregulators and have increased their heat tolerance by 2 °C, on average, over the same period. Seasonal comparisons, acclimation experiments, and laboratory-rearing experiments indicate that contemporary increases in heat tolerance likely reflect contributions from rapid evolutionary change and physiological plasticity. Thermal ecology, not phylogenetic or spatial proximity, is the key factor driving responses to rising temperatures. Our results consistently link organismal responses to habitat complexity and thermoregulatory behavior; we suggest that these factors are key to predicting how ectotherms respond to climate warming.

items.abstract: Albanycada bellinganorum Villet & Price sp. nov. Figs 3 C, 3 D, 4, 5, 7, 8 ≡ Albanycada sp. 1 sensu Price et al. (2019, 845). Type material examined. Holotype, 1 ♂ (Figs 3 C, 4, 7); “ RSA: Eastern Cape | Miller | Rietfontein Farm | S32°58'8.76" | E23°42'54.45" | 12. Dec. 2024 | T. A. Bellingan J. Zaayman | J. E. Bellingan A. J. Bellingan || 102190 || HOLOTYPE | Albanycada bellinganorum | Villet & Price ”; AMGS. Paratypes (2 ♂♂), 1 ♂ “ RSA: Eastern Cape | Miller | Rietfontein Farm | S32°58'8.76" | E23°42'54.45" | 12. Dec. 2024 | T. A. Bellingan J. Zaayman | J. E. Bellingan A. J. Bellingan || 102191 || Albanycada bellinganorum | Villet & Price ”; AMGS. 1 ♂; “ RSA: Eastern Cape | Miller | Rietfontein Farm | S32°58'8.76" | E23°42'54.45" | 12. Dec. 2024 | T. A. Bellingan J. Zaayman | J. E. Bellingan A. J. Bellingan || 102192 || PARATYPE | Albanycada bellinganorum | Villet & Price ”; AMGS. Additional material examined. 4 ♂♂; 1 ♀. The metadata on the labels of these specimens are not cited verbatim. South Africa – Eastern Cape • 1 ♂; nr Willowmore; 32.969°S, 23.715°E; 31 Jan. 2006; T. A. Bellingan leg.; MHV 0423; AMGS. • 2 ♂♂, 1 ♀; Rietfontein Farm; 32.969°S, 23.715°E; 19 Jan. 2008; B. W. Price & T. A. Bellingan leg.; MHV 1035; AMGS. – Western Cape • 1 ♂; Calitzdorp; 33.500°S, 21.750°E; 24 Dec. 1989; H. C. Ficq leg.; SANC. Morphological diagnosis. The external morphology and the male genitalia of A. bellinganorum Villet & Price, sp. nov. conform to the description of the genus (Figs 3 C, 3 D, 4). The primary feature distinguishing this species from A. albigera is the pigmentation pattern of its wings, especially the hind wing. Morphological description. Male fore wing length 23.4–24.3; fore wing width 9.4–10.1; body length 19.8–20.7; head width 8.0–8.3; mesonotum width 8.3–8.6. Female fore wing length 22.5; fore wing width 8.8; body length 18.3; head width 6.8; mesonotum width 8.1. Head with two black stripes running from eye to eye, one through the ocelli and the other across the bases of the antennae. Anteclypeus unmarked. Rostrum pale brown. Pronotum anterior margin blackened. Pronotal incisures variably black. Mesonotum the medial obconical spots black, the lateral obconical spots black with chestnut centres, a narrow median line brown, and a pair of spots just anterior to cruciform elevation black. Fore wing with grey feathering along the veins in the distal half, distinct blackening of the subapical crossveins, and two submarginal rows of dark grey spots that straddle the veins, the proximal spots being larger but not touching; the proximal half is opaque, marbled to a variable degree with grey, brown and white with an ill-defined, blackish disco-basal band, 3 rd and 4 th ulnar cells usually with a distinct whitish patch towards apex; venation pale brown; setae black. Hind wing burnt orange basally (fading to yellowish-ochre in dead specimens), area around distal veins and crossveins blackened, centres of apical cells hyaline; venation brown; crossveins not blackened; limbus crossed by evenly spaced black streaks hyaline; plaga greyish; jugum uniform. Legs brown; tibia often darker, with a dark brown patch near the proximal joint. Opercula dull brown. Abdominal tergites very dark brown; the posterior margins pale. Timbal cover brown. Tergite 8 bearing tomentum. Sternites unmarked. The sexes are similar in general appearance, colouration, body size and morphology, with the usual sexual dimorphisms of cicadas. Female opercula brown; tergite VII bearing tomentum; sternites unmarked; pygofer lacking ventral thorn, caudodorsal beak with apex sharply pointed; ovipositor sheaths reaching apex of caudodorsal beak; with 15 teeth. Molecular systematics and phylogenetic history. Sequences from four genes (genseq- 3 16S: FJ 168837; genseq- 3 COI: FJ 169041; genseq- 3 COII: GU 344010; and genseq- 3 EF- 1 α: GU 343829) are available for identifying this species (Price et al. 2019), which is estimated to have diverged from A. albigera about 5 Ma at the end of the Miocene (Price et al. 2019). Etymology. “Bellinganorum” is the Latin genitive neutral plural adjective indicating that this species is named in honour of the Bellingan family, who generously provided hospitality and assistance in obtaining specimens and sound recordings of A. bellinganorum Villet & Price, sp. nov. around their farm, Rietfontein. Distribution, ecology and biology. South Africa: apparently endemic to Arid Thicket and Mosaic Thicket with Fynbos variants of the Albany Thicket Biome of the westernmost Eastern Cape and eastern Western Cape, but the distribution is poorly sampled (Fig. 5). The biology of this species is known only from observations made in a patch of Arid Thicket vegetation on the farm Rietfontein, near Willowmore (Fig. 5), in the Albany Thicket Biome (Hoare et al. 2006; South African National Biodiversity Institute 2021). Adults are associated with Rhigozum obovatum Burch. (Granaatbos / Yellow Pomegranate), a relatively widespread bush. The type locality has a population of the endemic Aloe comptonii Reynolds, which may be a marker plant for this variant of Arid Thicket (van Wyk and Smith 2001; Klopper and Smith 2011). Apart from its plant associations, this species’ biology is probably similar to that of A. albigera. Adults are known to be active in January. Males do not form choruses. Like that of A. albigera, the calling song of A. bellinganorum Villet & Price, sp. nov. is a continuous, unmodulated whine that individual insects can sustain for long periods. It is pitched between 6.5–12.75 kHz, emphasized around 9.0 kHz, and with a pulse repetition rate of about 160 Hz (Fig. 8). The pulses are arranged in pairs in a manner similar to those in the calling songs of A. albigera and Kongota punctigera (Walker, 1850) (Villet 1989 figs 42–45). Recordings are available on the Bioacoustica website (https://bio.acousti.ca/sv/classification/albanycada-sp-01). Conservation. Area of Occupation (AOO) 8 km 2; Extent of Occurrence (EOO) 0 km 2 (only two sites); altitudinal range 255–935 m. The species inhabits one of the smallest biomes in South Africa; the biome is resistant to many natural perturbations but not resilient to degradation (South African National Biodiversity Institute 2021), and ~ 50 % of it is already transformed, although less so in the western parts (Carvalho et al. 2022). Although the known occurrences of A. bellinganorum are about 190 km apart, the intervening habitat is very elongated and very narrow (Fig. 5), so its true distribution merits investigation. The species’ IUCN status is Not Evaluated (NE); by criteria linked to its AOO and EOO and the characteristics of its habitat, it may well qualify as Critically Endangered (CR). Relevant conservation measures are lacking (Carvalho et al. 2022) and the species is not yet known from any formally conserved area.

items.title: Fire asymmetries across global borders reveal distinct ecological governance and cooperation priorities
items.abstract: Abstract International borders divide governance systems but often cut across continuous ecosystems, creating potential mismatches in fire management. We analyze 277 terrestrial international border pairs using a 21-year satellite fire record and integrate fire burden, relative cross-border asymmetry, ecological value, institutional challenge and cooperation challenge. Border fire burden broadly reproduces global fire geography, with the highest activity concentrated in major fire-prone regions, but our analysis shows that management implications differ markedly among borders. Among 128 active-fire pairs, fire burden and proportional asymmetry are weakly negatively associated and identify partly distinct priorities. Ecological value further reshapes priority geographies, while institutional and cooperation constraints define different governance contexts. Multivariate analysis separates these borders into operational profiles with contrasting management needs. Here, we show that transboundary fire priority cannot be inferred from fire activity alone but emerges from distinct combinations of fire, ecological and governance conditions, requiring border-specific approaches to monitoring, conservation and cooperation.

items.title: Marinas act as persistent introduction hubs driving the decadal accumulation of non-indigenous fouling species in an oceanic island system
items.abstract: Long–term monitoring of marine fouling assemblages and non‑indigenous species (NIS) has been historically scarce globally, particularly in island ecosystems, limiting the ability to distinguish transient detections from persistent populations. Using an 11–year monitoring dataset (2013–2025; 33 surveys, 131 sampling events) across four Madeira Archipelago marinas, we evaluated spatio-temporal patterns in biofouling assemblages. Across 71 recorded taxa, cumulative NIS richness increased steadily, ultimately accounting for nearly half (45–48%; 27–30 NIS per marina) of all recorded fouling species, reflecting major community transformation. Multivariate analyses identified marina identity as the primary driver structuring assemblages, maintaining distinct spatial signatures despite minimal thermal variation. Temporally, seasonal dynamics revealed a clear functional decoupling: mean observed richness per sampling event peaked during warmer periods, whereas cumulative multi-year species turnover was highest during cooler periods. This decoupling reflects seasonal thermal regimes, where summer warming creates windows that trigger reproductive pulses and space preemption by fast-growing colonial NIS, while cooler periods permit broader species turnover. Together, these findings confirm marinas as persistent introduction hubs, where repeated introductions, recruitment, and population persistence. Long–term, seasonally informed monitoring is therefore vital for early detection and marine biosecurity in island ecosystems.

items.title: Beyond the Green Image: A Visual-Documentary Framework for Evaluating Nature-Positive Evidence in Architecture
items.abstract: As architecture increasingly adopts biodiversity and nature-positive terminology, visually prominent greenness is often treated as evidence of ecological value. This chapter develops a visual-documentary framework that separates architectural visibility from ecological verifiability. Twelve international buildings comprising 16 ecological subsystems were examined through criterion-based purposive sampling. Visual Greenness Prominence was assessed independently from nine ecological criteria, while evidence level, source quality, baseline status and evidence architecture were coded separately. The analysis shows that high visual greenness is neither necessary nor sufficient for strong verified ecological response. The principal gap occurred between ecological provision and demonstrated outcome: habitat provision, heterogeneity and natural-process integration were common, but none of the subsystems demonstrated the full combination of broad quantified biodiversity improvement, a defensible baseline or counterfactual, and evidence sufficient to establish baseline- or counterfactual-relative positive biodiversity change. The framework therefore calibrates ecological claims to the quality and completeness of the evidence supporting them.

items.title: Reconstructing ancient ecosystems: guanaco and marine carrion as drivers of predator-prey networks in Southern South America
items.abstract: Understanding ancient trophic dynamics and human integration in terrestrial high-latitude ecosystems requires moving beyond traditional taxonomic lists to evaluate structural biological interactions. This study presents the first probabilistic, trait-based bipartite network reconstruction of ancient predator-prey assemblages in northern Tierra del Fuego, Southern South America, based on archeological records. By integrating a comprehensive zooarcheological dataset spanning 50 spatial-temporal contexts from the late Pleistocene through the late Holocene across steppe and forest habitats, we model trophic interactions including human subsistence strategies. In this region, dominated by grassy steppes and the forest-steppe ecotone, terrestrial hunter-gatherer societies were embedded in a complex predator-prey network in which the guanaco ( Lama guanicoe ) played a central role. However, the trophic structure of these interactions and how the introduction of humans as an unprecedented predator affected community-level properties is poorly understood. Our results reveal a significant chronological transformation in network architecture and diet composition. During the late Pleistocene, communities exhibited lower interaction diversity and high specialization centered around megaherbivores and multiple large predators. Following megafaunal extinction and island isolation during the mid-Holocene, the guanaco emerged as an enduring keystone herbivore and dietary anchor, while marine-derived carrion and littoral resources (mollusks and pinnipeds) provided critical energy subsidies. Humans acted as highly plastic generalist consumers, influencing network architecture across diverse habitats. In the steppe, foragers employed broad-spectrum strategies, whereas forest assemblages reflected specialized reliance on coastal resources. Ultimately, this community-level framework demonstrates that despite intense environmental shifts and insularization, the guanaco and marine necromass served as foundational trophic stabilizers, maintaining ecosystem and subsistence resilience over millennia.

items.title: From Jupyter Notebooks to DNA Encoding and Tensor Networks: A Mini-Review of Computational Bioinformatics Education and Insect Barcoding
items.abstract: Computational biology increasingly depends on algorithms, yet many life-science learners lack programming experience and practical strategies for transforming DNA strings into machine-readable data. This mini-review examines three connected themes: Python instruction through Jupyter notebooks, nucleotide representation using one-hot, binary, and integer encodings, and tensor-network classification of DNA barcodes. Synthesizing complementary publications spanning bioinformatics education, sequence modeling, DNA barcoding, and tensor methods, we explore the transition from instruction to model deployment. Jupyter notebooks integrate explanations, executable code, and visualization, supporting reproducible learning. Encoding determines information geometry, memory demands, and assumptions passed to classifiers. A published tensor-network model reported greater than 99% accuracy on a four-class Orthoptera dataset; this result remains dataset-specific and does not establish encoding superiority. We argue that strong computational foundations, paired with rigorous representation choices and external validation, can responsibly enable accurate machine learning for agriculture, ecology, and biodiversity monitoring in real-world settings.

items.title: Tracking deep-time environmental stability exposes a global conservation gap
items.abstract: Abstract Continents drift across latitudinal climate zones that are themselves shifting as Earth's climate evolves [1-5]. The relative speed of these two motions (tectonic versus climatic velocity) determines how much climate change a given landmass experiences over geological time: where plates and climate zones move in concert, local climates can remain stable for millions of years, allowing lineages to persist and diversify. However, whether this interplay has shaped deep-time environmental stability and, in turn, present-day biodiversity patterns remains untested. Here, using a Lagrangian framework to track land parcels through 60 million years of palaeogeographic, palaeoclimatic, and palaeoproductivity reconstructions, we show that in amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals, species richness increases with the time a parcel has spent within a stable environmental envelope. This accumulation shows no sign of saturation, instead accelerating across nearly all combinations of taxonomic group and environment. Integrating stability along tectonic trajectories identifies modern macroevolutionary refugia (>20 Myr of cumulative stability). Of these refugia, 77.9% lack legal protection---rising to 91.5% in Asia---and just 2.1% fall within strictly protected areas. Refugia are only modestly better protected than unstable land (22.1% versus 15.8%), with over three-quarters of this difference driven by the weakest protection tiers. Having assembled while their environments moved at centimetres to metres per year, these biotas face present-day climate velocities of hundreds of metres to kilometres per year [6, 7], a kinematic debt that protecting static coordinates alone cannot address.

items.title: Ecology and Sustainability in the 21st Century: An Interdisciplinary Integrative and Critical Review with a Focus on Portugal
items.abstract: Sustainability is an interdisciplinary scientific and institutional challenge that isolated improvements in technological efficiency, emissions reduction, or material substitution cannot adequately address. This study presents an interdisciplinary, integrative, and critical review of ecology and sustainability, complemented by documentary analysis and selected case studies. It examines ecological integrity, biodiversity, biophysical constraints, economic systems, environmental governance, and the distribution of environmental impacts across territories and generations, with particular attention to Portugal. The analysis highlights the limitations of treating efficiency, circularity, and innovation as sufficient evidence of environmental sustainability. Robust assessment requires explicit system boundaries, comparable functional units, consideration of indirect effects, and attention to the displacement of environmental costs. Selected SCI research cases illustrate the importance of evidence traceability and the limits of quantitative conclusions when underlying data cannot be adequately reconciled. The study distinguishes established scientific knowledge, documented SCI findings, and analytical interpretations. It does not constitute a systematic review or a scoping review conducted under PRISMA-ScR. Its conclusions are limited to the evidence examined. The paper contributes an interdisciplinary framework for understanding sustainability as preserving ecological functions alongside human well-being, social justice, and long-term institutional responsibility.

items.title: From fragmentation to conditional coordination: China Coast Guard environmental enforcement under ecological codification and the BBNJ Agreement
items.abstract: China’s consolidated maritime enforcement system connects dispersed domestic powers with new obligations under the Ecological and Environmental Code (EEC) and the Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement. This study examines the relationship between China’s implementation responsibility and the legality of a specified China Coast Guard (CCG) measure. Five analytical inquiries distinguish institutional competence, applicable requirements, legal consequences, measure-specific authority, and international jurisdiction across three legal domains. They develop established legality review by pairing its measure-specific conclusion with a diagnosis of the implementation task that remains. Controlled variations show how the same rejection of boarding can correspond to referral, a necessary domestic implementing instrument, or procedural completion. Alternative routes are assessed against the applicable obligation’s addressee, required legal effect, timing, and mandatory procedures. For activities involving foreign-flagged vessels, Chinese incorporation identifies a personal nexus but must be connected to the corporation’s role in the particular activity. A proposed operational-control criterion examines executable decision powers over initiation, continuation, or environmentally material aspects of that activity. The framework distinguishes established, unresolved, absent and inapplicable requirements and links proposed implementation routes to administrative follow-up, operator responses and verification.

items.title: Inferring Long-Term Human Legacies in the Bornean Forests
items.abstract: The question of whether past human communities have left lasting ecological legacies in the forests they inhabited is a defining debate in tropical forest ecology. Borneo offers a unique context for examining this question, with an extensive archaeological record spanning at least 45,000 years and high-biodiversity forests. However, the ecological consequences of longterm human presence have remained largely unexamined. In this thesis, I use an interdisciplinary approach combining archaeology, remote sensing, environmental data, and functional and community ecology to produce the first integrated assessment of long-term human legacies in contemporary Bornean forests. I compiled the first island-wide synthesis of 73 archaeological sites across Borneo, characterising their climatic and environmental conditions against simulated random locations. Archaeological sites occur non-randomly under warmer, drier, low-elevation conditions near coasts and river networks, an environmental signature consistent with landscapes that concentrated resources and supported localised subsistence practices. Building on this foundation, I found that forests with long-term human activity exhibit a distinctive combination of conservative and acquisitive functional strategies, occupying an intermediate functional space between old-growth forests, regenerating forests, and agroforests, with lasting implications for how these ecosystems may respond to future environmental change. At the landscape scale, species diversity and basal area declined towards archaeological settlements, with the onset and duration of human occupation as significant predictors of diversity. Species composition near settlements remained floristically distinct, with an enrichment of ethnobotanically valued taxa and pioneer and mid-succesional species. Nearly 40% of all recorded taxa had documented ethnobotanical uses, identified independently of local knowledge, indicating that these forests preserve human legacies of past forest management that persist at least three millennia after abandonment. These findings reveal Bornean forests not as pristine but as landscapes shaped by the human communities that inhabited them, underscoring the need to integrate the deep history of human–forest interaction into the frameworks we use to identify, conserve and manage these irreplaceable ecosystems.

items.title: Sensory Ecology of Disturbance: Turbidity Mediates Estuarine Community Stability Following Extreme Events
items.abstract: Predators play a critical role in structuring communities, but their effects are mediated by environmental conditions that alter their foraging capability. In Texas oyster reef communities, visually foraging fish predators enhance biodiversity by suppressing mesopredators, but their forging effectiveness declines with increasing turbidity. We used widespread fish mortality caused by Winter Storm Uri (February 2021) to test how water clarity mediates oyster reef community response to disturbance. Fish abundance was higher in low turbidity, where foraging conditions were most favorable. Following the freeze, oyster community responses diverged; turbid reefs exhibited over double the annual variance in community composition relative to clear sites. We propose that sensory constraints on predation and lower fish abundance in turbid habitats amplified the effects of predator loss. In contrast, freeze effects were dampened in clear-water conditions that enhanced fish foraging and supported higher fish abundance. Our results demonstrate that sensory environments can influence the strength and stability of trophic interactions, with implications for predicting ecosystem responses to disturbance in increasingly turbid coastal systems.

items.title: A decade of open biodiversity data in the Azores: closing knowledge gaps and building a foundation for long-term monitoring
items.abstract: Ten years of dedicated biodiversity research and coordinated open-data publication have built an extensive, reusable knowledge base for the Azores. We synthesize this collective achievement through the AZORES BIOTA and BioMonI-Plot collections, evaluating its contribution to addressing the Wallacean and Prestonian shortfalls and identifying priorities for future research and monitoring. Focusing on the nine islands of this North Atlantic archipelago, we review publications issued between 2016 and May 2026, encompassing terrestrial and marine organisms across six kingdoms. We combine curated publication and dataset metadata with Darwin Core occurrenceID-linked species and subspecies records to assess spatial, taxonomic, temporal and methodological coverage, species accumulation by colonization status, and island species–area relationships. Across 91 publications, the collections document 931 animal, 1,185 plant and 742 fungal species and subspecies, alongside taxa from three additional kingdoms, and identify 598 additions to the Azorean Biodiversity Portal reference list. This sustained effort has substantially expanded accessible knowledge of species distributions, contributing to reducing the Wallacean shortfall. Arthropod abundance datasets and repeated standardized surveys also alleviate the Prestonian shortfall by enabling assessments of population and community change. Together, these resources establish valuable baselines for biodiversity assessment, invasion surveillance and conservation planning. The synthesis also reveals uneven coverage among islands, taxa and habitats, with spatial differences in research effort complicating interpretation of species–area relationships. The Azorean experience demonstrates the substantial scientific value of sustained regional expertise, collaboration and standardized open-data publication for understanding island biodiversity. By consolidating achievements and making remaining gaps explicit, this synthesis provides a foundation for targeted investment in underrepresented biota, spatially balanced surveys and sustained abundance monitoring, strengthening the evidence base for future biodiversity research and conservation.

items.title: Dark Energy Survey year 6 results: Cosmological constraints from galaxy clustering and weak lensing
items.abstract: We present cosmology results combining galaxy clustering and weak gravitational lensing measured in the full six years (Y6) of observations by the Dark Energy Survey (DES) covering $\sim$5000 deg$^2$. We perform a large-scale structure analysis using three two-point correlation functions (3$\times$2pt): (i) cosmic shear from 140 million source galaxy shapes, (ii) galaxy clustering of 9 million lens galaxy positions, and (iii) galaxy-galaxy lensing from their cross-correlation. We model the data in flat $Λ$CDM and $w$CDM cosmologies. The combined analysis yields $S_8\equiv σ_8 (Ω_{\rm m}/0.3)^{0.5} = 0.789^{+0.012}_{-0.012}$ and matter density $Ω_{\rm m} = 0.333^{+0.023}_{-0.028}$ in $Λ$CDM (68\% CL), where $σ_8$ is the clustering amplitude. These constraints show a (full-space) parameter difference of 1.8$σ$ from a combination of cosmic microwave background (CMB) primary anisotropy datasets from Planck 2018, ACT-DR6, and SPT-3G DR1. Projected only into $S_8$ the difference is $2.6σ$. In $w$CDM the Y6 3$\times$2pt results yield $S_8 = 0.782^{+0.021}_{-0.020}$, $Ω_{\rm m} = 0.325^{+0.032}_{-0.035}$, and dark energy equation-of-state parameter $w = -1.12^{+0.26}_{-0.20}$. For the first time, we combine all DES dark-energy probes: 3$\times$2pt, SNe Ia, BAO and Clusters. In $Λ$CDM this combination yields a $2.8σ$ parameter difference from the CMB. When combining DES 3$\times$2pt with other low-redshift datasets (DESI DR2 BAO, DES SNe Ia, SPT clusters), we find a 2.3$σ$ parameter difference with CMB. A joint fit of Y6 3$\times$2pt, CMB, and those low-redshift datasets produces the tightest $Λ$CDM constraints to date: $S_8 = 0.806^{+0.006}_{-0.007}$, $Ω_{\rm m} = 0.302^{+0.003}_{-0.003}$, $h = 0.683^{+0.003}_{-0.002}$, and $\sum m_ν< 0.14$ eV (95\% CL). In $w$CDM, this combination yields $w = -0.981^{+0.021}_{-0.022}$.

items.title: INNOVATIVE TRENDS AND EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICES IN ENGLISH LANGUAGE TEACHING IN HIGHER EDUCATION
items.abstract: English language teaching (ELT) in higher education is undergoing a transformative phase driven by globalization, technological advancement, and evolving learner expectations.This article explores the latest innovations in ELT and evaluates evidencebased pedagogical practices that enhance language proficiency, learner engagement, and academic outcomes.It identifies technology integration, learner-centered approaches, and data-driven instruction as the most impactful trends, providing a comprehensive overview of methods such as Learning Management Systems, task-based language teaching, content and language integrated learning, flipped classrooms, and adaptive learning systems.The article emphasizes that the adoption of these innovations should be grounded in empirical research to ensure their effectiveness and sustainability in diverse university contexts.The scientific contribution of this work lies in synthesizing recent theoretical and practical advancements in ELT, offering a clear framework for implementing innovative and research-backed strategies.The study highlights the practical significance for educators, curriculum designers, and policymakers by suggesting actionable approaches for improving teaching quality, promoting learner autonomy, and addressing challenges such as digital inequality and resistance to change.The findings support a paradigm shift from teacher-centered to learner-centered and technology-enhanced instruction, reinforcing the importance of continuous professional development for instructors.By integrating innovative trends with evidence-based practices, higher education institutions can foster more effective and adaptive English language learning environments.

items.title: Opportunities for creative thinking in an out-of-school learning environment: perceptions and experiences of children attending the Discovery Campus
items.abstract: Creative thinking emerges as a critical skill that adds meaning to individuals’ lives in today’s competitive world. One of the learning environments aimed at developing this skill is the Discovery Campus, which serves as a children’s university. This qualitative study aimed to investigate the perceptions and experiences regarding creative thinking of 32 children aged 11–13 who regularly attend the Discovery Campus in Gaziantep, Türkiye. The participants were selected through criterion sampling, a purposive sampling method. Data were collected via written interview forms and analysed using the content analysis method. The findings indicated that participants perceive the Discovery Campus as a learning environment where, in addition to acquiring new knowledge, they can apply what they have learned, discover their own potential, and develop original ideas. It was determined that creative project ideas aim to develop solutions to problems based on the needs of humans, society, and living organisms; and that experiences at the Discovery Campus are associated with an approach based on hands-on learning, material use, enquiry, observation, and imagination, which differs from formal school environments. Furthermore, in the children’s narratives, it was observed that opportunities for creative thinking are shaped by the processes of conducting research, focusing on areas of interest, participating in workshop activities, transforming ideas into projects, and sharing the developed designs. Accordingly, in order to support children’s creative thinking processes, it is recommended to expand science centres that bring together different disciplines and provide opportunities for practical application and project production.

items.title: Scientific Explicitization Process of Humankind Destiny Estimated by Zhang Extrapolation Formulas via Newton, Gauss, and Historical Data as well as Reflections
items.abstract: This work investigates what is termed the scientific explicitization process of humankind destiny from a historical and chronological perspective. Newton and Gauss are selected as two initial historical anchors. Newton, together with the development of calculus and his writings on chronology, is associated with a ``Calculating'' mode, whereas Gauss is associated with an ``Asking'' mode, symbolizing rigorous inquiry into the future, human destination, and the limits of knowledge. Based on the chronological interval between these anchors, the Zhang extrapolation method and Zhang extrapolation formulas (ZEF) are used to estimate three subsequent intervals, interpreted as ``Computing'', ``Destining'', and ``Steady-State''. The Comte–Zhang year 2300, derived from the reference years 1300 and 1800, is further introduced as an indicative completion or cutoff point, and possibly as a ``Great Completion'' reference within the proposed framework. Historical and conceptual reflections involving Pascal, Laplace, von Neumann, Hilbert, Rees, Bostrom, and related Chinese future-oriented thought are incorporated as supplementary perspectives. The purpose of this study is to organize an abstract question concerning humankind destiny into a chronological and interpretable framework. The resulting stages are therefore intended as symbolic and exploratory constructs for examining possible long-term historical patterns.

items.title: Pixel-UMI: Learning Environment-Aware Whole-Body Manipulation from Sensorized Human Demonstrations
items.abstract: Sensorized human demonstrations offer scalable data for mobile manipulation, but embodiment differences complicate policy learning. We present Pixel-UMI, a pipeline for learning environment-aware whole-body policies from human data. We first introduce Environment-Aware Retargeting (EAR), which combines reconstructed scene geometry with demonstrated head and gripper trajectories to determine robot posture and generate collision-aware joint and base targets. Delay-calibrated action assignment converts these trajectories into actions. However, kinematic differences can leave residual pose errors, creating viewpoint mismatches between human demonstrations and robot observations. We therefore introduce Retargeting-Error-Aware Masking (REAM), which uses these errors during training to reduce reliance on mismatched views at deployment. Finally, because estimated actions cannot fully capture contact-rich interactions, we collect on-policy human corrections through DAgger to improve performance. We evaluate Pixel-UMI on five challenging tasks spanning articulated-object manipulation, deformable-object handling, constrained-space reaching, whole-body collision avoidance, and contact-rich bimanual coordination, achieving 87.0% average task progress. Video results are available at https://pixel-robot.com/pixel-umi

items.title: Pixel: A Co-Designed Full-Stack Robot System for Learning General-Purpose Mobile Manipulation
items.abstract: General-purpose mobile manipulation requires a combination of capable robot hardware, scalable demonstration collection, expressive whole-body control, and effective policy learning. Yet these components are often developed independently, creating mismatches that limit the capabilities of the complete system. We present Pixel, a co-designed full-stack system for learning general-purpose mobile manipulation. Pixel combines a low-cost wheeled humanoid with human-aligned kinematics and compliant grippers, multiple teleoperation and robot-free human data-collection interfaces, a unified whole-body controller, and a common policy learning pipeline across human and robot demonstrations. A hierarchical learning stack further enables language-conditioned visuomotor control and long-horizon task execution. We evaluate the system across hardware, data collection, and policy learning, and demonstrate mobile-manipulation behaviors requiring dexterity, active perception, navigation, and whole-body coordination. We hope that Pixel provides an integrated and extensible foundation for studying how robot hardware, data, control, and learning can be designed together for robot learning. More results at https://pixel-robot.com/pixel

items.title: D&A: Decoupling Description and Assessment Enables VLMs as Zero-Shot Robotic Reward Models
items.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) hold promise for zero-shot video task-progress estimation in robot learning, yet existing frameworks frequently suffer from confirmation bias, hallucinating progress in failed executions due to implicit success assumptions or relative temporal ranking designs. Naive prompting of frontier models collapses into a binary success detector that fails to capture nuanced, non-linear progress and failures. While post-training approaches can mitigate this through explicit training, they demand expensive real-world robotics data and require computationally intensive post-training for every individual base model. To resolve these limitations, we introduce D&A (Describe & Assess): our approach decouples progress estimation into an objective, task-grounded textual description of scene dynamics followed by an assessment phase using explicit rubrics. By compelling the VLM to synthesize an explicit, text-based definition of absolute success before scoring, the framework anchors evaluations to an external, global criterion rather than the video's internal timeline. Empirical results demonstrate that our method calibrates zero-shot estimates and mitigates confirmation bias, providing fine-grained, partial progress metrics that accurately penalize failed executions while correctly interpolating successful runs. Being purely prompt-based, D&A generalizes across tasks, embodiments, and benchmarks---matching or surpassing post-trained reward models---and its reward estimates enable efficient downstream reinforcement learning.

items.title: Mediating Human-Swarm Interactions Through a Robot Helper: A Shepherding-Inspired Approach
items.abstract: This work investigates human-swarm interaction (HSI) for steering large collectives through an intermediary robot helper. While prior robot-swarm control and HSI techniques commonly assume swarm members are addressable, these assumptions often fail for ``ungovernable'' swarms such as wildlife flocks and schools of fish. Motivated by pastoral shepherding, we compare low-level teleoperation to a higher-autonomy motion-primitives interface in a virtual reality (VR) shepherding task under varied swarm cohesion dynamics. Results indicate that motion primitives that operate on collective shape (e.g., boundary-based control) improve task performance and reduce perceived workload.

items.title: PanoTac: A Dense Three-Axis Tactile Sensor for Robust Touch-Centric Manipulation
items.abstract: Contact-rich manipulation benefits from tactile feedback that captures both detailed contact geometry and interaction forces. When scooping grains, contact patterns help infer spoon orientation, while resistance transmitted through the grasp guides motion. To provide these complementary sensing capabilities, we present PanoTac, a low-cost, compliant tactile fingertip designed for dense three-axis tactile sensing. Each fingertip provides a $12 \times 32 \times 3$ tactile representation, with one normal ($z$) and two shear ($x$, $y$) response components at each taxel. The sensor operates at 60 Hz and costs less than $50 per fingertip. Sensor characterization quantifies response repeatability and consistency across sensor instances and contact locations. We integrate PanoTac into a robotic system with a visuo-tactile pipeline. Across test-tube preparation, grain scooping, and salt pouring, the resulting policies outperform vision-only baselines by an average of 46.7 percentage points. Ablations show that removing either spatial contact information or shear feedback reduces overall performance across the task suite. Our project page is available at https://panotac.github.io.

items.title: EmbryoProfiler: A Visual Clinical Decision Support System for IVF
items.abstract: In-vitro fertilization (IVF) has become standard practice to address infertility, which affects more than one in ten couples in the US. However, current protocols yield relatively low success rates of about 20% per treatment cycle. A critical but complex and time-consuming step is the grading and selection of embryos for implantation. Although incubators with time-lapse microscopy have enabled computational analysis of embryo development, existing automated approaches either require extensive manual annotations or use opaque deep learning models that are hard for clinicians to validate and trust. We present EmbryoProfiler, a visual analytics system collaboratively developed with embryologists, biologists, and machine learning researchers to support clinicians in visually assessing embryo viability from time-lapse microscopy imagery. Our system incorporates a deep learning pipeline that automatically annotates microscopy images and extracts clinically interpretable features relevant for embryo grading. Our contributions include: (1) a semi-automatic, visualization-based workflow that guides clinicians through fertilization assessment, developmental timing evaluation, morphological inspection, and comparative analysis of embryos; (2) innovative interactive visualizations, such as cell-shape plots, designed to facilitate efficient analysis of morphological and developmental characteristics; and (3) an integrated, explainable machine learning classifier offering transparent, clinically-informed embryo viability scoring to predict live birth outcomes. Quantitative evaluation of our classifier and qualitative case studies conducted with practitioners demonstrate that EmbryoProfiler enables clinicians to make better-informed embryo selection decisions, potentially leading to improved clinical outcomes in IVF treatments.

items.title: Harder Than the Task: From Technical to Organizational Difficulty in AI Benchmarking
items.abstract: AI benchmarks have made remarkable progress in measuring the ability of AI systems to perform increasingly demanding cognitive and technical tasks. Yet, many of these benchmarks treat technical tasks as the unit of analysis, while much economically valuable work takes place within organizations, where tasks are embedded in a system of relations. Within organizations, successful task performance depends not only on solving the technical demands of the task but also on navigating the interdependence of activities, distributed knowledge, differentiated authority, temporal constraints, conflicting interests, and changing environmental conditions while the task is underway. Accordingly, we argue that organizational task difficulty constitutes a distinct and insufficiently recognized dimension of AI capability, and that existing approaches to benchmarking provide an incomplete basis for assessing how effectively AI agents can perform real-world organizational work. By drawing on organization theory, we develop a taxonomy of the structure of work that characterizes the conditions that agents face in organizational work. Applying this taxonomy to analyze existing benchmarks, we find limited and uneven coverage of organizational dimensions, with fewer than one quarter of prominent benchmarks claiming any of them. We therefore argue that AI benchmarks should increasingly move beyond the evaluation of technically difficult tasks toward the systematic assessment of agents' ability to navigate the organizational conditions under which economically valuable work takes place.

items.title: OpenZilo: An Open Smart-Ring Platform for Human-Centric Sensing and Interaction with Robots
items.abstract: Wearable robot interfaces must connect user input to timely physical action. We present the proposed platform, an open smart-ring platform for studying this connection across task stages. The ring integrates a microphone, an inertial measurement unit, photoplethysmography, and skin-temperature sensing. Its software architecture separates acquisition, event interpretation, interaction policy, and robot execution. We characterize seven operating modes and evaluate speech and gesture control with 10 participants. Across five commands and 250 trials per modality, speech and gestures achieved task success rates of 90.4% and 88.8%, respectively. Recognition accuracy exceeded task success for both modalities. Gaussian hidden Markov models achieved higher accuracy than a support vector machine across three vocabulary sizes, with longer scoring times. Following a shared spoken task start, gesture-based adjustments had shorter median response times than speech. Whole-task success was 70.0% with gestures and 64.0% with speech. We further examine physiological-event-triggered robot interaction using simulated event notifications. Mean notification-receipt-to-arrival times were 11.71 s for the robot and 9.20 s for an on-site person. These descriptive findings support evaluating wearable robot interfaces through both recognition and physical outcomes, with timing measures appropriate to each task stage.

items.title: CrowdForge: Effects of Audio and Visual Audience Participation Modalities on Agency, Collaboration, and Engagement in AI-Mediated MR Performances
items.abstract: Technology-mediated audience participation (TMAP) enables audiences to influence live performances, yet balancing interaction with meaningful agency remains challenging. While AI-generated music and MR enable new forms of audio and visual audience participation, little is known about how these participation modalities influence audience experiences during live musical performance. In particular, it remains unclear how they shape perceived agency, collaboration, and engagement, and how they complement one another within TMAP systems. We present CrowdForge, an AI- and MR-mediated paradigm where audiences collectively control generative music and virtual environments during a live performance featuring a guitarist and DJ. Through a mixedmethods concert study evaluating three interaction conditions (audio, visual, and combined audio-visual), we demonstrate that observability is the primary driver of audience agency. While visual interaction provided easily observable feedback, audio parameters offered macro-structural control over the music. Audiences tended to use the control enabled by AI audio generation to test musical boundaries, introducing a productive adversarial tension between the crowd and the musicians. This dynamic pushed creative limits, deepened engagement, and generated moments of musical coherence when performers successfully resolved audience-induced challenges. We argue future TMAP systems should prioritize human-centered, highly observable interactions to build agency, while combining the expressiveness of music with the clarity of visual feedback.

items.title: Psychobiotics for nurturing the mental health through gut-brain-signalling: current status and future directions.
items.abstract: The gut-microbiota-brain axis is a pivotal regulator of mental and neurological health, positioning psychobiotics as promising adjunct therapies. Specific microbial strains with inherent psychobiotic potential are known to enhance mental health, cognitive, or stress-preventive qualities. They mediate the promotion of a healthy intestinal barrier by the production of neurotransmitters, neuro-hormones and neuro-protectors, which include short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), serotonin, etc. This review explores the myriad ways that psychobiotics impact neurocognitive health and the potential use as an adjunct therapy for mental well-being. We further emphasise the revolutionary potential of nanotechnology in overcoming traditional delivery obstacles of psychobiotics with enhanced stability, bioavailability and efficacy, which are least explored in previous reviews. Hence, a detailed understanding of the development and applications of psychobiotics may offer new therapeutic possibilities and improved emotional balance. Together, these insights underscore the evolving landscape of psychobiotic research and outline future directions for developing more effective, microbiota-based interventions for mental health. The review affirms that, alongside the mechanistic effects of psychobiotics on neurocognitive health, the reinforcement of the gut-brain axis is pivotal. Thus, this review opens the scope for future investigations into personalised psychobiotics with site-directed enhanced action using nanotechnology.

items.title: The Association of MRI-Derived Tissue Bridge Morphometrics with Baseline Impairment and Recovery in Traumatic Spinal Cord Injury: A Subanalysis of the RISCIS Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.abstract: Early prognostic biomarkers are essential to optimize treatment and trial design in spinal cord injury (SCI). The Riluzole in SCI Study (RISCIS), a multicenter randomized controlled trial, provided evidence on secondary analyses that riluzole improved functional recovery in acute cervical SCI. The current analysis uses magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to assess lesion and tissue bridge morphometrics against baseline impairment, functional recovery, and treatment response in RISCIS participants. In this preplanned ambispective subanalysis, 24 participants underwent T2-weighted MRI for acute cervical SCI together with neurological and functional assessments to 12 months. A subset also had diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), used to extract fractional anisotropy (FA) values. Segmentation with the Spinal Cord Toolbox (v7.2) gave ventral, dorsal, and total tissue-bridge widths and lesion volume and length. Associations with American Spinal Injury Association Impairment Scale (AIS) grade, upper extremity motor score (UEMS) and total motor score (TMS), lower extremity motor score (LEMS), light touch and pinprick sensory scores, Spinal Cord Independence Measure (SCIM), and Short Form-36 (SF-36) domains at baseline and follow-up were analyzed with regression models adjusted for age and sex. Overall recovery across TMS, SCIM, and SF-36 Physical Component Summary was analyzed with an O'Brien-style global statistical test (GST). Interactions tested whether bridge metrics modified riluzole's effect. At baseline, greater ventral ( β = 9.65, p = 0.017) and total ( β = 6.16, p = 0.021) tissue-bridge widths were associated with higher TMS, and ventral width with higher UEMS ( β = 6.61, p = 0.010). Larger dorsal (odds ratio [OR] = 21.92, p = 0.013), ventral (OR = 4.91, p = 0.049), and total (OR = 3.70, p = 0.019) bridges corresponded to less severe baseline AIS grade. Pinprick scores increased with ventral ( β = 26.56, p = 0.020) and total ( β = 17.50, p = 0.023) bridge width, and light touch scores increased with total bridge width ( β = 16.22, p = 0.045). No imaging metric was associated with LEMS. These individual-metric associations were nominally significant but did not survive correction. In GST analyses, larger ventral ( T = 4.63, p = 0.012, p '= 0.048) and total ( T = 4.30, p = 0.019, p '=0.048) bridges predicted greater overall recovery; both remained significant after correction and were stable across sensitivity analyses. Ventral and total bridge width showed nominally significant interactions with riluzole treatment for upper-limb motor recovery. Exploratory DTI findings were inconclusive and sensitive to individual observations: both the FA-recovery association and the observation of poor outcome despite a preserved tissue bridge rested on a single participant. Overall, we found that midsagittal tissue-bridge width measured ∼72 h after injury from standard-of-care T2-weighted MRI was associated with baseline injury severity and multidomain functional recovery, at a timepoint substantially earlier than the 1 month at which tissue bridges have previously been quantified. Because edema may obscure lesion margins this early, acute bridge widths may underestimate spared tissue resolvable later. The treatment-interaction observation is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective confirmation. These findings support MRI-derived tissue bridges as candidate biomarkers for prognostication and enrichment of neuroprotective trials in SCI.

items.title: Attitudes toward eating disorders among primary care physicians.
items.abstract: Background Eating disorders are severe conditions associated with high morbidity, mortality and socioeconomic burden. Primary care physicians are central in their early detection and treatment, but clinicians have been found to have limited knowledge and even negative attitudes toward eating disorder patients. Most studies have focused on anorexia nervosa (AN) and bulimia nervosa (BN), while less is known about attitudes toward binge eating disorder (BED) and avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID). Aim To examine primary care physicians' attitudes toward eating disorders and assess whether education and clinical experience predict comfort in management and willingness to work with affected patients. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted among primary care physicians ( n = 191) attending a mandatory seminar. Attitudes toward AN, BN, BED and ARFID were assessed using Likert-type items based on prior research. Ordinal logistic regression analyses examined associations between education, experience and selected attitudes. Results Overall attitudes were similar across diagnoses. Only 14-21% reported enjoying working with eating disorder patients. Education was consistently associated with greater comfort in management and enjoyment of working with these patients, whereas clinical experience was more strongly associated with comfort in management than with enjoyment. Familiarity with ARFID was low, reflected in reduced response rate (14.6%). Conclusions Attitudes toward eating disorders were broadly similar across diagnoses, but positive attitudes toward working with affected patients were uncommon. Education was consistently associated with more favorable attitudes and greater confidence in management, highlighting the potential value of continuing professional education and support for eating disorder care in primary care.

items.title: Real-time geometric complexity of language is associated with global functioning across psychosis and major depression.
items.abstract: Language disturbances are prominent across psychiatric disorders, yet their underlying organization and relationship to clinical functioning remain poorly understood. We conceptualized spontaneous speech as a temporally evolving sequence of contextual representations through semantic space, in which successive concepts define transitions between large-language-model embeddings. We characterized the local dynamics of these representations using Lyapunov-inspired measures of sensitivity to perturbation and anisotropy-the extent to which nearby neighboring contextual representations diverge differently depending on direction in representational space. We applied this approach to picture descriptions from 129 German-speaking participants with major depressive disorder (n = 43), schizophrenia spectrum disorders (n = 42), or no psychiatric diagnosis (n = 44). Individual differences in local geometric dynamics predicted multiple clinical dimensions, with the strongest association observed for global functioning, for which the geometric measures explained 51% of the variance. Clinically informative geometric structure was already detectable within the first three sentences of speech, where distinct dynamical profiles were associated with differences in negative and positive symptoms, anxiety, depression, and global functioning. These associations suggest that the dynamics of local representational divergence and contraction during speech reflect broad variation in cognitive and social functioning rather than diagnosis alone. Together, these findings suggest that psychiatric variation is reflected not simply in what people say, but in the dynamics by which semantic representations evolve during ongoing language production. A dynamical-geometric analysis of language may provide a compact, transdiagnostic marker of clinically meaningful variation in psychopathology.

items.title: Serum selenium, iron and rubidium are altered in treatment-resistant schizophrenia.
items.abstract: The molecular basis of schizophrenia is complex, involving an interplay of genetic and environmental factors. In recent postmortem and imaging studies, we identified disturbances in iron homeostasis in cortical and subcortical regions of individuals with schizophrenia. These may be relevant to neuropathology identified in the disorder and could relate to mechanisms of oxidative stress and inflammation. Recent work has proposed that there is a dysregulation of brain metals and other elements in schizophrenia that might impact on oxidative stress. Using a metallomics approach, we report robust changes in serum levels of pro-oxidant iron, anti-oxidant selenium, and the potassium-marker, rubidium, in a cohort of people with treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS). The cohort also expressed elevated levels of serum pro-inflammatory cytokines and hepcidin, and lower levels of anti-oxidant selenoproteins, selenoprotein-P1 (SEPP1) and glutathione peroxidase 3 (GPX3). The changes in serum iron, rubidium and selenium discriminate between control individuals and TRS cases, and they were not affected by age or clozapine serum levels. We propose that the changes in selenium and cytokines might drive the expression of hepcidin, resulting in reduced serum iron levels. Further research should investigate the relationship between peripheral and central measures of these elements and their metabolism, and further explore the relevance of pro-oxidant stress to the neuropathology of schizophrenia.

items.title: Dynamic epigenetic changes during antidepressant pharmacotherapy in major depressive disorder.
items.abstract: Although antidepressants remain the main pharmacological treatment for major depressive disorder (MDD), therapeutic response varies, highlighting the need for molecular markers that predict treatment response, as well as insights into the biological processes underlying antidepressant efficacy. Candidate-gene and cross-sectional epigenome-wide association studies (EWAS) have reported DNA methylation signatures associated with antidepressant response; however, findings remain inconsistent. To date, no longitudinal EWAS has examined methylation trajectories across multiple time points during antidepressant treatment in MDD. Within the Early Medication Change trial, DNA methylation data was generated for 162 patients with MDD (81 responders, 81 non-responders) and 48 matched healthy controls. Patients were assessed at four times across eight-weeks of standardized antidepressant treatment, while controls were assessed twice. Differentially methylated positions (DMPs) and regions (DMRs) were identified using longitudinal EWAS models and the comb-p algorithm. Baseline methylation levels were associated with depressive symptom severity at day 28 and day 56 through two and six DMRs, respectively (e.g., TNRC6C, CAT), whereas no single DMP reached significance. Longitudinal analyses identified one DMP associated with improvement in depressive symptoms (YLMP1) and three DMRs showing methylation changes over time (e.g., GPR126, PM20D1). Combined patient-control analyses revealed additional DMPs and DMRs associated with diagnosis and temporal effects. This study provides first longitudinal evidence of regionally coordinated DNA methylation changes during antidepressant pharmacotherapy, revealing alterations in genes involved in neuroplasticity and inflammatory processes that are associated with clinical response. Replication and functional validation will be essential to determine their relevance for personalized antidepressant treatment.

items.title: High-fat diet feeding rapidly induces sex-specific neuronal plasticity in lateral hypothalamic glutamatergic neurons.
items.abstract: Hypothalamic circuits play a central role in coordinating feeding and energy balance, yet how these circuits adapt to dietary excess to regulate body weight remains poorly understood. Lateral hypothalamic area glutamatergic (LHA Vglut2 ) neurons critically mediate food intake and body weight, but how they adapt their function to acute overfeeding and whether such adaptation is sexually dimorphic are unknown. Here, we examined the impact of high-fat diet (HFD) on LHA Vglut2 neurons in mice. Whole-cell recordings revealed baseline sex differences in neuronal properties: female LHA Vglut2 neurons exhibited higher basal excitability and differential synaptic input compared to males. HFD feeding produced distinct forms of neuronal plasticity between sexes within 1 day. In males, HFD increased intrinsic excitability while excitatory synaptic input was decreased. In contrast, excitability of female LHA Vglut2 neurons remained unchanged, but inhibitory synaptic strength was selectively reduced. To test the causal relationship between enhanced LHA Vglut2 neuron excitability and weight gain during overfeeding, we expressed the depolarizing sodium channel NaChBac to chronically increase LHA Vglut2 neuron excitability. Chronic elevation of LHA Vglut2 neuron excitability suppressed body weight gain during acute HFD exposure in males, whereas females displayed significant weight loss during HFD exposure. Together, these results suggest that female mice may be protected from diet-induced obesity via sexually dimorphic LHA Vglut2 neurons. In males, overfeeding rapidly induces compensatory changes in LHA Vglut2 neuron excitability that may act to limit body weight gain. Further enhancement of LHA Vglut2 neuron excitability can suppress weight gain in an obesogenic environment for both males and females. Significance Statement Chronic overeating alters hypothalamic circuits that regulate feeding, but the time course of these adaptations and whether they differ between sexes is poorly understood. Here we show that overeating engages lateral hypothalamic glutamatergic neurons, which negatively regulate food intake and body weight, through sexually dimorphic mechanisms. In males but not females, overfeeding rapidly enhances excitability of lateral hypothalamic glutamatergic neurons. These sex-specific adaptations lead to distinct behavioral outcomes following chronic neuronal activation. Our findings reveal that hypothalamic circuits employ fundamentally different strategies across sexes to respond to dietary excess, providing insight into sex-dependent vulnerability to metabolic disorders.

items.title: Adult-onset auditory deprivation enhances attenuation of neural responses in the visual cortex and improves peripheral visual acuity.
items.abstract: The ability of the brain to undergo plastic changes throughout the lifespan of an organism is essential to optimize its interactions with its environment. Adaptation to sensory loss is observed as cross-modal recruitment of the cortical areas deprived of their own sensory inputs by the spared senses and as compensatory plasticity of the spared cortical areas. The former is thought to increase the cortical resource for processing information related to the spared modalities and the latter is thought to refine the spared senses. In animal models, synaptic and circuit-level plasticity have been observed in both the deprived primary sensory cortex and in the spared primary sensory cortices. In this study, we examined how the primary visual cortex (V1) adapts to cross-modal auditory deprivation initiated in adult mice of both sexes. To do this, we recorded the stimulus-evoked neural activity in V1 layer 2/3 (L2/3) using 2-photon calcium imaging and presented visual stimuli restricted to either the central or the peripheral visual field. We found that adult-onset deafening intensified the attenuation of stimulus-evoked responses to a range of stimuli, largely in the medial V1 representing the peripheral monocular visual field, without affecting the population decoding capability. Furthermore, adult-onset deaf mice exhibited selective behavioral improvement on peripheral visual acuity for detecting static gratings, without changes in contrast sensitivity for detecting moving gratings. Our findings suggest enhancement of neural attenuation may support compensatory plasticity in adult V1, which may benefit the stimulus encoding efficiency to improve detection of fine peripheral visual features. Significance Statement Losing a sensory modality leads to widespread brain adaptation to enhance the remaining senses. In addition to cross-modal recruitment, which repurposes the deprived brain areas to process the spared senses, there is functional refinement of the spared sensory areas referred to as compensatory plasticity. While plasticity is prominent for early-onset sensory loss, functional compensation is also observed after adult-onset sensory loss. Here, we report that adult-onset deafness in mice accentuates attenuation of visual cortical responses to visual stimuli, especially in the peripheral visual field, with indications of more efficient coding. Additionally, deafened adult mice show rather selective improvement on peripheral visual acuity. Our study suggests a mechanism of compensatory plasticity in the adult visual cortex, which may benefit visual function.

items.title: Aquaporin channels in cytotoxic brain edema following severe head trauma: Systematic review of molecular mechanisms and therapy.
items.abstract: Cytotoxic brain edema significantly worsens outcomes in severe traumatic brain injury (TBI), but the molecular pathways involved aren't fully characterized. This review draws on studies published since 2015 to assess how aquaporin-4 (AQP4), the only AQP isoform evaluated across the included studies, contributes to edema formation and resolution, and interventions targeting it. PubMed, Scopus, and CINAHL were searched for studies published between January 2015 and December 2025 examining AQPs in post-TBI cytotoxic edema in preclinical or human observational studies. Study design, TBI model, edema metrics, and intervention effects were extracted. Risk of bias was appraised narratively (SYRCLE for animal studies; Newcastle-Ottawa for the single human study). Forty-two studies described post-TBI changes in AQP4 expression and polarity across controlled cortical impact, cryogenic, and diffuse injury models. Loss of perivascular AQP4 polarity accompanied impaired water clearance and worsening swelling, whereas restored polarization accompanied edema resolution. Because the measures used could not cleanly separate cytotoxic from ionic and vasogenic edema, outcomes are reported as total or mixed edema except where a method isolated intracellular swelling. Direct strategies (siRNA, antisense oligonucleotides, knockout) reduced brain water but faced delivery and timing barriers; pharmacologic agents such as fingolimod and minocycline modulated AQP4 and improved edema and function. Translational readiness varied across models and metrics. These predominantly preclinical findings identify AQP4 modulation as a mechanistically compelling strategy for cytotoxic edema after severe TBI; however, direct clinical evidence remains minimal, and translational claims should be interpreted with caution. Standardized preclinical frameworks and early-phase safety evaluation are needed.
